爸爸仔細看著紅圈圈：「原來你常把字母的順序弄反了。我們來玩個遊戲！」爸爸拿出小白板，念一個單字，{name}就寫一個。寫錯了，兩人就一起拍手唸三遍字母，再寫一次。{name}越寫越順，還咯咯笑出聲。
最後，爸爸在考卷上簽了名，旁邊畫了一個小笑臉。「你願意跟我說實話，我就知道我可以相信你。以後遇到難題，先來找我，好嗎？」{name}用力點點頭。那天晚上，{name}抱著枕頭，睡得又香又甜。
en: On Monday afternoon, {name} came home holding a spelling test very tightly. There was a big 60 at the top and red circles all over the page. The teacher wanted Dad to sign it, and it had to go back to school on Friday.

"How was school today, {name}?" Dad called from the kitchen. {name}'s heart went thump, thump. "Fine!" Then {name} hurried to the bedroom, folded the test into a tiny square, and pushed it under the socks at the very back of a drawer.

On Tuesday, Dad made {name}'s favorite tomato eggs, but they didn't taste good at all. On Wednesday, Dad told a silly joke, and {name} could only give a small smile. The hidden test felt like a heavy rock that followed {name} everywhere.

On Thursday night, {name} tossed and turned and could not fall asleep. "Will Dad be disappointed in me?" {name} wondered. But the test was due tomorrow. Quietly, {name} opened the drawer, took out the wrinkled paper, and took a deep breath.

{name} carried the test into the living room. Dad looked up from a book. "Still awake?" In a very small voice, {name} said, "Dad, I did badly on my spelling test, and I hid it because I was afraid you'd be mad." {his} eyes felt hot and teary.

Dad set down the book and lifted {name} onto his lap. Gently, he smoothed the paper flat. "Thank you for telling me," Dad said softly. "That took a lot of courage, didn't it?" {name} nodded, and the heavy rock suddenly felt as light as a feather.

Dad studied the red circles. "I see! You often mix up the order of the letters. Let's play a game." He grabbed a little whiteboard and read out words for {name} to write. After each mistake, they clapped out the letters three times and tried again. Soon {name} was giggling and getting them right.

At last, Dad signed the test and drew a tiny smiley face beside his name. "When you tell me the truth, I know I can trust you. Next time something is hard, come to me first, okay?" {name} nodded hard, then hugged a pillow and slept sweetly all night.

questions: {name}把考卷藏起來以後，心裡有什麼感覺？為什麼會這樣？
{name}說了實話以後，爸爸怎麼幫忙？
如果你做錯了事，有點害怕說出來，你可以怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這週每天睡前，和孩子玩「今天的小實話」：彼此說一件今天發生、有點難開口的小事，聽完先說一句「謝謝你告訴我」。

questions: How did {name} feel while the test was hidden? Why do you think so?
What did Dad do to help after {name} told the truth?
If you made a mistake and felt scared to tell, what could you do?
en.tip: This week at bedtime, play "One True Thing": each of you shares one small thing from the day that was a little hard to say, and the listener always answers first with "Thank you for telling me."

zh: 星期一早上，班上來了一位新同學，她叫安安。安安戴著一副厚厚的圓眼鏡，說話小小聲的。下課時，阿哲指著她大笑：「你們看，貓頭鷹眼睛！」幾個同學也跟著笑起來，安安低下頭，手指緊緊捏著鉛筆。
{name}坐在旁邊，心裡像吞了一顆小石頭，沉沉的、怪怪的。{name}想說點什麼，可是嘴巴好像被黏住了。那一整個上午，「貓頭鷹眼睛」這幾個字一直在教室裡飄來飄去，安安一次也沒有抬起頭。
午餐時間到了，大家都找好朋友坐在一起，只有安安一個人坐在角落。{name}端著餐盤，站在原地猶豫了好一會兒，然後深深吸一口氣，走過去問：「我可以坐這裡嗎？」安安愣了一下，輕輕點點頭，嘴角悄悄往上翹。
兩個人一邊吃飯一邊聊天。原來安安很會畫畫，還知道好多星星的名字。「其實我很喜歡貓頭鷹，」安安小聲說，「可是他們那樣叫我，是在笑我。」{name}認真地說：「笑別人是他們不對，你一點錯都沒有。」
下午體育課要玩傳球遊戲，阿哲又喊：「別讓貓頭鷹加入，她一定會漏接！」{name}的心怦怦跳，還是舉起手說：「安安跟我同一隊！」第一球飛過來，安安穩穩接住了。{name}拍手大喊：「接得好！」其他隊友也跟著歡呼。
放學前，{name}站在老師辦公室門口，腳步停了又停。要是被說愛告狀怎麼辦？可是一想起安安低著頭的樣子，{name}還是敲了敲門，把事情一五一十告訴林老師。林老師蹲下來，溫柔地說：「謝謝你告訴我。這不是告狀，是在幫安安找大人幫忙。」
第二天，林老師請大家圍成一圈，問：「如果有人叫你一個你不喜歡的綽號，你會有什麼感覺？」教室安靜下來。有人說會難過，有人說會想躲起來。阿哲的臉紅紅的，過了一會兒，他走到安安面前說：「對不起，我以後不會再那樣叫你了。」
林老師請每個人替旁邊的同學想一個好聽的稱呼，寫在小卡片上。安安拿到的卡片寫著「星星小畫家」，她笑得眼睛彎彎的。下課鐘一響，安安跑過來拉著{name}的手：「我們再去玩傳球吧！」{name}笑著點頭，心裡輕飄飄的，好像長了翅膀。
en: On Monday morning, a new girl named An-An joined the class. She wore thick, round glasses and spoke in a tiny voice. At recess, A-Zhe pointed and laughed. "Look, Owl Eyes!" A few kids giggled along. An-An looked down and squeezed her pencil tight.

{name} sat nearby, and a heavy, wobbly feeling settled inside, like swallowing a small stone. {name} wanted to say something, but the words seemed stuck. All morning, the words "Owl Eyes" floated around the classroom, and An-An never once lifted her head.

At lunchtime, everyone sat with their friends, but An-An sat all alone in the corner. {name} stood holding a lunch tray, unsure, for a long moment. Then {name} took a deep breath, walked over, and asked, "Can I sit here?" An-An blinked, nodded, and smiled a little.

As they ate, they chatted. An-An loved drawing and knew the names of lots of stars. "I actually like owls," she whispered. "But when they call me that, they're laughing at me." {name} said firmly, "Laughing at you is wrong. It's not your fault at all."

In the afternoon, the class played a passing game in gym. A-Zhe called out, "Don't let Owl Eyes play. She'll drop it!" {name}'s heart thumped, but up went {his} hand. "An-An is on my team!" The first ball flew over, and An-An caught it. "Great catch!" {name} cheered, and the team cheered too.

Before going home, {name} stood outside the teacher's office, stopping and starting. What if people called it tattling? Then {name} remembered An-An's lowered head, knocked, and told Ms. Lin everything. Ms. Lin knelt down and said gently, "Thank you for telling me. That's not tattling. You're getting help for An-An."

The next day, Ms. Lin asked everyone to sit in a circle. "How would you feel if someone called you a name you didn't like?" The room went quiet. Some said sad. Some said they'd want to hide. A-Zhe's cheeks turned pink. He walked over to An-An. "I'm sorry. I won't call you that again."

Ms. Lin asked each child to think of a kind name for a classmate and write it on a card. An-An's card said "Little Star Artist," and her eyes crinkled with joy. When the bell rang, she grabbed {name}'s hand. "Let's play catch again!" {name} nodded, feeling light enough to fly.

questions: 當同學叫安安「貓頭鷹眼睛」時，{name}做了哪些事來幫她？
{name}在老師辦公室門口為什麼猶豫？你覺得告訴老師是告狀，還是找人幫忙？
如果你看到有人被取笑，或是你自己被取笑，你可以怎麼做、可以找誰？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子一起練習一句話：「我需要幫忙，有人一直取笑我（或某某同學）。」並一起列出在學校和家裡可以求助的大人名字。

questions: When classmates called An-An "Owl Eyes," what did {name} do to help her?
Why did {name} hesitate outside the teacher's office? Do you think telling the teacher was tattling or getting help?
If you saw someone being teased, or if someone teased you, what could you do and who could you tell?
en.tip: This week, practice one sentence together: "I need help, someone keeps teasing me (or my classmate)." Then make a list of grown-ups at school and at home your child can go to.

zh: 晚餐後，{name}剛寫完數學作業，平板就「叮咚、叮咚」響個不停。班級群組裡，志豪貼了一張照片：那是偉廷上體育課跑步的樣子，卻被修成了豬鼻子、大耳朵，旁邊還寫著「偉廷豬衝刺中」。不到一分鐘，哈哈大笑的貼圖就像下冰雹一樣，劈哩啪啦地洗滿了整個螢幕。
{name}的手指停在笑臉貼圖上方，遲遲沒有按下去。腦海裡浮現的，是上星期偉廷默默把新橡皮擦切一半借給{him}的畫面，還有他總是靦腆地低頭微笑的樣子。{name}的胃像打了一個結。大家都在笑，可是這件事，真的好笑嗎？
{name}深吸一口氣，關掉群組，點開偉廷的名字，一個字一個字地打：「那張圖一點都不好笑，你沒有做錯任何事。明天下課要不要一起打躲避球？」按下送出後，訊息旁邊很快出現「已讀」，卻遲遲沒有回覆。{name}盯著螢幕，坐立難安，連最愛的布丁都忘了吃。
媽媽端著水果走過來：「布丁都快融化了，有心事嗎？」{name}支支吾吾地問：「如果我說出來，大家會不會覺得我是抓耙仔？」媽媽坐下來，輕聲問：「抓耙仔是想讓別人挨罵；求救是想讓人不再受傷。你現在想做的是哪一種？」{name}想了想，把平板遞了過去。
媽媽看完照片，眉頭一皺，立刻陪{name}傳訊息給陳老師。沒多久，老師就打電話來了。「謝謝你告訴我，這需要很大的勇氣。」陳老師的聲音溫和又堅定，「這種圖不管是誰做的、誰在笑，都不可以。偉廷一點錯也沒有，接下來交給老師處理。」{name}緊繃的肩膀，終於慢慢放鬆下來。
過了一會兒，偉廷回訊息了：「謝謝你。我剛剛本來想退出群組。」後面附了一張畫，兩個小人正在操場上丟躲避球，其中一個還誇張地飛了起來。這時，陳老師也在群組發了言，那張照片被收回，志豪傳了一句「偉廷，對不起」。剛才還鬧哄哄的群組，忽然安靜得連一根針掉下來都聽得見。
正要去刷牙時，平板又叮咚響了，這次是三則私訊。小美寫：「其實我也覺得不好笑，按貼圖只是怕被當成怪人。」阿凱和佳佳也說了差不多的話，還問：「明天躲避球，可以算我們一份嗎？」{name}愣了一下，忍不住笑出聲來，飛快地回覆：「當然！人越多越好玩，記得找偉廷當隊長！」
en: After dinner, {name} had just finished math homework when the tablet began to ding, ding, ding. In the class group chat, Zhi-Hao had posted a photo of Wei-Ting running in gym class. Someone had edited it to give him a pig snout and floppy ears, with the words "Piggy Wei-Ting Sprints!" Within a minute, laughing stickers were pelting the screen like hailstones.

{name}'s finger hovered over a laughing sticker, but didn't press it. {name} remembered last week, when Wei-Ting had quietly cut his brand-new eraser in half to share, and the shy way he always smiled at the floor. {name}'s stomach twisted into a knot. Everyone was laughing. But was this actually funny?

Taking a deep breath, {name} closed the group chat, tapped Wei-Ting's name, and typed slowly: "That picture isn't funny at all. You didn't do anything wrong. Want to play dodgeball with me at recess tomorrow?" The message showed "Read" almost at once, but no answer came. {name} stared at the screen, fidgeting, and forgot all about a favorite pudding.

Mom came over with a plate of fruit. "Your pudding is melting. Something on your mind?" {name} hesitated. "If I tell, will everyone think I'm a tattletale?" Mom sat down and asked gently, "Tattling is trying to get someone in trouble. Asking for help is trying to stop someone from getting hurt. Which one are you doing?" {name} thought about it, then handed over the tablet.

Mom looked at the photo and frowned. Together, they sent a message to Ms. Chen, the teacher, and soon the phone rang. "Thank you for telling me. That took real courage," Ms. Chen said, warm but firm. "Pictures like this are never okay, no matter who makes them or laughs at them. Wei-Ting did nothing wrong. I'll take it from here." {name}'s tight shoulders finally relaxed.

A little later, Wei-Ting replied: "Thank you. I was about to leave the group." He added a drawing of two stick figures playing dodgeball, one leaping comically high into the air. Meanwhile, Ms. Chen posted in the group chat. The photo disappeared, and Zhi-Hao typed, "Sorry, Wei-Ting." The chat that had been so noisy went completely, pin-drop silent.

Just as {name} was heading off to brush teeth, the tablet dinged again. Three private messages. Mei wrote, "I didn't think it was funny either. I only sent a sticker so nobody would think I was weird." Kai and Jia-Jia said almost the same thing, and asked, "Can we join dodgeball tomorrow?" {name} blinked, then laughed out loud and typed, "Of course! The more the better. Let's make Wei-Ting team captain!"

questions: 大家都在傳笑臉貼圖時，{name}做了哪些不一樣的事？你覺得偉廷收到訊息時是什麼心情？
{name}擔心被說是「抓耙仔」。你覺得告訴老師或爸媽，和告狀有什麼不同？
如果你在群組或學校看到有人被取笑，你可以怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子一起練習一句話：「這不好笑，我們別這樣。」並約定好，只要在網路或學校看到讓人不舒服的事，隨時都可以拿給你看，你會陪著一起想辦法。

questions: When everyone was sending laughing stickers, what did {name} do differently? How do you think Wei-Ting felt when he got {name}'s message?
{name} worried about being called a tattletale. What's the difference between tattling and telling a grown-up to get help?
If you saw someone being made fun of in a group chat or at school, what could you do?
en.tip: This week, practice one simple phrase together: "That's not funny. Let's stop." Then agree that whenever your child sees something hurtful online or at school, they can show you anytime, and you'll figure it out together.

zh: 每天下課，林老師都會帶全班到學校旁邊的榕樹公園玩躲避球。草地上笑聲此起彼落，可是{name}總注意到一件事：每次分隊，柏安總是最後一個被叫到。他安安靜靜地站在溜滑梯旁，雙手插在口袋裡，而子豪和幾個同學會拉長聲音：「唉——又是他喔？」柏安只好低下頭，假裝在研究鞋帶。
{name}心裡像卡了一顆小石子。柏安明明什麼也沒做錯，為什麼要被這樣對待？星期三，林老師吹了一聲哨子：「今天換{name}和子豪當隊長！」{name}深吸一口氣，眼睛掃過整排同學，最後停在溜滑梯旁。「我第一個選柏安。」四周頓時鴉雀無聲，柏安抬起頭，眼睛睜得圓滾滾的，像不敢相信自己的耳朵。
子豪皺起眉頭：「你是認真的嗎？他連球都很少碰欸！」幾個同學又開始唉聲嘆氣。{name}的手心直冒汗，卻沒有退縮。「其他人我們用報數的好了，一、二、一、二，單數一隊，雙數一隊，這樣最公平。」林老師點點頭：「好主意。」大家只好排成一列，一個接一個報數，這下誰也不會是最後一個了。
比賽開始了。球咻咻地在草地上飛來飛去，同學們尖叫著四處閃躲。{name}很快就被打中，只好垂頭喪氣地走到場外。沒想到，柏安像一隻靈巧的松鼠，左閃右躲，球怎麼丟都碰不到他。子豪用力一扔，球直衝過來——柏安穩穩接住，順勢一回傳，竟然把子豪淘汰出局！場邊爆出一陣歡呼。
原來柏安每天傍晚都和爺爺在家門口練接球，只是從來沒有人給過他機會。下課鐘響時，子豪摸摸鼻子，小聲說：「你……接得滿厲害的。」柏安靦腆地笑了。可是{name}還記得那些唉聲嘆氣，還有柏安低頭盯著鞋帶的樣子。今天贏了一場球，那明天呢？
排隊回教室的路上，{name}放慢腳步，走到林老師身邊，心裡七上八下。「老師，我不是要打小報告……可是每次分隊，都有人對柏安唉聲嘆氣，他看起來很難過。」林老師停下來，認真地看著{name}：「謝謝你告訴我。這不是打小報告，這是在幫柏安找幫手。被這樣對待，從來都不是柏安的錯。」
第二天，林老師宣布：以後躲避球一律報數分隊，全班還要一起訂「好隊友守則」。子豪舉手說：「第一條，不可以唉聲嘆氣！」大家哄堂大笑。那天下課，柏安不再站在溜滑梯旁，他直接走到{name}身邊，輕輕撞了一下{his}肩膀：「一、二，我們同一隊？」{name}笑著點頭：「當然！」
en: Every day at recess, Ms. Lin walked the class to Banyan Park next to the school for dodgeball. The grass rang with laughter, but {name} kept noticing one thing. When teams were picked, Bo-an was always called last. He waited quietly by the slide, hands in his pockets, while Zihao and a few others groaned, "Ugh, him again?" Bo-an would stare at his shoelaces as if they were fascinating.

The groaning sat in {name}'s chest like a pebble in a shoe. Bo-an hadn't done anything wrong, so why did this keep happening? On Wednesday, Ms. Lin blew her whistle. "Today's captains are {name} and Zihao!" {name} took a deep breath, scanned the line, and looked toward the slide. "I pick Bo-an first." The park went silent. Bo-an's eyes went wide, as if he'd misheard.

Zihao frowned. "Are you serious? He barely touches the ball!" A few kids sighed loudly. {name}'s palms were sweaty, but {he} didn't back down. "Let's count off for everyone else. One, two, one, two. Ones on my team, twos on Zihao's. That's fair." "Good idea," said Ms. Lin. So everyone lined up and counted off, and this time nobody had to be last.

The game began. The ball whizzed across the grass while kids shrieked and scattered. {name} got tagged early and trudged to the sideline. Then something unexpected happened. Bo-an darted left and right like a nimble squirrel, and no throw could touch him. Zihao hurled the ball hard, but Bo-an snatched it out of the air and fired it back, knocking Zihao out! The sideline erupted in cheers.

It turned out Bo-an practiced catching with his grandpa every evening outside their home. Nobody had ever given him a chance to show it. When the bell rang, Zihao rubbed his nose and mumbled, "You... catch pretty well." Bo-an grinned shyly. But {name} still remembered the groans and the way Bo-an had stared at his shoes. One good game was great. But what about tomorrow?

On the walk back, {name} slowed down to walk beside Ms. Lin, stomach fluttering. "I'm not trying to tattle, but every time we pick teams, some kids groan about Bo-an. He looks really sad." Ms. Lin stopped and looked right at {name}. "Thank you for telling me. That's not tattling. That's getting Bo-an some help. And being treated that way is never his fault."

The next day, Ms. Lin announced that dodgeball teams would always be counted off, and the class would write Good Teammate Rules together. Zihao raised his hand. "Rule one: no groaning!" Everyone burst out laughing. At recess, Bo-an didn't wait by the slide. He walked straight over to {name} and gently bumped {his} shoulder. "One, two... same team?" {name} grinned. "Definitely!"

questions: {name}當隊長時做了哪些事，讓柏安不再是最後一個？
{name}去找林老師時說「我不是要打小報告」，你覺得告訴大人和打小報告有什麼不一樣？
如果你看到有同學一直被冷落或被取笑，你可以怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子練習一句「求助句」：「老師，我看到有人一直被欺負，可以請您幫忙嗎？」並告訴孩子，任何時候來告訴你，你都會認真聽。

questions: What did {name} do as captain so Bo-an wasn't last anymore?
When {name} told Ms. Lin, {he} said, "I'm not trying to tattle." How is telling a grown-up different from tattling?
If you saw a classmate being left out or teased again and again, what could you do?
en.tip: This week, practice one "getting help" sentence together: "Teacher, someone keeps getting picked on. Can you help?" Let your child know you will always listen carefully whenever they come to tell you.

zh: 午後的陽光，暖暖地照進客廳。窗台上亮亮的，可是空空的。以前，豆豆最愛躺在那裡。她會捲成一顆橘色毛球，瞇著眼睛曬太陽。豆豆是一隻很老很老的貓。上個星期，她安安靜靜地去世了。{name}站在窗台旁，輕輕摸著那塊暖暖的地方。
{name}覺得眼睛熱熱的，眼淚掉了下來。爸爸走過來，蹲在旁邊。他把{name}抱進懷裡，抱得好緊好緊。「我也好想豆豆。」爸爸小聲說。「我們會哭，是因為好愛她。」{name}靠著爸爸，哭了一下下。爸爸的手，一下一下輕拍著{his}背。
過了一會兒，爸爸說：「我想到一個好主意。我們來做一本小小的圖畫書，畫豆豆最喜歡的地方，好不好？」{name}擦擦眼淚，點點頭。爸爸拿來白白的紙，{name}拿來一盒蠟筆。他們一起坐在地毯上，準備開始畫。
第一頁，{name}畫了窗台。{he}畫了一個圓圓的大太陽，又畫了一隻捲成一團的橘貓。那就是豆豆！爸爸問：「還記得嗎？她曬太陽時，會呼嚕呼嚕地叫。」{name}點點頭。那輕輕的呼嚕聲，好像又在耳邊了。
第二頁，是沙發上的軟毯子。豆豆冷的時候，最愛鑽進毯子裡。第三頁，是裝襪子的小籃子。有一次，豆豆睡在襪子堆裡，還叼走一隻小襪子！{name}想到這裡，忍不住笑了。爸爸也笑了。「原來想她的時候，也可以笑。」{name}說。
窗外的天空慢慢變成橘色，又變成深藍色。晚上到了。爸爸用釘書機把紙釘好，在封面寫上「豆豆最愛的地方」。{name}在旁邊畫了一顆小愛心。洗完澡，刷好牙，屋子裡好安靜。只聽見時鐘滴答、滴答地走著。
{name}躺進軟軟的被窩。床邊的小燈亮著，黃黃的，暖暖的。爸爸翻開小書，慢慢地念。「豆豆在窗台上，曬著暖暖的太陽。」「豆豆在毯子裡，睡得好香好香。」「豆豆在籃子裡，抱著一隻小襪子。」爸爸慢慢念，{name}輕輕聽。
念完了，{name}小聲說：「我還是有一點難過。」爸爸輕輕抱住{him}。「我小時候養過一隻小狗。一開始，我想牠就會哭。後來，想到牠，我會微笑。我們對豆豆的愛，會一直都在。」{name}把小書放在枕頭旁。屋子好安靜，{name}慢慢睡著了。晚安，{name}。晚安，豆豆。
en: Afternoon sun warmed the living room. The windowsill was bright, but empty. Doudou used to nap there. She curled up like a fuzzy orange ball. Doudou was a very, very old cat. Last week, she died peacefully. {name} touched the warm, empty spot.

{name}'s eyes felt hot, and tears fell. Dad came over and knelt down. He gave {name} a big, tight hug. "I miss Doudou too," he whispered. "We cry because we love her so much." Dad patted {his} back, softly, softly.

After a while, Dad had an idea. "Let's make a little picture book," he said. "We can draw Doudou's favorite spots." {name} wiped away the tears and nodded. Dad brought paper. {name} brought crayons. They sat together on the rug.

On page one, {name} drew the windowsill. Next came a big round sun. Then a curled-up orange cat. That was Doudou! "Remember her purr?" Dad asked. "Purr, purr, purr." {name} nodded. The soft sound felt close again.

Page two showed the cozy blanket on the sofa. Doudou loved to snuggle under it. Page three showed the sock basket. Once, Doudou napped in the socks and carried one away! {name} giggled. Dad laughed too. "I can miss her and still smile," {name} said.

Outside, the sky turned orange, then deep blue. Evening had come. Dad stapled the pages together. He wrote "Doudou's Favorite Spots" on the cover. {name} drew a little heart beside it. After bath time and brushing teeth, the house grew quiet. Tick, tock, went the clock.

{name} snuggled into the soft bed. The little lamp glowed warm and yellow. Dad opened the book and read slowly. "Doudou on the windowsill, warm in the sun." "Doudou in the blanket, sleeping snug." "Doudou in the basket, hugging a sock."

"I'm still a little sad," {name} whispered. Dad gave {him} a gentle hug. "When I was small, I had a puppy," Dad said. "At first, missing my puppy made me cry. Later, thinking of her made me smile. Our love for Doudou will always stay." {name} placed the book by the pillow. The house was quiet, and {name} drifted off to sleep. Goodnight, {name}. Goodnight, Doudou.

questions: {name}想豆豆、哭出來的時候，爸爸做了什麼？
如果你想念一個很愛的寵物或朋友，你會想畫什麼、說什麼故事？
爸爸說，他想到小狗時，從會哭變成會微笑。你覺得為什麼會這樣？
zh.tip: 這週找一個晚上，和孩子一起畫一張「最喜歡的回憶」小卡，放在床邊，難過時可以一起拿出來看看、說說。

questions: What did Dad do when {name} missed Doudou and cried?
If you missed a pet or friend you love, what would you draw or tell a story about?
Dad said thinking of his puppy changed from crying to smiling. Why do you think that happened?
en.tip: One night this week, draw a little "favorite memory" card together and keep it by the bed, so you can look at it and talk whenever sad feelings come.

zh: 小烏龜「小石頭」陪了{name}好多好多年。牠走路慢吞吞，吃菜葉也慢吞吞。這個星期，小石頭已經很老很老了，在睡夢中安詳地過世了。{name}看著空空的水箱，喉嚨好像卡住了一樣，什麼話都說不出來。
星期六下午，媽媽牽著{name}的手去公園。「我們去池塘邊坐一坐，好嗎？」{name}輕輕點頭。兩個人在離水邊有一段距離的長椅上坐下。池塘中間有一根大木頭，上面趴著三隻野生烏龜，伸長脖子，正舒服地曬太陽。
「你看，那隻把腳縮起來的，像不像小石頭？」媽媽小聲地說。{name}本來想笑，眼淚卻先掉了下來：「我好想牠。」媽媽把{name}抱進懷裡：「想哭就哭吧。媽媽也很想牠，因為我們都好愛牠。」{name}靠在媽媽肩上，哭了好一會兒。
哭完以後，{name}擦擦鼻子，覺得心裡鬆了一點點。媽媽說：「我們來說小石頭的故事，好不好？一人說一個。」{name}想了好久，要開口好難，可是{he}還是深吸一口氣說：「有一次，牠躲進拖鞋裡，我們找了一整個早上！」
媽媽笑出聲來：「對耶！還有牠最愛吃草莓，每次都吃得滿嘴紅紅的。」{name}也想起來了：「牠在水裡會慢慢划腳，好像在跳舞。」一個故事接著一個故事，木頭上的烏龜還在曬太陽，{name}的嘴角也慢慢翹了起來。
太陽漸漸往下沉，木頭上的烏龜一隻一隻滑回水裡。「我們回家吧，」媽媽說，「我有一個好點子。」走在回家的步道上，{name}撿到一顆圓圓滑滑的石頭，摸起來暖暖的，就像小石頭的殼。媽媽說，可以帶回家。
到了家，媽媽拿出小鏟子和一包花種子。{name}在院子角落挖土，土好硬，手都挖痠了。{name}停下來喘口氣，又繼續挖。兩個人一起撒下種子、蓋好土，最後把圓石頭放在正中間。{name}用彩色筆在石頭上畫了一隻小烏龜。
幾個星期過去了。有一天早上，{name}發現石頭旁邊冒出好多小綠芽。{name}蹲下來，摸摸畫著小烏龜的石頭，輕輕說：「小石頭，早安。今天我又想起你吃草莓的樣子。」{he}還是會想念牠，可是這一次，{name}是笑著說的。
en: Pebble the turtle had lived with {name} for many, many years. Pebble walked slowly and munched lettuce slowly, too. This week, Pebble, who was very, very old, died peacefully in a long sleep. {name} looked at the empty tank, and words felt stuck in {his} throat.

On Saturday afternoon, Mom held {name}'s hand and walked to the park. "Shall we sit by the pond for a while?" {name} gave a small nod. They sat on a bench, a good way back from the water. Out on a big log, three wild turtles stretched their necks, sunbathing.

"Look at that one with its feet tucked in. Doesn't it look like Pebble?" Mom said softly. {name} almost smiled, but tears came first. "I miss Pebble so much." Mom pulled {name} into a hug. "It's okay to cry. I miss Pebble too, because we loved Pebble so much." {name} cried on Mom's shoulder for a long while.

After the tears, {name} wiped {his} nose and felt a tiny bit lighter. "Let's tell Pebble stories," Mom said. "We'll take turns." {name} thought for a long time. Starting felt hard, but {name} took a deep breath. "Once Pebble hid inside a slipper, and we searched all morning!"

Mom laughed out loud. "Yes! And Pebble loved strawberries and always got a red, juicy mouth." {name} remembered more. "In the water, Pebble paddled slowly, like dancing." Story after story, the turtles on the log kept sunbathing, and the corners of {name}'s mouth slowly curled up.

The sun sank lower, and the turtles slid back into the water one by one. "Let's go home," Mom said. "I have an idea." On the path home, {name} found a smooth, round stone. It felt warm, just like Pebble's shell. Mom said they could take it home.

At home, Mom brought out a little shovel and a packet of flower seeds. {name} dug in a corner of the yard. The dirt was hard, and {his} arms grew tired. {name} rested, then kept digging. Together they sprinkled the seeds and placed the stone right in the middle. {name} drew a little turtle on it with markers.

A few weeks passed. One morning, {name} spotted tiny green sprouts all around the stone. {name} crouched down and touched the turtle drawing. "Good morning, Pebble. Today I remembered you eating strawberries." {name} still missed Pebble, but this time, {name} said it with a smile.

questions: {name}在池塘邊哭的時候，媽媽做了什麼？你難過的時候，希望別人怎麼陪你？
{name}和媽媽用哪些方法來記得小石頭？如果是你，你會怎麼記得一個你愛的動物或人？
幾個星期後，{name}想起小石頭時有什麼不一樣？
zh.tip: 這個星期找一個晚上，和孩子一起畫一張「最喜歡的回憶」圖，邊畫邊說說那個故事，畫好後貼在家裡一個特別的角落。

questions: What did Mom do when {name} cried by the pond? When you feel sad, how do you like others to help you?
What did {name} and Mom do to remember Pebble? How would you remember an animal or person you love?
A few weeks later, what was different when {name} remembered Pebble?
en.tip: One evening this week, draw a "favorite memory" picture together and tell the story behind it as you draw, then hang it somewhere special at home.

zh: 每天清晨，爺爺家的金絲雀小檸檬都會準時開唱，一串清亮的顫音從窗邊流瀉出來，比鬧鐘還可靠，整整十五年風雨無阻。可是這個星期天早上，屋子裡靜悄悄的。爺爺說，小檸檬年紀很大了，昨夜在睡夢中安詳地離開了。{name}看著空空的鳥籠，喉嚨像卡了一顆小石頭。
爺爺沒有多說什麼。他照常泡茶、看報，可是報紙拿反了也沒發現，茶涼了也沒喝。{name}悄悄注意到，爺爺好幾次走到窗邊，伸手想打開鳥籠的小門，又默默把手縮回來。{name}鼓起勇氣，輕聲問：「爺爺，你很想小檸檬，對不對？」爺爺的眼眶一下子紅了：「是啊，好想。」
祖孫倆並肩坐在沙發上，爺爺的眼淚一滴一滴落下來，{name}的眼淚也跟著湧了出來。爺爺沒有擦掉，只是摟緊{name}說：「會哭，是因為我們好愛牠。」哭了一會兒，心裡反而鬆了一點。{name}忽然跳起來，拿來一本空白筆記本：「我們把小檸檬的故事寫下來，這樣就不會忘記了！」
回憶一打開，就停不下來。爺爺說，小檸檬最愛偷啄他的餅乾屑，被抓到了還理直氣壯地叫兩聲。{name}想起第一次餵牠吃青菜，牠竟把菜葉甩得滿桌都是。兩人笑得東倒西歪。{name}還用蠟筆畫了一隻黃澄澄的小鳥，站在爺爺的茶杯邊，神氣十足。
寫著寫著，{name}停下筆：「可是小檸檬的歌要怎麼寫？」爺爺想了想，嘟起嘴，吹出一段輕快的口哨，高高低低，婉轉悠揚，跟小檸檬一模一樣。{name}瞪大眼睛，立刻拿來平板錄下來。接著{name}也想學，卻只吹出「呼——呼——」的氣聲，像一台洩了氣的打氣筒。
{name}不肯放棄，洗完澡練，刷完牙也練，嘴巴都吹痠了。到了第三天，總算吹出一個細細的音，接著是第二個、第三個。爺爺拍手大笑：「有模有樣！」然後他眨眨眼說：「告訴你一個祕密。這首歌，其實是我年輕時常吹的曲子，小檸檬是聽我吹，才學會的。」
{name}愣住了，原來小檸檬的歌一直住在爺爺心裡。那天傍晚，祖孫倆把錄音和筆記本收在一起，封面寫著「小檸檬之歌」。爺爺望著鳥籠，這次嘴角帶著微笑。日子一天天過去，想念不再那麼刺痛，而每天早上，屋子裡依然響起清亮的口哨聲——有時是爺爺，有時是{name}。
en: Every morning for fifteen years, Grandpa's canary, Lemon, began to sing right on time, pouring bright trills from the window like a feathered alarm clock. Rain or shine, Lemon never missed a day. But this Sunday morning, the house was hushed. Grandpa explained that Lemon had been very old and had died peacefully in the night. {name} stared at the empty cage, throat tight as a knot.

Grandpa didn't say much. He made tea and opened the newspaper as usual, but he held the paper upside down without noticing, and his tea went cold. {name} watched him wander to the window again and again, reach for the little cage door, then slowly pull his hand back. Gathering courage, {name} whispered, "Grandpa, you really miss Lemon, don't you?" Grandpa's eyes went red. "Yes. So much."

They sat side by side on the sofa. Grandpa's tears fell quietly, and soon {name}'s tears came too. Grandpa didn't wipe them away. He just hugged {name} close and said, "We cry because we loved Lemon so much." After a while, their hearts felt a little lighter. Suddenly {name} sprang up and fetched a blank notebook. "Let's write down Lemon's stories, so we never forget!"

Once they started, the memories tumbled out. Grandpa told how Lemon loved stealing his cookie crumbs and, when caught, chirped back boldly as if to say, "Mine!" {name} remembered feeding Lemon lettuce for the first time, and how Lemon flung the leaves all over the table. They laughed until they flopped sideways. Then {name} drew a sunny yellow bird perched proudly on Grandpa's teacup.

Halfway down a page, {name} paused. "But how do we write down Lemon's song?" Grandpa thought, puckered his lips, and whistled a lively tune that dipped and soared, exactly like Lemon. {name}'s eyes went wide. Quick as a wink, {name} grabbed the tablet and recorded it. Then {name} tried to whistle too, but only a "fffff" came out, like a leaky bicycle pump.

{name} refused to give up, practicing after bath time and after brushing teeth, until {his} cheeks ached. On the third day, one thin note finally peeped out, then a second, then a third. Grandpa clapped and laughed. "Now that's a whistle!" Then he winked. "Want to know a secret? That song is a tune I used to whistle when I was young. Lemon learned it from me."

{name} blinked in amazement. Lemon's song had been living inside Grandpa all along. That evening, they tucked the recording and the notebook together and wrote "Lemon's Song" on the cover. Grandpa looked at the cage, and this time he smiled. As the weeks went by, missing Lemon hurt a little less. And every morning, a bright whistle still filled the house: sometimes Grandpa's, sometimes {name}'s.

questions: 爺爺和{name}一起哭的時候，爺爺說了什麼？你覺得想念和哭，跟愛有什麼關係？
他們用了哪些方法記住小檸檬？如果要記住你喜歡的動物或人，你會怎麼做？
故事最後，爺爺看著鳥籠時為什麼會微笑？
zh.tip: 這個星期和孩子一起做一本「回憶小書」，畫下或寫下一件關於心愛寵物（或家人、玩偶）的趣事，一邊做一邊聊聊當時的感受。

questions: What did Grandpa say when he and {name} cried together? How do you think missing someone and crying are connected to loving them?
What did they do to remember Lemon? If you wanted to remember an animal or person you love, what would you do?
Why do you think Grandpa smiled at the cage at the end of the story?
en.tip: This week, make a little "memory book" with your child: draw or write one funny moment with a beloved pet (or family member or toy), and talk about how it felt as you make it.

zh: 星期六早上，{name}和爸爸要搭捷運去科學館看恐龍化石。月台上好多人，有背著大背包的大哥哥，也有推著娃娃車的阿姨。爸爸蹲下來問：「還記得我們的捷運約定嗎？」{name}點點頭，大聲說：「如果走散了，就在下一站下車，站在月台上等你！」
列車進站了，「嗶嗶嗶」的提示聲響起。人群一下子往前擠，{name}被輕輕推進了車廂。回頭一看，爸爸還在門外，被一位提著大箱子的伯伯擋住了。車門「咻」地關上，爸爸隔著玻璃豎起一根手指，嘴巴慢慢說著：「下、一、站！」
列車開動了，窗外的燈光一閃一閃往後跑。{name}的心跳得好快，手心也濕濕的。{name}抓緊扶手，深深吸了一口氣，在心裡默念：「下一站下車，站在月台上，不亂跑。」廣播傳來叮咚聲：「下一站，公園站。」{name}把這個站名牢牢記住。
車門一打開，{name}跟著人群走出車廂，然後停在月台的柱子旁邊。好多人往電扶梯走去，{name}很想跟上去找出口，可是一想起約定，雙腳就像釘在地上一樣，一步也沒有離開。「爸爸會來找我的。」{name}小聲對自己說。
這時，{name}看見一位穿著深藍色制服、戴著帽子的站務員姊姊，正沿著月台慢慢巡視。{name}鼓起勇氣，朝她揮揮手。姊姊走過來，彎下腰溫柔地問：「小朋友，你需要幫忙嗎？」{name}說：「我和爸爸走散了，爸爸還在上一站。」
姊姊點點頭，又問：「你知道爸爸的名字和電話號碼嗎？」{name}想起每天晚上和爸爸玩的「電話號碼歌」，先說出爸爸的全名，再像唱歌一樣，把十個數字一個一個清清楚楚地念出來。姊姊一邊聽，一邊拿出公務手機撥號。
電話很快就接通了。姊姊說：「先生您好，您的孩子在公園站二號月台，很安全，我會陪著一起等您。」她帶{name}坐到月台的椅子上，指著黑黑的隧道說：「你看，等那邊亮起燈，下一班車就來囉。」{name}盯著隧道，一點也不覺得害怕了。
沒多久，隧道亮起兩盞燈，列車慢慢進站。車門一打開，爸爸第一個走出來，張開雙手把{name}緊緊抱住。「你記得我們的約定，做得真好！」爸爸向站務員姊姊連聲道謝。{name}牽著爸爸的手，一起搭上下一班車，繼續出發去看恐龍化石。
en: On Saturday morning, {name} and Dad were taking the MRT to the science museum to see dinosaur fossils. The platform was packed with people, big backpacks, and strollers. Dad knelt down and asked, "Remember our MRT promise?" {name} nodded. "If we get separated, I get off at the next station and wait right on the platform!"

The train rolled in, and the doors began to beep. The crowd surged forward, and {name} was gently pushed inside. When {name} turned around, Dad was still outside, stuck behind a man with a huge suitcase. Whoosh! The doors slid shut. Through the glass, Dad held up one finger and mouthed, "Next station!"

The train started moving, and the tunnel lights flashed past the windows. {name}'s heart was pounding, and {his} hands felt sweaty. Holding the pole tightly, {name} took a deep breath and whispered, "Next station. Stay on the platform. Don't wander." Ding-dong! "Next stop, Park Station," said the speaker.

When the doors opened, {name} stepped out with the crowd and stopped beside a big pillar. Lots of people hurried toward the escalator, and {name} wanted to follow them to find an exit. But remembering the promise, {name} stayed put, feet planted like a tree. "Dad will come for me," {name} said softly.

Just then, {name} spotted a station worker in a dark blue uniform and cap, walking slowly along the platform. Feeling brave, {name} waved to her. She came over and bent down kindly. "Do you need some help?" she asked. "I got separated from my dad," {name} said. "He's still at the last station."

The worker nodded. "Do you know your dad's name and phone number?" {name} thought of the phone number song they sang together every night. First {name} said Dad's full name, then sang all ten numbers, one by one, nice and clear. The worker listened and dialed on her work phone.

Dad answered right away. "Hello, sir," said the worker. "Your child is safe on Platform Two at Park Station. I'll wait here with your child until you arrive." She sat with {name} on a bench and pointed at the dark tunnel. "When lights shine over there, the next train is coming."

Soon two bright lights glowed in the tunnel, and a train glided in. The doors opened, and Dad was the very first one out. He wrapped {name} in a giant hug. "You remembered our promise. Great job!" Dad thanked the worker again and again. Then, hand in hand, they hopped on the next train to go see the dinosaurs.

questions: 車門關上的時候，{name}做了哪些事情，讓爸爸能很快找到{him}？
如果你在人很多的地方看不到爸爸媽媽，你會停在哪裡？可以找誰幫忙？
你能說出爸爸或媽媽的全名和電話號碼嗎？要不要現在試試看？
zh.tip: 今晚和孩子一起把爸爸或媽媽的電話號碼編成一首小歌，每天睡前唱一次，直到孩子能自己完整說出來。下次出門前，也可以先約好「走散了就停在原地，找穿制服的工作人員幫忙」。

questions: When the doors closed, what did {name} do to help Dad find {him} quickly?
If you couldn't see your grown-up in a crowded place, where would you stay, and who could you ask for help?
Can you say your parent's full name and phone number? Want to try it right now?
en.tip: Tonight, turn your phone number into a little song with your child and sing it once every night before bed until they can say it on their own. Before your next outing, agree on a plan together: if we get separated, stop and stay put, and ask a worker in uniform for help.

zh: 星期二早上，{name}的數學作業寫錯了一題，偏偏橡皮擦不見了。坐在旁邊的浩浩從鉛筆盒裡拿出一個綠色的三角龍橡皮擦，小小的角翹翹的，可愛極了。「這是我阿嬤送我的生日禮物，借你用，要小心喔。」{name}點點頭說：「謝謝你，我用完就還你。」
{name}擦掉錯字，越看越喜歡那隻小恐龍。下課鐘一響，大家都往操場跑。{name}想讓三角龍也看看溜滑梯，就把它放進口袋，一起帶了出去。{he}在沙坑旁邊跑跑跳跳，又坐在大榕樹下的長椅上綁鞋帶，玩得好開心。
上課鐘響了，{name}回到教室，把手伸進口袋，裡面竟然空空的！{name}翻遍了書包、抽屜和鉛筆盒，都找不到那隻綠色的三角龍。{name}的心怦怦跳，手心也冷冰冰的。這時，浩浩轉過頭來問：「可以把我的恐龍橡皮擦還給我嗎？」
一句話差點從{name}嘴裡溜出來：「我早就還你了啊。」只要這樣說，浩浩可能會以為是自己弄丟的。可是{name}看見浩浩著急的眼睛，又想起那是阿嬤送的禮物，喉嚨好像被卡住了。{he}深深吸了一口氣，小聲地說：「對不起，我把它帶去操場，然後弄丟了。」
浩浩的嘴角垂了下來。{name}心裡緊張得不得了，但還是走到林老師的桌子旁，把事情從頭到尾說清楚：放進口袋、去了沙坑、坐過長椅。林老師認真聽完，溫和地點點頭說：「謝謝你告訴我真正發生的事，這樣我們就知道該去哪裡找了。」
林老師請班長先帶大家讀課文，然後帶著{name}和浩浩走到操場。他們先在沙坑裡輕輕撥開沙子，只找到一顆小石頭和一片樹葉。接著又到溜滑梯下面看，還是什麼也沒有。{name}有點想放棄，浩浩卻說：「你剛剛說還坐過長椅，對不對？」
三個人走到大榕樹下的長椅旁。林老師彎下腰，{name}也蹲得低低的，往椅子底下看。咦，草叢裡好像有一點綠綠的東西！{name}伸手一拿，正是那隻三角龍，角還是翹翹的，一點也沒壞。「找到了！」浩浩高興得跳了起來。
回到教室，{name}把三角龍放回浩浩的手心，又說了一次：「對不起，下次我會好好保管。」浩浩笑著說：「沒關係，你說了實話，我們才找得到它。」第二天，{name}忘了帶橡皮擦，浩浩馬上遞來三角龍：「拿去用吧，我相信你。」
en: On Tuesday morning, {name} made a mistake on a math problem, but {his} eraser was missing. Hao, who sat next door, pulled out a green triceratops eraser with tiny pointy horns. "My grandma gave me this for my birthday," he said. "You can borrow it. Please be careful." "Thanks! I'll give it right back," said {name}.

{name} rubbed out the mistake and couldn't stop admiring the little dinosaur. When the recess bell rang, everyone rushed outside. {name} wanted the triceratops to see the slide too, so it went into {his} pocket. Out on the playground, {name} ran around the sandbox and sat on the bench under the big banyan tree to tie a shoelace.

When the bell rang again, {name} hurried back to class and reached into {his} pocket. Empty! {name} searched the backpack, the desk, and the pencil case, but the green triceratops was nowhere to be found. {name}'s heart went thump, thump. Then Hao turned around. "Can I have my dinosaur eraser back?"

Words almost slipped out: "I already gave it back." If {name} said that, Hao might think he had lost it himself. But Hao's worried eyes, and the thought of his grandma's birthday gift, made {name}'s throat feel tight. Taking a deep breath, {name} whispered, "I'm sorry. I took it outside at recess, and I lost it."

Hao's smile drooped. {name} felt jittery inside but still walked up to Ms. Lin's desk and told her everything: the pocket, the sandbox, the bench. Ms. Lin listened carefully, then nodded kindly. "Thank you for telling me what really happened. Now we know just where to look."

Ms. Lin asked the class helper to lead everyone in reading, then took {name} and Hao out to the playground. They gently brushed through the sandbox and found only a pebble and a leaf. Under the slide, there was nothing at all. {name} almost wanted to give up, but Hao said, "You said you sat on a bench, right?"

The three of them walked to the bench under the big banyan tree. Ms. Lin bent down, and {name} crouched low to peek underneath. Wait, something green was hiding in the grass! {name} reached in and pulled it out. It was the triceratops, pointy horns and all, not broken one bit. "We found it!" Hao cheered, jumping up and down.

Back in class, {name} placed the triceratops in Hao's hand. "I'm sorry. Next time I'll take better care of it." Hao grinned. "That's okay. We found it because you told the truth." The next day, {name} forgot an eraser at home, and Hao held out the triceratops right away. "Here, use it. I trust you."

questions: {name}差點說「我早就還你了」，後來為什麼決定說實話？那時候{he}心裡可能有什麼感覺？
林老師知道真正發生的事以後，怎麼幫忙解決問題？
如果你不小心弄丟或弄壞了別人的東西，你會怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這個星期和孩子約定一句「勇敢說實話」的暗號，例如「我想說一件真的事」；每當孩子用它坦白小錯誤時，先謝謝孩子說實話，再一起想辦法解決。

questions: {name} almost said, "I already gave it back." Why do you think {he} told the truth instead, and how might {he} have felt?
What did Ms. Lin do to help once she knew what really happened?
What would you do if you lost or broke something that belonged to someone else?
en.tip: This week, agree on a brave-truth phrase like "I have something true to tell you." Whenever your child uses it to share a small mistake, thank them for being honest first, then solve the problem together.

title.en: The Afternoon the Fifth Floor Swayed

zh: 星期三下午，窗外的城市車水馬龍，五樓的課後教室裡卻只聽得見剪刀聲。大家正在做「未來城市」模型。阿凱的紙箱大樓疊了七層，搖搖欲墜，他還得意地說要蓋到天花板。{name}則慢條斯理地剪出幾個小紙人，把它們塞進一張用瓶蓋撐起的紙桌子底下。「它們在做防災演練。」{name}一本正經地說，美琪笑得差點打翻膠水。
其實上個月學校演練時，{name}覺得有點無聊：鈴聲一響就趴下、躲好、抓穩，像在玩一場慢動作的捉迷藏。林老師當時說：「要讓身體記得，不只是腦袋記得。」可是{name}只記得桌子底下黏著一塊乾掉的口香糖。正想著，桌上的鉛筆突然骨碌碌地滾了起來。
接著，整間教室輕輕一晃，又一晃。吊燈像鐘擺一樣擺來擺去，窗戶喀啦喀啦地響。阿凱「哇」地跳起來，拔腿就往門口衝：「快跑，去樓梯！」好幾個同學也跟著站起來，椅子東倒西歪。{name}的心怦怦狂跳，腦袋一片空白，可是膝蓋好像自己知道該怎麼做。
{name}立刻蹲下，鑽進結實的木頭桌底，一手護住後腦和脖子，一手緊緊抓住桌腳，大喊：「趴下、掩護、穩住！」聲音大得連自己都嚇一跳。林老師也同時喊：「大家留在原地，躲到桌子下面！離窗戶遠一點！」阿凱在門邊愣了一秒，馬上折回來，鑽進美琪旁邊的桌底。
桌子底下，{name}看見阿凱抱著桌腳，臉皺得像一顆梅乾。「搖的時候跑樓梯，反而更容易跌倒。」美琪小聲說。書櫃上的地球儀咚地掉下來，滾到窗邊的牆角。{name}數著自己的呼吸，一、二、三……搖晃慢慢變小，最後終於停了。教室安靜得連冷氣的嗡嗡聲都聽得一清二楚。
林老師先一個一個檢查大家，才說：「好，跟著我，排好隊，不推、不跑、不講話。」她走在最前面，大家用手護著頭，一層一層走下樓梯，來到大樓旁的空地。阿凱一路小聲說：「剛才我差點就衝出去了。」{name}拍拍他的肩：「我的腿也在發抖啊。」
第二天，大人檢查確定大樓安全後，大家回到教室收拾。阿凱的七層紙大樓倒成一座紙箱山，可是在瓶蓋撐起的紙桌下，{name}的小紙人一個也沒少，整整齊齊地「抓穩」著。美琪眨眨眼：「原來它們真的有練習耶！」全班哄堂大笑。林老師微笑說：「看吧，身體記得。」{name}也笑了，忽然覺得下次演練，連那塊口香糖都沒那麼討厭了。
en: On Wednesday afternoon, the city outside hummed with traffic, but the after-school classroom on the fifth floor was quiet except for snipping scissors. Everyone was building a Future City model. Kai's cardboard tower wobbled seven boxes high, and he bragged it would reach the ceiling. {name} calmly cut out tiny paper people and tucked them under a little paper table propped up on bottle caps. "They're doing an earthquake drill," {name} announced, and Meiqi nearly knocked over the glue.

Truthfully, {name} had found last month's school drill a bit dull. A bell rang, and you dropped, ducked, and held on, like a slow-motion game of hide-and-seek. Ms. Lin had said, "Your body needs to remember, not just your brain." But all {name} remembered was a crusty old piece of gum stuck under the desk. Just then, a pencil began rolling across the desktop all by itself.

Then the whole room swayed gently, and swayed again. The ceiling light swung like a pendulum, and the windows rattled. Kai yelped, leaped up, and bolted for the door. "Run! Get to the stairs!" Several kids scrambled after him, chairs tipping every which way. {name}'s heart thumped wildly and {his} mind went blank, yet {his} knees seemed to know exactly what to do.

{name} dropped down, crawled under the sturdy wooden desk, covered the back of {his} head and neck with one hand, and gripped a desk leg with the other. "Drop, cover, hold on!" The shout came out so loud it was startling. At the same moment Ms. Lin called, "Everyone stay where you are! Get under your desks! Move away from the windows!" Kai froze by the door, then hurried back and squeezed under the desk beside Meiqi.

Under the desk, {name} saw Kai hugging a desk leg, his face scrunched like a prune. "Stairs are slippery when everything's shaking," Meiqi whispered. The globe on the bookshelf thudded to the floor and rolled into the corner by the window. {name} counted slow breaths: one, two, three. Little by little the swaying faded, and at last it stopped. The room was so still you could hear the air conditioner hum.

Ms. Lin checked on every single student before she spoke. "Okay, follow me. Line up. No pushing, no running, no talking." She led the way, and everyone shielded their heads as they walked down the stairs, floor by floor, to the open square beside the building. "I almost ran right out," Kai mumbled. {name} patted his shoulder. "My legs were shaking too."

The next day, after the grown-ups made sure the building was safe, the class returned to tidy up. Kai's tower had collapsed into a heap of boxes, but under the bottle-cap table, every one of {name}'s paper people was still there, neatly holding on. Meiqi winked. "Guess they really did practice!" The whole class burst out laughing. "See?" Ms. Lin smiled. "Bodies remember." {name} grinned, thinking even that crusty gum wouldn't seem so bad at the next drill.

questions: 教室開始搖晃時，{name}做了哪些動作？為什麼要護住頭和脖子？
阿凱一開始想衝去樓梯，後來為什麼折回來？如果是你，你會怎麼做？
在家裡，哪一張桌子最適合躲？哪些地方要離遠一點，像窗戶或高櫃子？
zh.tip: 今晚和孩子在家裡玩一次「地震演練」：你喊「搖了！」，孩子就趴下、躲到結實的桌子下、抓穩桌腳，數到二十再出來，最後一起找出家裡離窗戶和高櫃最遠的躲避點。

questions: What did {name} do when the classroom started to shake? Why cover your head and neck?
Kai first ran toward the stairs. Why did he come back, and what would you do?
At home, which table is the best one to hide under? Which places should you stay away from, like windows or tall shelves?
en.tip: Tonight, play an earthquake drill game: when you call "Shake!", your child drops, crawls under a sturdy table, and holds on to a leg while counting to twenty. Then find together the safest spot in your home, away from windows and tall shelves.

zh: 學期末的音樂會上，禮堂裡座無虛席。輪到{name}上台時，心臟像小鼓一樣咚咚作響。{name}彈的是練了兩個月的〈小河圓舞曲〉，前半段行雲流水，音符一顆顆滾出來，清亮又輕快。可是彈到中間那串最難的轉音時，手指忽然像被凍住一樣，停在琴鍵上，一動也不動。
禮堂安靜得連翻節目單的聲音都聽得見。{name}的腦袋一片空白，下一個音躲到哪裡去了？過了好幾秒，{name}吞了一口口水，把雙手放回第一小節，從頭開始。這一次，音樂順順地流到了最後。台下響起掌聲，可是{name}鞠躬時，臉頰燙得像剛出爐的饅頭，只想變成一滴水滲進地板裡。
下台後，{name}躲到厚重的紅色布幕後面，抱著膝蓋縮成一團。音樂老師林老師輕輕掀開布幕，蹲了下來。「我們先一起呼吸，好嗎？吸氣，數到四；吐氣，數到六。」{name}跟著做了三次，胸口那團緊緊的結慢慢鬆開。林老師張開雙臂，給了{him}一個暖呼呼的擁抱，什麼也沒多說。
「我搞砸了，大家一定都在笑我。」{name}悶悶地說。林老師從包包裡拿出一張泛黃的節目單，上面印著一個小女孩的名字，正是林老師自己。名字旁邊，有人用鉛筆歪歪扭扭地寫著：「第二段忘了，重來一次。」{name}瞪大眼睛。林老師眨眨眼：「這是我九歲的第一場演奏會，我媽媽到現在還留著呢。」
「那妳後來還敢上台嗎？」「當然，而且下一次彈得更好，因為我知道卡住了也不會天塌下來。」林老師翻開譜，指著那串轉音。「我們把這裡拆成小段慢慢練，再在前面畫一個呼吸記號。」{name}盯著譜好一會兒，小聲問：「下個月的朝會，我可以再彈一次嗎？」林老師立刻在行事曆上寫下{name}的名字。
隔天下課，同學小葵拉著{name}下跳棋。昨天小葵坐在第一排，掌聲拍得最響。這盤棋{name}一路領先，最後卻被小葵連跳三格，輸得一敗塗地。{name}先是「唉」了一聲，接著吸氣數到四，吐氣數到六，然後笑著伸出手：「妳最後那一步真是神來一筆！再來一盤？」小葵開心地點頭，兩個人又把棋子排好。
接下來每天放學，{name}都到音樂教室練琴。彈到那串轉音前，{name}會看看鉛筆畫的小小呼吸記號，輕輕吸一口氣。有時手指還是會遲疑一下，{name}就停一停，再從那一小段重新彈起，一次比一次穩。朝會前一天，林老師在門口聽完，豎起大拇指。{name}收好琴譜，嘴角揚起：「明天見，小河。」
en: The school hall was packed for the end-of-term concert. When it was {name}'s turn, a drum seemed to be thumping inside {his} chest. {name} had practiced the River Waltz for two whole months, and the first half sparkled, notes tumbling out bright and quick. Then came the tricky run in the middle. {name}'s fingers froze on the keys and would not move.

The hall went so quiet that someone turning a program page sounded loud. {name}'s mind was blank. Where had the next note gone? After a few long seconds, {name} swallowed hard, set both hands back on the very first bar, and started over. This time the music flowed all the way to the end. People clapped, but during the bow, {name}'s cheeks burned. {name} wished to melt right into the floor.

Afterward, {name} hid behind the heavy red curtain, knees hugged tight. Ms. Lin, the music teacher, slipped behind it and crouched down. "Let's breathe together first. In for four, out for six." {name} tried it three times, and the tight knot in {his} chest slowly loosened. Then Ms. Lin opened her arms and gave {him} a warm, quiet hug.

"I ruined it," {name} mumbled. "Everyone was laughing." Ms. Lin pulled a faded, yellowed program from her bag. Printed on it was a little girl's name: her own. Beside it, someone had scribbled in pencil, "Forgot part two. Started again." {name} stared. Ms. Lin winked. "My very first recital. I was nine. My mom still keeps it."

"Did you ever play again?" "Of course. And I played better, because I knew getting stuck wouldn't make the sky fall." She opened the music and pointed at the tricky run. "Let's practice this in tiny pieces and draw a breath mark right before it." {name} studied the page, then asked softly, "Could I play it at next month's assembly?" Ms. Lin wrote {name}'s name in her calendar at once.

The next day at recess, Kui, who had clapped loudest in the front row, set up a game of Chinese checkers. {name} was ahead the whole time, until Kui hopped three marbles in one dazzling move and won. {name} groaned, then breathed in for four and out for six, and held out a hand with a grin. "That last move was brilliant! Rematch?" Kui laughed, and they lined up the marbles again.

Every day after school, {name} practiced in the music room. Before the tricky run, {name} glanced at the little pencil breath mark and took a slow breath. Sometimes the fingers still hesitated, so {name} paused and replayed just that small piece, steadier each time. The day before the assembly, Ms. Lin listened from the doorway and gave a big thumbs-up. {name} tucked the music away and smiled. "See you tomorrow, little river."

questions: {name}的手指卡住以後，做了什麼讓自己重新開始？
林老師的舊節目單讓{name}有什麼不一樣的想法？你有沒有犯錯後再試一次的經驗？
{name}下跳棋輸了，是怎麼對小葵說的？如果是你輸了，你會怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子一起練習「吸氣數到四、吐氣數到六」，在玩桌遊輸贏時都用上，並互相說一句「這步好厲害！再來一盤？」

questions: When {name}'s fingers froze, what did {name} do to start again?
How did Ms. Lin's old program change how {name} felt? Can you remember a time you made a mistake and tried again?
What did {name} say to Kui after losing at checkers? What would you say if you lost?
en.tip: This week, practice "breathe in for four, out for six" together, and use it during family board games, win or lose, followed by "Great move! Rematch?"

zh: 班長選舉前一個星期，{name}全力以赴。{name}畫了十二張海報，貼滿教室後面的布告欄，還在家對著鏡子練習演講，練到連鏡子好像都快背起來了。演講稿裡最響亮的一句是：「選我當班長，下課時間加長十分鐘！」林老師聽了，忍不住笑著搖頭：「這個承諾，恐怕連校長都辦不到喔。」
投票那天，大家把寫好名字的小紙條投進鐵盒子。林老師一張一張唸出來，黑板上的「正」字越來越多。{name}的正字和好朋友米亞的正字一路緊緊咬著，像兩隻拚命賽跑的螞蟻。最後一張紙條打開，老師宣布：「米亞，十六票；{name}，十三票。」教室響起掌聲，{name}卻覺得耳朵發燙，心像石頭一樣往下沉。
{name}很想趴在桌上，假裝什麼都沒聽見。可是{he}看見米亞站在台前，雙手緊張地捏著衣角。{name}慢慢吸了一口氣，在心裡數到五，然後站起來走過去，伸出手說：「恭喜你！你一定會是很棒的班長。」米亞愣了一下，接著眉開眼笑地握住{his}手：「謝謝你，其實我剛剛緊張得要命。」
第二天，林老師舉起一張通知單：「學校要舉辦一個月的資源回收比賽，我們班需要一位負責人。」教室裡頓時鴉雀無聲，有人盯著天花板，有人假裝低頭找橡皮擦。{name}想了想，把手舉得高高的：「我來試試看！」坐在前排的米亞回過頭，對{him}比了一個大大的讚。
可是第一個星期，回收角落簡直一團亂。紙類箱裡躺著吃剩的優格杯，寶特瓶箱裡塞著皺巴巴的考卷，還有人把香蕉皮丟進鋁罐箱。{name}手忙腳亂地一件一件挑出來，越挑越垂頭喪氣。「也許我根本不適合帶頭。」{name}小聲嘀咕。停了一會兒，{he}又想：一直提醒大家沒用，那就換個方法吧！
那天放學，{name}拿出彩色筆，在每個箱子上畫了一隻動物：紙類箱是愛啃書本的長頸鹿，瓶罐箱是喜歡叮叮噹噹的小烏龜，旁邊還寫著「請別餵我香蕉皮！」{name}又做了一張「分類小偵探」排行榜，分對了就能貼一顆星星。隔天，同學們搶著餵長頸鹿，連林老師的咖啡杯放錯箱子，都被小偵探們笑嘻嘻地抓了回來。
一個月後，校長在朝會上宣布：「回收比賽第一名，就是五年三班！請班長上台領獎。」米亞站起來，卻一把拉住{name}的手：「這個點子是{name}想的，我們一起上去！」兩個人並肩走上台，台下的掌聲像下雨一樣。{name}看看米亞胸前閃亮的班長徽章，又看看台下那群一起當過小偵探的同學，笑得比誰都燦爛。
en: The week before the class leader election, {name} gave it everything. {name} drew twelve posters, covered the back bulletin board, and practiced a speech in front of the mirror so many times the mirror probably knew it by heart. The loudest line was, "Vote for me, and recess gets ten minutes longer!" Ms. Lin chuckled and shook her head. "I'm afraid even the principal can't promise that one."

On voting day, everyone dropped folded slips of paper into a metal box. Ms. Lin read them aloud, one by one, and tally marks marched across the board. {name}'s marks and the marks for {his} best friend, Mia, raced side by side like two determined ants. Then the last slip was opened. "Mia, sixteen. {name}, thirteen." The class clapped, but {name}'s ears burned, and {his} heart sank like a stone.

{name} wanted to flop onto the desk and pretend nothing had happened. But Mia was standing at the front, twisting her sleeve nervously. {name} took a slow breath and counted to five. Then {name} walked over and held out a hand. "Congratulations! You're going to be a great leader." Mia blinked, then grinned and shook it. "Thanks. Honestly, I was so nervous I could barely breathe."

The next morning, Ms. Lin held up a notice. "Our school is having a month-long recycling contest, and our class needs someone in charge." The room went silent. Some kids studied the ceiling. Others suddenly needed to search for their erasers. {name} thought for a moment, then raised a hand high. "I'll give it a try!" From the front row, Mia turned around and flashed {him} a big thumbs-up.

But the first week, the recycling corner was a disaster. A half-eaten yogurt cup sat in the paper box. A crumpled spelling test was stuffed in with the bottles. Someone had even tossed a banana peel in with the cans. {name} fished things out one by one, feeling glummer by the minute. "Maybe I'm just not good at leading," {name} muttered. Then came a new thought: reminders weren't working, so why not try something different?

After school, {name} grabbed some markers and drew an animal on every box. The paper box became a giraffe that loved munching on pages. The bottle box became a little turtle that adored clinking sounds, with a sign that said, "Please don't feed me banana peels!" {name} also made a Sorting Detective chart, where every correct sort earned a star. The next day, kids lined up to feed the giraffe. When Ms. Lin dropped her coffee cup in the wrong box, the detectives caught it, giggling.

A month later, the principal stood up at assembly. "First place in the recycling contest goes to Class 5-3! Will the class leader please come up?" Mia stood, then grabbed {name}'s hand. "This was {name}'s idea. Let's go together!" They walked up side by side while applause poured down like rain. {name} glanced at the shiny leader badge on Mia's shirt, then at all the Sorting Detectives cheering below, and smiled the biggest smile of all.

questions: {name}知道自己輸了選舉時，心裡有什麼感覺？{he}做了什麼讓自己冷靜下來？
回收角落一團亂的時候，{name}是怎麼換個方法再試一次的？
如果你在比賽中輸給好朋友，你會想對對方說什麼？
zh.tip: 這個星期玩桌遊或遊戲時，全家一起練習：輸了先深呼吸數到五，再對贏的人說一句「恭喜你，玩得真好！」

questions: How did {name} feel after losing the election, and what did {he} do to calm down?
When the recycling corner was a mess, how did {name} try a different way?
If you lost a game to a good friend, what would you want to say to them?
en.tip: This week during a board game or other game, practice as a family: whoever loses takes a deep breath, counts to five, and tells the winner, "Congratulations, nice playing!"

zh: 每天早上七點半，黃色校車沿著車水馬龍的大街慢慢爬行，經過飄著香味的麵包店、人潮洶湧的捷運站，還有一閃一閃的紅綠燈。{name}總是坐在第五排靠窗的位子，數著窗外的鴿子。可是這個星期，{name}老是數到一半就亂了，因為後面總會傳來一陣刺耳的笑聲。
笑聲來自最後一排的三個高年級生。一年級的小天個子小小的，抱著比自己還寬的書包，每次剛坐好，就被他們用手肘擠到走道上。「這是我們的位子！」他們哈哈大笑。小天低著頭，耳朵紅得像番茄。{name}心裡七上八下，前兩天都假裝沒看見，可是胃裡像塞了一顆石頭。
第三天早上，小天又被擠出座位，書包啪地掉在地上，鉛筆滾了一地。{name}深吸一口氣，站起來，幫忙把鉛筆一枝一枝撿回來。「來坐我旁邊吧，靠窗這邊看得到工地的吊車喔。」小天愣了一下，小聲說：「真的可以嗎？」{name}拍拍座位：「當然，這裡本來就有空位。」
後排有人怪聲怪氣地喊：「喲，來了一個保鑣！」{name}的手心冒汗，但沒有回頭。{he}朝前面幾排的好朋友安妮揮揮手。安妮立刻背起書包，一屁股坐到走道另一邊，把小天穩穩護在中間。「我們三個是窗邊探險隊，」安妮眨眨眼，「隊長負責數吊車。」小天終於噗哧一笑。
快到學校時，{name}望向坐在司機旁邊的隨車林老師，腳步卻猶豫了。如果說出來，會不會被大家說是愛告狀的抓耙仔？安妮悄悄問：「你在想什麼？」{name}咬咬嘴唇：「我在想，小天明天還要坐這班車。」說完，{name}走到前面，把這三天看到的事，一五一十告訴林老師。
林老師認真聽完，點點頭：「謝謝你告訴我。我坐在前面，後面發生的事常常看不清楚。告狀是想讓別人挨罵，你是在幫小天找幫手，這兩件事不一樣。」她又蹲下來對小天說：「被推開不是你的錯，一點都不是。」小天用力吸吸鼻子，把書包抱得更緊，背卻挺得直直的。
第二天，校車上多了一張新的座位表，後排那三個高年級生被安排坐在林老師正後方，安靜得像三隻冬眠的熊。小天一上車，就從書包裡掏出一張皺巴巴的紙，上面用蠟筆寫著歪歪扭扭的大字：「窗邊探險隊，正式成立！」原來他昨晚畫了一整個晚上。{name}和安妮相視而笑，三個人一起數起窗外的吊車：一臺、兩臺、三臺。
en: Every morning at seven-thirty, the yellow school bus crawled through the busy city streets, past the sweet-smelling bakery, the crowded subway station, and the blinking traffic lights. {name} always sat by the window in row five, counting pigeons. But this week, {name} kept losing count, because a harsh burst of laughter kept rolling up from the back.

The laughter came from three older kids in the last row. Tian, a tiny first grader with a backpack almost wider than he was, would just settle into a seat when they'd elbow him out into the aisle. "Our seat!" they hooted. Tian stared at his shoes, ears red as tomatoes. For two days, {name} pretended not to notice, but it felt like swallowing a stone.

On the third morning, Tian got shoved out again. His backpack thumped to the floor, and pencils skittered everywhere. {name} took a deep breath, stood up, and gathered the pencils one by one. "Come sit with me. You can see the construction cranes from this window." Tian blinked. "Really?" {name} patted the seat. "Sure. There's plenty of room."

"Ooh, look, a bodyguard!" someone jeered from the back. {name}'s palms went sweaty, but {he} didn't turn around. Instead, {name} waved to Annie, a good friend a few rows up. Annie grabbed her backpack and plopped down across the aisle, so Tian was snug in the middle. "We're the Window Explorers," Annie announced. "The captain counts cranes." Tian finally giggled.

Near school, {name} looked toward Ms. Lin, the bus teacher sitting up front beside the driver, and hesitated. What if everyone called {him} a tattletale? "What are you thinking about?" Annie whispered. {name} bit {his} lip. "I'm thinking Tian has to ride this bus tomorrow, too." Then {name} walked to the front and told Ms. Lin everything from the last three days.

Ms. Lin listened carefully, then nodded. "Thank you for telling me. From up here, I can't always see what happens in the back. Tattling is trying to get someone in trouble. You were getting help for Tian. That's different." Then she crouched beside Tian. "Being pushed is never your fault. Not one bit." Tian sniffled, hugged his backpack, and sat up a little taller.

The next morning, the bus had a brand-new seating chart. The three older kids now sat right behind Ms. Lin, quiet as bears in winter. Tian climbed aboard and pulled out a crumpled sheet of paper. In wobbly crayon letters, it said: WINDOW EXPLORERS, OFFICIAL CLUB! He had worked on it all evening. {name} and Annie grinned at each other, and together the three of them began to count: one crane, two cranes, three.

questions: 當小天被擠出座位時，{name}和安妮做了哪些事？你覺得小天當時心裡是什麼感覺？
{name}本來擔心被說是「抓耙仔」。你覺得「告狀」和「找大人幫忙」有什麼不一樣？
如果你在學校或校車上看到有人被欺負，你可以找誰？可以怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子一起列出三位「求助大人」（例如老師、校車老師、家人），並練習一句話：「我看到有人需要幫忙，可以請你過來嗎？」

questions: When Tian was pushed out of his seat, what did {name} and Annie do? How do you think Tian felt?
{name} worried about being called a tattletale. What do you think is the difference between tattling and getting help?
If you saw someone being picked on at school or on the bus, who could you go to, and what could you do?
en.tip: This week, list three "help grown-ups" together (like a teacher, the bus teacher, and a family member), and practice one phrase: "I saw someone who needs help. Can you come with me?"

zh: 晚餐後，{name}窩在沙發上，對自己說：「只看一支短片就好。」第一支是會跳舞的鸚鵡，第二支是倒著走路的小狗，手指一滑，第三支、第四支又自動冒出來。等{name}抬起頭，牆上的時鐘竟然從七點跳到了八點！那一整個小時，好像被誰偷偷一口吞掉了。
{name}一頭霧水，跑進廚房問媽媽：「時間是不是會被手機吃掉？」媽媽忍住笑，從抽屜拿出一個番茄形狀的計時器。「那我們來做個實驗吧。開始看之前，先說好要看多久，鈴響就停。」{name}立刻翻開一本新筆記本，在封面寫下「時間偵探調查報告」，還鄭重其事地畫了一個放大鏡。
第一天，兩人說好看二十分鐘。番茄計時器「鈴——」地響起時，螢幕上的小貓正要跳上冰箱。「再一分鐘就好！」{name}哀嚎著，心裡像氣球洩了氣。媽媽輕輕拍拍{his}背：「捨不得很正常喔。先慢慢吸三口氣，再想想接下來要玩什麼。」{name}吸氣、吐氣，把手機放回充電座。
接下來幾天，{name}在筆記本上記錄「找回來的時間」。星期二，{name}和弟弟小豆在客廳比賽跳繩，跳得氣喘吁吁、笑成一團。星期三，{name}一口氣讀完半本冒險小說。星期四，爸爸陪{him}躺在陽台數星星，聊月亮為什麼會變胖變瘦。說也奇怪，眼睛不再乾巴巴的，腦袋也像被擦亮的窗戶。
星期六，計時器一響，{name}乾脆俐落地關掉螢幕，連自己都嚇了一跳。用找回來的時間，{name}畫了一本漫畫，叫做《吃時間的手機》。漫畫裡的手機長著小嘴巴，把分鐘像麵條一樣「咻嚕咻嚕」吸進去，吃飽了還打個嗝，吐出一根時鐘指針。最後，主角按下番茄計時器，「鈴——」一響，手機就乖乖蓋上被子睡覺了。
星期天晚上，{name}把漫畫念給全家聽。小豆笑得在沙發上滾來滾去，媽媽笑到眼淚都流出來。可是笑得最大聲的，竟然是爸爸。他擦擦眼角，不好意思地說：「其實昨天晚上，我只是想查明天的天氣，結果一回神，已經看了一個小時的釣魚影片。原來我的時間也被吃掉了！」
全家人又笑得前仰後合。爸爸清清喉嚨，恭恭敬敬地向{name}借了番茄計時器：「時間偵探，從明天起我也要做實驗。」{name}心滿意足地翻開筆記本，在最後一頁畫上新的一格：手機在充電座上呼呼大睡，一家人圍著桌子下棋，每個人都笑得眼睛彎彎的。
en: After dinner, {name} curled up on the sofa and promised, "Just one short video." The first showed a dancing parrot. The second, a puppy walking backward. Then a third slid up all by itself, and a fourth. When {name} finally looked up, the clock on the wall had leaped from seven to eight! A whole hour had vanished, as if something had gobbled it in one bite.

Baffled, {name} found Mom in the kitchen. "Can a phone eat time?" Mom bit back a smile and pulled a tomato-shaped timer from a drawer. "Let's run an experiment. Before you start, we agree how long you'll watch. When it rings, you stop." {name} grabbed a fresh notebook, wrote TIME DETECTIVE REPORT on the cover, and very seriously added a magnifying glass.

On day one, they agreed on twenty minutes. The timer went ding just as a kitten on the screen crouched to leap onto the fridge. "One more minute!" {name} groaned, feeling like a balloon losing its air. Mom rubbed {his} back. "It's okay to feel disappointed. Take three slow breaths, then pick something fun to do next." {name} breathed in, breathed out, and set the phone on its charger.

All week, {name} logged the "found time." On Tuesday, {name} and little brother Dou held a jump-rope contest in the living room until they flopped down, giggling. On Wednesday, {name} devoured half an adventure novel. On Thursday, Dad and {name} lay on the balcony counting stars and wondering why the moon grows fat and thin. Strangely, {name}'s eyes stopped feeling scratchy, and {his} thoughts felt as clear as a freshly washed window.

On Saturday, the timer rang and {name} switched off the screen in one smooth click, which surprised even the detective. With the found time, {name} drew a comic called The Phone That Eats Time. The phone had a tiny mouth that slurped up minutes like noodles, then burped out a clock hand. In the end, the hero set the tomato timer. Ding! The phone pulled up a blanket and fell fast asleep.

On Sunday evening, {name} read the comic to the whole family. Dou rolled across the sofa, and Mom laughed until tears came. But the loudest laugh belonged to Dad. He wiped his eyes and sheepishly admitted, "Last night I only meant to check tomorrow's weather. Next thing I knew, I'd watched an hour of fishing videos. My time got eaten too!"

Everyone burst out laughing again. Dad cleared his throat and politely asked to borrow the tomato timer. "Detective, starting tomorrow, I'm running the experiment too." Beaming, {name} opened the notebook and drew one more panel on the last page: the phone snoring on its charger while the whole family played a board game, everyone's eyes crinkled with laughter.

questions: 計時器響的時候，{name}覺得捨不得，{he}做了什麼讓自己好過一點？
{name}用「找回來的時間」做了哪些事？如果是你，你想用找回來的時間做什麼？
你有沒有覺得時間突然「不見了」的經驗？那時候你在做什麼？
zh.tip: 這週每次開始用平板或手機前，先和孩子一起說好時間並設定計時器；鈴響時一起深呼吸三次，再從「找回來的時間清單」挑一件事來做。

questions: When the timer rang and {name} felt disappointed, what did {he} do to feel better?
What did {name} do with the found time? What would you like to do with yours?
Have you ever felt like time suddenly disappeared? What were you doing?
en.tip: This week, agree on a time and set a timer together before any screen starts; when it rings, take three deep breaths together and pick one activity from a family "found time list."

zh: 搬家卡車開走後，{name}站在阿嬤家門口，抬頭看了好久。這棟老房子又窄又長，像一個豎起來的鉛筆盒，樓梯陡得像梯子。爬樓梯很新鮮，{name}心裡卻悶悶的：台北的房間，還有天天一起打球的小宇和阿樂，全都留在北部了。爸爸拍拍{his}肩膀說：「我也是又期待又捨不得，兩種心情可以一起放在心裡。」
晚上，{name}在小閣樓拆開一個寫著「最重要」的紙箱。最上面是那顆舊籃球，歪歪扭扭簽滿了朋友的名字；底下是全班合照，還有那條用了好多年的小被子。{name}把照片貼在牆上，把籃球擺在枕頭邊，閣樓好像一下子沒那麼陌生了。樓下傳來阿嬤的聲音：「明天帶你去逛老街，順便找地方投籃！」
隔天一早，阿嬤牽著{name}走進老街。巷子窄窄彎彎，豆花攤冒著甜甜的白煙，打鐵店叮叮噹噹響個不停。阿嬤每走三步就停下來，跟賣肉圓的阿伯聊天，又和修鞋的阿姨說笑。{name}抱著籃球東張西望：這裡的人怎麼全都認識阿嬤？轉過一個彎，紅牆金瓦的廟出現了，廟旁的空地上，竟掛著一個掉了漆的籃框。
一個男孩正在運球，咚、咚、咚。他咧嘴一笑：「我叫阿凱，一起打嗎？」{name}點點頭，舉球就投，球卻砸到框邊，彈得老遠。第二球、第三球也落空，石板地凹凸不平，球老是亂跑。{name}臉都熱了，還是咬著牙繼續投。這時阿嬤把扇子一收，接過球，從膝蓋往上一拋——「唰！」空心進網。阿凱目瞪口呆，{name}笑得前仰後合。
阿嬤得意地說：「阿嬤年輕時可是校隊的。這個籃框，還是你阿公當年親手釘上去的呢。」{name}瞪大眼睛，原來這個陌生的角落，早就藏著家人的故事。{name}照阿嬤教的，膝蓋彎一點、手腕放軟，一次又一次地投。第十七球在框上轉了兩圈，終於掉進網裡！阿凱用力和{name}擊掌：「你學得超快！」
太陽偏西，阿凱說：「我知道一條捷徑，很快就能走回去！」阿嬤搖著扇子跟在後面：「好啊，阿嬤陪你們走。」三人鑽進只容一人通過的小巷，經過開滿九重葛的老牆，又穿過一隻橘貓睡午覺的屋簷下。最後阿凱推開一扇木門，{name}愣住了——眼前竟是阿嬤家的後院！阿凱指著對面：「我家就在那裡啊。」
晚上，{name}在紙上畫了一張地圖：廟旁的籃框、豆花攤、九重葛老牆、橘貓的屋簷，還有阿凱家的窗戶。{name}和小宇、阿樂視訊，把地圖舉到鏡頭前，一處一處介紹。小宇喊著：「暑假我們要去台南找你打球！」掛上電話，{name}把地圖貼在合照旁邊，抱著簽滿名字的籃球，心裡有點想念，也有點期待明天。
en: When the moving truck rumbled away, {name} stood outside Grandma's house and stared up. The old house was tall and skinny, like a pencil box standing on its end, with stairs as steep as a ladder. Climbing them was fun, but {name} felt heavy inside. The old bedroom up north, and Leo and Max, who played basketball every day, were all far away now. Dad squeezed {his} shoulder. "I'm excited and a little sad too," he said. "We can feel both at once."

That night, in the tiny attic room, {name} opened a box marked MOST IMPORTANT. On top lay the old basketball, covered in friends' wobbly signatures. Underneath were the class photo and a well-loved blanket. {name} taped the photo to the wall and set the ball beside the pillow. Suddenly the attic felt a little less strange. Grandma called up the stairs, "Tomorrow I'll show you the old street, and we'll find a place to shoot hoops!"

The next morning, Grandma held {name}'s hand as they walked down the old street. The lanes twisted and turned. Sweet steam rose from a tofu pudding stall, and a blacksmith's hammer went clang, clang, clang. Every few steps Grandma stopped to chat and joke with the shopkeepers. Hugging the basketball, {name} wondered how everyone here knew Grandma. Around one corner stood a red temple with a golden roof, and beside it, on an open courtyard wall, hung a faded old hoop.

A boy was already dribbling there, thump, thump, thump. He grinned. "I'm Kai. Want to play?" {name} nodded and shot. The ball smacked the rim and bounced far away. The second and third shots missed too, and the bumpy stones sent the ball skittering everywhere. Cheeks hot, {name} kept trying. Then Grandma snapped her fan shut, took the ball, and tossed it underhand from her knees. Swish! Kai's jaw dropped, and {name} laughed until it hurt.

"I was on my school team," Grandma said proudly. "And your grandpa hung this hoop himself, long ago." {name}'s eyes went wide. This strange new corner already held a family story. Following Grandma's advice, bend the knees and keep the wrist soft, {name} shot again and again. The seventeenth shot circled the rim twice and finally dropped in! Kai gave {name} a big high five. "You learn fast!"

As the sun sank lower, Kai said, "I know a shortcut home!" Grandma fanned herself and followed. "Lead the way. I'm right behind you." They squeezed through a lane only one person wide, passed an old wall bursting with pink flowers, and slipped under a roof where an orange cat napped. At last Kai pushed open a wooden gate, and {name} froze. It was Grandma's own backyard! Kai pointed across the lane. "I live right there."

That evening, {name} drew a map: the temple hoop, the tofu pudding stall, the flower wall, the sleepy cat's roof, and Kai's window. On a video call with Leo and Max, {name} held the map up to the screen and showed every spot. "We'll come to Tainan this summer and play!" Leo shouted. Afterward, {name} taped the map beside the class photo and hugged the signed basketball, missing old friends a little and looking forward to tomorrow.

questions: {name}剛搬到阿嬤家時，心裡有哪些不同的感覺？你有過又開心又難過的時候嗎？
{name}從台北帶了哪些重要的東西？如果你要搬家，你一定會帶什麼？
{name}的新地圖上畫了哪些地方？我們家附近，你最喜歡哪個角落？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子一起散步，畫一張「我們家附近的地圖」，每發現一個喜歡的新角落或認識一位鄰居，就在地圖上加一筆。

questions: How did {name} feel when the family first moved into Grandma's house? Have you ever felt happy and sad at the same time?
What special things did {name} bring from up north? If we moved, what would you be sure to bring?
What places did {name} draw on the new map? What is your favorite corner near our home?
en.tip: This week, take a walk together and draw a "map of our neighborhood," adding a new spot each time you find a favorite corner or meet a neighbor.

title.zh: 叮叮咚！{name}和奶奶的雨點樂團
title.en: Plink, Plonk! {name} and Grandma's Rain Band

zh: 滴答，滴答！下雨了。{name}和奶奶站在陽台上。陽台的屋頂是鐵皮做的。雨點落下來，叮叮咚！叮叮咚！「奶奶，雨在唱歌！」{name}笑了。
奶奶說：「我們來聽聽看。」雨打在屋頂上，叮叮叮。雨打在花盆上，咚咚咚。雨打在小水桶，噗噗噗。{name}點點頭：「好好聽喔！」
一滴好大的雨，啪！掉進水桶裡。{name}嚇一跳，又哈哈大笑。「水桶打嗝了！」奶奶也笑了：「對呀，水桶說嗝！」
「奶奶，我也想打鼓！」{name}說。奶奶眨眨眼：「等我一下喔。」奶奶走進廚房。拿來兩個空鍋子，一個小盆子，還有兩支木湯匙。
{name}拿起木湯匙。敲敲大鍋子，咚咚咚！敲敲小鍋子，噹噹噹！敲敲小盆子，叮叮叮！「好像雨點一樣！」奶奶拍拍手。
奶奶也拿起湯匙。雨點叮叮，{name}咚咚。奶奶噹噹，雨點啪啪。大家一起唱：「下雨天，真好玩，叮叮咚咚敲一敲！」
雨變大了，嘩啦嘩啦！{name}敲得好快，咚咚咚咚咚！雨變小了，滴答滴答。{name}敲得好輕，叮，叮，叮。奶奶說：「你跟得真好！」
慢慢地，雨停了。最後一滴，咚！掉進水桶裡。「雨在說再見！」{name}揮揮手：「再見，雨點！」小湯匙輕輕一敲，噹！奶奶抱抱{him}：「我們的樂團好棒！」
en: Plink, plonk! It is raining. {name} and Grandma stand on the balcony. The roof is made of tin. Plink, plonk! Plink, plonk! "Grandma, the rain is singing!" {name} giggles.
"Let's listen," says Grandma. Rain taps the tin roof. Ting, ting, ting! Rain pats the flowerpots. Dum, dum, dum! Rain drips in the bucket. Plip, plip, plip! "So pretty!" says {name}.
A big fat drop falls. Plop! Right into the bucket. {name} jumps, then laughs and laughs. "The bucket burped!" Grandma laughs too. "Yes! The bucket said burp!"
"Grandma, I want to drum too!" says {name}. Grandma winks. "Wait right here." She goes to the kitchen. She brings two empty pots, one little bowl, and two wooden spoons.
{name} picks up a spoon. Tap the big pot. Boom, boom, boom! Tap the small pot. Bong, bong, bong! Tap the little bowl. Ting, ting, ting! "Just like raindrops!" Grandma claps.
Grandma picks up a spoon too. The rain goes ting. {name} goes boom. Grandma goes bong. The rain goes plop. They sing together, "Rainy day, rainy play, tap and drum the day away!"
The rain gets loud. Whoosh, whoosh! {name} drums fast. Boom-boom-boom-boom! The rain gets soft. Drip, drop. {name} drums gently. Ting, ting, ting. "You keep up so well!" says Grandma.

Slowly, the rain stops. One last drop. Plop! Into the bucket. "The rain is saying goodbye!" {name} waves. "Bye-bye, raindrops!" One soft tap on the pot. Bong! Grandma hugs {him}. "What a wonderful band!"

questions: 雨打在水桶裡，會發出什麼聲音呢？
{name}最喜歡敲大鍋子、小鍋子，還是小盆子？
雨停的時候，你想跟雨點說什麼？
zh.tip: 今晚躺在床上，用手指在棉被上輕輕敲出小雨點的聲音，一起慢慢變小聲，直到雨停。

questions: What sound did the rain make in the bucket?
Which did {name} like best: the big pot, the small pot, or the little bowl?
When the rain stopped, what would you say to the raindrops?
en.tip: Tonight in bed, tap soft little raindrops on the blanket with your fingers, getting quieter and quieter together until the rain stops.

zh: 早上，太陽暖暖的。{name}和媽媽去森林散步。小路彎彎，樹葉沙沙。{name}牽著媽媽的手。一步，兩步，三步。「我們去探險囉！」媽媽笑著說。
走呀走，走呀走。咦？樹上有聲音。「嘎嘎，嘎嘎！」{name}抬頭看。高高的樹上，有一隻大鳥。藍藍的身體，長長的尾巴。媽媽小聲說：「那是台灣藍鵲。」
再看低一點。咦，還有一隻！小小的藍鵲，站在矮樹枝上。牠的尾巴也好長。牠是藍鵲寶寶。寶寶看看天空，看看地上。牠還不會飛呢。
藍鵲寶寶跳一下。跳跳！樹枝搖一搖。牠又跳一下。跳跳！樹葉晃一晃。{name}輕輕拍小手。小小聲說：「加油，加油！」媽媽也說：「加油！」
藍鵲寶寶張開翅膀。拍拍，拍拍！飛起來一點點。又落回樹枝上。沒關係，再試一次。拍拍，拍拍！{name}和媽媽站在樹下，靜靜地看。
高高的樹上，藍鵲媽媽叫了。「嘎嘎，嘎嘎！」好像在說：「寶寶，來這裡。」藍鵲寶寶抬起頭。{name}握緊媽媽的手。大家都安安靜靜的。
拍拍，拍拍！呼——藍鵲寶寶飛起來了！長長的尾巴，在風裡飄呀飄。牠飛呀飛，飛到家人身邊。「哇！」{name}開心地跳起來。「牠會飛了！」
藍鵲一家，排排站好。「嘎嘎，嘎嘎！」好像在說謝謝。{name}揮揮手：「再見，藍鵲寶寶！」{name}和媽媽手牽手，慢慢走回家。小路彎彎，樹葉沙沙。
en: One sunny morning, {name} and Mom went to the forest. The path was twisty. Rustle, rustle went the leaves. "Let's have an adventure!" said Mom.
They walked and walked. "Kak-kak! Kak-kak!" {name} looked up. A big bird sat up high. It was bright blue, with a long, long tail. "A blue magpie," Mom whispered.
Then {name} looked lower. Look, another one! A tiny magpie sat on a low branch. It looked at the sky. It was a baby. It could not fly yet.
The baby bird hopped. Hop, hop! The branch went wiggle. It hopped again. Hop, hop! The leaves went jiggle. {name} clapped softly. "You can do it!" Mom whispered, "You can do it!"
The baby opened its wings. Flap, flap! It rose a tiny bit, then landed again. That was okay. It tried once more. Flap, flap! {name} and Mom watched quietly below.
High in the tree, the mama magpie called. "Kak-kak! Kak-kak!" It sounded like, "Come here, little one." The baby bird looked up. {name} held Mom's hand tight. Everyone was very still.
Flap, flap! Whoosh! The baby bird flew! Its long tail floated in the breeze. Up, up it went, all the way to its family. "Wow!" {name} jumped for joy. "It's flying!"
The magpie family sat in a row. "Kak-kak! Kak-kak!" Thank you, they seemed to say. {name} waved. "Bye-bye, baby bird!" Then {name} and Mom walked home, hand in hand.

questions: 藍鵲寶寶的尾巴長長的，你可以用小手比比看有多長嗎？
藍鵲寶寶跳跳、拍拍翅膀的時候，你想對牠說什麼？
藍鵲寶寶飛起來了，{name}心裡覺得怎麼樣？
zh.tip: 今晚躺在床上，一起輕輕說「嘎嘎，嘎嘎」，再用小手當翅膀慢慢拍拍，陪藍鵲寶寶飛回家睡覺。

questions: The baby bird had a long, long tail. Can you show me how long with your hands?
When the baby bird hopped and flapped, what would you say to it?
The baby bird flew! How did {name} feel?
en.tip: Tonight in bed, whisper "kak-kak, kak-kak" together, then make soft, slow wings with your hands and fly the baby bird home to sleep.

title.en: {name} Says Goodnight to the Last Train

zh: 夜晚來了。城市好安靜。{name}躺在小床上。窗外遠遠的，有一列火車。叩隆，叩隆。這是最後一班車。它慢慢開，慢慢開。它要回家睡覺了。
媽媽坐在床邊。她輕輕摸摸被子。「火車累了喔。」媽媽小聲說。{name}點點頭。「我來哄它睡。」{name}閉上眼睛。在心裡，火車好小好小。小到可以抱一抱。
火車開進車站。車站暖暖的，亮亮的。叩隆……叩隆……慢慢停下來。{name}在心裡說：「晚安，車門。」嘶——車門關上了。一扇，兩扇，三扇。車門關得好好的。
「晚安，座位。」座位軟軟的。座位暖暖的。今天坐了好多人。有阿公，有寶寶。還有一隻小狗，汪汪。現在座位空空的。座位也想休息了。
「晚安，扶手。」扶手圓圓的。今天好多小手握著它。現在扶手不搖了。「晚安，車燈。」車燈眨一眨。一盞，兩盞，慢慢變暗。呼——車燈睡了。
「晚安，鐵軌。」鐵軌長長的。鐵軌亮晶晶。像兩條銀色的線。月亮照著鐵軌。鐵軌也閃閃的。好像在對{name}笑。晚安，亮亮的鐵軌。
{name}在心裡，拿出一條小被子。被子藍藍的，有星星。輕輕蓋在火車上。拍一拍，拍一拍。火車輕輕說：呼——。火車睡著了。車站好安靜。
窗外的燈，一閃，一閃。紅紅的，黃黃的，好溫柔。城市也在說晚安。{name}的眼睛慢慢閉上。媽媽親親{his}額頭。晚安，火車。晚安，城市。晚安，{name}。
en: Night has come. The city is quiet. {name} is snug in bed. Far outside the window, a train rolls by. Clackety-clack, clackety-clack. It is the last train today. Slow, slow. It is going home to sleep.
Mama sits by the bed. She smooths the soft blanket. "The train is tired," Mama whispers. {name} nods. "I will tuck it in." {name} closes {his} eyes. Now the train feels tiny. Tiny enough to hug.

The train rolls into the station. The station is warm and bright. Clackety... clack... it slowly stops. "Goodnight, doors," {name} whispers. Shhh, the doors slide shut. One, two, three. All closed, snug and tight.
"Goodnight, seats." The seats are soft. The seats are warm. Many people sat here today. A grandpa sat here. A baby sat here. A little dog said woof, woof. Now the seats are empty and sleepy.

"Goodnight, handles." The round handles swayed all day. So many small hands held them. Now they rest and stay still. "Goodnight, lights." The lights blink, blink. One by one, they dim. Whoosh. The lights sleep.
"Goodnight, rails." The rails are long. The rails are shiny. Like two silver ribbons. The moon shines on the rails. The rails twinkle back. They seem to smile at {name}. Goodnight, shiny rails.
{name} imagines a little blanket. It is blue, with tiny stars. Gently, it covers the train. Pat, pat. Pat, pat. The train sighs, "Hmmm." The train is fast asleep. The station is very quiet.
The city lights blink, blink. Red and yellow, soft and slow. The city says goodnight too. {name}'s eyes close slowly. Mama kisses {his} forehead. Goodnight, train. Goodnight, city. Goodnight, {name}.

questions: 火車怎麼叫？我們一起小小聲說：叩隆，叩隆。
你想跟火車的哪裡說晚安？車門、座位，還是車燈？
火車的被子上有星星，你的被子上有什麼？
zh.tip: 關燈前，和孩子一起小小聲跟房間裡的東西說晚安，像是「晚安，小枕頭」「晚安，小熊」，再輕輕拍一拍被子。

questions: What sound does the train make? Let's whisper it: clackety-clack.
What part of the train do you want to say goodnight to? The doors, the seats, or the lights?
The train's blanket has stars. What is on your blanket?
en.tip: Before lights out, whisper goodnight together to things in the room, like "Goodnight, pillow" and "Goodnight, teddy," then give the blanket a soft pat, pat.

title.en: The Little Turtle and the Moon Path

zh: 夜晚來了。小島好安靜。{name}和爸爸坐在沙灘上。沙子涼涼的，軟軟的。月亮圓圓的，掛在天上。海浪輕輕唱：「噓，噓。」
沙子動了一下。咦，那是什麼？是一隻小小的海龜。小小的頭，小小的腳。爸爸小聲說：「我們在這裡看。」{name}點點頭，輕輕坐好。
月亮照在海上。鋪了一條小路。亮亮的，銀銀的。一直通到海浪邊。小海龜看見了。慢慢地，慢慢地，牠往前爬。
爬呀爬，沙沙沙。小腳一步，又一步。沙灘上有小腳印。一個，兩個，三個。{name}輕輕數著。海浪說：「噓，噓。」
風吹過來，涼涼的。椰子樹沙沙響。遠遠的地方，小螃蟹走過去。小海龜停一停，休息一下。月光照著牠的小背。亮晶晶的，好漂亮。
小海龜又出發了。爬呀爬，沙沙沙。牠走到海浪邊。小浪花跑過來，輕輕摸摸牠。「噓，噓，」海浪說，「歡迎回家。」
小海龜游進水裡。游呀游，跟著月光。越來越遠，越來越小。{name}揮揮手：「晚安，小海龜。」爸爸也揮揮手。大海好安靜，好睏喔。
爸爸牽著{name}，慢慢走回家。月亮也跟著走。{name}躺進被子裡。被子暖暖的，軟軟的。窗外海浪輕輕唱：「噓，噓。」晚安，{name}。
en: Night comes to the little island. Everything is quiet. {name} sits on the sand with Dad. The sand is cool and soft. The moon is round and bright. The waves sing softly, "Shh, shh."
Then the sand wiggles. Oh! What is that? It is a tiny sea turtle. A tiny head. Tiny flippers. Dad whispers, "Let's watch from here." {name} nods and sits very still.
The moon makes a path on the sea. It is shiny and silver. It goes all the way to the waves. The little turtle sees it. Slowly, slowly, it starts to crawl.
Crawl, crawl. Swish, swish. One little step, then another. Tiny tracks dot the sand. One, two, three. {name} counts them softly. The waves say, "Shh, shh."
A cool breeze blows by. The palm trees rustle. Far away, a little crab scuttles past. The turtle stops for a rest. Moonlight shines on its small shell. It sparkles so softly.
Then the turtle sets off again. Crawl, crawl. Swish, swish. It reaches the edge of the sea. A small wave rolls up and pats it gently. "Shh, shh," says the wave. "Welcome home."
The little turtle swims into the water. It follows the silver path. Farther and farther. Smaller and smaller. {name} waves. "Goodnight, little turtle." Dad waves too. The sea is quiet and sleepy.
Dad holds {name}'s hand. They walk home slowly. The moon follows along. {name} snuggles into a warm, soft bed. Outside, the waves sing softly, "Shh, shh." Goodnight, {name}.

questions: 小海龜有多小呢？用你的小手比比看。
海浪是怎麼唱歌的？我們一起小小聲唱：「噓，噓。」
小海龜游回家了，你想跟牠說什麼？
zh.tip: 關燈後，用手指在{name}的背上慢慢爬，一邊輕輕說「爬呀爬，沙沙沙」，再一起小聲數小腳印：一、二、三。最後一起輕輕說：「噓，噓，晚安。」

questions: How tiny was the little turtle? Show me with your hands.
How did the waves sing? Let's whisper it together: "Shh, shh."
The little turtle swam home. What would you like to say to it?
en.tip: After lights out, slowly crawl your fingers across {his} back and whisper, "Crawl, crawl, swish, swish," then softly count the tiny tracks together: one, two, three. End with a quiet "Shh, shh, goodnight."

zh: 山上有一片茶園。綠綠的茶樹，一排又一排。太陽慢慢下山了。天空變成橘色。{name}和爺爺，坐在小木屋前。爺爺說：「你看，雲來了。」
白白的雲，軟軟的。像一隻一隻小綿羊。咩——咩——。雲羊慢慢走過來。走過茶樹，走過小路。{name}笑了：「是雲羊耶！」爺爺點點頭：「我們來數一數。」
第一隻雲羊，胖嘟嘟。飄過茶樹，輕輕的。「一隻。」{name}小聲數。第二隻雲羊，小小的。飄過茶樹，慢慢的。「兩隻。」爺爺也小聲數。
風輕輕吹，呼——呼——。茶葉沙沙響。好香好香的茶味。第三隻雲羊，尾巴長長的。「三隻。」第四隻雲羊，耳朵圓圓的。「四隻。」{name}伸出{his}小手，雲好軟喔。
天慢慢變暗了。山上好安靜。蟲兒唧唧叫。第五隻雲羊，打了個哈欠。「五隻。」第六隻雲羊，走得好慢好慢。「六隻。」{name}也打了個哈欠，啊——。
爺爺拿來小毯子。蓋在{name}身上，暖暖的。月亮出來了，亮亮的。第七隻雲羊，躺在月亮旁。「七隻。」第八隻雲羊，靠著山頭睡。「八……隻。」{his}聲音越來越小。
最後一隻雲羊，慢慢飄來。牠飄過茶樹，飄過小屋。牠停在山頂上。縮成小小一團。爺爺輕輕說：「最後一隻，要睡了。」{name}揉揉眼睛：「我也是。」
爺爺抱起{name}，走進小屋。輕輕放在小床上。窗外的雲羊，都睡著了。茶樹睡了，山也睡了。爺爺說：「晚安，{name}。」晚安，雲羊。晚安，小茶園。
en: High on a mountain is a tea farm. Tea bushes grow in green rows. The sun slowly sets. The sky turns orange. {name} sits with Grandpa. "Look," says Grandpa. "Clouds are coming."

The clouds are white and soft. They look like little sheep. Baa, baa. The cloud sheep drift closer. Over the tea bushes. Over the path. "Cloud sheep!" {name} giggles. Grandpa nods. "Let's count them."
The first cloud sheep is round and puffy. It floats by, soft and light. "One," {name} whispers. The second cloud sheep is tiny. It floats by, slow and quiet. "Two," Grandpa whispers.
The wind blows softly. Whoosh, whoosh. The tea leaves rustle. The air smells sweet. The third sheep has a long tail. "Three." The fourth sheep has round ears. "Four." {name} reaches up. So soft!
The sky grows dark. The mountain is quiet. Crickets sing, chirp, chirp. The fifth sheep gives a big yawn. "Five." The sixth sheep moves slow, so slow. "Six." {name} yawns too. Ahhh.

Grandpa brings a little blanket. He tucks it around {name}, warm and snug. The moon comes out, bright and round. The seventh sheep lies by the moon. "Seven." The eighth sheep rests on a peak. "Eight..." {his} voice grows soft.

The last cloud sheep drifts by. Over the tea bushes. Over the little house. It stops on the mountaintop. It curls up small. "The last one is sleepy," Grandpa whispers. {name} rubs {his} eyes. "Me too."

Grandpa carries {name} inside. He lays {him} in a cozy bed. Outside, the cloud sheep sleep. The tea bushes sleep. The mountain sleeps too. "Goodnight, {name}," says Grandpa. Goodnight, cloud sheep. Goodnight, little tea farm.

questions: 你最喜歡哪一隻雲羊？
雲羊打了個哈欠，你也打一個給我看看好嗎？
爺爺幫{name}蓋上小毯子，你的小被被摸起來是什麼感覺？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈後，抱著孩子一起閉上眼睛，用很小很小的聲音慢慢數想像中的雲羊，一隻、兩隻、三隻……數到誰先想睡都可以。

questions: Which cloud sheep did you like best?
The cloud sheep gave a big yawn. Can you show me your yawn?
Grandpa tucked a little blanket around {name}. How does your blanket feel?
en.tip: Tonight, with the lights off, cuddle up, close your eyes together, and whisper-count pretend cloud sheep very slowly, one, two, three, until someone gets sleepy.

zh: 中秋節的晚上，天空好安靜。月亮出來了，又圓又亮。{name}和爸爸媽媽，坐在院子的草地上。鋪好軟軟的野餐墊，一起來賞月囉。
媽媽拿出月餅，圓圓的。爸爸剝開柚子，香香的。柚子皮剝開了，沙沙沙。一片一片，好清甜。{name}拿起一片柚子，咬一口，好好吃。
風輕輕吹，呼——呼——。蟲兒輕輕唱，唧唧唧。{name}抬起頭，看著月亮。咦？月亮裡面，好像有一隻小兔子。長長的耳朵，圓圓的尾巴。
「媽媽你看！月亮裡有兔子！」媽媽笑著點點頭。「那是月兔，牠在月亮上搗藥喔。」咚、咚、咚，月兔好忙。{name}看得好開心。
{name}舉起手裡的柚子，輕輕搖一搖。「月兔，你好！」搖一搖，搖一搖。一朵小雲飄過去，月亮亮了一下。月兔好像也舉起小手，跟{name}揮一揮。
「月兔跟我揮手了！」{name}小小聲地說。爸爸揮揮手，媽媽揮揮手。月光灑下來，白白的，亮亮的。照在柚子上，照在月餅上，也照在{his}小手上。
夜深了，風好輕。蟲兒唱得好慢，好慢。{name}打了一個呵欠，哈——。眼睛眨呀眨，慢慢變重了。爸爸抱起{name}，輕輕走回屋裡。
躺進暖暖的被窩，軟軟的，香香的。窗外的月亮，還在笑。月兔也想睡了。{name}小小聲說：「月兔晚安，月亮晚安。」媽媽親一親{name}。晚安，好夢。
en: It is Mid-Autumn night. The sky is quiet. The moon comes up, round and bright. {name} sits on the soft grass with Mom and Dad. A cozy blanket is spread out. Time to watch the moon.
Mom brings out mooncakes, round and sweet. Dad peels a big pomelo. Rustle, rustle, goes the peel. Slice by slice, so juicy. {name} takes a slice. Mmm, yummy!
The wind blows softly, whoosh, whoosh. The crickets sing, chirp, chirp, chirp. {name} looks up at the moon. Oh! Is that a little rabbit? Long ears. A round, fluffy tail.
"Look, Mom! A rabbit in the moon!" Mom smiles and nods. "That's the moon rabbit. It's busy up there." Thump, thump, thump. {name} smiles too.
{name} holds up the pomelo slice. Wave, wave, wave. "Hello, moon rabbit!" A little cloud drifts by. The moon shines a bit brighter. The rabbit seems to wave back!
"The rabbit waved at me!" {name} whispers. Dad waves. Mom waves. Silver moonlight falls softly down. It shines on the pomelo. It shines on the mooncakes. It shines on {his} little hand.
The night grows late. The wind is gentle. The crickets sing slower and slower. {name} gives a big yawn. Aaah. Blink, blink, blink. Dad carries {name} inside, step by step.
The bed is warm and soft. Outside, the moon still glows. The moon rabbit is sleepy too. {name} whispers, "Goodnight, rabbit. Goodnight, moon." Mom kisses {name} gently. Sweet dreams.

questions: 柚子吃起來是什麼味道呢？
月兔有長長的耳朵，你可以比給我看嗎？
你想跟月兔說什麼悄悄話？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈後，和孩子一起小小聲說「月兔晚安，月亮晚安」，再輕輕抱一抱。

questions: What did the pomelo taste like?
The moon rabbit has long ears. Can you show me?
What would you whisper to the moon rabbit?
en.tip: Tonight, after the lights go off, whisper "Goodnight, rabbit. Goodnight, moon" together, then share a soft cuddle.

title.en: {name} and the Little Bird on the Tea Hill

zh: 阿嬤的茶園在山坡上。一排一排的茶樹，綠得發亮。阿嬤背著竹簍，在旁邊採茶葉。{name}和表哥阿傑、表妹小米，要玩捉迷藏。阿傑說：「我來找人，數到十喔！」{name}趕快跑進茶樹中間，蹲下來躲好。
「一、二、三……」阿傑大聲數著。這時，一隻小鳥飛過來。牠的羽毛綠綠的，眼睛有一圈白白的。小鳥停在茶樹上，「啾啾、啾啾」地叫。牠歪著頭看{name}，好像在說：「跟我來！」
小鳥往前飛了一小段。{name}輕輕跟過去。咦，茶樹上綁著一條黃絲帶！絲帶上掛著一張小紙條。紙條上畫著一顆蛋，還有一個箭頭。箭頭指向山坡上面。「這是線索耶！」{name}小聲地說。
這時，小米也躲到旁邊來了。「{name}，你在看什麼？」{name}把紙條拿給小米看。「我們一起找下一個線索吧！」兩個人手牽手，跟著小鳥慢慢往上走。阿嬤在不遠的地方，笑咪咪地向他們揮手。
阿傑數完了，到處找人。「找到你們了！」他從茶樹後面探出頭。{name}說：「噓，我們在跟小鳥找線索。」阿傑眼睛一亮：「我也要去！」小鳥又飛起來，停在一個小竹籃旁邊。竹籃裡有第二張紙條，上面畫著一座小山。
「小山上面是哪裡呢？」小米問。{name}抬頭看，看見高高的山頂。「是山頂！」三個人一起往上爬。小路有一點陡，大家走得很小心。風吹過來，茶葉香香的。小鳥在前面「啾啾」叫，好像在幫大家加油。
終於到山頂了！大樹下鋪著一塊花布。阿嬤已經坐在那裡，笑著等大家。原來阿嬤走另一條小路，先上來了。花布上有一個竹籃，裝滿茶葉蛋。蛋殼上有咖啡色的花紋，像一張小地圖。「哇！是驚喜野餐！」大家開心地叫。
阿嬤說：「線索是我留的，小鳥是來湊熱鬧的。」{name}剝開一顆茶葉蛋，香味飄出來。{name}先把蛋遞給阿嬤，再拿給阿傑和小米。大家一起吃蛋、喝茶，看山下的茶園。小鳥停在樹枝上，「啾啾」唱歌。{name}輕輕對牠說：「謝謝你帶路！」
en: Grandma's tea garden sits on a green hill. The tea bushes grow in long, shiny rows. Grandma picks tea leaves nearby with her basket. {name} plays hide-and-seek with cousins Jay and Mimi. "I'll count to ten!" says Jay. {name} hurries between the bushes and crouches down.

"One, two, three..." Jay counts loudly. Just then, a little bird flutters down. It has green feathers and white rings around its eyes. It lands on a tea bush. "Tweet, tweet!" it sings. The bird tilts its head, as if saying, "Follow me!"

The bird hops and flies a little way. {name} tiptoes after it. Look! A yellow ribbon is tied to a bush. A tiny note hangs from the ribbon. It shows a drawing of an egg and an arrow. The arrow points up the hill. "It's a clue!" {name} whispers.

Mimi slips into the same row to hide. "{name}, what are you looking at?" {name} shows Mimi the little note. "Let's find the next clue together!" Hand in hand, they follow the bird slowly uphill. Not far away, Grandma smiles and waves.

Jay finishes counting and starts searching. "Found you!" he says, peeking around a bush. "Shh," says {name}. "We're following a bird's clues." Jay's eyes light up. "Can I come too?" The bird lands beside a small bamboo basket. Inside is a second note. It shows a little mountain.

"What's on top of the mountain?" asks Mimi. {name} looks up at the high hilltop. "The very top!" The three cousins climb together. The path is a bit steep, so they step carefully. The breeze smells sweet like tea. Ahead, the bird tweets as if cheering them on.

At last, they reach the top! A flowered cloth lies under a big tree. Grandma is already sitting there, smiling. She took a shorter path to get there first. On the cloth sits a basket full of tea eggs. Their shells have brown lines like tiny maps. "A surprise picnic!" everyone cheers.

"I left the clues," Grandma laughs. "The bird just joined the fun." {name} peels a tea egg, and a warm smell drifts out. {name} gives the first egg to Grandma, then shares with Jay and Mimi. They eat, sip tea, and gaze at the garden below. The bird sings from a branch. "Thank you for leading the way," {name} says softly.

questions: 那隻綠色的小鳥，你最喜歡牠哪裡？
看到紙條上的蛋和箭頭，{name}心裡覺得怎麼樣？
山頂上的野餐，你最想吃什麼？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈後，輕聲玩「小小線索」猜謎：爸爸媽媽悄悄說一個提示，像「綠綠的、會啾啾叫」，讓孩子猜猜是故事裡的什麼。

questions: What do you like best about the little green bird?
When {name} found the note with the egg and the arrow, how did it feel?
What would you most like to eat at the hilltop picnic?
en.tip: After lights out tonight, play a whispered clue game: softly give a hint like "green and goes tweet, tweet," and let your child guess what it is from the story.

title.en: {name} and the Bunny Lantern with a Bow

zh: 元宵節的晚上，街上好熱鬧。{name}牽著爸爸的手，提著一盞紙兔子燈籠。兔子白白胖胖的，肚子裡有一顆小燈泡。燈一亮，兔子就變得暖暖的、亮亮的。可是，兔子的左耳朵軟軟的，一走路就晃來晃去。
「爸爸你看！兔子在跟我點頭。」{name}說。爸爸笑著說：「牠好像在說晚安晚安。」可是天才剛黑呀！{name}咯咯笑起來。走著走著，耳朵晃得更厲害了。最後，耳朵「啪」一聲垂下來，蓋住了兔子的眼睛。兔子看起來像在偷睡覺。
他們走到大廣場。哇！頭頂上有一條好長的金色大龍。大龍閃閃發亮，鬍鬚還會動呢。{name}抬頭看看大龍，再低頭看看兔子。兔子的耳朵還是垂著。「小兔子，你也想看大龍嗎？」{name}把耳朵輕輕撥起來。可是一放手，耳朵又掉下去了。
前面有一群紅色的大魚燈籠。大魚好像在空中游泳。魚尾巴搖呀搖，魚嘴巴一張一合。「小兔子，那是大魚喔。」{name}說。兔子的耳朵又垂下來，好像在說：「我看不到呀！」{name}嘟起嘴巴。「爸爸，兔子的耳朵壞掉了。」
