爸爸蹲下來，仔細看了看。「別擔心，我們一起想辦法。」爸爸手上提著一袋剛買的湯圓。袋子上綁著一條紅色的緞帶。爸爸把緞帶解下來，交給{name}。「你幫忙拿緞帶，我來扶耳朵。」{name}點點頭，把緞帶握得緊緊的。
他們走到路旁的長椅坐下。爸爸輕輕捏住兔子的兩隻耳朵，讓它們靠在一起。{name}拿紅緞帶繞過耳朵，一圈、兩圈。爸爸幫忙打了一個漂亮的蝴蝶結。耳朵站起來了！兔子頭上多了一個紅蝴蝶結，看起來好神氣。
{name}高高提起兔子燈籠。小燈泡照著紅緞帶，亮得好溫暖。一個小妹妹指著兔子說：「好可愛的兔子！」旁邊的奶奶也笑著點頭。大龍好大，大魚好多。可是{name}覺得，這隻戴蝴蝶結的小兔子，是最驕傲、最閃亮的燈籠。
夜深了，爸爸說：「我們回家吧。」{name}牽著爸爸，一路提著兔子燈籠。兔子的耳朵再也不晃了，蝴蝶結一跳一跳的。到了家門口，{name}對兔子說：「今天辛苦了，晚安喔。」兔子亮晶晶的，好像也在說晚安。
en: It was the night of the Lantern Festival. The city streets were busy and bright. {name} held Dad's hand and carried a paper bunny lantern. A tiny light bulb glowed inside its round tummy. But the bunny's left ear was floppy. It wobbled with every step.

"Look, Dad! The bunny is nodding at me," said {name}. Dad smiled. "Maybe it's saying goodnight." But it had only just gotten dark! {name} giggled. Then the ear wobbled more and more. Flop! It fell right over the bunny's eyes. Now the bunny looked like it was napping.

They reached the big square. Wow! A long golden dragon glowed high above them. Its whiskers even wiggled. {name} looked up at the dragon, then down at the bunny. "Do you want to see too?" {name} lifted the ear gently. But it flopped down again.

Next came a group of big red fish lanterns. They seemed to swim through the air. Their tails swished. Their mouths opened and closed. "Look, bunny, fish!" said {name}. Flop went the ear. The bunny couldn't see a thing. {name} pouted. "Dad, the bunny's ear is broken."

Dad crouched down and took a careful look. "Don't worry. We can fix it together." Dad was carrying a bag of sweet rice balls. A red ribbon was tied around the bag. Dad untied it and handed it to {name}. "You hold the ribbon. I'll hold the ears."

They sat down on a bench by the path. Dad gently pinched the two ears together. {name} wrapped the red ribbon around them. Once, twice. Dad helped tie a pretty bow. The ear stood up! Now the bunny wore a red bow on its head. It looked so proud.

{name} held the bunny lantern up high. The little light made the red ribbon shine warmly. A little girl pointed. "What a cute bunny!" Her grandma smiled and nodded. The dragon was huge, and the fish were many. But {name} thought the bunny glowed the proudest of all.

Soon it grew late. "Time to go home," said Dad. {name} held Dad's hand and carried the bunny all the way. The ear did not wobble once. The bow bounced happily. At the front door, {name} whispered, "Good job today. Goodnight, bunny." The bunny glowed back, as if saying goodnight too.

questions: 兔子的耳朵垂下來蓋住眼睛，你覺得牠看起來像在做什麼？
大龍和大魚，你最想看哪一個？
如果你也有一隻兔子燈籠，你想幫牠戴上什麼顏色的蝴蝶結？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈前，和{name}一起對枕邊的娃娃或小被子輕輕說「今天辛苦了，晚安喔」，再小聲聊聊故事裡最喜歡的一段。

questions: When the bunny's ear flopped over its eyes, what did it look like it was doing?
The dragon or the fish: which one would you most like to see?
If you had a bunny lantern too, what color bow would you give it?
en.tip: Before lights out tonight, whisper "Good job today, goodnight" to a favorite stuffed toy together with {name}, then quietly share your favorite part of the story.

zh: 下雨的傍晚，城市的燈一盞一盞亮起來。{name}和媽媽坐上公車回家，{his}黃色雨傘上畫著一群小鴨子，傘尖還在滴滴答答地滴水。{name}把雨傘靠在座位旁邊，趴在窗前，看著雨滴在玻璃上比賽誰跑得快。
「下一站到了！」媽媽牽起{name}的手，兩人急急忙忙下了車。走到騎樓下，{name}突然停住腳步，低頭一看，小手空空的。「我的小鴨傘！」公車已經噗噗地開走了，只留下兩盞紅色的尾燈，在雨中眨呀眨。
媽媽撐開自己的藍色大傘，把{name}摟到身邊。「別擔心，公車公司有失物招領處，專門保管大家忘記的東西，明天我們一起去問問。」{name}點點頭，可是一路上還是忍不住回頭看，好像小鴨傘會自己跳下車追上來。
晚上躺在床上，{name}望著天花板想：小鴨傘現在在哪裡呢？也許它正坐著公車，一路晃呀晃，開進一個祕密的車庫。那裡沒有乘客，只有好多好多走失的雨傘，高高矮矮地排成一排，安安靜靜地等著。
等到車庫的燈一關，雨傘們就悄悄地撐開了。一把格子傘說：「我昨天去了動物園，長頸鹿差點把我當成帽子戴！」一把透明傘咯咯笑：「我被忘在麵包店，現在全身都是奶油香。」小鴨傘也舉起傘柄，準備說自己的故事。
「我的主人叫{name}，」小鴨傘驕傲地說，「我們一起踩過好多水窪，還幫一隻小麻雀擋過雨呢。」其他雨傘聽得張大了傘骨，連最老的黑雨傘都點點頭：「聽起來，{name}一定會來接你。」想到這裡，{name}嘴角彎彎地睡著了。
第二天放學後，媽媽帶{name}來到公車總站。失物招領處的櫃檯後面，站著一位戴眼鏡的阿姨。{name}深吸一口氣，有禮貌地說：「您好，我昨天把一把黃色、畫著小鴨子的雨傘忘在公車上了。」阿姨笑著轉身，在一整排雨傘裡找呀找。
「是這一把嗎？」阿姨舉起一把黃色雨傘，上面的小鴨子好像正對著{name}眨眼睛。{name}開心地抱住它，連說了好幾聲謝謝。回家的路上，{name}把傘柄握得緊緊的，貼近小鴨子小聲問：「昨天晚上，你們聊得開心嗎？」
en: On a rainy evening, the city lights blinked on one by one. {name} and Mom rode the bus home. {his} yellow umbrella, covered in little ducks, was still dripping, drip, drop. {name} leaned it against the seat and watched raindrops race each other down the window.

"This is our stop!" Mom took {name} by the hand, and they hurried off the bus. Under the shop awning, {name} stopped and looked down. Empty hands! "My duck umbrella!" But the bus had already rumbled away, its red taillights winking through the rain.

Mom opened her big blue umbrella and pulled {name} close. "Don't worry. The bus company has a lost-and-found, a place that keeps things people forget. We'll go ask tomorrow." {name} nodded, but kept peeking back, as if the duck umbrella might hop off and run after them.

That night in bed, {name} stared at the ceiling and wondered. Where was the duck umbrella now? Maybe it was riding the bus, bumping along, all the way to a secret depot. No passengers there, just rows and rows of lost umbrellas, tall and short, waiting quietly.

When the depot lights clicked off, the umbrellas popped open. A plaid umbrella said, "Yesterday I went to the zoo, and a giraffe almost wore me as a hat!" A clear umbrella giggled. "I got left at a bakery. Now I smell like cream!" The duck umbrella raised its handle, ready for its turn.

"I belong to {name}," the duck umbrella said proudly. "We've splashed in lots of puddles, and we once kept a little sparrow dry." The other umbrellas spread their spokes wide in amazement. Even the oldest black umbrella nodded. "Sounds like {name} will come for you." Smiling at that thought, {name} drifted off to sleep.

The next day after school, Mom took {name} to the main bus station. Behind the lost-and-found counter stood a lady with glasses. {name} took a deep breath and said politely, "Hello. Yesterday I left a yellow umbrella with little ducks on the bus." The lady smiled and searched along a long row of umbrellas.

"Is this the one?" She held up a yellow umbrella, and the little ducks seemed to wink at {name}. {name} hugged it tight and said thank you again and again. On the way home, {name} held the handle snugly and whispered to the ducks, "So, did you all have fun chatting last night?"

questions: {name}發現小手空空、小鴨傘不見的時候，心裡是什麼感覺？
如果你也能偷偷溜進那個祕密車庫，你最想聽哪一把雨傘說故事？
要是小鴨傘真的會說話，你覺得它還會講哪一件和{name}一起做過的趣事？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈後，輪流小聲扮演一件家裡的小東西，說說它今天「看到了什麼」，猜猜是誰在說話。

questions: How do you think {name} felt when those hands were empty and the duck umbrella was gone?
If you could sneak into the secret depot too, which umbrella's story would you most want to hear?
If the duck umbrella could really talk, what other fun adventure with {name} might it tell about?
en.tip: Tonight after lights out, take turns whispering as a little object in your home and telling what it "saw" today, while the other guesses who is talking.

title.en: {name} and the Leopard Cat in the Moonlight

zh: 週末，{name}跟著研究野生動物的林阿姨，來到苗栗的山丘。林阿姨背著鼓鼓的大背包，裡面裝著筆記本、捲尺和一台小小的相機。「今天我們是森林偵探，」她眨眨眼說，「要找的是一位不愛露臉的住戶。」{name}興奮得摩拳擦掌，恨不得馬上出發。
山路兩旁長滿相思樹，空氣裡飄著泥土和落葉的香味。{name}一路東張西望，把枯葉踩得沙沙作響。林阿姨笑著豎起手指：「噓，森林裡的動物耳朵可靈了。」{name}趕緊放慢腳步，學她輕手輕腳地走，沒想到竟聽見頭頂傳來小鳥清脆的歌聲。
走到一條潺潺的小溪旁，林阿姨牽起{name}的手，停在岸邊的軟泥上。「快看！」{name}蹲下來，發現一串小小的腳印：圓圓的掌心，四個像豆子的趾印，卻看不見爪痕。「是鄰居家的貓嗎？」林阿姨拿出捲尺量了量，眼睛一亮：「也許是，也許不是喔。」
林阿姨在附近的樹幹上綁好相機，讓{name}按下測試鍵。喀嚓一聲，螢幕上出現一個大大的膝蓋，原來林阿姨剛好蹲在鏡頭前面！兩人笑得前仰後合。重新調整角度後，{name}小心地用落葉蓋住背帶，讓相機和樹皮融為一體。
「動物晚上才會出來嗎？」{name}問。林阿姨點點頭：「很多害羞的動物，喜歡趁著月光出門散步。我們不要留下來打擾牠們，明天再回來看答案。」{name}依依不捨，回頭看了好幾眼，才跟著阿姨沿原路慢慢下山。
那天晚上，{name}躺在民宿的床上，翻來覆去睡不著。會是走失的小貓嗎？還是貪吃的松鼠？窗外的月亮又圓又亮，{name}想像著小溪邊，有一雙眼睛正在草叢裡閃閃發光。
第二天一早，露珠還掛在草尖上，兩人就回到溪邊。林阿姨取下記憶卡，插進平板電腦。一張、兩張……前面幾張只有搖晃的樹葉。{name}屏住呼吸，盯著螢幕一動也不動。忽然，一個比家貓稍大的身影悄悄出現了！
牠身上布滿錢幣般的斑點，額頭有兩條白色條紋，耳朵後面還有白點。「是石虎！」林阿姨的聲音微微發抖，「這裡好多年沒拍到牠們了。」{name}滑到下一張，竟然又看見一隻毛茸茸的小石虎，緊跟在媽媽身後，踩著月光慢慢走過。{name}輕輕地笑了。
en: One weekend, {name} went to the hills of Miaoli with Aunt Lin, who studies wild animals. Her big backpack bulged with notebooks, a tape measure, and a tiny camera. "Today we're forest detectives," she said with a wink. "We're looking for a neighbor who hates to be seen." {name} could hardly wait.

Trees lined the trail, and the air smelled of mud and fallen leaves. {name} hurried along, looking everywhere and crunching every leaf. Aunt Lin smiled and raised a finger. "Shh. Forest animals have sharp ears." {name} slowed down and tiptoed like her, and soon a bird began to sing overhead.

At a babbling stream, Aunt Lin took {name}'s hand, and they stopped on the soft, muddy bank. "Look!" {name} crouched down beside a line of tiny paw prints: a round pad, four bean-shaped toes, and no claw marks. "A neighbor's cat?" Aunt Lin measured them, and her eyes lit up. "Maybe. Maybe not."

Aunt Lin strapped the camera to a tree trunk and let {name} press the test button. Click! The screen showed one enormous knee. Aunt Lin had been kneeling right in front of the lens! They both burst out laughing. After fixing the angle, {name} carefully tucked leaves over the strap until the camera blended into the bark.

"Do the animals only come out at night?" {name} asked. Aunt Lin nodded. "Lots of shy animals like to stroll by moonlight. We won't stay and bother them. We'll come back tomorrow for the answer." {name} glanced back again and again before following her down the trail.

That night, {name} lay in bed at the guesthouse, tossing and turning. Was it a lost kitten? A greedy squirrel? Outside, the moon hung round and bright. {name} pictured a pair of eyes shining in the grass beside the stream.

Early the next morning, with dew still on the grass, they hurried back. Aunt Lin slid the memory card into her tablet. One photo, two photos... just swaying leaves. {name} held very still, eyes fixed on the screen. Then, suddenly, a shape a little bigger than a house cat crept into view!

Its fur was covered in coin-shaped spots, with two white stripes on its forehead and white spots behind its ears. "A leopard cat!" Aunt Lin whispered, her voice shaking. "No one has photographed one here in years." {name} tapped to the next photo. There was a fluffy kitten too, padding behind its mother through the moonlight. {name} smiled softly.

questions: 在小溪邊看到那串小小的腳印時，你猜是誰留下的？
相機拍到林阿姨的大膝蓋時，你覺得哪裡最好笑？
看到小石虎跟在媽媽身後慢慢走，你心裡是什麼感覺？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈後，一起輕聲玩「森林偵探」：一個人小小聲描述一種動物的腳印或花紋，另一個人閉著眼睛猜猜看是誰。

questions: When you saw the tiny paw prints by the stream, who did you guess made them?
What was the funniest part when the camera snapped Aunt Lin's giant knee?
How did you feel when you saw the little leopard cat following its mother?
en.tip: After lights out tonight, play a whispery forest detective game: one person softly describes an animal's paw prints or spots, and the other guesses who it is with eyes closed.

zh: 春天的晚上，空氣暖暖的，帶著青草淡淡的香味。{name}和爸爸從奶奶家走回來，要穿過一條小小的森林步道。爸爸手上拿著一支大手電筒，{name}也握著自己的小手電筒，兩圈光在泥土路上輕輕晃著。
走到步道中間，爸爸停下腳步，小聲說：「我們把手電筒關掉，好不好？只要一下下就好。」{name}有一點猶豫，四周的樹影黑黑的，好像把天空都藏起來了。爸爸牽起{his}小手，說：「我就在這裡，我們一起等等看。」
喀嚓、喀嚓，兩支手電筒都關上了。一開始，什麼都看不見，只聽得到風輕輕吹過樹葉，沙沙、沙沙。遠遠的地方，青蛙在唱歌，呱、呱、呱。{name}慢慢地吸氣，再慢慢地吐氣，眼睛一點一點習慣了黑暗。
忽然，草叢裡亮起一個小小的光點，閃了一下，又暗了。接著，旁邊又亮起一個，再一個。「爸爸，你看！」{name}輕聲說。爸爸點點頭：「那是螢火蟲。牠們在用光說悄悄話呢。」小光點一閃一閃，好像在回答。
越來越多螢火蟲醒來了。十個、二十個、一百個……樹下、葉子邊、步道兩旁，到處都是柔柔的黃綠色光芒。牠們飄得好慢好慢，像一盞盞小燈籠浮在空中。{name}看得好入迷，連說話都忘記了。
有一隻螢火蟲飛到{name}面前，停在一片葉子上，亮了，又暗了。{name}好想把牠捧在手心裡，可是想了想，只是把手輕輕放下。「牠要回家找朋友，」{name}小聲說，「我不要嚇到牠。」爸爸輕輕捏了捏{his}小手，笑得好溫柔。
他們沒有再打開手電筒，就跟著螢火蟲的光，一步一步慢慢往前走。腳下的落葉軟軟的，發出沙、沙的聲音。貓頭鷹在高高的樹上叫：「咕咕、咕咕。」一閃一閃，一步一步，整座森林都好安靜。
走出森林，家裡的窗戶亮著暖暖的燈。{name}回頭看，螢火蟲還在樹林裡閃呀閃。洗好澡，躺進軟軟的被窩，{name}閉上眼睛，好像還能看見那些小燈籠。「晚安，螢火蟲。」{name}輕輕說，慢慢睡著了。
en: It was a warm spring night, and the air smelled softly of grass. {name} and Dad were walking home from Grandma's house along a little forest path. Dad carried a big flashlight, and {name} held a small one. Two round circles of light bobbed along the dirt.

Halfway down the path, Dad stopped. "Shall we turn our flashlights off?" he whispered. "Just for a little while." {name} wasn't so sure. The trees looked dark, as if they had hidden the whole sky. Dad took {his} hand. "I'm right here. Let's wait together."

Click, click. Both flashlights went off. At first, there was nothing to see at all. There was only the wind brushing the leaves, shh, shh, and frogs singing far away, ribbit, ribbit. {name} breathed in slowly, then out slowly, and little by little the darkness felt softer.

Then, deep in the grass, a tiny light blinked on, and off again. Another one glowed beside it, and then another. "Dad, look!" {name} whispered. Dad nodded. "Fireflies. They talk to each other with their lights." The little lights blinked, as if they were answering.

More and more fireflies woke up. Ten, twenty, a hundred! Under the trees, beside the leaves, all along the path, soft yellow-green lights were glowing. They drifted slowly, slowly, like tiny lanterns floating in the air. {name} watched quietly, too amazed to say a word.

One firefly floated right up to {name} and landed on a leaf. Glow, then dark. Glow, then dark. {name} wanted to scoop it up, but gently lowered both hands instead. "It needs to find its friends," {name} whispered. "I don't want to scare it." Dad squeezed {his} hand and smiled.

They kept their flashlights off and followed the fireflies' glow, one slow step at a time. Fallen leaves crunched softly underfoot. High in a tree, an owl called, "Hoo, hoo." Blink and glow, step and step. The whole forest felt hushed and sleepy.

At the edge of the woods, the windows of home shone warm and yellow. {name} looked back. The fireflies were still twinkling among the trees. After a bath, snug under a soft blanket, {name} closed {his} eyes and could still see the little lanterns. "Goodnight, fireflies," {name} whispered, and drifted off to sleep.

questions: 手電筒喀嚓關掉、四周黑黑的時候，你一開始覺得怎麼樣？
螢火蟲用光說悄悄話，你猜牠們在跟彼此說些什麼？
回家的路上，你最喜歡哪個聲音：沙沙的風、呱呱的青蛙，還是咕咕的貓頭鷹？
zh.tip: 關燈後一起躺在被窩裡，輪流小聲學一種森林裡的聲音，讓對方猜猜是什麼。最後一起輕輕說：「晚安，螢火蟲。」

questions: When the flashlights clicked off and everything went dark, how did it feel at first?
The fireflies talk with their lights. What do you think they were saying to each other?
On the walk home, which sound did you like best: the shh of the wind, the ribbit of the frogs, or the hoo of the owl?
en.tip: After the lights go out, snuggle under the blanket and take turns whispering a forest sound for the other to guess. Then say together, softly, "Goodnight, fireflies."

zh: 海邊的小山丘上，站著一座白色的燈塔。姑婆就住在燈塔裡，負責照顧頂端那盞大燈。今晚，{name}要在這裡過夜。姑婆的老貓「海苔」慢吞吞地走過來，在{name}腳邊蹭了又蹭，喉嚨裡發出輕輕的呼嚕聲，好像在說：歡迎你來。
晚餐後，天色一點一點暗了下來。{name}躺在小床上，聽著陌生的海浪聲，翻來覆去，怎麼也睡不著。「姑婆，這裡的聲音好不一樣喔。」姑婆坐到床邊，摸摸{his}頭，笑瞇瞇地說：「那我們一起上去，看看燈塔是怎麼守夜的吧。」
燈塔裡有一道彎彎繞繞的螺旋樓梯。姑婆牽著{name}的手，另一隻手扶著欄杆，一階一階慢慢往上爬。海苔走在最前面，尾巴翹得高高的，像一根小旗子。爬到一半，{name}有點喘了，海苔卻回頭打了個大呵欠，好像在笑：才這樣就累啦？
到了頂端的小房間，大燈正緩緩轉動。姑婆說燈很燙，站在玻璃窗邊看就好，{name}乖乖地點點頭。一道金黃色的光束掃過漆黑的海面，轉一圈，又轉一圈，不疾不徐，像一隻溫柔的大手，輕輕撫過每一朵浪花。
遠遠的海上，有幾艘小漁船亮著燈。光束掃過去，漁船就被照亮一下，又悄悄沉回夜色裡。{name}正看得入神，忽然，最近的那艘船閃了三下燈。過了一會兒，另一艘也閃了三下。{name}睜大眼睛：「姑婆，漁船在跟我們說話嗎？」
姑婆輕聲說：「那是漁夫們在說謝謝，也在說晚安。」原來，海苔每天晚上都會跳上窗台，陪姑婆等這三下燈光，一天也沒有錯過。難怪海苔白天總是睡得東倒西歪！{name}忍不住笑出聲，海苔卻一臉若無其事，舔了舔爪子。
{name}學著姑婆，對窗外的漁船輕輕揮手。海浪嘩啦——嘩啦——，一下一下拍著岩石，像在慢慢數拍子。風從窗縫溜進來，咻——咻——。剛才那些陌生的聲音，現在聽起來就像一首溫柔的搖籃曲，一點也不陌生了。
姑婆在窗邊的長椅上鋪好軟軟的毯子，{name}窩了進去，海苔也跳上來，捲成一顆暖呼呼的毛球。光束轉一圈，海浪嘩啦一聲；光束再轉一圈，海苔呼嚕一聲。{his}眼皮越來越重。燈塔繼續守著大海，而{name}和海苔，已經甜甜地睡著了。
en: On a little hill by the sea stood a white lighthouse. Great-Aunt lived inside and took care of the big lamp at the very top. Tonight, {name} was staying over. Her old cat, Nori, padded slowly across the floor, rubbed against {name}'s ankles, and purred a soft, rumbly welcome.

After supper, the sky dimmed little by little. {name} lay in the small bed, listening to the unfamiliar waves, tossing and turning. "Great-Aunt, everything sounds so different here." Great-Aunt sat down, patted {his} pillow, and smiled. "Then let's go up and see how a lighthouse keeps watch at night."

Inside the lighthouse, a staircase curled round and round like a seashell. Great-Aunt held {name}'s hand and gripped the railing, and they climbed one step at a time. Nori led the way, tail held high like a tiny flag. Halfway up, {name} was puffing, and Nori turned back with an enormous yawn, as if to say, "Tired already?"

At the top, the great lamp was turning slowly. Great-Aunt explained that it was very hot, so they would watch from the window, and {name} nodded and stayed put. A golden beam swept across the dark water, around and around, never hurrying, like a gentle hand smoothing every wave.

Far out on the sea, a few fishing boats glowed with tiny lights. Each time the beam passed, a boat lit up for a moment, then slipped quietly back into the night. Suddenly, the nearest boat blinked its light three times. Soon another blinked three times too. {name} stared. "Are the boats talking to us?"

"That's the fishermen saying thank you, and goodnight," Great-Aunt whispered. Every single night, it turned out, Nori hopped onto the windowsill to wait for those three blinks with her. No wonder Nori snoozed all day long! {name} giggled, but Nori just licked a paw, looking perfectly innocent.

{name} copied Great-Aunt and waved gently at the boats. Swish, swash went the waves against the rocks, slow and steady, like someone counting a lullaby. Whoo, whoo sang the breeze through the window. The sounds that had seemed so strange now felt soft and friendly, like an old song.

Great-Aunt spread a fluffy blanket on the bench by the window. {name} snuggled in, and Nori curled up nearby like a warm, furry ball. The beam went around, and the waves whispered swish. The beam went around again, and Nori purred. {name}'s eyes grew heavy. The lighthouse kept watch over the sea, while {name} and Nori drifted off to sleep.

questions: {name}剛到燈塔、聽到陌生的海浪聲睡不著時，你覺得心裡是什麼感覺？
爬螺旋樓梯時，海苔回頭打了個大呵欠，你最喜歡海苔的哪一個樣子？
如果你也能在燈塔上對漁船閃三下燈，你想跟漁夫們說什麼悄悄話？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈後，用手電筒在天花板上輕輕閃三下說「晚安」，再讓孩子閃回來，然後一起靜靜聽聽房間裡有哪些小小的聲音。

questions: When {name} first heard the strange waves and couldn't fall asleep, how do you think that felt?
On the curly stairs, Nori turned back with a big yawn. What was your favourite thing Nori did?
If you could blink a light three times to the fishing boats, what secret message would you send?
en.tip: After lights out tonight, blink a small flashlight three times on the ceiling to say goodnight and let your child blink back, then lie still together and listen for the quiet little sounds in the room.

zh: 中秋節一大早，{name}打開桌上的月餅盒，想先數一數。「一、二、三……七？」盒子裡明明有八個格子，現在卻空了一格，只剩一張皺巴巴的紙托。{name}揉揉眼睛又數一次，還是七個。這下可好，家裡發生了一樁月餅失蹤案！
{name}拿出放大鏡，像個小偵探一樣趴在地上。桌腳旁有一點金黃色的餅屑，往前一點，又有一點。餅屑一路蜿蜒，經過沙發，繞過電視櫃，簡直像有人故意留下的記號。「偷吃的人真是粗心大意。」{name}小聲嘀咕，一路跟了過去。
到了走廊，木地板上竟然有一個黏答答的小腳印，圓圓的，還有四顆小肉球。{name}蹲下來聞一聞，甜甜的，是蓮蓉的味道！這時，家裡的貓咪麻糬從門後探出頭，「喵——」地叫了一聲，鬍子上還沾著一點黃黃的東西。
「麻糬，是你嗎？」{name}湊近一看，麻糬卻慢條斯理地舔舔爪子，一臉無辜。原來牠鬍子上沾的是早餐的蛋黃，腳印則是踩到地上的餅屑留下的。小小的貓咪，怎麼搬得動一整個月餅呢？{name}嘆了口氣，線索只好繼續往下找。
餅屑經過表哥阿哲的房門口，還繼續往前延伸。偏偏這時，阿哲從房裡衝出來，一看到{name}，就把雙手藏到背後，臉紅得像熟透的柿子。「你、你在找什麼？」他結結巴巴地問。{name}瞇起眼睛：形跡可疑，嫌疑重大！
「阿哲，你是不是偷吃了月餅？」阿哲把頭搖得像波浪鼓，最後只好把手伸出來。原來是一盞還沒畫完的兔子燈籠，上面歪歪扭扭寫著「送給奶奶」。「本來想給大家驚喜的啦！」{name}耳朵一熱，連忙說：「對不起，我錯怪你了。我幫你一起畫吧！」
兩人正埋頭畫兔子的長耳朵，客廳傳來一聲響亮的呵欠。爺爺伸著懶腰說：「奇怪，我昨晚夢見和月亮上的兔子一起吃月餅，香得不得了！」{name}和阿哲互看一眼，同時盯住爺爺的睡衣口袋——那裡露出一角紙托，還黏著幾顆餅屑。
奶奶笑得眼淚都流出來：「你半夜夢遊到客廳，我叫你，你還說兔子在等你呢！」爺爺摸摸頭，哈哈大笑，懸案總算水落石出。到了晚上，圓圓的月亮升起，一家人把月餅切成小塊，人人有份；麻糬在一旁啃著小魚乾，兔子燈籠也亮晶晶地掛在窗邊。
en: Early on the morning of the Mid-Autumn Festival, {name} opened the mooncake box to count the treats. "One, two, three... seven?" There were eight little spaces, but one was empty except for a crumpled paper cup. {name} counted again. Still seven. A mooncake mystery had begun!

{name} grabbed a magnifying glass and crept along the floor like a real detective. By the table leg sat a golden crumb. A little farther, another. The crumbs wound past the sofa and around the TV stand. "Whoever did this was very careless," {name} whispered, following the trail.

In the hallway, {name} spotted a sticky little paw print, round with four tiny toe pads. It smelled sweet, just like lotus paste! Just then, Mochi the cat poked out from behind the door. "Meow!" There was something yellow stuck to her whiskers.

"Mochi, was it you?" {name} leaned closer. Mochi calmly licked her paw, looking perfectly innocent. The yellow stuff was only egg yolk from breakfast, and the paw print came from stepping on a crumb. Besides, how could a little cat carry a whole mooncake? The search went on.

The crumbs led past Cousin Jay's door and kept going. But right then, Jay burst out of his room. When he saw {name}, he hid both hands behind his back, and his cheeks turned red as ripe persimmons. "W-what are you looking for?" he stammered. Very suspicious!

"Jay, did you eat the mooncake?" Jay shook his head so hard his hair flopped. At last he showed his hands. He was holding a half-painted bunny lantern that said "For Grandma" in wobbly letters. "It was supposed to be a surprise!" {name} felt warm in the ears. "Sorry I blamed you. Can I help paint it?"

While they were painting the bunny's long ears, a huge yawn came from the living room. Grandpa stretched and said, "How odd! Last night I dreamed I shared a mooncake with the rabbit on the moon. Delicious!" {name} and Jay stared at his pajama pocket. A paper cup and a few crumbs were peeking out.

Grandma laughed until she cried. "You sleepwalked to the living room at midnight! When I called you, you said the rabbit was waiting!" Grandpa chuckled and scratched his head. Case closed. That evening, under the round moon, everyone shared mooncake pieces, Mochi nibbled a fish treat, and the bunny lantern glowed by the window.

questions: {name}拿著放大鏡跟著餅屑走的時候，你覺得哪一個線索最好玩？
如果你也要畫一盞燈籠送給家人，你想畫成什麼樣子？
爺爺夢見和月亮上的兔子一起吃月餅，如果你也做了這個夢，你想跟兔子聊些什麼？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈後，和孩子輪流用悄悄話出一個「小偵探謎題」，例如「我想到房間裡一個圓圓的東西」，讓對方躺在被窩裡慢慢猜。

questions: When {name} followed the crumb trail with a magnifying glass, which clue was the most fun to you?
If you could paint a lantern for someone in your family, what would it look like?
Grandpa dreamed of sharing a mooncake with the moon rabbit. If you had that dream, what would you talk about with the rabbit?
en.tip: After lights out tonight, take turns whispering a little detective riddle, like "I'm thinking of something round in this room," and let the other person guess while snuggled under the covers.

zh: 每到傍晚，{name}都會牽著阿嬤的手，走過熱鬧的巷子，來到街角的廟口。廟前的廣場上，舞獅隊正在練習。紅色的大獅子搖頭擺尾，金色的小獅子跳上跳下，而最讓{name}移不開眼睛的，是那面比桌子還大的大鼓。
打鼓的是阿忠伯。他的鼓棒一落下，「咚！咚！咚！」聲音就像打雷一樣，連地板都在微微發抖。獅子跟著鼓聲前進、轉圈、眨眼睛。{name}站在旁邊，小手不自覺地跟著拍大腿，心裡偷偷想著：「要是我也能打鼓就好了。」
有一天練習結束，阿忠伯擦著汗走過來，笑著問：「你每天都來，是不是很想試試看？」{name}用力點頭。阿忠伯把一對鼓棒放進{his}手裡，說：「我教你一個最簡單的節奏，叫做『咚、咚、咚咚咚』。小獅子出場時，就靠它喔。」
鼓棒比想像中重多了。{name}第一下打得太輕，鼓只發出小小的「噗」；第二下又太用力，鼓棒差點彈飛出去。打不到十下，{his}手臂就痠了，節奏也越打越快，亂成一團。{name}咬著嘴唇，覺得臉頰燙燙的。
阿忠伯沒有笑，只是蹲下來說：「打鼓不是比誰大聲，是要穩。先用耳朵聽，再用心數。」他輕輕跟著唸：「一、二、一二三。」{name}深吸一口氣，慢慢地打，一下、兩下……這一次，鼓聲終於整整齊齊的了。
從那天起，{name}回家就拿兩根筷子，在枕頭上練習，一邊打一邊小聲數。阿嬤坐在旁邊幫忙拍手。每天傍晚，{name}也到廟口跟著阿忠伯練。手臂不痠了，節奏越來越穩，連小獅子隊的哥哥姊姊都說：「聽你的鼓，我們跳得好順！」
廟會那天，街上掛滿紅燈籠，人擠得滿滿的，阿嬤就站在鼓旁邊陪著。{name}握緊鼓棒，心跳得好快，第一段竟然又越打越急，小獅子差點踩錯步。{name}想起阿忠伯的話，先用耳朵聽，再在心裡數：「一、二、一二三。」
鼓聲重新穩了下來。「咚、咚、咚咚咚！」小獅子抬起頭，眨眨大眼睛，輕巧地跳上了小木台。圍觀的大家一起拍手叫好，阿忠伯也對{name}豎起大拇指。{name}望著金色的小獅子，笑得比滿街的燈籠還要亮。
en: Every evening, {name} held Grandma's hand and walked down the busy lane to the temple on the corner. In the square out front, the lion dance troupe practiced. The big red lion shook its head, the little golden lion hopped and bounced, but {name} could only stare at the huge drum, bigger than a table.

Uncle Zhong played the drum. When his sticks came down, BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! It sounded like thunder, and the ground seemed to tremble. The lions stepped, spun, and blinked along with the beat. {name} stood nearby, tapping along without thinking, and secretly wished, "I want to play that drum too."

One day after practice, Uncle Zhong wiped his forehead and walked over with a smile. "You come every day. Would you like to try?" {name} nodded hard. He placed a pair of drumsticks in {his} hands. "I'll teach you the easiest beat: boom, boom, boom-boom-boom. The little lion needs it to come out."

The sticks were much heavier than they looked. {name}'s first hit was too soft, and the drum only went pff. The second was too hard, and a stick nearly bounced away. Before ten hits, {his} arms ached, and the beat got faster and messier. {name} bit {his} lip, cheeks feeling warm.

Uncle Zhong didn't laugh. He knelt down and said, "Drumming isn't about being loud. It's about being steady. Listen first, then count inside." He softly counted, "One, two, one-two-three." {name} took a deep breath and played slowly, one hit, then two. This time, the beat came out neat and even.

From then on, {name} practiced at home with two chopsticks on a pillow, counting quietly. Grandma clapped along. Every evening, {name} practiced at the temple with Uncle Zhong too. The aching went away and the beat grew steady. Even the big kids in the little lion said, "Your drum makes dancing so easy!"

On festival day, red lanterns hung everywhere and the street was packed. Grandma stood right beside the drum. {name} gripped the sticks, heart racing, and the first part rushed faster and faster. The little lion almost missed a step! {name} remembered Uncle Zhong's words: listen first, then count. "One, two, one-two-three."

The beat grew steady again. Boom, boom, boom-boom-boom! The little lion lifted its head, blinked its big eyes, and leaped lightly onto the wooden stand. The crowd clapped and cheered, and Uncle Zhong gave {name} a big thumbs-up. Watching the little golden lion, {name} smiled brighter than all the lanterns on the street.

questions: 阿忠伯的大鼓「咚！咚！咚！」響起來，你覺得聽起來像什麼聲音？
廟會那天，{name}握著鼓棒，心跳得好快。如果是你站在大鼓旁邊，你會有什麼感覺？
小獅子跳上木台的時候，如果你能跟金色的小獅子說一句話，你想說什麼？
zh.tip: 今晚躺在床上，和孩子用手指在枕頭上輕輕敲「咚、咚、咚咚咚」，一邊小聲數「一、二、一二三」，輪流敲，一次比一次更輕，直到慢慢想睡。

questions: When Uncle Zhong's big drum goes BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!, what does it sound like to you?
On festival day, {name} held the drumsticks with a racing heart. If you were standing by the big drum, how would you feel?
When the little lion leaped onto the wooden stand, what would you want to say to the little golden lion?
en.tip: Tonight in bed, take turns tapping a soft "boom, boom, boom-boom-boom" on the pillow with your fingers while whispering "one, two, one-two-three," making each round a little quieter until you both feel sleepy.

zh: 春天快結束的時候，{name}和阿嬤搭電梯到公寓頂樓的空中花園。阿嬤從口袋拿出一顆扁扁的白色種子，放在{name}手心。「這是南瓜種子，想不想試試看？」{name}用力點點頭，把種子埋進木箱的泥土裡，再輕輕拍了拍。
從那天起，{name}每天放學都和阿嬤一起提著小水壺上樓。過了七天，土裡冒出兩片圓圓的嫩芽。又過了幾個星期，藤蔓越爬越長，還開出黃澄澄的大花。隔壁的陳伯伯看了笑著說：「長得真有精神！」{name}開心得在花園裡轉了一圈。
七月時，新聞說颱風要來了。天空變得灰灰的，風開始呼呼地吹。{name}和阿嬤趕在風雨變大以前上樓，用竹竿和繩子把藤蔓綁牢，再把木箱推到牆角躲風。繩子滑來滑去，{name}試了好幾次，才終於打好一個結實的結。
那天晚上，雨嘩啦啦地打在窗戶上。{name}躺在床上，一直惦記著頂樓的南瓜。第二天風停了，{name}跟著阿嬤快步上樓。幾片葉子破了，竹竿也歪了，可是藤蔓還緊緊抓著繩子。{name}把竹竿扶正，小聲說：「你好勇敢喔。」
颱風走了，太陽卻像火爐一樣烤著屋頂。葉子曬得垂下頭，泥土裂出細細的縫。{name}想了一個辦法：每天清晨和傍晚各澆一次水，還跟阿嬤借了一把舊洋傘，撐在南瓜旁邊遮陽。慢慢地，葉子又一片一片挺了起來。
有一天，{name}在大葉子底下發現一顆綠色的小南瓜，只有拳頭那麼大。從此{he}每天都拿捲尺量一量，記在小本子上。小南瓜一天比一天胖，顏色也從綠色變成橘色。到了秋天，它大得要{name}用兩隻手臂才抱得住。
陳伯伯、樓下的林阿姨，還有好多鄰居都上來看。「哇，這是我們大樓種過最大的南瓜！」{name}看著大家驚喜的笑臉，忽然有了一個主意：「我們一起煮南瓜湯，大家一起喝，好不好？」鄰居們都拍手說好。
傍晚，阿嬤和林阿姨在廚房切南瓜、煮熱湯，{name}幫忙擺碗和湯匙。大家把長桌搬到頂樓花園，一人捧著一碗香甜的南瓜湯。夕陽把天空染成和南瓜一樣的橘色。阿嬤把洗好的南瓜籽放進{name}手心，明年春天，又可以種了。
en: As spring was ending, {name} and Grandma rode the elevator up to the rooftop garden of their apartment building. Grandma took a flat white seed from her pocket and set it in {name}'s palm. "It's a pumpkin seed. Want to give it a try?" {name} nodded, buried it in a wooden box of soil, and patted it gently.

From then on, {name} and Grandma carried a little watering can upstairs every day after school. After a week, two round sprouts poked out of the soil. A few weeks later, the vine was creeping along and opening bright yellow flowers. "Look how lively it is!" said Mr. Chen next door. {name} spun around with joy.

In July, the news said a typhoon was coming. The sky turned gray, and the wind began to whoosh. Before the storm grew strong, {name} and Grandma hurried upstairs. They tied the vine to bamboo poles and pushed the box into a sheltered corner. The rope kept slipping, but {name} tried again and again until the knot held tight.

That night, rain drummed against the windows. Lying in bed, {name} kept thinking about the pumpkin. The next morning the wind was gone, and {name} followed Grandma upstairs. Some leaves were torn and a pole had tipped, but the vine was still holding on. {name} straightened the pole and whispered, "You were so brave."

After the typhoon, the sun baked the rooftop like an oven. The leaves drooped, and thin cracks spread through the dry soil. {name} came up with a plan: water once at sunrise and once at sunset. {name} also borrowed Grandma's old umbrella and opened it beside the vine for shade. Little by little, the leaves lifted up again.

One day, under a big leaf, {name} found a tiny green pumpkin no bigger than a fist. Every day after that, {he} measured it with a tape measure and wrote the number in a notebook. The pumpkin grew rounder and turned from green to orange. By autumn, {name} needed both arms just to hug it.

Mr. Chen, Ms. Lin from downstairs, and lots of other neighbors came up to see. "Wow, it's the biggest pumpkin our building has ever grown!" Looking at all the happy, surprised faces, {name} had an idea. "Let's make pumpkin soup and share it together!" Everyone clapped and cheered.

That evening, Grandma and Ms. Lin chopped the pumpkin and cooked the soup in the kitchen while {name} set out bowls and spoons. The neighbors carried a long table up to the rooftop garden, and everyone held a warm, sweet bowl. The sunset glowed as orange as the pumpkin. Grandma placed the washed seeds in {name}'s hand, ready for next spring.

questions: 颱風來的那天晚上，{name}躺在床上一直想著南瓜，你覺得那時候心裡是什麼感覺？
第一次在大葉子底下發現小南瓜，如果是你，你會想對它說什麼？
明年春天再種下南瓜籽，你想種出什麼樣的南瓜，或是想種別的東西嗎？
zh.tip: 睡前一起躺著，輕聲聊聊「如果我們也有一個小花園，想種什麼」，明天再一起把它畫下來。

questions: On the night of the typhoon, {name} lay in bed thinking about the pumpkin. How do you think that felt?
If you found a tiny pumpkin hiding under a big leaf, what would you say to it?
When the seeds are planted next spring, what kind of pumpkin would you want to grow, or would you plant something else?
en.tip: Snuggle up and whisper about what you would grow if you had a little garden of your own, then draw it together tomorrow.

zh: 退潮的早晨，北海岸的岩石像一本被掀開的大書，一格一格的潮池在陽光下閃閃發亮。{name}握著一本藍色筆記本，表哥小安拿著放大鏡，美玲阿姨就站在幾步外，叮嚀道：「只看不抓，跟緊我，浪花一靠近就往後退。」兩位小偵探立刻點頭如搗蒜。
第一條線索出現在潮池邊的濕沙上：一個個小洞，旁邊還有細細的爪痕。{name}蹲下來，屏住呼吸。忽然，一隻招潮蟹探出頭，舉起一隻比身體還大的螯，左右揮舞，活像在指揮一支看不見的樂隊。「牠在跟我們打招呼嗎？」小安悄聲問。{name}忍不住笑出聲，趕緊在筆記本上畫下那隻神氣的大螯。
數著數著，{name}發現整片沙地都在揮手。「我想抓一隻回家養！」{name}一邊喊，一邊伸手就要去撈。美玲阿姨沒有責備，只是輕聲說：「你看，牠們的家都在這裡呀。」話才說完，螃蟹們一溜煙全鑽回洞裡，沙灘頓時空空蕩蕩。{name}的手僵在半空中，有點不好意思地收了回來。
{name}乾脆趴在岩石旁，一動也不動，像一尊石像。小安也想學，結果鼻子一癢，「哈啾！」打了個大噴嚏。他們等了又等，終於，小螃蟹一隻接一隻冒出來，又開始揮舞大螯。{name}認真寫下：「上午九點，二十三隻，全部在揮手，疑似在遊行。」小安笑得趕快摀住嘴巴。
接著，他們來到一個深一點的潮池。池底躺著一塊布滿斑點的褐色石頭，旁邊散著幾片空貝殼。「這裡什麼都沒有。」小安嘆了口氣。{name}卻目不轉睛地盯著那塊石頭——它剛剛是不是動了一下？忽然，「石頭」由褐轉白，八隻腕足緩緩舒展開來。原來是一隻章魚！牠眨眨眼，又悄悄滑進岩縫裡。
兩人看得目瞪口呆，連美玲阿姨都讚嘆：「好眼力，偵探！」{name}立刻把章魚畫進筆記本，旁邊寫上「偽裝高手」。不遠處的岩壁上，一顆橘紅色的海星緊緊貼著，五隻腕像張開的手掌。小安想把牠翻過來瞧瞧，{name}搖搖頭：「讓牠待在那裡吧，放大鏡就能幫我們看清楚。」
遠處的浪花漸漸靠近，美玲阿姨招招手：「漲潮囉，偵探們該收工了。」{name}回頭看了最後一眼：招潮蟹還在揮手，章魚躲在岩縫，海星依舊貼在原處，一切都和來時一模一樣。{name}在{his}筆記本最後一頁寫下：「本日案件：全部破案，無人失蹤。」小安哈哈大笑，三個人小心翼翼地踩著岩石，慢慢走回岸上。
en: At low tide, the rocks of the north coast lay open like the pages of a giant book, and every tide pool glittered in the sun. {name} held a blue notebook, and cousin An carried a magnifying glass. Aunt Mei stood just a few steps away. "Look, but don't grab," she said. "Stay close to me, and step back whenever the waves come near." The two detectives nodded hard.

The first clue was on the wet sand beside a pool: tiny holes and thin, scratchy tracks. {name} crouched down and held {his} breath. Suddenly a fiddler crab popped up and waved a claw bigger than its whole body, back and forth, like a conductor leading an invisible band. "Is it saying hello?" An whispered. {name} giggled and sketched the proud claw in the notebook.

Soon {name} noticed that the whole patch of sand was waving. "I want to take one home!" {name} cried, reaching out. Aunt Mei didn't scold. She only said softly, "Look, this is where they live." Before she even finished, every crab zipped back into its hole, and the sand went completely empty. {name}'s hand froze in midair, then slowly pulled back.

So {name} lay flat beside a rock, still as a statue. An tried to do the same, but his nose tickled. "Achoo!" They waited. And waited. At last, one by one, the crabs crept out and began waving again. {name} wrote carefully: "9:00 a.m. Twenty-three crabs. All waving. Possibly a parade." An clapped a hand over his mouth to keep from laughing.

Next they came to a deeper pool. On the bottom sat a speckled brown rock beside a few empty shells. "Nothing here," An sighed. But {name} kept staring. Had that rock just moved? Then the "rock" turned from brown to pale white, and eight arms slowly unfurled. It was an octopus! It blinked at them, then slipped quietly into a crack.

Both cousins stood with their mouths wide open, and even Aunt Mei said, "Sharp eyes, detective!" {name} quickly drew the octopus and labeled it "Master of Disguise." Nearby, an orange sea star clung to the rock wall, its five arms spread like an open hand. An wanted to flip it over, but {name} shook {his} head. "Let's leave it there. The magnifying glass can do the work."

Far off, the waves began creeping closer. "Tide's coming in," Aunt Mei called. "Time to close the case." {name} took one last look: the crabs still waving, the octopus tucked in its crack, the sea star right where it had been. On the final page of {his} notebook, {name} wrote: "Case closed. Nobody missing." An burst out laughing, and the three of them picked their way carefully back to shore.

questions: 招潮蟹揮著大螯，像在指揮一支看不見的樂隊，你覺得牠們在演奏什麼樣的音樂？
那塊褐色的「石頭」突然變成章魚時，如果你也在旁邊，你的心情會是怎樣？
如果{name}的筆記本還多一頁，你最想在潮池裡發現什麼生物？你會幫牠取什麼稱號？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈後，輪流用三個悄悄話線索描述故事裡的一種海洋生物，讓對方猜猜是誰；明天再一起畫一頁屬於你們的「偵探筆記」。

questions: The fiddler crab waved its claw like a conductor leading an invisible band. What kind of music do you think the band was playing?
If you had been there when the brown "rock" turned into an octopus, how would you have felt?
If {name}'s notebook had one more page, what tide-pool creature would you most want to discover, and what title would you give it?
en.tip: After lights out, take turns whispering three clues about a sea creature from the story and let the other person guess who it is. Tomorrow, draw your own "detective notebook" page together.

title.en: {name} and the Red Eagle in the Hsinchu Wind

zh: 新竹的秋天，九降風呼呼地吹，連路邊的招牌都被吹得喀啦喀啦響。{name}趴在客廳地板上，用竹條和描圖紙做了一只紅色的菱形風箏，還在上面畫了一隻張開翅膀的老鷹。「星期六的風箏節，我一定要讓牠飛得比誰都高！」{name}把風箏高高舉過頭頂，彷彿已經聽見了滿場的歡呼聲。
星期三下午，媽媽陪{name}到社區公園的大草地試飛。風一來，風箏猛地竄上天空，可是才撐了三秒，就像陀螺一樣左搖右晃，接著一個倒栽蔥，「啪」地摔進草堆裡。{name}不服氣，試了一次又一次，結果屢戰屢敗，竹條斷了一根，老鷹的翅膀也撕破了一個大洞。
回家的電梯裡，{name}抱著破風箏，一句話也不說，媽媽在一旁陪著。住在隔壁的林爺爺正好提著菜走進來，推了推老花眼鏡，仔細端詳那只風箏。「我以前在工廠設計機器，最喜歡研究東西為什麼會壞。」他眨眨眼說，「明天放學，要不要和媽媽一起來我家陽台當一天工程師？」媽媽笑著答應了，{name}半信半疑地點了點頭。
第二天，媽媽陪著{name}來到林爺爺家。陽台像一間小小的實驗室，擺滿了螺絲起子、捲尺，還有一台老舊的電風扇。他打開風扇，讓{name}舉著修好的風箏對著吹。風箏立刻瘋狂打轉。「看出來了嗎？」林爺爺說，「風太強，尾巴太短，抓不住平衡，就像走鋼索的人手裡沒拿長竿。」{name}恍然大悟，眼睛一亮。
「那我把尾巴做得又長又重！」{name}迫不及待地綁上一條厚布條，結果風箏像拖著一顆石頭，連飛都飛不起來。林爺爺哈哈大笑：「工程師的第一課，失敗要記筆記。」於是{name}拿出筆記本，認真寫下：太短會轉，太重會沉。接下來兩天，他們剪剪貼貼、量了又量，終於找到答案：尾巴要長，但一定要輕。
可是又輕又長的材料要去哪裡找呢？{name}翻遍了抽屜，最後目光落在桌角那堆摔壞的描圖紙碎片上。{he}把碎片剪成細條，一段一段串起來，接成一條三公尺長的尾巴，末端再綁上一個小紙漏斗，用來兜住風。那些曾經讓{name}垂頭喪氣的破紙，現在在風扇前輕輕飄動，穩穩當當。
星期六，風箏節的草地上人山人海，爸爸、媽媽和林爺爺都來了。九降風比平常更猛，好幾只風箏東倒西歪地栽了下來。{name}深吸一口氣，最後一次放手。紅色老鷹抖了抖長長的尾巴，扶搖直上，越飛越高，在藍天裡穩穩地停住了。林爺爺豎起大拇指，{name}握緊線軸，笑得合不攏嘴。
en: In autumn, the wind in Hsinchu howls so hard that shop signs rattle and clatter. {name} knelt on the living room floor and built a red diamond kite from bamboo strips and tracing paper, then painted a bold eagle with outstretched wings across it. "At Saturday's kite festival, this one will fly higher than anyone's!" {name} lifted the kite overhead, already imagining the cheering crowd.

On Wednesday afternoon, Mom took {name} to the big lawn in the neighborhood park for a test flight. A gust caught the kite and it shot upward, but after three seconds it began to wobble like a dizzy top. Then it flipped and smacked into the grass. {name} tried again and again. Each time it crashed, until a bamboo strip snapped and the eagle's wing tore wide open.

In the elevator home with Mom, {name} hugged the broken kite and said nothing. Grandpa Lin from next door stepped in with his groceries, nudged up his reading glasses, and studied the kite closely. "I used to design machines in a factory," he said. "Figuring out why things break was my favorite part. Want to come with your mom and be an engineer on my balcony tomorrow after school?" Mom smiled and said yes, and {name} nodded, not quite sure.

The next day, Mom came along with {name}. Grandpa Lin's balcony was like a tiny laboratory, crowded with screwdrivers, tape measures, and a creaky old electric fan. He switched on the fan and had {name} hold the mended kite in front of it. Instantly, the kite whirled in wild circles. "See it?" Grandpa Lin asked. "The wind is strong, and the tail is too short to keep balance, like a tightrope walker without a pole." {name}'s eyes lit up.

"Then I'll make the tail long and heavy!" {name} eagerly tied on a thick strip of cloth. Now the kite dragged like it was hauling a rock and wouldn't lift at all. Grandpa Lin chuckled. "Lesson one for engineers: write down every failure." So {name} opened a notebook and wrote: too short spins, too heavy sinks. For two days they snipped, taped, and measured, until the answer was clear: long, but light.

But where could they find something long and light? {name} searched every drawer, then noticed the pile of torn tracing paper from all the crashed tries. {he} cut the scraps into thin ribbons and joined them into a tail three meters long, adding a little paper funnel at the end to catch the wind. The scraps that once made {name} so gloomy now fluttered calmly and steadily in front of the fan.

On Saturday, the festival lawn was packed, and Mom, Dad, and Grandpa Lin all came to watch. The wind was fiercer than ever, and kite after kite tumbled down. {name} took a deep breath and let go for one last try. The red eagle shook out its long tail and climbed higher and higher, then held perfectly still against the blue sky. Grandpa Lin gave a thumbs-up, and {name} gripped the spool, grinning from ear to ear.

questions: 風箏一次又一次摔進草堆、翅膀還破了洞的時候，你覺得{name}心裡是什麼感覺？
在林爺爺的陽台實驗室裡，你最想試試看哪一樣東西？
紅色老鷹在藍天裡穩穩停住時，如果你是{name}，第一句想對林爺爺說什麼？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈前，輕聲聊聊彼此最喜歡故事裡的哪一幕；明天有空時，再一起在紙上畫出你們夢想中的風箏。

questions: When the kite kept crashing and the eagle's wing tore, how do you think {name} felt inside?
On Grandpa Lin's balcony laboratory, which thing would you most like to try out?
When the red eagle held still in the blue sky, if you were {name}, what would you say to Grandpa Lin first?
en.tip: Before lights out, take turns whispering your favorite part of the story; tomorrow, draw your dream kites together on paper.

title.en: The Letter Under the Gray Cat

zh: 週六下午，{name}跟著外公鑽進巷口那家「老時光書店」。書架高得快頂到天花板，書本擠得水洩不通，空氣裡飄著紙張和舊木頭的味道。外公一進門就和林老闆聊得眉飛色舞，{name}只好自己在書堆間東張西望，想找本有趣的書打發時間。
角落的矮櫃上，趴著一隻圓滾滾的灰貓。牠的肚子底下，壓著一本封面發黃、積滿灰塵的厚書。{name}伸手想把書抽出來，灰貓卻「喵——」地拖長聲音，尾巴一甩，屁股往下一沉，坐得更穩了。{name}換個角度再試，牠乾脆打了個呵欠，把下巴擱在書脊上，一副「此路不通」的模樣。
「牠叫湯圓，」林老闆笑著走過來，「這三天牠天天守著那本書，像個盡忠職守的小警衛。」{name}靈機一動，從口袋掏出一段毛線，在湯圓眼前晃呀晃。湯圓的眼珠跟著毛線轉了兩圈，終於按捺不住撲了出去。{name}趁機捧起那本書，拍掉灰塵，封面寫著《城市的四季花》。
{name}盤腿坐在地上翻書。翻到一半，一個淡藍色的信封輕輕滑落，郵戳上印著一九七五年。信封沒有封口，信紙上的字跡工整：「秀蘭，桂花開的時候，我想帶妳去看河邊的燈。如果妳願意，就在書裡夾一朵花給我。——文德」{name}瞪大眼睛，心跳得像在打鼓。
{name}捧著信跑去找林老闆和外公。林老闆戴上老花眼鏡，翻出一本厚厚的舊帳本，手指沿著密密麻麻的字慢慢往下滑。「找到了！這本書是對面花店的周家送來的。」外公摸摸下巴：「周文德……該不會就是花店的老周吧？」三個人面面相覷，湯圓在一旁舔爪子，彷彿早就知道答案。
外公牽著{name}的手，林老闆抱著湯圓，三人等綠燈過了馬路，走進對面的小花店。周姐姐一看見湯圓就叫起來：「湯圓！原來你天天溜去書店！」原來湯圓是她養的貓。她讀完信，笑出了眼淚：「這是我阿公寫給阿嬤的信！阿嬤說，阿公當年緊張得忘了寄，最後是直接跑來敲門的。」
周姐姐把信小心收進相框，又從花桶裡挑了一小枝桂花，夾進那本《城市的四季花》，送給{name}。「這下，這封信終於有回音了。」走回書店的路上，湯圓窩在林老闆懷裡打呼嚕。{name}低頭聞了聞書頁間的桂花香，偷偷決定：下週六還要來，看看湯圓又坐在哪本書上。
en: On Saturday afternoon, {name} followed Grandpa into the Old Times Bookshop at the end of the lane. The shelves towered almost to the ceiling, books were crammed into every gap, and the air smelled of paper and old wood. Grandpa was soon chatting happily with Mr. Lin, the owner, so {name} wandered between the stacks, hunting for something good to read.

On a low cabinet in the corner lay a plump gray cat. Squashed beneath its belly was a thick, dusty book with a yellowed cover. When {name} reached to slide it out, the cat gave a long, stretchy "Meeeow," flicked its tail, and plopped down even harder. {name} tried from another side. The cat simply yawned and rested its chin on the spine, as if to say, "No entry."

"That's Dumpling," Mr. Lin said with a chuckle. "For three days she's guarded that book like a very serious little security guard." {name} had an idea and pulled a piece of yarn from a pocket, swinging it back and forth. Dumpling's eyes circled once, twice, and then she pounced. Quickly, {name} scooped up the book and brushed off the dust. The cover read Flowers of the City Through the Seasons.

Sitting cross-legged on the floor, {name} flipped through the pages. Halfway in, a pale blue envelope slid out. Its postmark said 1975. Inside was a neatly written letter: "Xiulan, when the sweet osmanthus blooms, I'd like to take you to see the lanterns by the river. If you say yes, tuck a flower in this book for me. Wenda." {name}'s heart thumped like a drum.

{name} rushed the letter over to Mr. Lin and Grandpa. Mr. Lin put on his reading glasses and pulled out a fat old record book, running his finger slowly down the crowded columns. "Here it is! The Zhou family from the flower shop across the street brought this book in." Grandpa rubbed his chin. "Zhou Wenda... could that be old Mr. Zhou?" Dumpling just licked her paw, as if she'd known all along.

Grandpa held {name}'s hand, Mr. Lin carried Dumpling, and the three of them waited for the green light before crossing to the little flower shop. Miss Zhou, the florist, gasped. "Dumpling! So that's where you sneak off to every day!" Dumpling was her cat. Reading the letter, she laughed until her eyes were wet. "Grandpa wrote this to Grandma! He was so nervous he forgot to mail it and just knocked on her door instead."

Miss Zhou slipped the letter carefully into a picture frame. Then she chose a tiny sprig of sweet osmanthus, tucked it into the flower book, and handed the book to {name}. "There. Now the letter finally has its answer." On the walk back, Dumpling purred in Mr. Lin's arms. {name} sniffed the sweet scent between the pages and made a secret plan: next Saturday, come back and see which book Dumpling was sitting on.

questions: 湯圓一屁股坐在書上、還把下巴擱在書脊上的時候，你覺得牠心裡在想什麼？
{name}看到那封一九七五年的信時心跳得像打鼓，如果是你發現了這封信，你會有什麼感覺？
下週六{name}再去書店，你猜湯圓會坐在哪一本書上？那本書裡可能藏著什麼秘密？
zh.tip: 睡前關燈後，和孩子輪流小聲說出一種花或一種香味，猜猜它會藏在哪本書裡；明天也可以一起摘一片葉子或小花，夾進家裡的書中當作小秘密。

questions: When Dumpling plopped down on the book and rested her chin on it, what do you think she was thinking?
{name}'s heart thumped like a drum on finding the 1975 letter. If you had found that letter, how would you have felt?
When {name} goes back next Saturday, which book do you guess Dumpling will be sitting on, and what secret might be hidden inside?
en.tip: After the lights go out, take turns whispering the name of a flower or a nice smell and guessing which book it might be hiding in. Tomorrow, you could pick a leaf or small flower together and tuck it into a book at home as your own little secret.

zh: 山頂的暗空公園裡，草地涼涼的。媽媽把格子毯子鋪平，打開一盞紅色小手電筒，光線柔得像一顆熟透的櫻桃。{name}躺下來，抬頭一看，忍不住嘟起嘴：「星星好少喔，而且有一大片雲橫在天上，剛好擋住最好看的地方。」媽媽只是笑笑，輕輕說：「再等一下。」
媽媽關掉紅燈，四周頓時萬籟俱寂。不，仔細聽，還有蟋蟀唧唧，松樹被風吹得沙沙響，遠處一隻貓頭鷹低低地叫：「呼——呼——」{name}數著自己的呼吸，一口、兩口、三口。星星像有人慢慢轉亮燈光似的，一顆，又一顆，悄悄地冒了出來。
就在這時，那片「雲」開始閃爍了。{name}屏氣凝神，目不轉睛地盯著看：原來它根本不是雲，而是不計其數的星星擠在一起，像一條撒滿糖粉的河，從山這頭流到山那頭。「那是銀河。」媽媽說。{name}恍然大悟，噗哧笑出來：「我剛剛竟然在跟幾千億顆星星生氣！」
媽媽握著{name}的手指，在夜空中慢慢描。「先找七顆亮星，連起來像一支大湯匙。」{name}的手指一格一格移動，湯匙柄、湯匙口，真的出現了！「那是北斗七星。」{name}瞇起眼睛想了想：「這麼大的湯匙，巨人要舀多少碗湯，才吃得飽啊？」媽媽笑得毯子都抖了一下。
「我們來編自己的星星故事吧。」媽媽提議。{name}指著銀河旁三顆排成彎線的小星：「那是一隻星星烏龜，背著燈籠慢慢過河。牠從來不趕時間，因為牠知道，慢慢走才看得見最多風景。」媽媽接著說：「河對岸有一隻小兔子，每天晚上都泡好一壺茶，等烏龜來。」
夜風越來越涼，媽媽從背包拿出第二條毯子，把兩個人裹成一顆軟軟的飯糰。保溫瓶裡的可可還溫溫的，{name}捧著杯子小口小口喝，甜香一路暖到肚子裡。忽然，一道細細的光從天邊滑過，安安靜靜，像有人輕輕畫了一筆。{name}閉上眼睛，悄悄許了一個願。
蟋蟀唱得慢了，風也吹得輕了，媽媽的聲音愈來愈柔：「烏龜還在走，兔子還在等，銀河還在流。」{name}的眼皮愈來愈重。星星一顆一顆，像在眨眼說晚安。{name}靠著媽媽，小聲地說：「晚安，銀河。晚安，烏龜。」然後，在滿天星光底下，慢慢睡著了。
en: At the top of the mountain, in a dark-sky park, the grass felt cool and damp. Mom smoothed out a checkered blanket and switched on a small red flashlight, its glow as soft as a ripe cherry. {name} lay back, looked up, and frowned. "There are hardly any stars. And a big cloud is smeared right across the best part of the sky." Mom only smiled. "Give it a little while."

Mom clicked off the red light, and the whole meadow went hushed. Well, almost. Crickets chirped in the grass, the pines whispered in the wind, and far away an owl called, "Hoo-hoo." {name} counted slow breaths: one, two, three. Little by little, as if someone were turning up a dimmer switch, stars appeared, one, then another, then another.

Then the cloud began to sparkle. {name} held perfectly still and stared. It wasn't a cloud at all. It was countless stars crowded together, like a river dusted with powdered sugar, flowing from one mountaintop to the other. "That's the Milky Way," Mom said softly. {name} burst out giggling. "I was grumbling at billions of stars!"

Mom took {name}'s finger and guided it slowly across the sky. "Find seven bright stars that make a giant spoon." Bit by bit, the finger traced the handle, then the bowl, and there it was. "The Big Dipper," Mom said. {name} squinted thoughtfully. "With a spoon that big, how many bowls of soup would a giant need before getting full?" Mom laughed so hard the blanket shook.

"Let's make up our own star stories," Mom suggested. {name} pointed to three small stars curving beside the Milky Way. "That's a star turtle carrying a lantern across the river. It's never in a hurry, because going slowly lets you see the most." Mom added, "And on the far bank, a little rabbit brews a pot of tea every night and waits for the turtle."

The breeze grew chilly, so Mom pulled a second blanket from her backpack and bundled them both up like a soft rice ball. The cocoa in the thermos was still warm, and {name} sipped it slowly, sweetness spreading all the way down. Suddenly a thin line of light slid across the sky, silent as a pencil stroke. {name} closed {his} eyes and quietly made a wish.

The crickets slowed. The wind softened. Mom's voice grew gentle and low. "The turtle is still walking. The rabbit is still waiting. The river of stars is still flowing." {name}'s eyelids grew heavy. The stars blinked, one by one, as if saying goodnight. Leaning against Mom, {name} whispered, "Goodnight, Milky Way. Goodnight, turtle." And beneath a sky full of starlight, {name} drifted off to sleep.

questions: 一開始{name}以為那片「雲」擋住了星星，後來發現是銀河的時候，你覺得那一刻是什麼感覺？
北斗七星像一支巨人的大湯匙，如果你是那個巨人，你想用它舀什麼來吃？
星星烏龜背著燈籠慢慢過河，兔子泡好茶在等牠，你覺得牠們見面時會聊些什麼？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈後，和孩子一起閉上眼睛，輪流小聲編一句星星烏龜和兔子的故事，慢慢接下去，直到有人睏了為止。

questions: At first {name} thought a cloud was blocking the stars. What do you think that moment felt like when it turned out to be the Milky Way?
The Big Dipper looks like a giant's spoon. If you were the giant, what would you scoop up with it?
The star turtle carries a lantern across the river while the rabbit waits with tea. What do you think they talk about when they finally meet?
en.tip: After lights out tonight, close your eyes together and take turns whispering one sentence of a new turtle-and-rabbit star story, passing it back and forth until someone gets sleepy.

zh: 清晨，花蓮港的海風帶著淡淡的鹹味。{name}跟著外婆登上賞鯨船，懷裡抱著一本全新的素描本，第一頁寫著大大的「鯨魚」兩個字。船長阿海伯笑呵呵地說：「大海可不照課表上課，要有耐心喔。」{name}用力點頭，心想：耐心？我最不缺的就是耐心了。
船駛出港口，浪一層接一層湧來，把船身推得搖搖晃晃。{name}緊握欄杆，外婆就站在旁邊，一隻手輕輕搭在{his}肩上。一小時過去，海面上只有浪。兩小時過去，還是只有浪。素描本裡畫滿了彎彎曲曲的線條，{name}長長嘆了口氣：「我好像在畫一本《海浪大全》。」
太陽越爬越高，船艙裡有人打起瞌睡，有個小弟弟乾脆躺在椅子上數雲朵。{name}也覺得眼皮沉甸甸的。遠方有幾個白點一閃一閃，{he}只瞄了一眼，以為又是浪花碎開，便悶悶地闔上素描本：「外婆，我們回去好不好？鯨魚今天一定放假了。」外婆沒有回答，只是瞇起眼睛，靜靜望著那些白點。
忽然，阿海伯的聲音從廣播傳來：「右前方！大家看船頭！」那些白點越來越近，原來根本不是浪花，是一大群海豚在跳躍！牠們像被彈簧彈起來似的，一隻接一隻衝出水面，在半空中旋轉兩三圈，再「啪」地落回海裡。「是飛旋海豚！」外婆驚呼。{name}看得目瞪口呆，素描本差點從手中滑落。
海豚追逐著船頭翻起的浪花，時而並肩齊游，時而一躍而起，好像在比賽誰轉的圈數最多。有一隻轉到一半，竟然歪歪斜斜地跌進水裡，濺起一大片水花，全船的人都哈哈大笑。{name}笑得前仰後合，趕緊重新翻開素描本，手忙腳亂地畫。線條歪七扭八，可是每一筆都在跳舞。
海豚漸漸游遠了。{name}正要補上最後一筆，外婆卻輕輕拉了拉{his}手臂，指向很遠很遠的海面。一道細細的水霧噴向天空，接著，一條巨大的尾巴緩緩升起，黑得發亮，像一扇敞開的門，在陽光下停了一秒，又悄悄沉入深藍之中。全船鴉雀無聲，連海風彷彿都屏住了呼吸。
回港的路上，{name}一頁頁翻著素描本：前面全是海浪，後面是旋轉的海豚，最後一頁，是那條只出現一秒鐘的尾巴。{name}拿起筆，在每一頁海浪旁寫下小小的「還在等」，又在鯨尾那頁寫上「等到了」。外婆問：「下次還來嗎？」{name}把素描本抱得緊緊的：「來！我要畫《海浪大全》第二集！」
en: Early in the morning, the sea breeze at Hualien Harbor tasted faintly of salt. {name} climbed aboard the whale-watching boat with Grandma, hugging a brand-new sketchbook. The first page said WHALE in big letters. Captain Ahai chuckled. "The ocean doesn't follow a schedule, you know. You'll need patience." {name} nodded hard. Patience? That was easy. {name} had loads of it.

The boat chugged out of the harbor, and wave after wave rolled in, rocking it from side to side. {name} gripped the railing, with Grandma right beside and one hand resting gently on {his} shoulder. One hour passed. Nothing but waves. Two hours passed. Still nothing but waves. The sketchbook filled with wiggly lines. {name} sighed. "I think I'm drawing The Complete Book of Waves."

The sun climbed higher. Some passengers dozed off, and one little boy gave up and lay on a bench counting clouds. {name}'s eyelids felt heavy too. Far away, a few white specks flickered. {name} glanced at them, decided they were just more waves breaking, and shut the sketchbook. "Grandma, can we go back? The whales must have the day off." Grandma didn't answer. She just squinted at the specks.

Suddenly Captain Ahai's voice crackled over the speaker. "Front right! Everyone, look at the bow!" The white specks were racing closer. They weren't waves at all. They were dolphins, a whole crowd of them, leaping! One after another they shot out of the water as if bounced by springs, spun two or three times in midair, and splashed back down. "Spinner dolphins!" Grandma gasped. {name} stared, and the sketchbook nearly slipped away.

The dolphins chased the foamy wave at the front of the boat, swimming side by side, then bursting into the air as if competing to see who could spin the most. One wobbled halfway through a spin and flopped sideways into the sea with an enormous splash. The whole boat burst out laughing. {name} laughed hardest of all, flipped the sketchbook open again, and scribbled fast. The lines were crooked, but every single one was dancing.

Slowly the dolphins swam away. {name} was finishing one last line when Grandma tugged gently at {his} arm and pointed far, far across the water. A thin puff of mist sprayed into the sky. Then a gigantic tail rose slowly from the sea, glossy and dark, like a door swinging open. It paused in the sunlight for one second, then slid quietly into the deep blue. Nobody on the boat said a word. Even the wind seemed to hold its breath.

On the way back to the harbor, {name} turned the pages one by one: waves at the beginning, spinning dolphins after that, and on the very last page, a tail that had appeared for only one second. {name} picked up the pen and wrote "still waiting" beside every page of waves, then wrote "worth it" beside the tail. "Want to come again?" Grandma asked. {name} hugged the sketchbook tight. "Yes! I'm going to draw The Complete Book of Waves, Part Two!"

questions: 在海上等了好幾個小時，只看到海浪的時候，如果你也在船上，你會想做什麼來打發時間？
那隻轉到一半跌進水裡的海豚，你猜牠當時心裡在想什麼？你會幫牠取什麼名字？
那條鯨魚尾巴像一扇敞開的門，如果真的能走進去，你覺得門後的深海裡會有什麼？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈後，和孩子輪流用悄悄話描述故事裡最想畫下來的一個畫面；明天找個時間，兩人並肩各畫一頁自己的「賞鯨日記」。

questions: During all those hours of nothing but waves, what would you have done to pass the time if you were on the boat?
What do you think the dolphin that flopped sideways mid-spin was thinking? What name would you give it?
The whale's tail looked like a door swinging open. If you could step through it, what do you imagine you'd find in the deep blue?
en.tip: After lights out tonight, take turns whispering about the one moment from the story you'd most like to sketch. Tomorrow, sit side by side and each draw a page of your own whale-watching sketchbook.

zh: 放學後，{name}牽著阿嬤的手穿過熱鬧的巷子，忽然聽見一陣鑼鼓聲從一扇半開的木門裡傳出來。門內是一座小小的布袋戲臺，雕花已經褪了色，紅布幕卻洗得乾乾淨淨。白髮蒼蒼的阿成伯正讓一尊布偶劍客翻身、拔劍，動作行雲流水。{name}看得目瞪口呆，連手裡的豆花都忘了吃。
「阿成伯，可以教我嗎？」{name}一連問了三天。阿嬤笑著答應，只要功課寫完，週末都陪{him}來。第四天，阿成伯終於從架上取下一尊小劍客，白袍黑靴，背著一把木劍。「它叫小白，脾氣可不小喔。」{name}興奮地把手伸進布偶裡，照著指點，用食指撐住頭，拇指和中指撐起兩隻手臂。
結果小白一點也不聽話。{name}想讓它鞠躬，它卻一頭栽下去；想讓它拔劍，木劍竟然飛了出去，啪的一聲落在阿嬤的茶杯旁邊。{name}的臉一下子燙了起來。阿成伯哈哈大笑：「好劍法，差點把阿嬤的茶劈成兩半！」「我的手太笨了。」{name}垂頭喪氣地說。
阿成伯沒有多說，只拿出一顆乒乓球，要{name}用三根手指把它轉來轉去。接下來好幾個星期，{name}在公車上轉，在客廳轉，連刷牙時都偷偷轉。週末一到戲臺，就讓小白一遍又一遍地走路、回頭、抬手。手指痠了，就甩一甩，再來一次，從不半途而廢。
漸漸地，小白的腳步不再踉踉蹌蹌。有一天，{name}讓它輕輕躍上欄杆，旋身拔劍，木劍穩穩停在半空中。阿成伯瞇起眼睛，滿意地點點頭：「下個月廟會，開場那一小段，就交給你演。」{name}倒吸一口氣，心臟怦怦直跳，卻還是用力點了點頭。
廟會那晚，廟埕燈籠高掛，香煙裊裊，人山人海。阿嬤坐在第一排，緊緊握著手機準備錄影。鑼鼓一響，{name}深吸一口氣，讓小白從布幕後一躍而出。翻身、拔劍、收劍、鞠躬，一氣呵成。台下先是一片安靜，接著掌聲如雷，有個小朋友還大喊：「再來一次！」
散場後，{name}小心翼翼地替小白整理衣袍，卻發現袖子內側繡著幾個褪色的小字：「阿成，學劍第一天，掉劍十七次。」{name}抬頭望向阿成伯。老師傅不好意思地搔搔頭：「那是我八歲時的事啦。」{name}忍不住笑出聲來，輕輕把小白放回架上，心裡盤算著明天要練的新招式。
en: After school, {name} was walking hand in hand with Grandma down a busy lane when a clatter of gongs and drums spilled out of a half-open wooden door. Inside stood a tiny glove-puppet stage. Its carvings had faded, but the red curtain was spotless. A white-haired man named Uncle Cheng was making a puppet swordsman flip and draw his blade, smooth as flowing water. {name} forgot all about the sweet tofu pudding in hand.

"Uncle Cheng, will you teach me?" {name} asked three days in a row. Grandma smiled and promised to bring {him} every weekend, as long as homework came first. On the fourth day, Uncle Cheng lifted a small swordsman from the shelf: white robe, black boots, a wooden sword on its back. "This is Little White. He has quite a temper." {name} eagerly slipped a hand inside, one finger for the head, a thumb and a middle finger for the arms.

Little White refused to cooperate. When {name} tried to make it bow, it toppled face-first. When {name} tried to draw the sword, the sword went flying and landed with a clack right beside Grandma's teacup. {name}'s cheeks burned. Uncle Cheng roared with laughter. "Fine swordsmanship! You nearly sliced Grandma's tea in two!" "My fingers are just too clumsy," {name} mumbled.

Uncle Cheng said nothing more. He simply handed over a ping-pong ball and showed {name} how to roll it around with three fingers. For weeks afterward, {name} rolled it on the bus, rolled it in the living room, even rolled it while brushing teeth. Every weekend at the stage, Little White walked, turned, and raised his arms, again and again. When {his} fingers ached, {name} shook them out and tried once more.

Little by little, Little White stopped stumbling. One afternoon, {name} made him spring lightly onto the railing, spin, and draw his sword, which hung perfectly still in the air. Uncle Cheng narrowed his eyes and nodded. "Next month is the temple festival. The opening scene is yours." {name} gasped, heart thumping like a drum, but nodded firmly.

On festival night, lanterns glowed over the temple square, incense curled into the air, and crowds packed every corner. Grandma sat in the front row, phone ready to record. The gongs crashed. {name} took a deep breath and sent Little White leaping out from behind the curtain. Flip, draw, sheathe, bow, all in one graceful sweep. For a moment the crowd was silent. Then applause thundered, and a little kid shouted, "Do it again!"

Afterward, as {name} gently smoothed Little White's robe, a few faded stitches peeked out from inside the sleeve: "Cheng. First day of sword practice. Dropped it seventeen times." {name} looked up at Uncle Cheng. The old master scratched his head sheepishly. "I was eight years old." {name} burst out laughing, set Little White carefully back on the shelf, and started planning tomorrow's new move.

questions: 木劍飛到阿嬤茶杯旁邊的時候，你覺得{name}心裡在想什麼？
廟會那晚，台下有人大喊「再來一次！」，那一刻你覺得{name}是什麼感覺？
你猜{name}明天想讓小白練什麼新招式？你會幫這個招式取什麼名字？
zh.tip: 睡前關小燈，用手指在棉被上當小劍客，輪流演一個慢動作的招式，再小聲猜猜對方演的是什麼。

questions: When the wooden sword landed beside Grandma's teacup, what do you think {name} was thinking?
On festival night, when a kid shouted "Do it again!", how do you think {name} felt right then?
What new move do you think {name} will teach Little White tomorrow? What would you name it?
en.tip: With the lights low, take turns making your fingers into a tiny swordsman on the blanket and act out a slow-motion move, then whisper guesses about what move it was.

zh: 清晨的港口飄著鹹鹹的海風，海鷗在桅杆上吵個不停。{name}跟著隊友繫緊救生衣，爬上龍舟最前端的小座位。教練阿海伯把一對鼓棒交到{name}手上，笑著說：「十個划手，一顆心跳。從今天起，這顆心跳就交給你了。」{name}握緊鼓棒，心裡像揣了一隻小兔子，怦怦亂跳。
「出發！」阿海伯坐在船尾掌舵。{name}深吸一口氣，咚咚咚咚，鼓聲又急又響，彷彿在追趕什麼東西。可是划手們各划各的，有人快、有人慢，船槳在水面上互相碰撞，喀啦喀啦響。龍舟像一隻喝醉的螃蟹，歪歪扭扭地原地打轉。一隻海鷗停在浮標上「嘎嘎」叫，好像在看熱鬧。
坐在第一排的阿偉皺起眉頭，乾脆把頭轉開，只顧自己埋頭猛划。{name}的臉一下子燙了起來，手上的鼓棒越打越亂，簡直手忙腳亂。休息時，大家坐在碼頭邊喝水聊天，卻沒有人提起鼓聲。{name}低頭盯著鼓面，悶悶地想：是不是坐在最前面的人，根本不該是我？
阿海伯慢慢走過來，沒有多說什麼，只指了指港口外一艘緩緩前進的漁船。「你看那些浪。」他說，「浪不聽誰的命令，可是船會順著浪走。」{name}聽得一頭霧水，還是盯著海面看了好久。浪一波接一波，有起有落，從不慌張。忽然，{name}想起阿偉划槳的樣子，那一下一下，不也是有起有落嗎？
第二次下水，{name}不急著打鼓，而是目不轉睛地觀察每一位划手。槳葉插進水裡、用力拉回、抬起，再插進水裡。{name}默默數了幾輪，等到槳葉剛要入水的那一瞬間，才落下第一聲鼓：「咚！」接著又是一聲，不早也不晚，正好踩在大家的節奏上。阿偉愣了一下，轉頭望向船頭。
鼓聲穩穩的，像大海在深深呼吸。划手們的槳漸漸對齊了，十支槳一起入水，水花整整齊齊地濺起。{name}感覺到船身輕輕一震，便悄悄把鼓點加快一點點，再加快一點點。龍舟彷彿被喚醒的巨龍，劈開浪花向前飛馳，連剛才那隻海鷗都得拚命拍翅膀，才追得上。
船回到碼頭，大家氣喘吁吁，卻個個笑得合不攏嘴。阿偉走到船頭，抹了抹額頭的汗，有點不好意思地說：「划到一半我才發現，不是我在拉著船跑，是你的鼓在帶著我跑。」他伸出拳頭，{name}也伸出拳頭，輕輕一碰。阿海伯在船尾哈哈大笑：「明天早上，心跳記得準時報到！」
en: The harbor smelled of salt that morning, and the seagulls squabbled on the masts. {name} buckled up with the rest of the team and climbed into the small seat at the very front of the dragon boat. Coach Hai handed over a pair of drumsticks and grinned. "Ten paddlers, one heartbeat. Starting today, that heartbeat is you." {name} gripped the sticks, heart thumping like a rabbit's.

"Let's go!" called Coach Hai from the steering oar at the back. {name} took a deep breath and pounded away. BOOM-BOOM-BOOM-BOOM! The beat raced as if chasing something. But the paddlers each went their own speed, some fast, some slow, and their paddles clattered together. The boat wobbled in circles like a dizzy crab. A seagull perched on a buoy and squawked, enjoying the show.

In the first row, Wei frowned and turned away, digging his paddle in hard and ignoring the drum completely. {name}'s cheeks burned, and the drumbeat tumbled into a jumble. At the break, everyone sat on the dock sipping water and chatting, but nobody mentioned the drumming. {name} stared at the drum and wondered, maybe the front seat belongs to someone else?

Coach Hai wandered over. He didn't give a speech. He simply pointed at a fishing boat gliding out past the harbor. "Look at the waves," he said. "Waves don't take orders, but a boat learns to ride them." Puzzled, {name} watched the sea for a long time. The waves rose and fell, rose and fell, never in a hurry. Then {name} remembered Wei's paddle. It rose and fell too.

On the second run, {name} didn't start drumming right away. Instead, {name} watched every paddler closely. Blades dipped, pulled, lifted, and dipped again. {name} counted a few strokes silently, then struck the drum at the exact moment the blades touched the water. BOOM! Then another, not early, not late, right on their rhythm. Wei blinked and glanced toward the front.

The drumbeat stayed steady, like the ocean breathing slowly. One by one, the paddles lined up until all ten splashed in together, sending up neat sprays of water. {name} felt the boat shiver forward, then nudged the beat a little faster, and a little faster still. The dragon boat surged ahead like a dragon waking up, and the seagull had to flap hard just to keep up.

Back at the dock, everyone was panting and grinning from ear to ear. Wei walked to the front, wiped his forehead, and said a bit shyly, "Halfway through, I realized I wasn't pulling the boat. Your drum was pulling me." He held out a fist, and {name} bumped it. Coach Hai laughed from the back. "See you tomorrow morning, heartbeat. Don't be late!"

questions: 接過鼓棒時，{name}心裡像揣了一隻小兔子。你猜那隻小兔子在說什麼？
龍舟像喝醉的螃蟹一樣原地打轉時，如果你也坐在船上，你會有什麼感覺？
龍舟像被喚醒的巨龍劈開浪花往前衝，如果它能一直衝下去，你希望它帶大家去哪裡？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈後，和孩子並肩躺著，用手指在被子上輕輕敲出像海浪呼吸一樣的慢節奏，一起越敲越慢、越敲越輕。

questions: When {name} took the drumsticks, there was a rabbit thumping inside. What do you think that little rabbit was saying?
When the boat spun in circles like a dizzy crab, how would you have felt sitting on it?
When the dragon boat surged ahead like a waking dragon, where would you want it to carry everyone if it never stopped?
en.tip: Tonight after lights out, lie side by side and tap a slow, wave-like rhythm on the blanket with your fingers, letting it get softer and slower together.

zh: 星期六早上，爺爺牽著{name}出門。兩人走過熱鬧的街道，來到社區游泳池。泳池在高高的大樓旁邊。池水藍藍的，亮晶晶的。{name}在淺水區玩水，雙腳穩穩踩到池底。爺爺坐在池邊，眼睛一直看著{name}。
「{name}，爺爺要去一下廁所。」爺爺站起來說。淺水區好好玩喔！有小朋友在丟球，有人在吹泡泡。{name}好想繼續玩。可是爺爺不在，沒有大人看著。{name}慢慢爬上池邊，坐到{his}大毛巾上。「我在這裡等你！」爺爺笑著點點頭。
{name}決定玩數數遊戲。「一、二、三……」戴黃泳帽的阿姨，是第一個。用力踢水的哥哥，是第二個。救生員方阿姨坐在高高的椅子上。她戴著哨子，也看著大家。{name}一個一個數，一共數到七個人。
鄰居美美也在淺水區玩。美美爸爸站在旁邊看著她。忽然，球漂走了，美美追了過去。她走到比較深的地方。她的腳踩不到底了，小手拍呀拍。{name}沒有跳下水。{name}站起來大聲喊：「救生員！快來幫忙！」
{name}抓起{his}浮板，用力丟過去。浮板輕輕的，漂到美美旁邊。美美緊緊抱住浮板，浮起來了。方阿姨很快游了過來。美美爸爸也趕到了。大家把美美帶回淺水區。美美咳了一下，又笑了。
方阿姨對{name}豎起大拇指。「你喊得好大聲，浮板丟得好準！」美美說：「謝謝你的浮板！」這時，爺爺回來了。爺爺聽完，摸摸{name}的頭。「你乖乖等我，還幫了好朋友。」爺爺坐回池邊說：「好了，可以下水囉！」
{name}走進淺水區，腳踩得到池底。{name}和美美一起丟球，玩得好開心。爺爺說：「下星期，我們去河濱公園坐小船。」{name}問：「坐船要穿救生衣嗎？」「對，每個人都要穿。」{name}想到橘色的救生衣，鼓鼓的，像個大抱枕。「我要扣得緊緊的！」
太陽慢慢下山了，天空變成橘紅色。爺爺牽著{name}，走在回家的路上。城市的燈一盞一盞亮起來。{name}開始數路燈：「一、二、三……」數著數著，家就到了。今天真是一場好棒的冒險！
en: On Saturday morning, Grandpa took {name} out. They walked down a busy city street. They came to the neighborhood pool. It sat beside tall buildings. The water was blue and sparkly. {name} played in the shallow end. {his} feet stood flat on the bottom. Grandpa sat at the edge, watching.

"{name}, I need a quick bathroom break," said Grandpa. The shallow end looked so fun! Kids were tossing a ball. Someone was blowing bubbles. {name} wanted to keep playing. But no grown-up was watching now. So {name} climbed out and sat on {his} big towel. "I'll wait right here!" Grandpa smiled and nodded.

{name} played a counting game. "One, two, three..." A lady in a yellow cap was number one. A big kid kicking hard was number two. Ms. Fang, the lifeguard, sat on a tall chair. She had a whistle and watched everyone. {name} counted seven swimmers in all.

Neighbor Mei was in the shallow end too. Her dad stood close, watching her. Suddenly, the ball floated away. Mei followed it to a deeper spot. Her feet could not touch anymore. Her hands splashed and splashed. {name} did not jump in. {name} stood up and shouted, "Lifeguard! Help, please!"

{name} grabbed {his} kickboard and threw it hard. The light board floated right next to Mei. Mei hugged it tight and bobbed up. Ms. Fang swam over fast. Mei's dad hurried over too. Together they brought Mei back to the shallow end. Mei coughed a little, then giggled.

Ms. Fang gave {name} a big thumbs-up. "Such a loud shout, and a great throw!" Mei said, "Thank you for the kickboard!" Just then, Grandpa came back. He heard everything and patted {name} gently. "You waited for me, and you helped a friend." Grandpa sat down. "Okay, in you go!"

{name} stepped into the shallow end. {his} feet touched the bottom. {name} and Mei tossed the ball together. "Next week, let's ride a little boat at the river park," said Grandpa. "Do we wear life jackets?" asked {name}. "Yes, everyone does." Orange, puffy, like a big pillow! "I'll buckle mine tight!"

The sun slowly went down. The sky turned orange and pink. Grandpa held {name}'s hand on the way home. City lights blinked on, one by one. {name} counted the streetlights. "One, two, three..." Soon they were home. What a wonderful adventure!

questions: 爺爺去廁所的時候，{name}做了什麼？為什麼？
美美的腳踩不到底時，{name}怎麼幫忙？如果是你，你會怎麼做？
坐船的時候，我們要穿什麼？
zh.tip: 這星期玩一個「小幫手」遊戲：把玩偶放在床邊當作在水裡，練習大聲喊「大人快來！」再丟一個枕頭過去。下次玩水前，一起說好：「大人看著，我才下水。」

questions: What did {name} do when Grandpa went to the bathroom? Why?
When Mei's feet couldn't touch, how did {name} help? What would you do?
What do we wear when we ride a boat?
en.tip: This week, play a "little helper" game: put a stuffed toy by the bed as if it's in water, practice shouting "Grown-up, come help!" and toss it a pillow. Before your next swim, agree together: "I only go in when a grown-up is watching."

zh: 星期三晚上，{name}在「方塊城市」遊戲裡，和隊友「彗星十號」聯手蓋好一座會發光的摩天輪。彗星十號打字飛快：「我也十歲！你是我遇過最厲害的隊友。」{name}得意洋洋，手指在鍵盤上跳起舞來。對方接著問：「你讀哪間學校？傳張照片給我看嘛。」{name}的手指停在半空中，想了想，只回了一個笑臉。
星期四，訊息又來了：「星期六下午兩點，車站旁的購物中心見，我請你喝珍珠奶茶。記得，這是我們的祕密，誰都不能說喔！」{name}盯著螢幕，肚子像打了一個結。好朋友見面，為什麼要偷偷摸摸？那天晚上，{name}翻來覆去，枕頭被揉得皺巴巴的，像一團洩了氣的麵糰。
星期五早上，{name}端著早餐，在廚房門口徘徊了三圈，終於開口：「媽媽，我說一件事，你不要生氣好不好？」{name}把平板遞過去。媽媽看完訊息，放下杯子，給了{name}一個大大的擁抱。「謝謝你告訴我。你一點錯都沒有，這正是最勇敢的做法。」{name}心裡那個結，一下子鬆開了一半。
媽媽陪{name}坐下來。「網路上的人，看不見臉，也聽不到真正的聲音。說自己十歲的，可能是任何人。」她指著螢幕：「你沒給學校名字、沒傳照片，也沒說我們住哪裡，做得非常好。」兩人一起截圖存證，再按下封鎖和檢舉。「那星期六呢？」{name}問。媽媽眨眨眼：「星期六，我們有別的任務。」
星期六一早，媽媽交給{name}一張手繪地圖，上面畫著三個謎題。第一站，搭捷運找「會唱歌的柱子」，原來是車站裡的一架老鋼琴，{name}彈了兩個音，旁邊的阿伯還拍手叫好。第二站，在老街找「屋頂上的守門員」，{name}仰著脖子找了半天，才發現是一隻趴在瓦片上打盹的橘貓。媽媽一路都走在旁邊。
最後一站是圖書館旁的小咖啡店。推開門，同班的阿凱和阿凱的爸爸正朝他們揮手。大人一聊才知道，阿凱也收到「彗星十號」的訊息，而且一字不差：「你是我遇過最厲害的隊友……這是我們的祕密。」{name}和阿凱面面相覷。阿凱哭笑不得：「它對每個人都說一樣的話？我還以為自己是天下第一呢！」
原來阿凱也早就告訴了爸爸。兩家人約好星期一一起去找老師，提醒全班同學。回家的捷運上，夕陽把車窗染成橘子汽水的顏色。{name}靠著媽媽說：「以後網路上誰叫我保守祕密，我就第一個跟你說。」媽媽笑了：「成交！下一張藏寶圖，換你來畫。」{name}已經開始盤算，第三個謎題要藏在哪裡了。
en: On Wednesday night, {name} and a teammate called Comet10 finished building a glowing Ferris wheel in a game called Block City. Comet10 typed fast: "I'm ten too! You're the best teammate I've ever had." {name} grinned, fingers dancing across the keys. Then a new message popped up: "What school do you go to? Send me a photo!" {name} paused, thought for a moment, and sent back only a smiley face.

On Thursday, another message arrived: "Meet me at the mall by the station on Saturday at two. I'll buy you bubble tea. Remember, this is our secret. Don't tell anyone!" {name} stared at the screen, and {his} stomach twisted into a knot. Why would a real friend want to sneak around? That night, {name} tossed and turned until the pillow looked like squashed bread dough.

On Friday morning, {name} carried breakfast to the kitchen doorway and circled it three times before speaking. "Mom, can I tell you something? Promise you won't be mad?" {name} handed over the tablet. Mom read the messages, set down her cup, and pulled {name} into a big hug. "Thank you for telling me. You did nothing wrong. This was the bravest thing to do." The knot in {name}'s stomach loosened.

Mom sat down beside {name}. "Online, you can't see anyone's face or hear their real voice. Someone who says they're ten could be anybody." She tapped the screen. "You didn't share your school, your photo, or where we live. That was smart." Together they saved screenshots, then pressed Block and Report. "What about Saturday?" {name} asked. Mom winked. "Saturday, we have a different mission."

Early Saturday, Mom handed {name} a hand-drawn map with three riddles. The first said, "Ride the subway and find the singing pillar." It turned out to be an old piano in the station! {name} played two notes, and a grandpa nearby clapped. The second said, "Find the goalkeeper on the roof." After much neck-craning, {name} spotted an orange cat napping on the tiles. Mom stayed close the whole way.

The last stop was a tiny café beside the library. When they pushed open the door, classmate Kai and his dad were waving at them. As the grown-ups talked, the truth tumbled out: Kai had gotten messages from Comet10 too, word for word the same. "You're the best teammate I've ever had... this is our secret." {name} and Kai stared at each other. Kai groaned and laughed. "It says that to everyone? And I thought I was a superstar!"

Kai had told his dad right away too. The two families agreed to visit the teacher together on Monday so the whole class would know. On the subway home, the sunset turned the windows the color of orange soda. {name} leaned against Mom. "If anyone online ever asks me to keep a secret, you'll be the first to know." Mom smiled. "Deal! And next time, you draw the treasure map." {name} was already planning the third riddle.

questions: 彗星十號要{name}傳照片、說學校、還要保守祕密時，{name}覺得怎麼樣？又做了什麼？
阿凱收到一模一樣的訊息，這讓你對網路上的「朋友」有什麼新的想法？
如果網路上有人讓你覺得怪怪的，你會第一個告訴誰？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子一起約定一句「暗號」，例如「我有個網路的事想說」，孩子說出這句話時，你保證先聽完、先說謝謝，不責罵。

questions: How did {name} feel when Comet10 asked for a photo, a school name, and a secret? What did {name} do?
Kai got the exact same messages. What does that tell you about friends you meet online?
If something online ever felt strange to you, who would you tell first?
en.tip: This week, agree on a code phrase with your child, like "I have an online thing to tell you," and promise that whenever they say it, you'll listen all the way through and say thank you before anything else.

zh: 新制服送來的那天，{name}興奮得在客廳裡轉圈圈。早上上學前，媽媽在公車站幫{him}拍了一張照片，背景有站牌，有對街的麵包店，制服胸口還繡著「晨光國小」四個字。{name}捧著平板，迫不及待想把照片貼到畫畫社群上，讓常常留言的網友「米米」也看看。
「等一下，」媽媽笑著拉了張椅子坐下，「我們先來玩個偵探遊戲。假如你是一個陌生人，光看這張照片，能找到我們家嗎？」{name}半信半疑地放大照片，第一眼就看見胸前的校名。「這個太明顯了！」接著是站牌上斗大的「榕樹里」三個字。兩條線索，一下子就到手了。
媽媽指了指照片的角落：「還有呢？」{name}瞇起眼睛，覺得簡直像大海撈針。公車路線號碼、麵包店的招牌，甚至遠處那棵歪脖子老榕樹，都在悄悄透露位置。「怎麼到處都是線索啊！」{name}垮下肩膀，嘟囔著說這張照片好像會說話，而且還是個大嘴巴。媽媽忍不住笑出聲來。
{name}可不服輸，把照片放到最大，一格一格慢慢檢查。忽然，{he}倒抽一口氣：站牌的玻璃上，竟然映出了公寓大門，門牌「十八號」清清楚楚！媽媽湊過來看了半天，瞪大眼睛說：「連我都沒發現，你真是火眼金睛！」{name}得意地挺起胸膛，像剛破了一樁大案。
兩人開始動手裁切。剪掉校名，剪掉站牌，剪掉麵包店，也剪掉那片會洩密的玻璃，最後只剩{name}比讚的手和一角藍天。「看起來好像天空在跟大家比讚。」{name}咯咯笑。想了想，{name}又說：「這張還是只傳給阿嬤就好。網路上的人，我其實都不是真的認識。」
就在這時，平板叮咚一聲。米米傳來訊息：「你念哪間學校？在哪一站等公車？我們放學約出來見面吧！不過別告訴大人，這是我們的秘密喔。」{name}的手指停在螢幕上，心裡七上八下，怪怪的。{he}沒有回覆，直接把平板遞給媽媽：「媽媽，這個讓我覺得不太對勁。」
媽媽緊緊抱了抱{name}：「謝謝你馬上告訴我，你一點都沒做錯，以後遇到這種事也一樣。」兩人一起封鎖並檢舉了那個帳號。不久，家族群組跳出阿嬤的回覆：「好神氣的藍天大拇指！」{name}在便條紙上畫了一個放大鏡，貼在平板背面，寫著：「貼文之前，偵探先上工。」
en: The day the new school uniform arrived, {name} spun circles around the living room. That morning, Mom had snapped a photo of {him} at the bus stop, with the stop sign, the bakery across the street, and the words "Morning Light Elementary" stitched right on the uniform. {name} grabbed the tablet, eager to post it on a drawing app so an online friend named Mimi could see.

"Hold on," Mom said, pulling up a chair with a grin. "Let's play detective first. If you were a stranger, could you find our home from this picture?" {name} zoomed in, a little doubtful. The school name jumped out immediately. "Well, that's obvious!" Next came the big letters on the bus stop sign: Banyan Lane. Two clues, found in seconds.

Mom tapped a corner of the screen. "Anything else?" {name} squinted. It felt like hunting for a needle in a haystack, yet clues kept popping up: the bus route number, the bakery's sign, even the crooked old banyan tree down the road. "They're everywhere!" {name} groaned. "This photo talks too much. It's a total blabbermouth!" Mom burst out laughing.

Refusing to give up, {name} zoomed in as far as the screen allowed and inspected the picture square by square. Suddenly came a gasp. Reflected in the glass of the bus shelter was the front door of their building, with the number 18 as clear as day! Mom leaned in and stared. "I completely missed that. You have eagle eyes!" {name} sat up tall, like a detective who had cracked the case.

Together they began cropping. Snip went the school name, the stop sign, the bakery, and the sneaky reflecting glass. All that remained was {name}'s thumbs-up and a patch of blue sky. "It looks like the sky is giving everyone a thumbs-up," {name} giggled. Then, after a moment: "Let's just send this one to Grandma. I don't really know the people online."

Just then, the tablet chimed. A message from Mimi popped up: "Which school do you go to? Which bus stop? Let's meet after school! But don't tell any grown-ups. It's our secret." {name}'s finger froze above the screen. Something felt wrong, like a wobbly tooth. Instead of answering, {name} handed the tablet straight to Mom. "This message feels weird."

Mom gave {name} a big hug. "Thank you for telling me right away. You didn't do anything wrong, and you never will by telling me." Together they blocked and reported the account. Soon Grandma replied in the family chat: "What a proud sky thumbs-up!" {name} drew a magnifying glass on a sticky note, stuck it on the back of the tablet, and wrote: "Before you post, the detective checks first."

questions: {name}在照片裡找到了哪些會透露住家位置的線索？你覺得還有哪些東西也不該放上網路？
米米要{name}保守秘密、約出來見面時，{name}怎麼做？如果你遇到類似的訊息，你會告訴誰？
為什麼{name}最後決定只把照片傳給阿嬤？
zh.tip: 這週挑一張家裡的舊照片，和孩子一起玩「照片偵探」遊戲，找出校名、門牌、站牌等線索；並約定一句暗號：「怪怪的，就告訴大人」，讓孩子知道說出來永遠不會被罵。

questions: What clues did {name} find in the photo that could show where the family lives? What else do you think should never go online?
What did {name} do when Mimi asked to meet and keep it a secret? Who would you tell if you got a message like that?
Why did {name} decide to send the photo only to Grandma?
en.tip: This week, pick an old family photo and play "Photo Detective" together, hunting for school names, house numbers, and street signs. Agree on a family phrase, "If it feels weird, tell a grown-up," and remind your child they will never be in trouble for speaking up.

zh: 今天是第一天上幼兒園。媽媽牽著{name}的手。走呀走，走進教室。教室好大，好亮。玩具好多好多。{name}緊緊抓著媽媽。
美老師笑咪咪地說：「歡迎你！」「這是你的小櫃子喔。」櫃子上有一張貼紙。是一隻藍色小魚。小魚游游游，泡泡咕嚕嚕。這是{name}自己的位置。小書包放進去囉！
媽媽蹲下來說：「媽媽要去上班了。」「放學時間，媽媽就回來。」{name}的眼睛紅紅的。眼淚滴答滴答，掉下來。「媽媽不要走……」
美老師張開手臂。「哭哭沒關係，老師在這裡。」老師抱抱{name}。拍拍背，拍拍背。老師輕輕唱：「小魚游，小魚游，媽媽放學就回來。」{name}慢慢不哭了。媽媽揮揮手：「放學見！」{name}也揮揮手。
小魚櫃子靜靜等著。{name}去玩積木。叩叩叩，疊高高。一個小朋友走過來。「我叫樂樂，一起玩好嗎？」{name}點點頭。積木塔變得好高好高！
唱歌時間到了。拍拍手，啦啦啦。點心時間到了。餅乾脆脆，咔滋咔滋。午睡時間到了。{name}抱著小被被，閉上眼睛。小魚櫃子還在等。
太陽慢慢往下走。美老師說：「放學時間到囉！」{name}跑到小魚櫃子前。拿出小書包，背在背上。小魚貼紙好像在笑。門口有人在揮手。
是媽媽！媽媽回來了！「媽媽！」{name}撲進媽媽懷裡。媽媽抱緊緊：「我說過會回來呀。」{name}回頭揮揮手。「小魚，明天見！美老師，明天見！樂樂，明天見！」
en: Today is {name}'s first school day. Mom holds {his} hand. Step, step, into the classroom. The room is big and bright. So many toys! {name} holds Mom tight.
Teacher Mei smiles. "Welcome! Look here." A little cubby has a sticker. It is a blue fish. Swish, swish, blub, blub! This is {name}'s very own spot. In goes {his} little backpack.
Mom kneels down. "I am going to work now. I will come back at pick-up time." {name}'s eyes feel wet. Drip, drop, drip go the tears. "Don't go, Mom!"

Teacher Mei opens her arms. "It's okay to cry. I am here." She gives {name} a big hug. Pat, pat, pat. She sings softly, "Little fish, swim, swim. Mom comes back again." Slowly the tears stop. Mom waves. "See you at pick-up!" {name} waves too.
The fish cubby waits quietly. {name} plays with blocks. Clack, clack, stack them high! A friend comes over. "I'm Lele. Can I play?" {name} nods. Up, up goes the tower!
Song time! Clap, clap, la la la. Snack time! Crunch, crunch go the crackers. Nap time! {name} hugs a soft blanket. The fish cubby keeps waiting.
The sun goes slowly down. Teacher Mei says, "Pick-up time!" {name} runs to the fish cubby. Out comes the backpack. The little fish seems to smile. Someone waves at the door.
It's Mom! Mom came back! "Mom!" {name} runs into a big hug. "I said I'd come back," Mom says. {name} turns and waves. "Bye, fish! Bye, Teacher Mei! Bye, Lele! See you tomorrow!"

questions: {name}哭哭的時候，美老師做了什麼？
在學校裡，{name}做了哪些好玩的事？你最想玩哪一個？
放學的時候，是誰來接{name}？如果你想媽媽或爸爸，可以怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子練習一個專屬的道別小儀式，例如抱一下、揮揮手，再說「放學見！」，每天分開時都用同一句話，並準時出現。

questions: What did Teacher Mei do when {name} cried?
What fun things did {name} do at school? Which one would you like to try?
Who came at pick-up time? What can you do if you miss Mom or Dad at school?
en.tip: This week, practice a special goodbye ritual together, like one hug, one wave, and "See you at pick-up!" Use the same words every drop-off, and be on time at pick-up.

zh: 媽媽在摺衣服。妹妹在搖籃裡睡覺。籃子裡好多襪子。{name}找到一雙小襪子。那是妹妹的襪子。好小，好小喔！比{name}的手還小呢！
{name}拿出自己的襪子。放在小襪子旁邊。大襪子，小襪子。一大，一小。現在大家都抱妹妹。{name}看了好久。心裡悶悶的。
{name}走到媽媽身邊。拉拉媽媽的衣服。「媽媽，媽媽。」{name}小小聲地問：「你還愛我嗎？」媽媽停下手。輕輕摸摸{his}頭。「謝謝你告訴我。」
媽媽拿起兩隻襪子。一隻大，一隻小。「這隻是你的。這隻是妹妹的。」媽媽用手比愛心。一顆給大襪子。一顆給小襪子。「媽媽的心會長大喔。」
「愛不會變少。每個人都有。」咿咿呀呀，妹妹醒了。媽媽抱起妹妹。再張開手抱住{name}。一個大大的抱抱，給你們兩個。暖暖的，好舒服。
「妹妹的腳冷冷的。你可以幫忙嗎？」「我可以！」{name}拿起小襪子。拉呀拉，套呀套。哎呀，襪子滑掉了！小腳丫動來動去。
{name}再試一次。「妹妹，不要動喔。」慢慢地，輕輕地。先套腳趾頭，再拉過腳跟。一隻，穿好了！兩隻，也穿好了！妹妹笑了，咯咯咯。
「你是很棒的小幫手。」媽媽說。妹妹又睡著了。媽媽和{name}窩在沙發上。一起看繪本，只有兩個人。大襪子，小襪子，排在一起。兩顆心，都滿滿的。
en: Mom is folding laundry. Baby sister sleeps in her crib. The basket is full of socks. {name} finds a tiny pair. They are baby sister's socks. So small! Smaller than {name}'s hand!
{name} gets {his} own sock. {name} sets it by the tiny one. Big sock, tiny sock. Big, tiny. Everyone hugs the baby now. {name} looks for a long time. Inside feels a little cloudy.
{name} walks over to Mom. Tug, tug on her sleeve. "Mommy, Mommy?" {name} asks softly. "Do you still love me?" Mom stops folding. She gently pats {name}'s head. "Thank you for telling me."

Mom holds up two socks. One big, one tiny. "This one is yours. This one is Sister's." She makes a heart with her hands. One heart for the big sock. One heart for the tiny sock. "My heart grows bigger."
"Love never gets smaller. There's enough for everyone." Ah-goo! Baby sister wakes up. Mom picks her up. Then she opens her arm for {name}. One big hug for both. Snug and warm.
"Sister's toes are chilly. Can you help?" "I can help!" says {name}. {name} picks up a tiny sock. Pull, pull. Tug, tug. Oops! The sock slips off. Wiggle, wiggle go the toes.
{name} tries again. "Hold still, little one." Slowly, gently. Toes go in first. Then over the heel. One sock on! Two socks on! Baby sister giggles. Hee, hee, hee!

"You are a wonderful helper," says Mom. Soon baby sister naps again. Mom and {name} cuddle on the couch. They share a book, just the two of them. Big sock, tiny sock, side by side. Two hearts, both full.

questions: {name}心裡悶悶的時候，{he}做了什麼？媽媽怎麼回答？
如果你也覺得大家都在看寶寶，你會怎麼告訴爸爸媽媽？
你覺得當哥哥姐姐，可以幫寶寶做哪些事？
zh.tip: 這星期每天留五分鐘「只有我們兩個」的時間，一起看書或抱抱，並對孩子說：「你想要媽媽陪的時候，隨時都可以告訴我。」

questions: What did {name} do when {he} felt cloudy inside? What did Mom say?
If you feel like everyone is looking at the baby, how could you tell Mom or Dad?
What special jobs can a big sibling do to help a baby?
en.tip: Each day this week, set aside five minutes of "just us" time to read or cuddle, and tell your child: "Whenever you want time with me, you can always tell me."

zh: 清晨的雲霧還纏在山腰，{name}跟著巡山員林姊姊踏上高山步道。出發前，林姊姊在{his}背包上繫了一顆銅色熊鈴，每走一步就「叮鈴、叮鈴」響個不停。{name}忍不住嘟起嘴：「這麼吵，熊早就跑得無影無蹤了，我們還找得到牠嗎？」林姊姊只是眨眨眼：「誰說我們一定要親眼看到熊，才算找到牠？」
走進一片鐵杉林，林姊姊忽然停下腳步，指著一棵粗壯的樹幹。樹皮上刻著好幾道深深的刮痕，從大人腰際一路往上延伸，像被一把巨大的梳子梳過。「這是爪痕，臺灣黑熊爬樹找果子時留下的簽名。」{name}伸出手掌在旁邊比了比，每道痕跡都比手指還寬，看得{him}目不轉睛，心臟怦怦直跳。
再往上爬，林姊姊蹲在落葉堆旁，撿起一顆被咬掉一半的野生獼猴桃。果肉還濕濕亮亮的，邊緣留著一排整齊的齒痕。「很新鮮，大概是今天早上的點心。」她說。{name}嚥了嚥口水，下意識地晃了晃背包，熊鈴清脆地叮噹作響。奇怪的是，這一次{name}竟覺得那聲音一點也不惱人，反而有點像在替自己壯膽。
轉過一個彎，小徑變得泥濘。「快看！」{name}壓低聲音喊道。泥巴上印著一個寬寬的腳印，前端排著五個圓圓的趾印，趾尖還有細細的爪痕。林姊姊拿出捲尺量了量：「十五公分，是隻成年黑熊。」{name}把手掌懸在腳印上方比一比，忍不住咯咯笑：「要是跟牠擊掌，我一定會被拍到山的另一頭去！」
林姊姊收起捲尺，輕聲說：「黑熊其實很害羞。牠聽見鈴聲，就會先悄悄躲開。我們不是去偷看牠，而是有禮貌地告訴牠：『我們來了，請慢慢走。』」{name}低頭看看背包上的熊鈴，恍然大悟，故意邁開大步向前，讓鈴聲叮叮噹噹地響徹山林，像在跟整座森林熱情地打招呼。
中午時分，他們爬上一道視野開闊的稜線。林姊姊遞來望遠鏡，指向對面山谷的草坡。一個黑影正慢吞吞地橫越草地，胸前隱約閃著一彎白色的月牙。「是臺灣黑熊！」{name}屏住呼吸。就在這時，草叢裡又滾出一團更小的黑毛球，跌跌撞撞地追在後面。
「熊媽媽帶著寶寶出門散步呢。」林姊姊笑得眼睛都瞇成一條線。母子倆一前一後，慢悠悠地鑽進遠方的樹林，消失不見。{name}放下望遠鏡，久久捨不得移開視線。下山的路上，{name}走在前頭，熊鈴一路叮鈴叮鈴。「這是我們的暗號，」{he}得意地說，「告訴熊寶寶：別擔心，我們只是路過！」
en: Morning mist still clung to the mountainside as {name} set off up a high trail with Ranger Lin. Before they started, she tied a little brass bear bell to {his} backpack. Jingle, jingle, it went with every single step. {name} frowned. "With all this racket, any bear will be long gone! How will we ever find one?" Ranger Lin just winked. "Who says we have to see a bear to find it?"

In a grove of tall hemlocks, Ranger Lin stopped and pointed at a thick trunk. Deep scratches raked the bark, starting at grown-up waist height and climbing higher, as if a giant comb had been dragged up the tree. "Claw marks," she said. "A Formosan black bear signs its name like this when it climbs for fruit." {name} held up a hand beside them. Each groove was wider than a finger.

Farther up, Ranger Lin crouched by a pile of leaves and lifted a wild kiwi fruit with one half bitten clean away. The flesh still glistened, edged with a neat row of tooth marks. "Very fresh.
