zh: 星期六早上，{name}和媽媽來到水族館。媽媽在門口蹲下來，輕聲問：「如果看不到媽媽，要怎麼辦？」{name}大聲說：「站在原地，不要亂跑！」媽媽點點頭：「對，媽媽一定會回來找你。」{name}又說：「還要找戴名牌的工作人員幫忙。」
走進水族館，裡面藍藍的，好像在海底。小丑魚在海葵裡玩躲貓貓。一隻海馬把尾巴捲在海草上。媽媽問：「還記得媽媽的電話號碼嗎？」{name}像唱歌一樣，一個數字一個數字唸出來。媽媽開心地拍手：「全對！」
前面是一條長長的玻璃隧道。魚兒從頭頂游過去，好像在天上飛。忽然，一片好大的影子滑了過來。「哇！是鬼蝠魟！」牠的大鰭慢慢拍動，像在海裡跳舞。{name}看得張大眼睛，一動也不動，好久好久。
鬼蝠魟慢慢游遠了。{name}轉過頭說：「媽媽，你看！」可是，旁邊沒有媽媽。只有好多不認識的人走來走去。{name}的心咚咚咚跳得好快。這時，{he}想起門口的約定。{name}深吸一口氣，雙腳站穩，不亂跑。
「媽媽會回來找我。」{name}小聲說。{name}仔細看看四周。就在幾步外，站著一位阿姨。她穿著藍色制服，胸前掛著名牌。名牌上寫著「林」。她正在跟一家人介紹海龜。
{name}走到阿姨身邊。「阿姨，我找不到媽媽。」林阿姨馬上蹲下來，溫柔地笑。「謝謝你告訴我。你記得媽媽的電話嗎？」{name}點點頭，把號碼一個一個說清楚。還說：「我媽媽叫陳美華。」
林阿姨拿起對講機呼叫。「陳美華小姐，您的孩子在玻璃隧道。」林阿姨一直陪在{name}旁邊。「鬼蝠魟很溫和，最愛吃浮游生物。那是小到看不見的小生物喔。」這時，那隻鬼蝠魟又游回來了。{name}笑著說：「牠也在陪我等！」
忽然，有人喊：「{name}！」媽媽快步走過來，給{name}一個大大的擁抱。「你站著等，還找對了人，好棒！」{name}緊緊抱住媽媽，心裡暖暖的。兩人一起向林阿姨說謝謝。然後手牽著手，看鬼蝠魟拍拍大鰭說再見。
en: On Saturday, {name} and Mom went to the aquarium. Mom knelt by the door. "What if you can't see me?" "I stop and stay right there!" said {name}. "Yes. I'll always come back for you." "And I find a helper with a name badge," {name} added.

Inside, everything glowed blue, like under the sea. Clownfish played hide-and-seek in the anemones. A seahorse curled its tail on the seaweed. "Remember my phone number?" Mom asked. {name} sang it, one number at a time. "All right!" Mom cheered.

Next came a long glass tunnel. Fish swam right over their heads. Then a giant shadow glided close. "Wow! A manta ray!" Its wide fins flapped slowly, like it was dancing. {name} stood very still and stared and stared.

The manta ray swam away. "Mom, look!" {name} said, turning around. But Mom wasn't there. Only strangers walked by. {name}'s heart went thump, thump, thump. Then {he} remembered the plan. {name} took a deep breath and stood still.

"Mom will come back for me," {name} whispered. {name} looked around carefully. Just a few steps away stood a woman in a blue uniform. A name badge on her shirt said "Lin." She was telling a family about sea turtles.

{name} stepped over to her. "Excuse me. I can't find my mom." Ms. Lin knelt down with a kind smile. "Thank you for telling me. Do you know Mom's phone number?" {name} nodded and said each number clearly. "My mom's name is Mei Chen."

Ms. Lin called on her radio. "Mei Chen, your child is in the glass tunnel." Ms. Lin stayed close to {name}. "Manta rays are gentle. They eat plankton, tiny creatures too small to see." Then the manta ray swam back. "It's waiting with me!" {name} giggled.

Then a voice called, "{name}!" Mom hurried over with a big, warm hug. "You stayed put and found the right helper. Wonderful!" {name} hugged Mom tight. They thanked Ms. Lin together. Then, hand in hand, they watched the manta ray flap goodbye.

questions: {name}看不到媽媽的時候，第一件事做了什麼？
如果你在很多人的地方找不到我，你可以找誰幫忙？
你可以把我的名字和電話說給我聽嗎？
zh.tip: 這週每天和孩子玩一次「電話號碼歌」，把爸媽的名字和電話編成小曲一起唱。出門前再快速練習一次「停下來、找名牌、說電話」。

questions: What was the first thing {name} did when Mom wasn't there?
If you couldn't find me in a busy place, who could you ask for help?
Can you tell me my name and phone number?
en.tip: This week, make up a little "phone number song" with your child and sing your name and number together once a day. Before outings, quickly practice: stop, find a badge, say the number.

zh: 公園裡有一個鞦韆。只有一個喔！{name}跑過去，坐上去。咻——飛高高！咻——飛低低！媽媽坐在旁邊的長椅上，笑咪咪地看著。
{name}盪了一下，又一下。「我還要！我還要！」旁邊站著一個小女孩，叫小米。小米抱著小熊，一直看著鞦韆。她的小嘴巴，扁扁的。
小米走過來，小小聲地問：「你盪完了，可以換我嗎？」{name}想了想。鞦韆好好玩。可是，小米也好想玩。「好！我們輪流！」
媽媽說：「我們來數數，每人盪二十下。」{name}開始盪。一、二、三……咻、咻、咻！小米幫忙數，數得好大聲。十八、十九、二十！
換小米了！{name}站在旁邊等。等待好難喔！{his}小腳一直跳呀跳。小米盪呀盪，{name}跟著數。一、二、三……十九、二十！
又換{name}了！真的會輪到耶！{name}笑嘻嘻地坐上去。小米說：「我幫你推！」小米輕輕推，一下、兩下。鞦韆搖呀搖，像一艘小船。
「換我推你！」{name}輕輕推小米。一個盪，一個推。小米咯咯笑，{name}嘻嘻笑。小熊也在搖頭晃腦。笑聲飛得好高，好高。
太陽變成橘色了。媽媽說：「該回家囉。」{name}和小米揮揮手。「明天再一起盪！」「好！我推你，你推我！」鞦韆輕輕晃，好像在說拜拜。
en: The park has one swing. Just one! {name} runs over and hops on. Whoosh, up high! Whoosh, down low! Mom smiles from the bench nearby.
{name} swings once, then again. "More! More!" A little girl named Mimi stands close by. She hugs her teddy bear. Her lip wobbles a bit.
Mimi steps up and asks softly, "Can I have a turn when you're done?" {name} thinks. The swing is so fun. But Mimi wants to swing too. "Okay! Let's take turns!"
Mom says, "Let's count. Twenty swings each." {name} starts to swing. One, two, three... whoosh, whoosh! Mimi counts out loud. Eighteen, nineteen, twenty!
Now it's Mimi's turn! {name} waits beside her. Waiting is hard! Little feet hop, hop, hop. {name} counts along. One, two, three... nineteen, twenty!
It's {name}'s turn again! It really came back! {name} climbs on, grinning. "I'll push you!" says Mimi. Gentle push, one, two. The swing rocks like a little boat.
"My turn to push!" {name} pushes Mimi gently. One swings, one pushes. Mimi giggles. {name} giggles too. Even Teddy seems to bounce. Their laughter floats up high.
The sun turns orange. Mom says, "Time to go home." {name} and Mimi wave. "Let's swing tomorrow!" "Yes! I push you, you push me!" The swing sways goodbye.

questions: 小米想玩鞦韆時，她是怎麼問{name}的？
等待輪到自己的時候，你會做什麼讓等待變容易？
{name}和小米一起推鞦韆時，為什麼笑得那麼開心？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子玩一個「數到二十換人」的遊戲，並一起練習說：「你玩完了，可以換我嗎？」

questions: How did Mimi ask {name} for a turn on the swing?
When you have to wait for your turn, what can you do to make waiting easier?
Why do you think {name} and Mimi laughed so much when they pushed each other?
en.tip: This week, play a "count to twenty, then switch" game with a toy, and practice saying together, "Can I have a turn when you're done?"

zh: 星期一早上，{name}背著書包走進教室。書包裡有一個新蠟筆盒，大大的，有四十八種顏色！{name}輕輕打開盒子。最中間有一支金色蠟筆，亮晶晶的，好像會發光。「這是我最寶貝的。」{name}小聲說。
林老師拍拍手說：「今天我們一起畫一面大壁畫，題目是美麗的早晨！」一張好長的白紙，貼在教室後面的牆上。大家都好興奮。{name}把蠟筆盒放在桌上，再把金色蠟筆收進口袋。{name}心想：「金色只給我用。」
小傑在紙的上面畫天空。他畫了白白的雲，又畫了一個圓圓的太陽。可是，他的盒子裡沒有金色。小傑拿起黃色試試看，又搖搖頭。「黃色不夠亮。」他嘆了一口氣。阿德看見{name}口袋裡的金色蠟筆，伸手就要拿。
「等一下！」小美拉住阿德。「不可以用搶的。要先問：『你用完，可以換我嗎？』」阿德紅著臉，點點頭說：「對不起。」小傑走到{name}旁邊，輕輕地問：「{name}，你用完的時候，可以換我用一下嗎？」
{name}摸摸口袋，心裡好糾結。金色是{his}寶貝。借出去，變短了怎麼辦？可是小傑的太陽，還是空空的，沒有顏色。{name}看看小傑期待的眼睛，深深吸一口氣，把金色蠟筆拿了出來。「給你，你先用。」
小傑小心地塗太陽。太陽變得金閃閃的，好像在微笑。「哇，好漂亮！」大家都圍過來看。阿德問：「小傑用完，可以換我嗎？」小美說：「我排在阿德後面。」大家排成一小排，一個接一個輪流。等待有點難，可是每個人都乖乖地等。
阿德畫了一條金色的小魚。小美畫了金色的花心。{name}站在旁邊，心裡有一點著急。「什麼時候輪到我呢？」最後，小美把蠟筆還給{name}，笑著說：「輪到你了，謝謝你！」{name}在紙的四個角落，畫上金色的星星和蝴蝶。
放學前，林老師退後一步看壁畫。整面牆亮亮的，好像在發光！金色的太陽，金色的魚，每個角落都有金色的星星。「這是大家一起畫的喔。」林老師說。{name}看看變短一點的金色蠟筆，又看看朋友們的笑臉。{he}的心裡，也暖暖的，亮亮的。
en: On Monday morning, {name} walked into class with a new crayon box. It was big, with forty-eight colors! {name} opened it gently. In the middle sat a gold crayon. It shimmered like sunshine. "This one is my treasure," {name} whispered.

Ms. Lin clapped her hands. "Today we will make a big mural together. It's called A Beautiful Morning!" A long sheet of white paper hung on the back wall. Everyone cheered. {name} put the box on the table. Then the gold crayon went into {his} pocket. "Only I will use gold," {name} thought.

Jay drew the sky at the top. He colored fluffy clouds and a round sun. But Jay had no gold crayon. He tried yellow and shook his head. "Yellow isn't bright enough," he sighed. Leo spotted the gold crayon in {name}'s pocket. He reached out to grab it.

"Wait!" said Mia, holding Leo's arm. "Don't grab. Ask first. Say, 'Can I have a turn when you're done?'" Leo's cheeks turned pink. "Sorry," he said. Jay walked over to {name}. "{name}, can I have a turn when you're done?" he asked softly.

{name} touched {his} pocket and felt torn. The gold crayon was so special. What if it got short? But Jay's sun was still pale and empty. {name} looked at Jay's hopeful eyes. Then {name} took a deep breath and held out the crayon. "Here. You go first."

Jay carefully colored the sun. It glowed and seemed to smile! "Wow, so pretty!" everyone said, crowding close. Leo asked, "Can I have a turn after Jay?" "I'll go after Leo," said Mia. The children made a little line. Waiting was hard, but everyone waited nicely.

Leo drew a little gold fish. Mia drew gold centers in her flowers. {name} stood nearby, feeling a bit wiggly. "When will it be my turn?" At last, Mia handed the crayon back. "Your turn! Thank you!" she said. {name} drew gold stars and butterflies in all four corners.

Before home time, Ms. Lin stepped back to look. The whole wall glowed! A gold sun, a gold fish, and gold stars in every corner. "We made this together," said Ms. Lin. {name} looked at the gold crayon, a little shorter now. Then {name} looked at all the smiling friends. {name}'s heart felt warm and bright too.

questions: 小傑想用金色蠟筆的時候，他是怎麼問{name}的？
{name}等著輪到自己的時候，心裡有什麼感覺？你等待的時候會怎麼做？
大家一起用金色蠟筆以後，壁畫變得怎麼樣？你有沒有和朋友分享，結果玩得更開心的經驗？
zh.tip: 這週玩玩具或畫畫時，和孩子一起練習說「你用完，可以換我嗎？」，並用計時器輪流，每次輪到時開心地說「換你了！」。

questions: How did Jay ask {name} for the gold crayon?
How did {name} feel while waiting for a turn? What can you do while you wait?
What happened to the mural when everyone shared the gold crayon? When has sharing made playing more fun for you?
en.tip: This week, during play or drawing time, practice saying "Can I have a turn when you're done?" together, and use a timer to take turns, cheering "Your turn!" each time.

zh: 早上，太陽暖暖的。{name}和媽媽去麵包店。叮咚！門開了。哇，好香好香呀！架子上有圓圓的麵包。有彎彎的麵包。還有可愛的小熊麵包！
{name}踮起腳尖。小手指一指。「那個！」麵包師傅王伯伯笑一笑。王伯伯等一等。王伯伯沒有動。{name}眨眨眼。咦？怎麼了呢？
媽媽彎下腰。媽媽小小聲說：「要說魔法話喔。」魔法話？{name}想一想。再想一想。啊！想起來了！「請給我小熊麵包。」
王伯伯的臉亮起來。「好呀好呀！」王伯伯拿出小熊麵包。放進紙袋裡。沙沙沙。{name}接過紙袋。「謝謝王伯伯！」王伯伯笑得眼睛彎彎。
走出麵包店，街上好熱鬧。{name}牽著媽媽的手。走在人行道上。咚！{name}撞到一位奶奶。奶奶的橘子掉了。咕嚕咕嚕，滾滿地。
{name}停下來。「對不起，奶奶。」{name}和媽媽一起撿。一顆，兩顆，三顆。放回奶奶的籃子裡。奶奶笑咪咪。「謝謝你，好貼心喔！」
再來是花店。{name}想聞聞花。「請問，我可以聞嗎？」花店阿姨點點頭。「可以喔！」嗅嗅嗅，好香呀！「謝謝阿姨！」阿姨送{him}一朵小黃花。
回到家，{name}好開心。魔法話真的有用耶！請，謝謝，對不起。今天大家都笑了。{name}心裡也暖暖的。一起吃小熊麵包吧！「媽媽請吃！」「謝謝你！」啊嗚一口，好好吃！
en: The morning sun is warm. {name} and Mom walk to the bakery. Ding-dong! The door opens. Mmm, what a yummy smell! Round buns. Curly buns. And little bear buns!
{name} stands on tiptoe. A little finger points. "That one!" Mr. Wang the baker smiles. He waits. He does not move. {name} blinks. Hmm? What is wrong?
Mom bends down low. She whispers, "Try the magic words." Magic words? {name} thinks and thinks. Oh! {name} remembers! "A bear bun, please!"
Mr. Wang's face lights up. "Yes, yes!" He picks a bear bun. Into a paper bag it goes. Crinkle, crinkle. {name} holds the bag. "Thank you, Mr. Wang!" His eyes crinkle too.
Outside, the street is busy. {name} holds Mom's hand. They walk on the sidewalk. Bump! {name} bumps into a grandma. Her oranges fall. Roll, roll, roll!
{name} stops. "Sorry, Grandma!" {name} and Mom pick them up. One, two, three oranges. Back into her basket. Grandma smiles big. "Thank you, sweetie!"
Next comes the flower shop. {name} wants a sniff. "May I smell, please?" The flower lady nods. "Sure!" Sniff, sniff. So sweet! "Thank you!" She gives {him} a yellow flower.

Back home, {name} feels so happy. The magic words really work! Please. Thank you. Sorry. Today, everyone smiled. {name} feels warm inside. Time to share the bear bun! "Mom, have some, please!" "Thank you!" Chomp! Yummy!

questions: {name}說了「請」以後，王伯伯有什麼表情？
{name}撞到奶奶的時候，說了什麼？又做了什麼？
今天有誰幫助你呢？你可以跟他說什麼？
zh.tip: 這個星期，吃飯或拿東西時，全家一起玩「魔法話」遊戲：說「請」和「謝謝」就拍拍手。不小心碰到人時，練習說「對不起」，再一起想辦法幫忙。

questions: How did Mr. Wang look when {name} said "please"?
What did {name} say and do after bumping into Grandma?
Who helped you today? What could you say to them?
en.tip: This week, play a "magic words" game at meals: clap together whenever someone says "please" or "thank you." If someone bumps another by accident, practice saying "sorry" and find a way to help together.

zh: 晚上到了。燈關了。房間黑黑的。{name}躺在床上。咦？房間好奇怪。椅子像大石頭。窗簾輕輕晃。{name}抱緊小熊。「媽媽！」{name}輕輕喊。
媽媽馬上來了。「媽媽在這裡。」媽媽坐在床邊。「有點怕，對嗎？」「沒關係喔。」媽媽打開燈。看，椅子還是椅子。書還是書。小熊也還在。媽媽關上燈。「東西都還在。」「燈只是在休息。」
呼——呼——什麼聲音？「是風在唱歌。」滴答，滴答。「是時鐘在走路。」嘩啦，嘩啦。「是爸爸在洗碗。」{name}笑了。聲音都是好朋友。
「來做發光罐吧！」媽媽拿來空罐子。還有一盞小夜燈。還有好多紙星星。{name}把星星貼上去。貼一顆，貼兩顆。貼三顆，亮晶晶。
小夜燈放進罐子。啪！燈亮了。暖暖的光。黃黃的光。光從罐子跑出來。牆上有好多影子。{name}睜大眼睛看。
媽媽舉起雙手。牆上跳出一隻兔子！長長的耳朵。跳呀跳，跳呀跳。{name}也舉起{his}小手。牆上出現小船。搖呀搖，搖呀搖。兔子跳上小船。
「媽媽就在隔壁。」「叫一聲，我就來。」媽媽親親{name}。{name}抱著小熊。發光罐亮亮的。房間靜靜的。窗外的風輕輕吹。
{name}數一數影子。一隻兔子。一艘小船。一顆星星，兩顆星星。三顆星星……眼睛慢慢閉上了。小熊陪著{name}。發光罐守著夜晚。晚安，{name}。
en: Night came. The light went off. The room was dark. {name} lay in bed. Hmm, the room felt strange. The chair looked like a big rock. The curtains swayed softly. {name} hugged Teddy tight. "Mommy!" {name} called softly.

Mom came right away. "I'm here," Mom said. She sat on the bed. "A little scared? That's okay." Mom turned on the light. The chair was still a chair. The book was still a book. Teddy was there too. Mom turned off the light. "Everything is still here. The light is just resting."
Whoo, whoo. What was that? "That's the wind singing." Tick, tock. "That's the clock walking." Splash, splash. "That's Daddy washing dishes." {name} smiled. The sounds were friends.
"Let's make a glow jar!" said Mom. She brought an empty jar. She brought a little night light. She brought paper stars too. {name} stuck stars on the jar. One star, two stars. Three stars, so bright.
The night light went into the jar. Click! It glowed. Warm light. Soft yellow light. The light spilled out of the jar. Shadows danced on the wall. {name} watched with wide eyes.
Mom raised her hands. A rabbit hopped on the wall! Long, long ears. Hop, hop, hop. {name} raised {his} hands too. A little boat appeared. Rock, rock, rock. The rabbit hopped into the boat.
"I'm right next door," said Mom. "Call me, and I'll come." Mom kissed {name}. {name} cuddled Teddy. The glow jar shone softly. The room was quiet. The wind whispered outside.
{name} counted the shadows. One rabbit. One little boat. One star, two stars. Three stars... Eyes closed slowly. Teddy stayed close. The glow jar kept watch. Goodnight, {name}.

questions: 燈關掉以後，房間裡的椅子和小熊還在嗎？
{name}聽到呼呼、滴答的聲音時，媽媽說那是什麼？
如果你晚上覺得怕怕的，你可以怎麼做？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈前，和孩子一起說出房間裡的三樣東西，關燈後再輕聲說「它們都還在」。也可以用手電筒在牆上玩一分鐘手影遊戲。

questions: When the light went off, were the chair and Teddy still there?
When {name} heard whoo and tick-tock, what did Mom say they were?
If you feel scared at night, what could you do?
en.tip: Tonight, before lights out, name three things in the room together, then whisper "they're all still here" in the dark. You can also play a one-minute hand shadow game with a flashlight.

zh: 晚飯後，爸爸說：「我們去散步吧！」{name}跟著爸爸媽媽，走到村子外的小路。{name}抱著小兔布布，手裡拿著小手電筒。路燈一盞一盞變少了。最後一盞燈也不見了。哇，這裡好黑喔！比{his}房間關燈還要黑。
{name}停下腳步，小聲說：「爸爸，我有點怕。」爸爸蹲下來，握住{his}小手。「怕也沒關係，爸爸就在這裡。」媽媽摸摸布布的耳朵。「布布也陪著你喔。」{name}把布布抱得更緊。手電筒照出一圈小小的光。他們慢慢往前走。
草叢裡忽然傳來聲音。「呱呱、呱呱！」{name}嚇了一跳。「那是什麼？」爸爸笑著說：「是青蛙在唱歌。牠們晚上最愛聊天。」接著又傳來「唧唧、唧唧」。媽媽說：「那是蟋蟀，牠在搓翅膀呢。」{name}側耳聽一聽。原來夜晚這麼熱鬧！
遠遠的樹上，傳來「呼——呼——」。{name}拉拉爸爸的衣角。「爸爸，誰在樹上？」爸爸輕聲說：「是貓頭鷹。牠在跟家人說晚安。」{name}也學著喊：「呼——呼——」媽媽笑了，布布好像也在笑。{name}的心，慢慢不跳那麼快了。
爸爸問：「要不要玩一個勇敢遊戲？我們把手電筒關掉，數到十。」{name}想了想，有點緊張。「爸爸會一直牽著我嗎？」「當然，一秒都不放開。」{name}點點頭，按下開關。喀！四周全黑了。
「一、二、三……」{name}和爸爸一起數。{name}閉著眼睛，抱緊布布。「四、五、六……」青蛙還在唱歌。爸爸的手還是暖暖的。「七、八、九……」媽媽輕輕說：「小路還在，大樹也還在喔。只是燈去休息了。」「十！」
{name}慢慢張開眼睛，抬頭一看。哇！天上滿滿都是星星。一顆一顆閃呀閃，像撒了一地的糖。草叢裡，還飛出點點小綠光。「那是什麼？」{name}睜大眼睛問。媽媽說：「是螢火蟲！牠們提著小燈籠，出來散步了。」
一隻螢火蟲飛到布布的耳朵旁。{name}笑出聲來。「原來黑黑的地方，藏著這麼多寶貝！」回家的路上，{name}一手牽爸爸，一手抱布布。手電筒一直沒有打開。星星和螢火蟲，一路陪著{him}回家。
en: After dinner, Dad said, "Let's take a walk!" {name} went with Mom and Dad down a country path. {name} hugged Bobo the bunny and held a small flashlight. Soon the last streetlight was gone. Wow, it was so dark! It was darker than {his} bedroom at night.

{name} stopped. "Dad, I'm a little scared." Dad knelt and took {his} hand. "It's okay to feel scared. I'm right here." Mom patted Bobo's ears. "Bobo is with you too." {name} held Bobo tighter. The flashlight made a small circle of light. Slowly, they walked on.

Suddenly, the grass went "Ribbit, ribbit!" {name} jumped. "What's that?" Dad smiled. "A frog singing. Frogs love to chat at night." Then came "Chirp, chirp." "That's a cricket rubbing its wings," said Mom. {name} listened closely. The night was full of little voices!

From a far-off tree came "Hoo, hoo." {name} tugged Dad's sleeve. "Who's up in the tree?" "An owl," Dad said softly. "It's saying goodnight to its family." {name} called back, "Hoo, hoo!" Mom laughed. Even Bobo seemed to smile. {name}'s heart slowed down, little by little.

"Want to play a brave game?" Dad asked. "Let's turn off the flashlight and count to ten." {name} felt a bit nervous. "Will you hold my hand the whole time?" "Of course. I won't let go for a second." {name} nodded and pressed the switch. Click! Everything went dark.

"One, two, three..." {name} and Dad counted together. {name} closed {his} eyes and hugged Bobo. "Four, five, six..." The frogs still sang. Dad's hand was still warm. "Seven, eight, nine..." Mom whispered, "The path and the trees are still here. The lights are just resting." "Ten!"

{name} opened {his} eyes and looked up. Wow! The sky was full of twinkling stars, like sprinkled sugar. Then tiny green lights floated up from the grass. "What are those?" {name} asked with wide eyes. "Fireflies!" said Mom. "They carry little lanterns on their night walk."

One firefly flew close to Bobo's ear. {name} giggled. "The dark hides so many treasures!" On the way home, {name} held Dad's hand and hugged Bobo. The flashlight stayed switched off. The stars and fireflies lit the way home.

questions: {name}覺得害怕的時候，做了什麼事讓自己好一點？
燈關掉以後，小路和大樹還在嗎？你房間關燈後，有哪些東西還在？
晚上如果聽到奇怪的聲音，你可以怎麼做？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈前，和孩子一起玩「勇敢十秒鐘」：牽著手關燈數到十，再一起說出房間裡還在的三樣東西。

questions: What did {name} do to feel better when {he} felt scared?
When the light was off, were the path and trees still there? What stays in your room when the lights go off?
What could you do if you hear a strange sound at night?
en.tip: Tonight before bed, play "Ten Brave Seconds": hold hands, switch off the light, count to ten, then name three things still in the room together.

zh: 星期五晚上，媽媽要出差兩天。爸爸會在家陪{name}。媽媽帶{name}走到陽台。那裡有番茄、薄荷，還有一小盆九層塔。「週末要記得澆水喔。」媽媽說。{name}用力點頭：「我答應妳！」媽媽笑著，輕輕抱了抱{him}。
星期六，太陽又大又亮。爸爸陪{name}在客廳蓋積木城堡。城堡越蓋越高，還有一座小塔。下午，{name}畫了一隻會飛的大象。晚上，爸爸講了一個好長的故事。{name}笑著笑著就睡著了。陽台上的小盆栽，靜靜等了一整天。
星期天早上，{name}到陽台看雲。咦？九層塔怎麼了？它的葉子垂下來，軟軟的。看起來好像累壞了。土摸起來好乾，一點也不濕。{name}的心咚了一下。「糟糕，我忘記澆水了！」這時，門口傳來鑰匙聲。媽媽回來了！
媽媽放下包包，走到陽台。「哎呀，九層塔怎麼垂頭了？」{name}的臉熱熱的。「是太陽太大了。」這句話差點說出口。可是，{name}想起星期五的約定。{his}小手緊緊握在一起。
{name}深深吸了一口氣。「媽媽，不是太陽。」{name}小小聲說。「是我玩得太開心，忘記澆水了。」說完，{he}低下頭，心跳得好快。媽媽蹲下來，摸摸{name}的頭。「謝謝你告訴我真的發生什麼事。這要很勇敢呢。」
「現在我知道了，就能一起幫它。」媽媽說。九層塔需要喝水，也需要休息。{name}提著小澆水壺，慢慢倒水。咕嚕咕嚕，水滲進土裡了。媽媽把盆栽搬到陰涼的地方。「讓它躲躲太陽，我們等一等。」
到了傍晚，陽光變得溫柔了。{name}跑去陽台看。九層塔的葉子，一片一片挺起來了！聞起來香香的，好清新。{name}開心得跳起來。媽媽笑著說：「你跟我說實話，我好放心。以後你說的話，我都相信。」
吃完晚餐，{name}拿出紙和蠟筆。{he}畫了一張澆水表，上面有七個格子。每個格子裡，都有一顆小水滴。「澆完水，我就畫一個笑臉。」{name}把表貼在陽台門邊。月亮出來了，九層塔好好休息。{name}也甜甜地睡著了。
en: On Friday night, Mom had to go on a work trip. Dad would stay home with {name}. Mom showed {name} the balcony plants. There were tomatoes, mint, and a little pot of basil. "Please water them this weekend," Mom said. "I promise!" said {name}. Mom gave {him} a warm hug.

On Saturday, the sun was big and bright. {name} and Dad built a block castle. It grew taller and taller, with a tiny tower. Later, {name} drew a flying elephant. At night, Dad read a long story. {name} fell asleep smiling. Out on the balcony, the plants waited all day.

On Sunday morning, {name} went to the balcony to watch the clouds. Oh no! The basil was drooping. Its leaves hung down, soft and tired. The soil felt dry and dusty. {name}'s heart went thump. "I forgot to water!" Just then, keys jingled at the door. Mom was home!

Mom put down her bag and came to the balcony. "Oh dear, why is the basil drooping?" {name}'s cheeks felt warm. "The hot sun did it." The words were almost out. But {name} remembered Friday's promise. {his} fingers squeezed together tight.

{name} took a deep breath. "Mom, it wasn't the sun," {name} said softly. "I played all day and forgot to water." Then {he} looked down, heart beating fast. Mom knelt and patted {name} on the head. "Thank you for telling me what really happened. That was brave."

"Now that I know, we can help it together," Mom said. The basil needed water and a rest. {name} held the little watering can and poured slowly. Glug, glug, the water sank into the soil. Mom moved the pot into the cool shade. "Now we wait a little," she said.

By evening, the sunshine felt gentle. {name} ran to check. The basil leaves were standing up again, one by one! They smelled sweet and fresh. {name} jumped for joy. Mom smiled. "You told me the truth, so I feel calm. When you tell me something, I can believe you."

After dinner, {name} got paper and crayons. {he} drew a watering chart with seven boxes. Each box had a little water drop. "After I water, I'll draw a smiley face," said {name}. The chart went up by the balcony door. The moon came out, and the basil rested. {name} fell sweetly asleep, too.

questions: {name}差點說是太陽害的，後來為什麼決定說實話？
媽媽知道真正發生的事以後，媽媽和{name}一起做了什麼來幫九層塔？
如果你不小心忘記一件答應過的事，你會怎麼告訴大人？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子一起做一張小小的任務表，例如澆花或收玩具，完成後畫一個笑臉。當孩子主動說出小錯誤時，先說「謝謝你告訴我」，再一起想辦法。

questions: {name} almost said the sun did it. Why do you think {name} told the truth instead?
After Mom knew what really happened, what did they do together to help the basil?
If you forgot something you promised, how would you tell a grown-up?
en.tip: This week, make a tiny task chart with your child, like watering a plant or tidying toys, and add a smiley face when it's done. When your child admits a small mistake, start with "Thank you for telling me," then fix it together.

zh: 星期六下午，{name}和爺爺一起走到街角的小雜貨店。爺爺把一張一百元交給{name}，笑著說：「你自己進去買一瓶牛奶，我就在門口等你。」{name}點點頭，推開叮噹響的玻璃門，心裡有一點緊張，也有一點驕傲。
店裡的陳阿姨正忙著，電話響個不停，還有客人在問郵票放在哪裡。{name}把牛奶放上櫃檯，遞出一百元。陳阿姨一邊講電話，一邊很快地把零錢放進{name}的手心。走出店門，{name}低頭一數，咦？牛奶三十五元，應該找六十五元，手上卻多了一枚亮晶晶的五十元硬幣。
{name}握著那枚硬幣，腦袋裡突然冒出好多畫面：一大支彩色棒棒糖、一包閃亮的貼紙卡，還有冰涼的布丁。{he}把硬幣悄悄放進口袋，跟著爺爺往前走。可是才走幾步，口袋好像變得好重好重，重到{name}的腳步都慢了下來。
{name}想起陳阿姨每天晚上關店前，都會坐在櫃檯後面，一枚一枚數著抽屜裡的錢。如果今天少了五十元，陳阿姨一定會皺起眉頭，數了一遍又一遍，怎麼數都不對。想到這裡，{name}的心像被輕輕捏了一下。
可是，要說出來好難。如果大家以為是故意拿走的呢？{name}吸了一口氣，拉拉爺爺的袖子，小聲地說：「爺爺，阿姨多找我五十元，我剛剛……本來想拿去買糖果。」爺爺停下腳步，蹲下來握住{his}手：「謝謝你告訴我。走，我們一起回去。」
爺爺牽著{name}，沿著人行道走回雜貨店。玻璃門又叮噹一響。{name}把五十元放在櫃檯上，聲音有點抖：「陳阿姨，你剛剛多找我這個。我一出門就發現了，可是差一點就把它留下來了。」爺爺在旁邊輕輕拍了拍{his}肩膀。
陳阿姨眼睛一亮，露出暖暖的笑容。「謝謝你！我跟你說一個故事。很多年前，也有一個小客人把多找的錢送回來。後來那個孩子長大了，就是隔壁麵包店的林叔叔。現在我出遠門的時候，都放心把店裡的鑰匙交給林叔叔保管喔！」
陳阿姨把硬幣收進抽屜，眨眨眼說：「下次我會數慢一點。而且我知道，找錢給你，我可以很放心。」回家的路上，夕陽把街道照得金黃。{name}的口袋輕輕的，腳步也輕輕的，牽著爺爺的手，一路蹦蹦跳跳。
en: On Saturday afternoon, {name} and Grandpa walked to the little corner shop on their street. Grandpa handed {name} a hundred-dollar bill. "Go in and buy a bottle of milk on your own," he said with a smile. "I'll wait right here by the door." {name} pushed open the jingly glass door, feeling a little nervous and a little proud.

Inside, Auntie Chen was very busy. The phone kept ringing, and a customer was asking where the stamps were. {name} put the milk on the counter and paid. Still talking on the phone, Auntie Chen quickly dropped the change into {his} hand. Outside, {name} counted it. The milk cost thirty-five, so the change should be sixty-five. But there was an extra shiny fifty-dollar coin!

{name} held the coin tight, and pictures popped into {his} head: a giant rainbow lollipop, a pack of sparkly sticker cards, a cold, wobbly pudding. {name} slipped the coin into a pocket and started walking with Grandpa. But after a few steps, the pocket felt heavy, so heavy that {his} feet began to slow down.

{name} remembered that every night before closing, Auntie Chen sat behind the counter and counted the money in the drawer, coin by coin. If fifty dollars were missing tonight, she would frown and count again and again, and it would never come out right. Thinking about it gave {name} a small squeeze inside.

But saying something felt hard. What if Auntie Chen thought it was taken on purpose? {name} took a deep breath and tugged Grandpa's sleeve. "Grandpa," {he} whispered, "Auntie gave me fifty extra, and I almost kept it for candy." Grandpa stopped and knelt down, holding {his} hand. "Thank you for telling me. Come on, let's go back together."

Holding hands, Grandpa and {name} walked back along the sidewalk to the shop. The glass door jingled again. {name} set the coin on the counter, voice a little shaky. "Auntie Chen, you gave me this by mistake. I noticed right away, but I almost kept it." Grandpa gave {his} shoulder a gentle pat.

Auntie Chen's eyes lit up, and she gave a warm smile. "Thank you! Let me tell you a story. Many years ago, another young customer brought back extra change. That child grew up to be Mr. Lin, who runs the bakery next door. Now, whenever I go away, I trust Mr. Lin to keep my shop key safe!"

Auntie Chen put the coin in the drawer and winked. "Next time I'll count more slowly. And I know I can always trust you with my change." On the way home, the setting sun turned the street golden. {name}'s pocket felt light, {his} steps felt light, and {he} skipped all the way home, holding Grandpa's hand.

questions: {name}發現多了五十元的時候，心裡在想什麼？後來為什麼決定說出來？
{name}告訴爺爺實話以後，爺爺是怎麼幫忙的？
陳阿姨為什麼會放心把鑰匙交給林叔叔？你覺得說實話會讓別人怎麼看你？
zh.tip: 這週試試「說實話不罵人」的約定：孩子主動說出小錯誤時，先說一句「謝謝你告訴我」，再一起想辦法解決。

questions: What was {name} thinking when {he} found the extra coin? Why did {he} decide to speak up?
After {name} told Grandpa the truth, how did Grandpa help?
Why does Auntie Chen trust Mr. Lin with her key? How do you think telling the truth changes how people see you?
en.tip: This week, try a "truth-telling promise": whenever your child owns up to a small mistake, first say "Thank you for telling me," then work out a fix together.

zh: 星期三下午，美術社的教室裡飄著蠟筆和水彩的味道。新來的米拉安靜地坐在角落，低著頭，一筆一筆在紙上點著小圓點。藍的、黃的、綠的，密密麻麻，像一場停不下來的彩色小雨。{name}偷偷看了一眼，心裡好奇極了。
「哈哈，她在畫芝麻嗎？」阿凱指著米拉的紙大笑。小凡也跟著起鬨：「點點怪！點點怪！」旁邊好幾個人笑得前俯後仰，差點從椅子上滑下來。米拉的耳朵紅了，畫筆停在半空中，慢慢把畫紙往懷裡藏。
{name}的心怦怦跳。好想大聲說「不要再笑了」，可是喉嚨像被膠水黏住，一個字也擠不出來。阿凱他們人多勢眾，{name}只有一個人。不過，{name}想到一件小小的、自己做得到的事。
{name}拿起畫具，走到角落，在米拉旁邊坐下。「我可以坐這裡嗎？妳畫的是什麼呀？」米拉愣了一下，小聲說：「你退後三步再看看。」{name}半信半疑地往後退，一步、兩步、三步。
那些小點點忽然像手牽著手，變成一座金色的燈塔，海浪在月光下閃閃發亮！「哇，太厲害了！」{name}驚訝得張大了嘴巴。米拉的嘴角終於翹起一點點：「這是我以前家旁邊的燈塔。」
下課前，阿凱又在米拉的新畫上寫了一個大大的「怪」字。{name}深吸一口氣，走到林老師身邊：「老師，有人一直笑米拉的畫，還在上面亂寫。」這樣算告狀嗎？林老師蹲下來說：「謝謝你告訴我，這是在找人幫忙，不是告狀。米拉一點錯也沒有。」
隔週，林老師請大家圍成一圈，一起想美術社的約定。「看不懂的畫，先問問看。」「不拿別人的畫開玩笑。」「有人難過，就坐到他旁邊。」{name}舉手說：「有人被欺負，就去找大人幫忙。」大家把約定寫在海報上，每個人都簽了名。
米拉把燈塔的畫貼在教室後面。阿凱站得遠遠的，看了好久，終於小聲說：「對不起，原來點點這麼厲害。妳可以教我嗎？」米拉笑了，笑得像燈塔一樣亮。{name}在旁邊拿起畫筆，點下第一個彩色的小圓點。
en: On Wednesday afternoon, the art club room smelled of crayons and paint. Mila, the new student, sat quietly in the corner, dabbing tiny dots onto her paper. Blue, yellow, green, hundreds of them, like a rainbow drizzle that wouldn't stop. {name} peeked over, very curious.

"Ha! Is she drawing sesame seeds?" Kai pointed and laughed. Fan joined in. "Dotty! Dotty!" A few others giggled so hard they nearly slid off their stools. Mila's ears turned pink. Her brush froze in midair, and she slowly tucked the paper under her arm.

{name}'s heart thumped. The words "Stop laughing!" wanted to burst out, but they stuck in {his} throat like glue. Kai and Fan had a whole crowd around them, and {name} was just one kid. Still, there was one small thing {name} could do.

{name} gathered up {his} paints, walked to the corner, and sat right beside Mila. "Can I sit here? What are you painting?" Mila blinked in surprise. "Try stepping back three steps," she whispered. Not quite sure, {name} backed away: one, two, three.

Suddenly the dots seemed to hold hands and become a golden lighthouse, with waves shimmering under the moon! "Wow, that's amazing!" {name} gasped. The corner of Mila's mouth lifted, just a little. "It's the lighthouse near my old home."

Before club ended, Kai scribbled "WEIRD" across Mila's new painting. {name} took a deep breath and went to Ms. Lin. "Some kids keep laughing at Mila's pictures, and now they wrote on one." Was that tattling? Ms. Lin knelt down. "Thank you for telling me. That's getting help, not tattling. And Mila did nothing wrong."

The next week, Ms. Lin gathered everyone in a circle to make club promises. "If you don't understand a picture, ask about it." "No jokes about other people's art." "If someone looks sad, sit with them." {name} raised a hand. "If someone is being picked on, tell a grown-up." Everyone signed the big poster.

Mila hung her lighthouse on the back wall. Kai stared at it from far away for a long time. At last he mumbled, "Sorry. Your dots are really cool. Could you teach me?" Mila smiled, bright as a lighthouse. Beside her, {name} picked up a brush and dabbed a first colorful dot.

questions: 當大家在笑米拉的時候，{name}做了哪些事來幫忙？
{name}擔心告訴老師是在告狀，你覺得告狀和找人幫忙有什麼不一樣？
如果你看到有人被取笑，你可以坐到誰旁邊、去告訴哪位大人？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子一起練習一句話：「老師，我需要幫忙，有人一直在欺負別人。」並一起列出在學校和家裡可以求助的三位大人。

questions: When everyone was laughing at Mila, what did {name} do to help?
{name} worried that telling the teacher was tattling. How is tattling different from getting help?
If you saw someone being teased, who could you sit beside, and which grown-up could you tell?
en.tip: This week, practice one sentence together: "Teacher, I need help. Someone keeps being picked on." Then list three grown-ups at school and at home your child can go to for help.

title.en: {name} and the Little Lighthouse in the Group Chat

zh: 城市的晚上，公寓窗外的霓虹燈一閃一閃，捷運從高架橋上轟隆隆滑過。{name}正在寫數學作業，手機忽然「叮咚、叮咚」響個不停。打開一看，是四年二班的群組。有人傳了一張戴眼鏡的蝸牛貼圖，上面寫著「宇恩又當啞巴了」。接著，大笑的表情排山倒海般湧了進來。
宇恩是班上最安靜的同學，午餐時總是一個人坐在窗邊，低頭在小本子上畫畫。這時，阿豪又傳了一句：「大家快跟上啊！」{name}的拇指懸在螢幕上，肚子像打了一個結。不跟，會不會也被笑？{name}深吸一口氣，把手機放下，一張貼圖也沒傳。可是，光是「不傳」，好像還不夠。
{name}拿著手機走進客廳。爸爸正在看新聞，一看到螢幕，眉頭立刻皺了起來。「我這樣是不是在告狀？」{name}小聲問。爸爸搖搖頭：「這不是告狀，是在找人幫忙。被取笑，也絕對不是宇恩的錯。」{name}和爸爸一起把訊息截圖，爸爸用一根手指慢吞吞地打信給陳老師，還打錯三個字，{name}忍不住笑了出來。
回到房間，{name}點開宇恩的名字，打了一行字，又刪掉；再打，又刪掉。最後，{name}寫下：「那些貼圖很過分，不是你的錯。明天午餐要不要一起坐？」按下送出的那一刻，{his}心臟怦怦直跳。螢幕上的三個小點閃了好久好久，終於跳出一張手畫的小燈塔，旁邊寫著：「好。謝謝你。」
第二天早上，陳老師沒有點任何人的名字，只是把椅子圍成一個圓圈。「群組應該是讓每個人都安心的地方，」老師說，「我們一起來想規則吧。」同學們你一言我一語：「不傳取笑別人的貼圖。」「看到不對勁，就告訴大人。」「有人被冷落，就邀請對方加入。」阿豪盯著自己的鞋子好一會兒，才走到宇恩旁邊，低聲說了句「對不起」。
午餐時，{name}端著餐盤坐到窗邊。宇恩有點害羞地翻開小本子，{name}一看，眼睛都亮了：裡面畫滿了撐著傘的貓、披著披風的蝸牛，還有那座小燈塔，每一張都栩栩如生，好像隨時會從紙上跳出來。原來，大家眼中「不說話」的宇恩，把滿肚子的話都畫成了圖。旁邊兩個同學湊過來，驚呼：「這可以做成貼圖耶！」
一週後，班級群組換上了一整套新貼圖，全是宇恩畫的。披著披風的蝸牛說「慢慢來也很棒」，小燈塔說「我陪你」。陳老師把新規則釘在教室後面，宇恩在旁邊畫了一圈小星星。{name}想起那天按下送出時發抖的手指。現在，那根手指穩穩地點了一下小燈塔，傳給了宇恩。
en: Outside the apartment window, neon signs blinked and a train rumbled across the elevated tracks. {name} was halfway through math homework when the phone started buzzing. Ding! Ding! Ding! It was the Class 4B group chat. Someone had posted a sticker of a snail in glasses that said, "Yu-en forgot how to talk again." Then laughing faces poured in like a flood.

Yu-en was the quietest kid in class, the one who ate lunch alone by the window, sketching in a little notebook. Now Hao typed, "Come on, everybody, join in!" {name}'s thumb hovered over the screen, and {name}'s stomach twisted into a knot. Would they laugh if {name} stayed out? Taking a deep breath, {name} set the phone down without sending a thing. Still, just not sending felt like only half of something.

{name} carried the phone into the living room. Dad was watching the news, but one look at the screen made his eyebrows crunch together. "Am I tattling?" {name} asked quietly. Dad shook his head. "This isn't tattling. It's getting help. And being teased is never Yu-en's fault." Together they took screenshots, and Dad wrote to Ms. Chen, pecking with one finger. He made three typos. {name} couldn't help giggling.

Back in the bedroom, {name} tapped Yu-en's name and typed a line. Delete. Typed again. Delete. Finally {name} wrote, "Those stickers were really unkind, and it's not your fault. Want to sit together at lunch tomorrow?" {name}'s heart thumped as the message flew away. Three little dots blinked for ages. At last a hand-drawn lighthouse popped up with two words beside it: "Okay. Thanks."

The next morning, Ms. Chen didn't name anyone. She simply arranged the chairs in a circle. "Our group chat should feel safe for everyone," she said. "Let's make the rules together." Ideas bounced around the room. "No stickers that make fun of people." "If something feels wrong, tell a grown-up." "If someone's left out, invite them in." Hao stared at his shoes for a long moment. Then he walked over to Yu-en and mumbled, "Sorry."

At lunch, {name} carried a tray to the window seat. A little shyly, Yu-en opened the notebook, and {name}'s eyes went wide. Every page was crowded with drawings: a cat holding an umbrella, a snail in a flapping cape, and the little lighthouse, all so lively they seemed ready to hop off the paper. The quiet kid had been saying plenty all along, just in pictures. Two classmates leaned over. "Whoa! These could be stickers!"

A week later, the class chat had a brand-new sticker set, every one drawn by Yu-en. The caped snail said, "Slow is awesome too." The lighthouse said, "I'm with you." Ms. Chen pinned the new rules on the classroom wall, and Yu-en drew a ring of stars around them. {name} remembered how shaky that thumb had felt pressing send. Now it was steady as it tapped the little lighthouse and sent it to Yu-en.

questions: 群組裡出現取笑宇恩的貼圖時，{name}做了哪些事？你覺得哪一件最需要勇氣？
{name}擔心告訴爸爸是在「告狀」。你覺得告狀和找大人幫忙有什麼不一樣？
如果你看到有同學被取笑或被冷落，你可以怎麼陪伴對方？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子約定一個「求救暗號」，例如一句「我需要聊聊」，只要孩子說出口，你就放下手邊的事專心聽，並一起想下一步。

questions: What did {name} do when the mean stickers showed up in the group chat? Which step do you think took the most courage?
{name} worried that showing Dad was tattling. How is tattling different from getting help from a grown-up?
If you saw a classmate being teased or left out, what could you do to stand with them?
en.tip: This week, agree on a "help phrase" with your child, like "I need to talk." Whenever your child says it, put everything down, listen closely, and figure out the next step together.

zh: 家裡來了一個小寶寶。寶寶好小，好軟。哇——哇——寶寶哭了。媽媽忙著抱寶寶。爸爸忙著換尿布。奶奶忙著泡奶。大家都好忙，好忙，好忙。
{name}拿著小熊，站在門邊。「媽媽，看我跳！」沒有人回頭。「爸爸，看我轉圈！」還是沒有人看。{name}的嘴巴嘟起來了。小熊好像也嘟起來了。
{name}抱著小熊，走到媽媽身邊。「媽媽，大家都忘記我了。」{name}小小聲說。「我也想要抱抱。」媽媽輕輕放下寶寶，張開手。「謝謝你告訴我。來，抱一個！」
媽媽拿出一本藍色的大相簿。「這是誰的呀？」媽媽眨眨眼。翻開第一頁，有一個小小寶寶。寶寶坐在澡盆裡。頭上頂著好多泡泡。「這是你喔，{name}！」
{name}睜大眼睛。「我好小喔！」照片裡的小{name}，抓著一隻小黃鴨。嘴巴張得圓圓的，像在說「哦」。{name}咯咯笑。媽媽也咯咯笑。嘻嘻，哈哈，停不下來！
「那時候，我天天抱你。」媽媽說。「現在，我也天天愛你。」「愛會不會變少？」{name}問。媽媽搖搖頭。「愛像泡泡，越吹越多。每個人都有好多好多。」
哇——哇——寶寶又哭了。「大孩子有特別的工作喔。」媽媽說。「你想唱歌給寶寶聽嗎？」{name}想一想，點點頭。「我要唱泡泡歌！」
{name}輕輕唱：「泡泡圓，泡泡高，噗噗噗，飛呀飄。」寶寶不哭了。小小的手，抓住{his}手指。媽媽抱住{name}和寶寶。「明天再一起看相簿，好嗎？」「好！」{name}笑了。
en: A new baby came home. The baby was tiny and soft. "Waah! Waah!" the baby cried. Mom rocked the baby. Dad changed a diaper. Grandma warmed the milk. Everyone was busy, busy, busy.
{name} stood by the door with Teddy. "Mom, watch me jump!" Nobody looked. "Dad, watch me spin!" Still nobody looked. {name} made a pouty face. Even Teddy looked a little pouty.
{name} hugged Teddy and went to Mom. "Everyone forgot about me," {name} said softly. "I want a hug too." Mom gently set the baby down. She opened her arms. "Thank you for telling me. Come here!"
Mom pulled out a big blue photo album. "Whose book is this?" she asked with a wink. On the first page was a tiny baby. The baby sat in a bath. Bubbles sat on top! "That's you, {name}!"
{name}'s eyes grew big. "I was so small!" Little {name} held a yellow rubber duck. {his} mouth made a round little "Oh!" {name} giggled. Mom giggled too. Hee hee, ha ha! They could not stop.

"I held you every day back then," Mom said. "And I love you every day now." "Will love get smaller?" {name} asked. Mom shook her head. "Love is like bubbles. Blow more, get more. Enough for everyone."
"Waah! Waah!" The baby cried again. "Big kids have special jobs," Mom said. "Want to sing to the baby?" {name} thought, then nodded. "I'll sing the bubble song!"

{name} sang softly, "Bubbles round, bubbles high, pop, pop, pop, float on by." The baby stopped crying. A tiny hand held {his} finger. Mom hugged {name} and the baby. "Album time again tomorrow?" "Yes!" {name} said with a smile.

questions: {name}覺得大家都忘記{him}的時候，{he}做了什麼？
你有沒有想要媽媽或爸爸多抱抱你的時候？你可以怎麼說？
如果家裡有小寶寶，你想幫寶寶做什麼特別的工作？
zh.tip: 這週找一個晚上，和孩子一起翻看孩子小時候的照片，說說當時你有多愛他。也可以約定一句暗號，例如「我想要抱抱」，讓孩子隨時能說出自己的需要。

questions: What did {name} do when {he} felt everyone forgot about {him}?
Have you ever wanted more hugs from Mom or Dad? What could you say?
If there were a baby at home, what special job would you like to do?
en.tip: One night this week, look through your child's baby photos together and share how much you loved them then and now. You can also agree on a simple phrase, like "I need a hug," that your child can use anytime.

zh: 傍晚，窗外的天空變成橘色。家裡好安靜。{name}坐在小籠子旁邊。籠子裡空空的。小滾輪不轉了，小水瓶也不滴了。倉鼠小豆今天早上走了。小豆已經很老很老了。牠是在睡夢中，安安靜靜離開的。{name}的眼淚，一滴一滴掉下來。
媽媽輕輕走過來，坐在{name}旁邊。媽媽沒有說話，只是抱著{him}。媽媽的毛衣軟軟的，暖暖的。「我好想小豆。」{name}小聲說。「我也好想牠。」媽媽說。媽媽的眼睛也紅紅的。原來媽媽也會哭。{name}靠在媽媽懷裡，哭了好一會兒。
哭完以後，心裡好像鬆了一點點。媽媽拿來一個小紙盒。「我們來做一個回憶盒，好不好？」媽媽說。「我們把小豆的寶貝，都收在這裡面。」{name}用{his}小手擦擦眼睛。然後，{he}輕輕點了點頭。
{name}拿出蠟筆，開始畫畫。沙沙，沙沙。{name}畫了小豆圓圓的身體。還畫了小小的粉紅鼻子。{name}又畫了小豆在滾輪上跑步。滾輪咕嚕咕嚕地轉。媽媽看了，笑著說：「畫得好像喔！小豆一定很喜歡。」
媽媽從抽屜拿出一張照片。照片裡，小豆捧著一顆葵花子。牠的臉頰鼓鼓的，像兩顆小氣球。{name}忍不住笑了一下。「小豆最愛葵花子了！」{name}從袋子裡拿出一顆葵花子。{he}把照片和葵花子，輕輕放進盒子裡。
「媽媽，你記得嗎？」{name}說。「小豆會把葵花子藏在小床底下！」媽媽笑了：「記得！藏了好多好多呢。」媽媽也說了一個故事。小豆剛來家裡那天，躲在木屑裡，只露出兩隻小耳朵。牠還「吱吱、吱吱」地叫。{name}和媽媽都笑了。
{name}摸摸盒子，小聲問：「我會一直這麼難過嗎？」媽媽想了想，慢慢地說：「難過會一點一點變輕。就像大雨，會慢慢變成小雨。可是你愛小豆的心，會一直留著。」{name}抱緊回憶盒。心裡還是有一點痠，可是也暖暖的。
窗外的天黑了，月亮出來了。{name}把回憶盒放在床邊。媽媽關上大燈，只留一盞小夜燈。黃黃的光，柔柔的。屋子裡好安靜，只聽得到時鐘滴答、滴答。「晚安，小豆。」{name}輕輕說。「晚安，{name}。」媽媽親親{his}額頭。{name}慢慢閉上眼睛，睡著了。
en: The evening sky turned orange. The house was very quiet. {name} sat by the little cage. The cage was empty now. The wheel did not spin. Little Bean the hamster was very, very old. This morning, Little Bean died peacefully in its sleep. {name}'s tears fell, drip, drip.

Mom came and sat down close by. She did not say anything. She just held {name} tight. Her sweater was soft and warm. "I miss Little Bean," {name} whispered. "I miss Little Bean too," Mom said. Her eyes were wet. Mom was crying too. They cried together for a while.

After crying, {name} felt a tiny bit lighter. Mom brought a small paper box. "Let's make a memory box," she said. "We can keep Little Bean's treasures inside." {name} wiped {his} eyes with one small hand. Then {name} slowly nodded.

{name} took out the crayons. Scritch, scratch. First came Little Bean's round, fluffy body. Then a tiny pink nose. Next, {name} drew Little Bean running on the wheel. Round and round it went. Mom smiled. "That looks just like Little Bean!"

Mom found a photo in the drawer. In it, Little Bean held a sunflower seed. Its cheeks puffed out like two tiny balloons. {name} gave a little smile. "Little Bean loved sunflower seeds!" {name} put the photo inside. Then in went one sunflower seed, too.

"Mom, remember this?" {name} said. "Little Bean hid seeds under the bed!" Mom laughed. "Yes! So many seeds!" Then Mom told a story, too. On Little Bean's first day, it hid in the wood shavings. Only two tiny ears peeked out. Squeak, squeak! They both laughed.

{name} touched the box gently. "Will I always feel this sad?" Mom thought for a moment. "The sad will get softer, little by little. Like big rain turning into gentle rain. But your love for Little Bean stays." {name} hugged the box close. It still hurt a little, but it felt warm too.

Outside, the sky grew dark. The moon came out. {name} set the memory box beside the bed. Mom turned off the big light. Only the night-light glowed, soft and yellow. Tick, tock, went the clock. "Goodnight, Little Bean," {name} whispered. "Goodnight, {name}," Mom said with a kiss. {name} closed {his} eyes and fell asleep.

questions: {name}很想小豆的時候，媽媽做了什麼？
如果你很想念一個很愛的人或動物，你會想畫什麼、說什麼故事？
你覺得為什麼想念會讓心裡又痠又暖？
zh.tip: 今晚睡前，和孩子各說一個關於寵物或心愛之人的快樂回憶，也可以一起畫一張畫放進「回憶盒」。告訴孩子：「難過的時候可以哭，媽媽／爸爸會陪著你。」

questions: What did Mom do when {name} missed Little Bean so much?
If you missed someone you love, what would you draw or what story would you tell?
Why do you think missing someone can feel both sad and warm?
en.tip: Tonight at bedtime, take turns sharing one happy memory of a pet or loved one, and maybe draw a picture for a memory box together. Let your child know: "It's okay to cry, and I'm right here with you."

title.en: {name} Waits for Snow on Hehuan Mountain

zh: 寒流來了，天氣變得好冷好冷。晚餐時，爸爸說：「週末我們去合歡山，看看會不會下雪！」{name}開心得跳起來。{name}從來沒看過真的雪。{he}抱著小熊毛毛說：「毛毛，我們要去找雪囉！」
車子沿著彎彎的山路，慢慢往上開。窗外的大樹，一棵一棵往後跑。媽媽說：「山越高，就越冷喔。」{name}趴在車窗邊看。咦，外面怎麼白白的？「是雪嗎？」爸爸笑著說：「那是霧，是飄在山上的雲。」
終於到了山上的停車場。爸爸把車停好，大家都穿得暖暖的。媽媽幫{name}戴上手套。{name}牽著媽媽的手下車。哇，風好冰呀！{name}呼一口氣，就冒出一團白白的煙。「我會變魔術耶！」{name}咯咯笑。
可是，到處都是灰灰的霧。地上沒有雪，只有濕濕的草。{name}東看看，西看看。「雪躲在哪裡呀？」爸爸說：「我們耐心等一等。」大家坐在長椅上。媽媽倒了一杯暖暖的可可，{name}小口小口地喝。
等了好久，雪還是沒有來。霧冷冷的，手指也冰冰的。{name}踢踢小石頭，嘆了一口氣。「雪是不是不來了？」{name}小聲說。{he}把毛毛抱得緊緊的。媽媽輕輕抱住{name}，說：「天空可能在準備驚喜喔。」
爸爸說：「我們來玩個遊戲吧！」大家一起抬起頭，數到三。「一、二、三，雪花你好！」一隻小鳥從霧裡飛過，啾啾地叫。{name}也學小鳥，啾啾、啾啾。風輕輕吹，霧慢慢變薄，天空亮了一點點。
忽然，一個小小的白點飄下來。接著又一個，又一個。它們輕輕的，慢慢的，好像在跳舞。有一片雪花，落在{his}手套上。{name}不敢動，仔細地看。雪花有六個小尖角，好像一顆亮晶晶的小星星！
「下雪了！下雪了！」{name}大聲歡呼。爸爸媽媽也開心地笑了。{name}把手套舉到毛毛面前。「毛毛你看，是星星雪！」雪花越飄越多，草地慢慢變白了。{name}輕輕說：「雪花，謝謝你來找我們。」
en: A cold wave came, and the air turned chilly. Dad said, "Let's drive up Hehuan Mountain this weekend. Maybe we'll see snow!" {name} jumped for joy. It would be {his} very first snow. {name} hugged Momo the teddy bear. "Momo, we're going to find snow!"

The car climbed slowly up the winding road. Trees zipped past, one by one. "The higher we go, the colder it gets," said Mom. {name} peeked outside. Everything looked white! "Is that snow?" Dad smiled. "That's fog, a cloud resting on the mountain."

At last, they parked near the top. Everyone was bundled up warm. Mom helped {name} put on mittens. Holding Mom's hand, {name} stepped out. Brrr, the wind was icy! {name} puffed, and a little white cloud appeared. "I can do magic!"

But gray fog was everywhere. There was no snow, just wet grass. {name} looked this way and that. "Where is the snow hiding?" "Let's wait patiently," said Dad. They sat on a bench. Mom poured warm cocoa, and {name} took tiny sips.

They waited and waited. Still no snow came. The fog was chilly, and fingers felt cold. {name} kicked a pebble and sighed. "Maybe the snow isn't coming." {he} held Momo tight. Mom gave {name} a gentle hug. "Maybe the sky is getting a surprise ready."

"Let's play a game!" said Dad. Everyone looked up and counted. "One, two, three, hello, snowflakes!" A little bird flew out of the fog. "Tweet, tweet!" {name} tweeted back, just like the bird. The wind blew softly. The fog thinned, and the sky grew brighter.

Suddenly, a tiny white dot drifted down. Then another, and another. They floated slowly, as if they were dancing. One snowflake landed on {his} mitten. {name} kept very still and looked closely. The snowflake had six tiny points. It looked like a sparkly little star!

"It's snowing! It's snowing!" {name} cheered. Mom and Dad laughed too. {name} held up the mitten for Momo. "Look, Momo! Star snow!" More and more snowflakes fell, and the grass slowly turned white. {name} whispered, "Thank you, snowflakes, for finding us."

questions: {name}呼一口氣冒出白白的煙，好像在變魔術，你覺得那團白煙像什麼？
等雪等好久的時候，{name}和毛毛心裡是什麼感覺？
雪花像亮晶晶的小星星，如果有一片落在你手上，你想跟它說什麼？
zh.tip: 今晚躺在被窩裡，和孩子一起用手指在對方手心輕輕畫一片六個尖角的雪花，再小聲說出今天故事裡最喜歡的一刻。

questions: When {name} puffed out a little white cloud, it was like magic. What did that cloud look like to you?
While {name} and Momo waited and waited for snow, how do you think they felt?
The snowflake looked like a sparkly little star. If one landed on your hand, what would you say to it?
en.tip: Tonight, snuggled in bed, take turns gently drawing a six-pointed snowflake on each other's palm with a finger, then whisper your favourite part of the story.

zh: 太陽下山後，動物園的大門又悄悄打開了。{name}和家人來參加一場特別的「夜間探險」。保育員阿明哥哥發給每個人一支手電筒，{name}按下開關，照出來的卻是淡淡的紅光。阿明哥哥小聲說：「動物看紅光不刺眼，我們才能偷偷看見牠們。」
大家沿著小路慢慢走，頭頂的樹葉沙沙作響。白天{name}來過這裡，那時候到處都是吵鬧的人聲，動物們卻縮在角落睡大覺。現在四周好安靜，只有蟲兒唧唧叫。{name}握緊手電筒，心裡撲通撲通跳，好像要去尋找一個祕密。
第一站是穿山甲的家。紅光照過去，一個圓滾滾、披著鱗片的小傢伙正在泥土裡用力挖。牠的爪子又長又彎，一下、兩下，泥土就飛了起來。「牠在找螞蟻當晚餐。」阿明哥哥輕聲說。{name}看得目不轉睛，連呼吸都放得好輕好輕。
{name}忍不住興奮地喊：「哇，牠好厲害！」穿山甲嚇了一跳，立刻捲成一顆硬硬的球，一動也不動。{name}趕緊摀住嘴巴，心裡好難過。阿明哥哥蹲下來，輕輕拍拍{his}肩膀，豎起一根手指，比了一個「噓」的手勢。
大家安安靜靜地等著。一分鐘、兩分鐘……那顆球慢慢鬆開了，先探出一條尾巴，接著是尖尖的鼻子。穿山甲又開始挖土了！{name}笑了，用氣音說：「對不起，你繼續吃吧。」從那時起，{he}走路都踮著腳尖。
第二站，阿明哥哥把紅光照向一棵倒下的大樹。樹幹上趴著一隻石虎，額頭有白色條紋，耳朵後面還有小白點。石虎張大嘴打了個哈欠，前腳往前伸，背弓得高高的，好像剛睡醒。「早安呀。」{name}輕輕地說，雖然天上已經掛滿了星星。
最後一站是貓頭鷹的大鳥籠。「咕——咕——」低低的叫聲從高處傳來。突然，一道影子張開翅膀，從這根樹枝滑到那根樹枝，竟然一點聲音也沒有。{name}驚訝得睜大眼睛：「牠飛得好安靜，像一片落葉！」阿明哥哥點點頭：「這樣才抓得到老鼠喔。」
探險結束了，{name}和家人慢慢走向大門。回頭一看，穿山甲在挖土，石虎在散步，貓頭鷹在樹上眨著眼睛。城市正要睡著，動物園卻正熱鬧起來呢。{name}揮揮手，小聲地說：「晚安——不對，是早安！現在換我回家睡覺了。」
en: After the sun went down, the zoo gates quietly opened again. {name} and the family had come for a special night adventure. Ah-Ming, the zookeeper, handed everyone a flashlight. When {name} clicked it on, the light glowed soft and red. "Red light is gentle on animal eyes," Ah-Ming whispered, "so we can watch without bothering them."

They walked slowly along the path while leaves rustled overhead. {name} had visited in the daytime, when the zoo was full of noisy crowds and the animals were curled up asleep. Now everything was hushed except the chirping crickets. {name} held the flashlight tight. It felt like hunting for a secret.

The first stop was the pangolin's home. In the red glow, a round little creature covered in scales was digging hard in the dirt. Its long, curved claws scooped once, twice, and soil went flying. "It's looking for ants for dinner," Ah-Ming said softly. {name} watched without blinking, breathing as quietly as possible.

Then {name} couldn't hold it in. "Wow, it's amazing!" The startled pangolin rolled into a hard, tight ball and didn't move at all. {name} clapped both hands over {his} mouth, feeling terrible. Ah-Ming knelt down, gave {name} a gentle pat on the shoulder, and held up one finger. "Shh."

Everyone waited without a sound. One minute, two minutes... Slowly, the ball loosened. First a tail peeked out, then a pointy nose. The pangolin went back to digging! {name} smiled and whispered, "Sorry. Please keep eating." From then on, {he} walked on tiptoe.

At the second stop, Ah-Ming shone the red light on a fallen tree. A leopard cat lay along the trunk, with white stripes on its forehead and little white spots behind its ears. It gave a big yawn, stretched its front paws, and arched its back, just like someone waking up. "Good morning," {name} whispered, even though the sky was full of stars.

The last stop was the owls' tall aviary. "Hoo, hoo," came a low call from above. Suddenly a shadow spread its wings and glided from one branch to another without a single sound. {name}'s eyes went wide. "It flies as quietly as a falling leaf!" Ah-Ming nodded. "That's how owls sneak up on mice."

When the adventure was over, {name} and the family walked slowly toward the gate. Looking back, {name} could see the pangolin digging, the leopard cat strolling, and the owls blinking in the trees. The city was falling asleep, but the zoo was just waking up. {name} waved and whispered, "Good night—no, good morning! Now it's my turn to sleep."

questions: {name}握著紅光手電筒走在安靜的小路上，心裡撲通撲通跳，你覺得那是什麼樣的感覺？
穿山甲、石虎和貓頭鷹，你最喜歡哪一隻？牠哪裡讓你覺得特別？
如果晚上你也能變成一種動物，你想變成誰？你會在夜裡做什麼？
zh.tip: 關燈後，和孩子玩「氣音猜動物」：輪流用小小聲的氣音描述一種夜裡醒著的動物，讓對方猜猜是誰，猜完說聲「晚安」就睡覺。

questions: When {name} walked down the quiet path holding the red flashlight, with a heart going thump-thump, what do you think that felt like?
The pangolin, the leopard cat, or the owl: which one did you like best? What made it special to you?
If you could turn into an animal at night, which one would you be? What would you do in the dark?
en.tip: After lights out, play a whisper animal guessing game: take turns softly describing a night-time animal while the other person guesses, then say a quiet "good night" and drift off to sleep.

zh: 雨停了。滴答，滴答。樹葉亮晶晶。{name}牽著爺爺的手，一起去森林散步。啪嗒，啪嗒，走過小水窪。森林聞起來好香。爺爺說：「慢慢走，慢慢看。」
咦？大樹下有東西。一朵、兩朵、三朵。是小蘑菇！小蘑菇圍成一個圓圈。圓圓的，像在手牽手。{name}蹲下來看。「爺爺，好可愛喔！」爺爺說：「噓，小聲一點。」
{name}眨眨眼睛。「爺爺，這是小村莊！」每朵蘑菇都是一間房子。紅屋頂，白屋頂。小小的窗，小小的門。爺爺點點頭：「誰住在這裡呢？」
慢吞吞，慢吞吞。一隻蝸牛爬過來。「是送信的蝸牛！」{name}說。「叩叩叩，有你的信！」蝸牛爬呀爬，爬呀爬。爺爺哈哈笑：「這封信會好晚到喔！」
沙沙沙，沙沙沙。一隻小甲蟲走過來。亮亮的，綠綠的。「是甲蟲公車！」{name}拍拍手。「嘟嘟，請上車！」甲蟲停一下，又走了。「公車開走囉！」爺爺笑彎了腰。
咚！一滴雨水掉下來。打在蘑菇屋頂上。「下雨了，大家快回家！」{name}小聲說。螞蟻跑呀跑。小蟲躲進蘑菇下。{name}咯咯笑：「好像撐小雨傘！」
{name}好想摸一摸。小手伸出去，又停下來。爺爺輕輕說：「我們用眼睛看。」{name}點點頭。不摘，不踩，不碰。「這是小鄰居的家。」{name}揮揮手：「小村莊，再見！」
太陽出來了。森林暖暖的。{name}和爺爺往回走。啪嗒，啪嗒，啪嗒。回頭再看一看。蝸牛還在送信。甲蟲公車還在跑。{name}笑著說：「明天再來看你們！」
en: The rain has stopped. Drip, drop, drip. Shiny wet leaves everywhere. {name} holds Grandpa's hand. They walk into the forest. Splish, splash, past little puddles. Grandpa smiles. "Slow steps, big eyes."
Look! Under a big tree. One, two, three mushrooms! They stand in a little circle. Like friends holding hands. {name} squats down low. "Grandpa, they're so cute!" "Shh," says Grandpa softly.
{name} blinks and grins. "It's a tiny village!" Each mushroom is a house. Red roofs, white roofs. Tiny windows, tiny doors. Grandpa nods. "Who lives here, I wonder?"
Slowly, slowly, a snail comes along. "The mail snail!" says {name}. "Knock, knock! A letter for you!" The snail creeps on and on. Grandpa laughs. "That letter will be late!"
Rustle, rustle. A little beetle walks by. It is shiny and green. "The beetle bus!" {name} claps. "Beep beep! All aboard!" The beetle stops, then hurries off. "Oops, the bus left!" Grandpa chuckles.

Plop! A raindrop falls from a leaf. It lands on a mushroom roof. "Rain! Everyone, run home!" whispers {name}. Ants scurry, scurry. A bug hides under a mushroom. {name} giggles. "Like a tiny umbrella!"

{name} wants to touch one. A little hand reaches out, then stops. "We look with our eyes," Grandpa says. {name} nods. No picking, no stepping, no poking. "This is their home." {name} waves. "Bye-bye, little village!"

The sun peeks out. The forest feels warm. {name} and Grandpa walk back. Splish, splash, splish. They look back once more. The mail snail is still creeping. The beetle bus is still rolling. "See you tomorrow!" calls {name}.

questions: 你最喜歡哪一間蘑菇房子？
甲蟲公車怎麼叫？我們一起小小聲說「嘟嘟」。
下雨了，你也想躲在蘑菇小雨傘下面嗎？
zh.tip: 睡前用手指當送信的蝸牛，慢吞吞爬過{his}小手和背，輕聲說「叩叩叩，有你的信！」，再送上一個晚安抱抱。

questions: Which mushroom house do you like best?
What does the beetle bus say? Let's whisper "beep beep" together.
When the rain came, would you like to hide under a mushroom umbrella too?
en.tip: At bedtime, let your fingers be the mail snail and creep slowly across {his} hand and back, whispering "Knock, knock! A letter for you!" Then deliver a goodnight cuddle.

title.en: {name}'s Paper Rocket Flies to the Moon

zh: 今天下午，{name}和爸爸坐在桌邊。桌上有藍色的紙，還有膠帶和蠟筆。爸爸小心地拿剪刀剪紙。{name}把紙捲成長長的筒子，再貼上尖尖的頭，和三片小翅膀。{name}在火箭上畫了好多星星。「它叫小星號！」{name}開心地說。
天色慢慢暗了，晚風輕輕地吹。{name}洗好了澡，也刷好了牙。{name}把小星號放在窗台上。窗外的月亮又圓又亮。{name}小聲地說：「月亮，我好想去找你。」月亮靜靜地發著光，好像在微笑。房間裡安安靜靜的。
媽媽幫{name}蓋好被子。被子暖暖的，好像一個大擁抱。床邊的小燈發出淡淡的黃光。「晚安，{name}。」媽媽輕輕親了{name}一下。{name}閉上眼睛，慢慢地數：「三、二、一……」咦？小星號好像變大了！{name}爬了進去，坐得穩穩的。
小星號慢慢地往上飛。飛過屋頂，飛過大樹。街燈變得好小好小，像一顆顆小豆子。風輕輕地吹，「咻——咻——」好溫柔。天上有好多星星，眨呀眨，眨得好慢。有一顆星星打了一個大哈欠。「晚安，{name}。」星星們輕聲說。
可是，有一顆小星星睡不著。「我的雲朵被子飛走了。」小星星小聲地說。{name}看見旁邊有一朵白雲。{name}輕輕地把白雲拉過來，幫小星星蓋好。雲朵軟綿綿的，像棉花糖一樣。「謝謝你！」小星星笑了，慢慢閉上了眼睛。
小星號繼續往上飛，月亮越來越近了。月亮上有一隻白白的月兔。月兔正在輕輕地搗著藥，咚、咚、咚。{name}揮揮手：「月兔，你好！」月兔動了動長耳朵，也向{name}揮手。「好晚了，該回家睡覺囉。」月兔溫柔地說。
小星號慢慢地往下飄，像一片輕輕的羽毛。經過睡著的星星，小星星還蓋著雲朵被子。經過安靜的屋頂，經過靜靜的大樹。風聲越來越小，四周越來越靜。小星號輕輕地飄回了{name}的房間。
{name}輕輕地落回床上。被子還是暖暖的，小燈還是淡淡的。{name}張開眼睛看了看。小星號正好好地站在窗台上。月光照著它，亮亮的。「晚安，小星號。晚安，月亮。」{name}微笑著，慢慢地睡著了。
en: This afternoon, {name} sat at the table with Dad. There was blue paper, tape, and crayons. Dad carefully cut the paper with scissors. {name} rolled it into a long tube. Then came a pointy top and three little wings. {name} drew lots of stars on it. "It's called Little Star!" {name} said happily.

Slowly, the sky grew dark. A soft evening breeze blew. {name} had a bath and brushed {his} teeth. Then {name} put Little Star on the windowsill. Outside, the moon was round and bright. "Moon, I really want to visit you," {name} whispered. The moon glowed quietly, as if it were smiling.

Mom tucked {name} into bed. The blanket was warm, like a big hug. The little lamp glowed soft and yellow. "Goodnight, {name}," Mom said with a gentle kiss. {name} closed {his} eyes and counted slowly. "Three, two, one..." Oh! Little Star seemed to grow bigger! {name} climbed inside and sat snug and still.

Little Star floated slowly up. Up past the rooftops, up past the trees. The streetlights looked tiny, like little beans. The wind went whoosh, whoosh, so gently. The sky was full of stars. They twinkled slowly, slowly. One star gave a big yawn. "Goodnight, {name}," the stars whispered.

But one little star could not sleep. "My cloud blanket floated away," it said softly. {name} saw a white cloud nearby. Gently, {name} pulled the cloud over and tucked the little star in. The cloud was soft, like cotton candy. "Thank you!" said the little star. It smiled and slowly closed its eyes.

Little Star kept flying, and the moon came closer. On the moon lived a white moon rabbit. The rabbit was gently pounding, thump, thump, thump. {name} waved. "Hello, Moon Rabbit!" The rabbit wiggled its long ears and waved back. "It's late now. Time to go home and sleep," it said kindly.

Little Star drifted down, light as a feather. Past the sleeping stars. The little star was still snug under its cloud. Past the quiet rooftops and the still trees. The wind grew softer. Everything grew quieter. Little Star floated gently back into {name}'s room.

{name} landed softly in bed. The blanket was still warm. The lamp was still glowing softly. {name} opened {his} eyes just a little. There was Little Star, standing on the windowsill. Moonlight made it shine. "Goodnight, Little Star. Goodnight, Moon." {name} smiled and slowly drifted off to sleep.

questions: 如果你也有一架紙火箭，你想在上面畫什麼？
{name}用雲朵幫小星星蓋被子，你的被子摸起來像什麼？
如果你也遇到月兔，你想跟牠說什麼？
zh.tip: 關燈後，和孩子一起躺著，輕輕說「晚安」給房間裡的東西聽，像是月亮、小燈、枕頭。明天有空時，再一起用紙捲一架小火箭。

questions: If you had a paper rocket too, what would you draw on it?
{name} tucked the little star in with a cloud. What does your blanket feel like?
If you met the moon rabbit too, what would you say to it?
en.tip: After the lights go off, lie together and take turns whispering goodnight to things in the room, like the moon, the lamp, and the pillow. Tomorrow, you can roll a little paper rocket together.

title.en: {name} and the Crab Family in the Tide Pool

zh: 早上，海水退得好遠好遠。媽媽說：「退潮了，我們去看潮池吧！」{name}牽著媽媽的手，往海邊走。東北角的岩石黑黑的，一塊一塊排在海邊。海風涼涼的，海鷗在天上叫。{name}心裡好興奮，冒險要開始了！
他們走到一個小潮池旁。潮池像一面小鏡子，亮晶晶的。{name}蹲下來，仔細的看。水裡有綠綠的海草，輕輕搖來搖去。還有一顆小海螺，慢慢爬過石頭。「媽媽，潮池裡好熱鬧！」{name}小聲的說。媽媽笑著點點頭。
忽然，有個小東西一閃，就不見了。「那是什麼？」{name}睜大眼睛。媽媽指著一塊圓圓的石頭說：「牠躲到下面了。」{name}好想快點知道，想用力把石頭翻開。媽媽輕輕握住{his}小手：「我們慢慢來，好嗎？」{name}點點頭。
媽媽教{name}用兩隻手，輕輕抬起石頭的一邊。石頭底下，有一隻大螃蟹，還有三隻小螃蟹！牠們的殼紅紅褐褐的，腳細細的。大螃蟹舉起大鉗子，小螃蟹擠成一團。「牠們好像有點害怕。」{name}小小聲的說。
{name}不說話了，只用眼睛看，也不伸手去摸。小螃蟹橫著走，一步、兩步、三步。一隻小螃蟹吐出小泡泡，啵、啵、啵。「牠在跟我打招呼嗎？」{name}笑了。媽媽說：「也許喔，牠知道你很溫柔。」大螃蟹慢慢放下了鉗子。
看了一會兒，媽媽說：「這塊石頭，是牠們的家喔。」{name}想了想：「那我要把家還給牠們。」{he}記得石頭原本的樣子，有青苔的那面朝上。{name}慢慢的、輕輕的，把石頭放回原位。螃蟹一家又安心的躲好了。
這時，海浪的聲音變大了。一波海水流進潮池，嘩啦嘩啦。媽媽說：「漲潮了，海水要回來囉。」{name}牽緊媽媽的手，一起往高高的岸上走。{he}回頭看看那塊圓石頭，海水正輕輕蓋過它，像蓋上一條藍被子。
「螃蟹一家會冷嗎？」{name}問。媽媽說：「不會，牠們最喜歡海水了。」{name}想像小螃蟹在水裡吐泡泡，開心的轉圈圈。{name}對著大海揮揮手：「螃蟹一家，下次見！」陽光照在海面上，閃閃發亮，好像大海也在揮手呢。
en: One morning, the sea pulled back far, far away. "It's low tide," said Mom. "Let's go look at tide pools!" {name} held Mom's hand and walked to the shore. Dark rocks lined the northeast coast. The wind felt cool. Seagulls called overhead. The adventure was starting!

They stopped beside a little tide pool. It shone like a tiny mirror. {name} squatted down to look closely. Green seaweed swayed back and forth. A small sea snail crept slowly over a stone. "Mom, the pool is so busy!" {name} whispered. Mom smiled and nodded.

Suddenly, something small darted away and vanished. "What was that?" {name} asked with wide eyes. Mom pointed to a round rock. "It's hiding under there." {name} wanted to flip the rock over fast. Mom gently held {his} hand. "Let's go slowly, okay?" {name} nodded.

Mom showed {name} how to use two hands. Together they lifted one side of the rock, very gently. Underneath was a big crab and three little crabs! Their shells were reddish brown. Their legs were thin. The big crab raised its claws. "They look a bit scared," {name} whispered.

{name} stayed quiet and just watched, without touching. The little crabs walked sideways, one, two, three steps. One little crab blew tiny bubbles. Pop, pop, pop! "Is it saying hello?" {name} giggled. "Maybe," said Mom. "It knows you're gentle." The big crab slowly lowered its claws.

After a while, Mom said, "This rock is their home." {name} thought about it. "Then I'll give their home back." {name} remembered how the rock had sat, mossy side up. Slowly and softly, {he} set it back in place. The crab family was safe and snug again.

Just then, the waves grew louder. Water rushed into the pool. Splash, splash! "The tide is coming in," said Mom. {name} held Mom's hand tight. They walked up to the high, dry shore. {name} looked back. The water was covering the round rock like a blue blanket.

"Will the crabs be cold?" {name} asked. "No," said Mom. "They love the sea." {name} pictured the little crabs blowing bubbles and spinning happily. {name} waved at the ocean. "Bye, crab family! See you next time!" The sunlight sparkled on the waves, as if the sea waved back.

questions: 潮池裡有綠綠的海草、小海螺，還有螃蟹，你最喜歡哪一個？
小螃蟹吐泡泡「啵、啵、啵」，你覺得牠在說什麼呢？
如果下次再去看螃蟹一家，你想跟牠們說什麼？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈後，和孩子窩在被子裡，一起小小聲的學小螃蟹「啵、啵、啵」，再輪流猜猜螃蟹一家在海水被子底下做了什麼夢。

questions: The tide pool had green seaweed, a little sea snail, and crabs. Which one did you like best?
When the little crab blew bubbles, pop, pop, pop, what do you think it was saying?
If you visit the crab family again, what would you like to tell them?
en.tip: After lights out tonight, snuggle under the covers and whisper "pop, pop, pop" like the little crab together, then take turns guessing what the crab family dreams about under their blue blanket of sea.

zh: 星期六早上，陽光暖暖的。{name}和媽媽來到公園。{name}手裡抱著一個新風箏。風箏是紅色的，像一條小魚。長長的尾巴上，綁著藍色緞帶。「今天我要讓它飛上天！」{name}笑著說。媽媽點點頭，在草地旁的長椅坐下。
{name}拉著線，用力往前跑。風箏飛起來一下下，咚！又掉進草裡。{name}撿起風箏，再跑一次。這次風箏轉了兩圈。可是，它又摔下來了。{name}停下腳步，嘆了一口氣。「為什麼你不肯飛呢？」
草地另一邊，有一位老爺爺。他的風箏是一隻大老鷹。老鷹高高飛在白雲旁邊。老爺爺看見{name}，慢慢走過來。他先向媽媽揮揮手。「妳好，我是林爺爺，常來這裡放風箏。」媽媽微笑說：「林爺爺好。」林爺爺彎下腰問：「要不要先聽聽風？」
「風要怎麼聽呢？」{name}好奇地問。林爺爺請{name}閉上眼睛，安靜站好。風輕輕吹過來，草地沙沙作響。「風從哪裡來呀？」林爺爺問。{name}伸出手指，仔細感覺。「從後面來！」林爺爺笑了：「對！背對著風，風才推得動風箏。」
林爺爺先把老鷹的線綁在長椅上，再幫{name}舉著風箏。他站在幾步遠的地方。「等一陣大一點的風。」林爺爺說，「風來了，你就跑。」{name}等呀等，等呀等。樹葉開始嘩嘩搖動了。「就是現在！」{name}拔腿就跑。風箏飛起來了，可是飛不高。它又慢慢落回草地上。
「沒關係，再試一次。」林爺爺說。{name}點點頭，又跑了一次。然後，再跑一次。有一次跑得太早，有一次跑得太慢。{name}跑得氣喘吁吁，可是沒有放棄。媽媽在長椅上拍手：「{name}，加油！你越來越厲害了！」{name}深深吸一口氣，又走回起點。
這一次，{name}先安靜聽風。樹葉搖起來，草地沙沙響。「一、二、三！」{name}用力往前跑。風把風箏輕輕托起來。風箏越飛越高，越飛越高！林爺爺說：「慢慢放線，線鬆了就輕輕拉。」{name}照著做。紅色小魚游上了藍天。
線在{his}小手裡一動一動的。好像風在跟{name}握手。又像好朋友拉著{him}一起玩。「林爺爺，風在跟我玩！」{name}開心地大喊。林爺爺的老鷹飛過來，陪著紅色小魚。媽媽走過來，站在{name}旁邊。大家一起抬頭，看兩個風箏在天上跳舞。
en: It was a warm Saturday morning. {name} and Mom went to the park. {name} hugged a brand-new kite. It was red, like a little fish. Its long tail had blue ribbons. "Today my kite will fly!" {name} said. Mom smiled and sat on a bench nearby.

{name} held the string and ran fast. The kite jumped up for a moment. Then, bump! It fell into the grass. {name} picked it up and ran again. The kite spun twice and crashed down. {name} stopped and sighed. "Why won't you fly?"

Across the grass stood an old man. His kite was a big eagle, soaring by the clouds. He walked over slowly and waved to Mom first. "Hello, I'm Grandpa Lin. I fly kites here often." Mom waved back. Grandpa Lin bent down. "Shall we listen to the wind first?"

"How do you listen to wind?" {name} asked. Grandpa Lin said, "Close your eyes and stand still." A breeze drifted by. The grass went swish, swish. "Where is the wind coming from?" {name} held up a finger. "From behind me!" "Yes! Keep your back to the wind. Then it can push your kite."

Grandpa Lin tied his eagle kite's string to the bench. Then he held the kite up for {name}. He stood a few steps away. "Wait for a strong gust," he said. "When it comes, run!" {name} waited and waited. The leaves began to rustle. "Now!" {name} dashed off. The kite rose, but not very high. Slowly, it drifted back down.

"That's okay. Try again," said Grandpa Lin. {name} nodded and ran again. And again. Once {name} ran too early. Once {name} ran too late. {name} was puffing hard but kept going. Mom clapped from the bench. "You're getting better, {name}!" {name} took a deep breath and walked back.

This time, {name} listened first. The leaves shook. The grass whispered. "One, two, three!" {name} ran with all {his} might. The wind lifted the kite gently. Up, up, up it went! "Let out the string slowly," said Grandpa Lin. "Tug it if it gets loose." Soon the red fish swam across the blue sky.

The string wiggled in {his} hands. It felt like the wind was shaking hands. It felt like a friend tugging, saying, "Come play!" "Grandpa Lin, the wind is playing with me!" {name} shouted. The eagle kite flew close to the little fish. Mom came over and stood beside {name}. Together they watched two kites dance in the sky.

questions: {name}的風箏一直掉下來的時候，你覺得{name}心裡是什麼感覺？
閉上眼睛聽風的時候，你猜會聽到什麼聲音？
如果你也有一個風箏，你想要它長成什麼樣子？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈前，和孩子一起閉上眼睛，輪流輕輕對彼此的小手吹氣，猜猜「風」是從哪一邊來的。

questions: When {name}'s kite kept falling down, how do you think {name} felt?
If you closed your eyes to listen to the wind, what sounds might you hear?
If you had a kite too, what would you want it to look like?
en.tip: Before lights out tonight, close your eyes together and take turns gently blowing on each other's hands, guessing which side the "wind" is coming from.

zh: 滴答，滴答，下雨了。星期六下雨，星期天也下雨。{name}趴在窗邊，嘆了一口氣：「好無聊喔。」小熊坐在沙發上，小兔躲在椅子下，小鴨待在書架旁。
這時候，爸爸抱來一個紙箱。好大好大的紙箱！爸爸眨眨眼：「{name}，這是什麼？」{name}想一想，大聲說：「是一艘船！」爸爸笑了：「對！是海盜船！」
爸爸拿來白紙和膠帶。{name}在紙上畫一個大笑臉。把紙黏在掃把棍上，變成船帆。爸爸再把紙捲一捲，做成望遠鏡。海盜船準備好囉！
客廳變成藍藍的大海。地毯是海浪，嘩啦啦！{name}坐進船裡，划呀划。爸爸在旁邊吹風：「呼——呼——」船帆抖一抖，出發囉！
{name}拿起望遠鏡看一看。咦？沙發島上有小熊！「小熊別怕，我來救你！」{name}伸出小手，把小熊抱上船。小熊坐好了，好像在笑呢。
船繼續划呀划。椅子下面有小兔！「小兔，快上來！」書架旁邊有小鴨！小鴨上船時，咚一聲，倒栽蔥！小鴨好像在說：「呱呱！謝謝！」{name}和爸爸哈哈大笑。
船上好擠喔！小熊、小兔、小鴨，還有{name}。爸爸問：「船長，大家都救到了嗎？」{name}數一數：「一、二、三，全部到齊！」爸爸拍拍手。
忽然，窗戶亮亮的。雨停了，太陽探出頭來！陽光照進客廳，照在海盜船上。{name}抱著大家，笑嘻嘻地說：「太陽也來玩囉！」
en: Drip, drop. Drip, drop. Rain on Saturday. Rain on Sunday, too. {name} sighed at the window. "I'm so bored." Teddy sat on the sofa. Bunny hid under a chair. Duck sat by the bookshelf.
Then Dad carried in a box. A giant, giant box! Dad gave a wink. "What could this be?" {name} thought hard. "A boat!" Dad laughed. "Yes! A pirate ship!"
Dad brought paper and tape. {name} drew a big smiley face. They taped it to a broom stick. Now the ship had a sail! Dad rolled more paper into a spyglass.
The living room became a big blue sea. The rug was the waves. Splash, splash! {name} climbed into the ship. Dad blew the wind. "Whoosh, whoosh!" Off they sailed!
{name} looked through the spyglass. Oh! Teddy was on Sofa Island! "Don't worry, Teddy! I'm coming!" {name} reached out and lifted Teddy aboard. Teddy seemed to smile.
Row, row, row. Bunny waited under the chair. "Hop in, Bunny!" Duck waited by the bookshelf. Duck tumbled in upside down. Plop! "Quack! Thank you!" {name} and Dad giggled and giggled.
The ship was very full now! Teddy, Bunny, Duck, and {name}. "Captain, is everyone safe?" Dad asked. {name} counted. "One, two, three. Everyone is here!" Dad clapped.
Suddenly the window grew bright. The rain stopped. The sun peeked out! Sunlight filled the room and shone on the pirate ship. {name} hugged everyone close. "The sun wants to play, too!"

questions: {name}在船帆上畫了一個大笑臉，你想畫什麼？
小鴨倒栽蔥的時候，你覺得好笑嗎？
你最想救哪一個好朋友上船？
zh.tip: 今晚抱著最喜歡的娃娃，輕輕假裝床是一艘小船，一起小聲說「呼——呼——」，慢慢划進夢裡。

questions: {name} drew a big smiley face on the sail. What would you draw?
Duck tumbled in upside down. Was that funny?
Which toy friend would you save first?
en.tip: Tonight, hug a favourite toy and pretend the bed is a little boat. Whisper "whoosh, whoosh" together and slowly sail off to sleep.

zh: 春天的早晨，{name}來到山上的阿姨家。阿姨有一大片茶園，一排排綠油油的茶樹像波浪一樣，從山坡一路排進白白的雲霧裡。採茶的阿姨們背著竹簍，手指在枝頭上輕輕一點一點，好像在跳舞。
「我也想採茶！」{name}興奮地說。阿姨笑著遞給{him}一個小竹簍。{name}跑進茶樹中間，大片的、小片的、黃的、綠的，看到葉子就摘。沒多久，小竹簍就滿了，{name}抱著竹簍跑回去，心裡好得意。
阿姨看了看，摸摸竹簍裡的葉子。「這些葉子太老、太硬了，泡出來的茶會苦苦的喔。」{name}低頭看著滿滿的竹簍，嘴巴扁了起來。原來忙了半天，摘的都不對。{his}心裡酸酸的，好想把竹簍放下。
阿姨牽著{name}走到一棵茶樹前，指著枝頭最上面。「你看，最尖端有一個捲捲的小芽，旁邊還有兩片嫩嫩的葉子，我們叫它『一心二葉』。」那個小芽摸起來軟軟的，上面有細細的白毛，在陽光下亮晶晶。
阿姨示範給{name}看：用拇指和食指輕輕捏住，往上一提，「啵」的一聲就下來了。{name}試了一次，太用力，把嫩葉捏爛了。再試一次，又只摘到一片葉子。{name}深深吸一口氣，放慢動作，第三次，終於摘下完整的一心二葉！
太陽慢慢爬高，{name}一棵一棵仔細找，不再急著把竹簍裝滿。手指沾上了綠綠的茶香，額頭冒出小汗珠。旁邊的採茶阿姨看了看竹簍，點點頭說：「每一片都好漂亮！」雖然只裝了淺淺一層，{name}卻覺得比早上那一簍還要重。
下午，阿姨把嫩葉攤在竹篩上，讓它們慢慢變軟，再放進大鍋裡翻炒。{name}站在旁邊安全的地方看，鍋裡的葉子沙沙作響，整間屋子都飄著香氣。阿姨一邊翻炒，一邊笑著說：「這裡面有你摘的葉子喔。」
傍晚，雲霧又飄回山頭。阿姨倒了一小杯金黃色的茶，先放涼一會兒，才遞給{name}。{name}小口小口喝著，茶香香甜甜的，一點也不苦。{he}望著窗外的茶園，悄悄對茶樹說：「明天，我還要來找一心二葉。」
en: One spring morning, {name} visited Auntie's home high in the mountains. Auntie had a big tea farm, with rows of green tea bushes rolling like waves up the hill and into the soft, white mist. The tea pickers carried bamboo baskets, and their fingers tapped the branches lightly, as if they were dancing.

"I want to pick tea too!" {name} said. Auntie smiled and handed {him} a small bamboo basket. {name} hurried between the bushes, grabbing every leaf in sight: big ones, small ones, yellow ones, green ones. Soon the basket was full, and {name} ran back, feeling very proud.

Auntie looked inside and touched the leaves. "These leaves are too old and tough. They would make the tea taste bitter." {name} stared at the full basket and frowned. All that work, and every leaf was the wrong kind. {name} felt like putting the basket down for good.

Auntie took {name} by the hand to a tea bush and pointed to the very top. "See the little curled bud at the tip, with two tender leaves beside it? We call that one bud, two leaves." The bud felt soft, and its tiny white hairs sparkled in the sunlight.

Auntie showed {name} how to do it: pinch gently with a thumb and finger, then lift. Pop! Off it came. {name} tried, but squeezed too hard and crushed the leaves. The next try only got one leaf. {name} took a deep breath, slowed down, and on the third try, picked a perfect bud with two leaves!

As the sun climbed higher, {name} searched bush by bush, no longer rushing to fill the basket. {his} fingers smelled green and fresh, and little drops of sweat appeared. A tea picker peeked into the basket and nodded. "Every one is lovely!" There was only a thin layer, yet it felt heavier than the morning's full basket.

In the afternoon, Auntie spread the tender leaves on a bamboo tray to soften, then tossed them in a big pan. {name} watched from a safe spot nearby. The leaves rustled in the pan, and the whole house filled with a sweet smell. "Some of these are the leaves you picked," Auntie said with a smile.

By evening, the mist drifted back over the mountain. Auntie poured a small cup of golden tea and let it cool before handing it to {name}. {name} took tiny sips. It tasted sweet and fragrant, not bitter at all. Looking out at the tea farm, {he} whispered, "Tomorrow, I'll find more buds with two leaves."

questions: {name}抱著滿滿一簍葉子跑回去，卻聽到葉子都不對，那時候{his}心裡是什麼感覺？
鍋裡的茶葉沙沙作響，整間屋子都香香的，你覺得那會是什麼樣的味道？
如果明天又去茶園找一心二葉，你還想在山上做些什麼？
zh.tip: 睡前一起躺著，用拇指和食指輕輕捏捏對方的指尖，像在採一心二葉一樣，每捏一下就小聲說一件今天喜歡的小事。

questions: When {name} ran back with a full basket and heard the leaves were the wrong kind, how do you think that felt?
The leaves rustled in the pan and the whole house smelled sweet. What do you imagine that smell was like?
If you went back to the tea farm tomorrow to find more buds, what else would you like to do on the mountain?
en.tip: Snuggle up at bedtime and take turns gently pinching each other's fingertips, like picking one bud, two leaves. With each little pinch, whisper one thing you liked about today.

zh: 下雨的星期六，{name}和媽媽搭捷運去外婆家。車廂裡暖烘烘的，窗外的城市像剛被雨水洗過，閃閃發亮。{name}對面坐著一位戴灰色帽子的老爺爺，正低著頭打瞌睡，腿邊靠著一把深綠色的長柄雨傘。
「下一站，公園站。」廣播一響，老爺爺猛然驚醒，慌慌張張地站起來，跟著人潮走出車門。{name}眨了眨眼，發現座位旁邊還靜靜躺著那把綠色雨傘。傘柄是木頭做的，雕成一隻小鳥的模樣。「媽媽，爺爺的傘忘了拿！」
媽媽一把拿起雨傘，牽緊{name}的手，趕在車門關上前跨上月台。月台上人山人海，到處是匆匆忙忙的腳步和滴著水的雨衣。那頂灰色帽子一下子就淹沒在人群裡，{name}踮起腳尖東張西望，心裡像打鼓一樣咚咚響。
「別急，我們看指標。」媽媽指著頭頂的黃色牌子。{name}一個字一個字念：「出口，往上。」兩人跟著箭頭踏上電扶梯，{name}乖乖握住扶手站穩，眼睛卻像小偵探一樣，仔細搜尋每一頂經過的帽子。
到了大廳，眼前竟然有四個出口！每條通道都擠得水洩不通。{name}急得直跺腳，忽然瞥見地上掉著一張皺巴巴的公園導覽圖。「爺爺剛剛手上拿的就是這個！」{name}抬頭一看，旁邊的箭頭寫著：二號出口，往公園。
媽媽把雨傘交給{name}，兩人刷卡出站，沿著長長的走廊快步前進。出口外嘩啦啦下著大雨，那位老爺爺正站在屋簷下，翻遍了每個口袋，眉頭皺成一團。「爺爺！您的雨傘！」{name}大聲喊，雙手把傘高高舉起。
老爺爺轉過身，眼睛一下子亮了起來。他小心翼翼地接過雨傘，用大拇指輕輕摸著那隻木頭小鳥。「這是我太太很多年前送我的禮物。」他笑著說，「她說這隻小鳥認得路，不管我把傘忘在哪裡，它都會飛回我身邊。」
老爺爺眨眨眼：「看來，它這次找了一位很厲害的小幫手帶路。」{name}忍不住咯咯笑。老爺爺撐開綠傘，揮揮手，慢慢走進雨中。回程的車廂裡，{name}靠在媽媽身邊，覺得整座城市的雨聲，都像在輕輕唱歌。
en: On a rainy Saturday, {name} and Mom rode the MRT to Grandma's house. The train car was warm and cozy, and the city outside sparkled as if the rain had scrubbed it clean. Across from {name} sat an old man in a gray hat, dozing, with a long dark green umbrella leaning against his knee.

"Next stop, Park Station," the speaker announced. The old man jolted awake, hurried to his feet, and shuffled out with the crowd. {name} blinked. The green umbrella was still lying on the seat. Its wooden handle was carved into the shape of a little bird. "Mom, he forgot his umbrella!"

Mom scooped up the umbrella, held {name}'s hand tight, and stepped onto the platform just before the doors slid shut. The platform was packed with rushing feet and dripping raincoats. The gray hat vanished into the crowd in a blink. {name} stood on tiptoe, peering everywhere, heart thumping like a drum.

"Don't worry. Let's follow the signs," Mom said, pointing to a yellow sign overhead. {name} read it slowly: "Exit. Up." They followed the arrow onto the escalator. {name} held the handrail and stood still, but {his} eyes darted around like a detective's, checking every hat that passed.

At the top, there were four exits! Every hallway was jammed with people. {name} stamped in frustration, then spotted a crumpled park map on the floor. "Grandpa was holding one just like this!" Right beside it, an arrow pointed the way: Exit 2, To the Park.

Mom handed the umbrella to {name}, and they tapped out and hurried down the long hallway. Outside, rain was pouring down. There stood the old man under the awning, patting every pocket, his forehead wrinkled with worry. "Sir! Your umbrella!" {name} called, holding it high with both hands.

The old man turned, and his eyes lit up. He took the umbrella gently and stroked the little wooden bird with his thumb. "My wife gave me this many years ago," he said with a smile. "She told me this bird knows the way. Wherever I leave it, it always flies back to me."

He gave a wink. "Looks like this time it found a very clever helper to lead the way." {name} giggled. The old man opened the green umbrella, waved goodbye, and strolled off into the rain. On the train ride back, {name} snuggled against Mom, and the whole rainy city seemed to be softly singing.

questions: 老爺爺下車、雨傘還留在座位上的時候，你覺得{name}心裡是什麼感覺？
在擠滿人的大廳裡，你最喜歡{name}發現導覽圖的那一刻，還是別的地方？為什麼？
如果那隻木頭小鳥真的會飛、會說話，你覺得它一路上會對{name}說什麼？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈後，可以一起輕聲聽聽窗外或想像中的雨聲，輪流悄悄說出「雨在唱什麼歌」。明天也可以一起畫一隻屬於自己的認路小鳥。

questions: When the old man got off and the umbrella was still on the seat, how do you think {name} felt?
In the crowded station, what was your favorite moment: finding the park map, or something else? What made it special?
If the little wooden bird could really fly and talk, what do you think it would say to {name} along the way?
en.tip: After lights out, listen together for the rain outside or imagine its sound, and take turns whispering what song the rain might be singing. Tomorrow you could draw your very own way-finding bird together.

zh: 科學展覽倒數三週，{name}決定研究「光線會怎麼影響綠豆芽」。{he}把二十四顆綠豆分進六個塑膠杯：兩杯放在窗邊曬太陽，兩杯放在檯燈下，另外兩杯鎖進教室後面的掃具櫃，讓它們在黑暗裡長大。其中一個杯子底部有道小裂縫，{name}本來想丟掉，最後還是捨不得，貼上膠帶，放到檯燈下湊合著用。
頭幾天，豆子爭先恐後地冒出白白的小芽，{name}每天一下課就衝去量高度，一筆一筆記在筆記本上。為了讓它們長得更快，{he}總是把杯子裡的水加得滿滿的。同學明浩探頭一看，笑著說：「你這不是種豆芽，是在煮綠豆湯吧！」大家哄堂大笑，{name}也跟著笑，卻一點也沒放在心上。
第二週的星期一，{name}打開掃具櫃，心一下子涼了半截。豆芽軟趴趴地倒在杯緣，根部發黑，還飄出一股酸味。窗邊和檯燈下的也好不到哪裡去，幾乎全都枯萎了。{name}盯著筆記本裡整整齊齊的數字，喉嚨一緊，差點想把整本撕掉，乾脆改做別的題目算了。
林老師走過來，沒有說什麼大道理，只是遞給{him}一枝紅筆。{name}深深吸了一口氣，把杯子一個一個端到桌上，仔細觀察。就在這時，{he}發現了一件怪事：那個貼著膠帶、有裂縫的杯子裡，竟然還有四株豆芽挺得直直的，綠油油地朝著檯燈伸懶腰。
{name}把杯子翻過來，看見底下的桌面濕了一小圈。原來多餘的水會從裂縫慢慢漏掉！其他杯子的水排不出去，根整天泡在水裡，根本喘不過氣來。{name}拿起紅筆，在筆記本上寫下：「失敗原因：水太多，杯底沒有洞。」接著又條理分明地列出第二次要改進的三件事。
這一次，{name}請林老師幫忙，在每個新杯子底下都鑽了小洞，墊上盤子，每天只澆一點點水。{he}依然天天測量、拍照，連明浩也忍不住跑來幫忙記錄。兩週後，窗邊的豆芽矮壯翠綠，檯燈下的稍微細一些，而櫃子裡的又高又瘦，黃澄澄的，像一群踮著腳找光的小孩。
展覽那天，{name}的海報分成兩半：左邊貼著第一次那排垂頭喪氣的豆芽照片，標題寫著「我搞砸了，也學到了」；右邊則是全新的成果。{name}從裂縫杯一路講到小洞，講得頭頭是道。說完後，教室安靜了一秒，接著響起全班最熱烈的掌聲，明浩拍得最用力。
en: With the science fair three weeks away, {name} chose a question: how does light change the way bean sprouts grow? {name} split twenty-four mung beans into six plastic cups. Two went on the sunny windowsill, two sat under a desk lamp, and two were tucked into the dark supply closet at the back of the classroom. One cup had a tiny crack in the bottom. {name} almost tossed it, then patched it with tape and put it under the lamp anyway.

For the first few days, the beans raced each other, poking out pale little shoots. Every recess, {name} hurried over with a ruler and logged each height in a notebook. Hoping to speed things up, {name} filled every cup to the brim with water. Ming-hao peeked in and grinned. "Are you growing sprouts or cooking bean soup?" The whole class roared, and {name} laughed too, not worried one bit.

Then came Monday of the second week. {name} opened the closet, and {his} heart sank. The sprouts drooped limply over the rims, their roots dark and slimy, giving off a sour smell. The window cups and lamp cups were no better; nearly everything had wilted. {name} stared at the neat columns of numbers, throat tight, half tempted to rip out every page and pick a brand-new project.

Ms. Lin walked over. She didn't give a speech. She simply handed {name} a red pen. Taking a deep breath, {name} carried the cups to a table one by one and examined them closely. That was when {he} noticed something odd. In the taped, cracked cup, four sprouts stood tall and bright green, stretching toward the lamp as if nothing had happened.

{name} flipped the cup over and found a small damp ring on the table. Extra water had been slowly leaking out through the crack! In the other cups, the water had nowhere to go, so the roots sat soaking all day and couldn't breathe. With the red pen, {name} wrote: "What went wrong: too much water, no holes in the cups." Below it, {he} listed three things to change.

This time, Ms. Lin helped {name} poke small holes in the bottom of each new cup, and every cup sat on a saucer. Just a splash of water each day. {name} still measured and snapped photos daily, and soon even Ming-hao was helping with the chart. Two weeks later, the window sprouts were short and sturdy, the lamp sprouts a bit thinner, and the closet sprouts tall, skinny, and yellow, like kids on tiptoe hunting for light.

On fair day, {name}'s poster had two halves. The left side showed the first batch, a row of sad, slumping sprouts, under the heading "I Messed Up, and I Learned." The right side showed the new results. {name} explained everything, from the cracked cup to the drainage holes. For one second the room was silent. Then came the loudest applause of the day, and Ming-hao clapped hardest of all.

questions: 打開掃具櫃、看到豆芽全倒下的那一刻，{name}心裡是什麼感覺？
如果你也能做一個屬於自己的實驗，你最想研究什麼？
櫃子裡又高又瘦的黃豆芽像踮著腳找光的小孩，你猜它們在黑暗裡會悄悄說些什麼？
zh.tip: 今晚熄燈前，一起小聲猜猜一顆綠豆要幾天才會冒出小芽；明天再找個小杯子，在杯底戳個洞，種幾顆看看。

questions: When {name} opened the closet and saw all the drooping sprouts, how did that moment feel?
If you could do an experiment of your very own, what would you want to find out?
The tall, yellow closet sprouts looked like kids on tiptoe hunting for light. What do you think they whispered to each other in the dark?
en.tip: Before lights out tonight, take quiet turns guessing how many days it takes a mung bean to sprout. Tomorrow, poke a hole in a small cup together and plant a few to find out.

zh: 傍晚，{name}跟著奶奶爬上燈塔的螺旋樓梯。一階、兩階、三階……{name}數到第一百零八階，終於氣喘吁吁地抵達頂端。奶奶拍拍膝蓋，笑著說：「年輕時我一口氣就衝上來了，現在膝蓋會唱歌。」窗外，太陽像一顆橘子糖，慢慢融進海裡，天空一點一點暗了下來。
燈塔頂端的小房間裡，有一張窄窄的床、一盞暖黃的檯燈，還有一扇圓圓的窗。{name}趴在窗邊，心裡有點空落落的：這裡離家好遠，連一點車聲都聽不到。只有海浪拍著礁石，嘩——嘩——，一遍又一遍，像有誰在遠方輕輕嘆氣。
奶奶按下開關，頭頂的大燈「喀」一聲亮了。一道金色的光束伸出窗外，慢慢掃過漆黑的海面，轉一圈，又轉一圈。「以前，照顧這盞燈就是我的工作。」奶奶替{name}蓋好被子，「每天晚上，我都守著它，讓迷路的船找到回家的方向。」
「有一年冬天，海上颳起大風雨，」奶奶的聲音低低柔柔的，「浪高得像一座座小山。有艘小漁船在黑暗中摸索，船上的年輕人急得團團轉。他看不見海岸，只看得見遠處一點光，忽明忽暗，忽明忽暗。」{name}目不轉睛地聽著，把被子拉到下巴。
「我整夜沒闔眼，一次又一次擦亮玻璃，讓光照得更遠。天快亮時，那艘小船終於平平安安地靠岸了。」奶奶眨眨眼，「那個年輕人爬上燈塔來道謝，手裡還捧著一條魚當謝禮，滴得我滿地都是水。」{name}忍不住噗哧一聲笑了出來。
「後來呢？」{name}問。奶奶從抽屜拿出一張泛黃的照片，上面是一位咧嘴大笑的年輕漁夫，懷裡抱著一條大魚。「後來啊，他每個星期都送魚來，送了整整一年。」奶奶輕聲說，「最後，他成了你的爺爺。」{name}睜大眼睛，原來這盞燈，曾經把爺爺帶回家。
光束又轉了一圈，掃過海面，掃過窗台，輕輕拂過{name}的被角。海浪還在唱，嘩——嘩——，越來越慢，越來越遠。這裡不再陌生了。{name}的眼皮愈來愈沉，彷彿自己也是一艘小船，在溫柔的光裡，安安穩穩地駛回了家。奶奶關上檯燈，輕聲說：「晚安。」
en: As evening fell, {name} followed Grandma up the winding stairs of the lighthouse. One step, two steps, three steps... {name} counted all the way to one hundred and eight before reaching the top, puffing and panting. Grandma patted her knees and chuckled. "When I was young, I raced up in one go. Now my knees sing on every step." Outside, the sun melted into the sea like an orange candy.

At the top was a tiny room with a narrow bed, a lamp glowing honey-yellow, and one round window. {name} leaned on the windowsill and felt a little hollow inside. Home was so far away, and there wasn't a single car to hear. There were only the waves against the rocks, hush, hush, over and over, like someone sighing softly far away.

Grandma flipped a switch, and the great lamp above clicked on. A golden beam stretched out across the dark water, sweeping slowly around, and around again. "Long ago, caring for this light was my job," Grandma said, tucking the blanket around {name}. "Every night I watched over it, so that lost ships could find their way home."

"One winter, a wild storm rolled across the sea," Grandma said, her voice low and gentle. "The waves rose like little mountains. A small fishing boat was groping through the darkness, and the young man aboard was frantic. He couldn't see the shore. All he could see was one faraway light, blinking on and off, on and off." {name} listened without blinking, blanket pulled up to the chin.

"I didn't close my eyes all night. I polished the glass again and again so the light would shine farther. Just before dawn, that little boat bumped safely against the dock." Grandma winked. "The young man climbed all the way up here to thank me, holding a fish as a gift. It dripped all over my floor." {name} burst out giggling.

"And then what?" {name} asked. Grandma took a faded photo from a drawer. It showed a young fisherman grinning from ear to ear, hugging an enormous fish. "Then he brought me a fish every single week, for a whole year," Grandma said softly. "In the end, he became your grandpa." {name}'s eyes went wide. This very light had once guided Grandpa home.

The beam swept around again, over the sea, over the windowsill, brushing gently across the corner of {name}'s blanket. The waves kept singing, hush, hush, slower and farther away. This place didn't feel strange anymore. {name}'s eyelids grew heavy, as if {he} were a little boat too, gliding safely home through the soft, warm light. Grandma switched off the lamp and whispered, "Goodnight."

questions: 如果你也爬完那一百零八階，趴在圓圓的窗邊，你最想先看什麼、聽什麼？
聽到那個捧著魚、滴得滿地是水的年輕漁夫，原來就是爺爺時，你心裡有什麼感覺？
如果你有一盞屬於自己的燈塔燈，你想讓它的光照到哪裡、照給誰看？
zh.tip: 今晚關燈後，和{name}一起輕輕發出海浪「嘩——嘩——」的聲音，一次比一次慢、一次比一次小。最後再悄悄分享一個家裡長輩年輕時的小故事。

questions: If you climbed all one hundred and eight steps and leaned on that round window, what would you want to see or hear first?
How did you feel when you found out the young fisherman with the dripping fish was really Grandpa?
If you had a lighthouse lamp of your own, where would you want its light to shine, and who would you want to see it?
en.tip: After the lights are off tonight, make soft wave sounds together with {name}, "hush, hush," a little slower and quieter each time. Then whisper one small story about a grown-up in your family when they were young.

zh: 今天天氣好晴朗。{name}和媽媽來到動物園。大象甩甩鼻子，長頸鹿點點頭。「哇，好熱鬧呀！」{name}開心地拍拍手。咦，那邊圍了好多人呢！
{name}踮起腳尖看。草地上有一隻貘媽媽。貘媽媽旁邊，躲著一隻小小貘。小小貘圓滾滾。身上一條一條，又一點一點。好像什麼呢？
飼養員阿姨笑著說：「小貘剛出生不久。牠還沒有名字喔。大家幫忙想一想！」小貘動動小鼻子。吱吱，吱吱。好像在說：「快幫我想！」
{name}歪著頭想。圓圓的，像皮球？不對不對。條紋的，像斑馬？不對不對。小貘翻個身，咕嚕咕嚕滾一圈。啪！躺平了。大家都笑了。
媽媽拿出小本子和蠟筆。{name}坐在長椅上，畫呀畫。綠色畫圓圈，深綠畫條紋。再點上小點點。咦，這是什麼？是一顆大西瓜！
{name}看看畫，又看看小貘。一條一條，一模一樣！{name}舉起畫說：「叫牠小西瓜！」小貘豎起小耳朵。吱吱，吱吱！
飼養員們都拍拍手。「小西瓜，好可愛！」「小西瓜，真好記！」阿姨把畫貼在牌子旁邊。小西瓜搖搖短尾巴，好像很喜歡。
