At lunch, they took the comic to Ms. Lin. She showed them how to tuck paper towels between the pages and press gently to soak up the juice. Then they stacked two heavy dictionaries on top. {name} swapped the towels page by page while Leo counted. They ate and guessed where Space Cat would fly next.

Before going home, they lifted the dictionaries. A faint orange mark was still there, but the cover lay flat, and Space Cat was smiling again. Leo packed it away and said, "Next time, I'll lend you book two." {name} grinned. "Deal. It goes in the folder, and the juice stays far away."

questions: 果汁噴到漫畫以後，{name}本來可以怎麼做？最後選擇了什麼？
{name}答應小樂之前，先想了什麼、做了什麼準備？
如果你答應了別人一件事，後來發現做不到，你會怎麼說？
zh.tip: 這個星期，和孩子一起練習「答應前先想一想」：每次要說「好」之前，先說出一個能做到的辦法。如果有約定沒做到，就一起練習說「對不起，我沒做到，我們可以怎麼補救？」

questions: After the juice spilled, what could {name} have done? What did {name} choose to do?
Before making the promise to Leo, what did {name} think about and do?
If you promised someone something and then couldn't do it, what would you say?
en.tip: This week, practice "think before you promise" together: before saying yes, name one way you'll make sure you can do it. If a promise slips, practice saying, "I'm sorry, I didn't do it. How can we make it right?"

zh: 動物園裡，太陽暖暖的。斑馬媽媽生了寶寶。寶寶叫點點。咦？點點沒有條紋。白白的身子上，是一顆一顆黑黑的圓點。
斑馬們圍過來看。「咦，怎麼是點點？」「斑馬不是都有條紋嗎？」小斑馬條條說：「你跟我們不一樣。」條條跑開了。點點低下頭，站在角落。
這天，{name}和家人來到動物園。{name}牽著家人的手，來看斑馬。{name}看見了點點。點點一個人，靜靜站著。{name}輕輕揮手：「嗨，點點！」
{name}睜大眼睛說：「哇，好漂亮！你的點點，像天上的星星。一閃一閃，亮晶晶！」點點抬起頭。「真的嗎？」點點的耳朵，開心地動一動。
長頸鹿們慢慢走過來。長頸鹿身上，也有花花的斑點。「點點，來玩躲貓貓！」點點跑呀跑，躲進長頸鹿的長腿中間。斑點靠著斑點，一點也看不出來。
條條來找點點。「點點在哪裡？」找呀找，找呀找，就是找不到。點點跳出來，條條笑了：「哇，你躲得好棒！」{name}拍拍手：「點點好厲害！」
條條小聲說：「點點，我也想玩。」點點說：「好呀，一起來！」條條躲進高高的草裡。條紋像小草，一條一條，也看不見了。大家都笑了。
太陽下山了，{name}要回家了。斑馬媽媽說：「條紋好看，點點也好看。」點點和條條靠在一起。{name}揮揮手：「下次見，小星星！」
en: The zoo was warm and sunny. Mama Zebra had a baby. The baby was named Dot. But look! Dot had no stripes. Dot had round black spots instead.
The zebras came to look. "Spots? Why spots?" "Zebras have stripes!" Little Stripe said, "You are not like us." Then Stripe ran off. Dot hung low and stood alone.
That day, {name} came to the zoo. {name} held a grown-up's hand. They went to see the zebras. {name} saw Dot standing all alone. {name} waved softly. "Hi, Dot!"
{name}'s eyes grew wide. "Wow, so pretty! Your spots look like stars. Twinkle, twinkle, shiny bright!" Dot looked up. "Really?" Dot's ears wiggled happily.
The giraffes came walking slowly. Giraffes have patches and spots too! "Dot, let's play hide-and-seek!" Dot ran and ran. Dot hid between their long legs. Spots next to spots. Nobody could see Dot!
Stripe came looking. "Where is Dot?" Stripe looked and looked. Stripe could not find Dot. Dot jumped out. Stripe laughed. "Wow, great hiding!" {name} clapped. "Dot is so good!"
Stripe said softly, "Dot, can I play too?" Dot said, "Yes! Come play!" Stripe hid in the tall grass. Stripes looked like grass. Now Stripe was hidden too! Everyone laughed.
The sun went down. Time for {name} to go home. Mama Zebra said, "Stripes are lovely. Spots are lovely too." Dot and Stripe snuggled close. {name} waved. "See you, little star!"

questions: 點點一個人站在角落時，{name}做了什麼？
最後條條為什麼想跟點點一起玩？
你和好朋友有哪裡不一樣？那裡有什麼好玩的地方？
zh.tip: 這週玩一個「不一樣真好」遊戲：每天找一個家人或朋友和你不一樣的地方，一起說「這樣也很棒！」

questions: What did {name} do when Dot stood all alone?
Why did Stripe want to play with Dot at the end?
How are you different from a friend? What is fun about that?
en.tip: This week, play a "Different Is Great" game: each day, name one way a family member or friend is different from you, and say together, "That's wonderful too!"

zh: 在學校的美勞角，有一盒蠟筆。盒子打開了，喀啦喀啦！紅色跳出來說：「紅色最棒！」「我是蘋果，我是草莓！」紅色挺起胸膛。
藍色也跳出來。「不對不對，藍色最棒！」「我是天空，我是大海！」紅色說：「紅色！」藍色說：「藍色！」吵吵鬧鬧，嘰嘰喳喳。
小小的紫色，躲在角落。紫色又短又圓。紅色噗哧笑了：「你好短喔！」紫色低下頭。紫色小聲說：「我也想畫畫……」
這時候，{name}來了。{name}看看紅色，看看藍色。再看看角落的紫色。{name}輕輕拿起紫色。「短短的，好好拿喔！」紫色笑了，眼睛亮亮的。
{name}把大家都拿起來。紅色、橘色、黃色。綠色、藍色、紫色。一枝、兩枝、三枝……六枝蠟筆，排排站好。「要畫什麼呀？」大家問。
紅色先畫，刷刷刷，彎彎的紅。橘色跟上，刷刷刷，彎彎的橘。黃色、綠色，刷刷刷。藍色也來，刷刷刷。
最後輪到紫色。紫色好緊張。{name}握著紫色，慢慢畫。刷——刷——彎彎的紫。哇！一道彩虹出現了！
紅色看呆了：「少了誰都不行耶！」藍色點點頭：「大家都好漂亮！」紅色對紫色說：「你畫得真好。」六枝蠟筆手牽手，回到盒子裡。{name}笑咪咪，彩虹也笑咪咪。
en: In the art corner at school sits a box of crayons. Click, clack! The lid pops open. Red jumps out. "Red is best!" "I'm apples! I'm strawberries!" Red puffs up proud.
Blue jumps out too. "No, no! Blue is best!" "I'm the sky! I'm the sea!" "Red!" says Red. "Blue!" says Blue. Chatter, chatter, natter, natter!
Little Purple hides in the corner. Purple is short and round. Red giggles. "You're so tiny!" Purple looks down. "I want to draw too," Purple whispers.
Then {name} comes over. {name} looks at Red. {name} looks at Blue. Then {name} spots Purple. {name} picks Purple up gently. "Short and round. Just right for my hand!" Purple gives a bright smile.
{name} picks everyone up. Red, orange, yellow. Green, blue, purple. One, two, three... six crayons in a row. "What will we draw?" they all ask.
Red goes first. Swish, swish! A red curve. Orange follows. Swish, swish! An orange curve. Yellow and Green. Swish, swish! Blue joins in. Swish, swish!
Purple goes last. Purple feels a little shy. {name} holds Purple and draws slowly. Swish... swish... a purple curve. Wow! A rainbow appears!
Red stares. "We need every color!" Blue nods. "We all look so pretty!" Red tells Purple, "You drew so well." Six crayons hold hands and hop back in the box. {name} smiles. The rainbow smiles too.

questions: 紅色笑紫色很短的時候，紫色有什麼感覺？{name}做了什麼？
如果彩虹少了一個顏色，會變成什麼樣子？
你和你的好朋友，有什麼地方不一樣？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子一起畫彩虹，每畫一個顏色，就說一句「我喜歡你的＿＿」，輪流說出家人或朋友身上不一樣的優點。

questions: How did Purple feel when Red laughed? What did {name} do?
What would the rainbow look like if one color were missing?
How are you and your best friend different?
en.tip: This week, draw a rainbow together. With each color, take turns saying "I like your ___" about something different and special in a family member or friend.

title.en: {name}, Wei, and the Chalk Password Circles

zh: 星期五下午，林老師帶全班到公園上戶外課。草地綠油油的，溜滑梯旁邊還有一大片平平的空地。{name}的新朋友阿威坐著輪椅，雙手轉動輪子，跟在大家旁邊。他瞇起眼睛笑著說：「今天的風好舒服喔！」
休息時間一到，同學們大喊：「來玩鬼抓人！」大家一下子就跑得遠遠的。阿威停在樹蔭下，看著別人跑來跑去，手指輕輕敲著輪子。小傑回頭笑著說：「阿威太慢了，當鬼一定抓不到人啦！」幾個同學也跟著笑起來。
{name}停下腳步，看見阿威低下頭。{name}走回樹下，站到阿威身邊，對小傑說：「阿威才不慢，他是用輪子走路，我們是用腳走路，只是不一樣而已。」小傑抓抓頭，不好意思地跑開了。{name}轉頭問：「我們自己想一個新遊戲，好不好？」
阿威的眼睛亮了起來，從背包裡拿出一盒彩色粉筆。「我們可以在地上畫圈圈！」兩個人在空地上畫了好多大圓圈，每個都大到輪椅能整台停進去，有紅的、黃的、藍的。可是{name}皺起眉頭：「圈圈畫好了，接下來要怎麼玩呢？」
阿威想了想，說：「每個圈圈都有一句密碼。想進圈圈，就要大聲說出密碼！」他們把密碼寫在圈圈旁邊：紅圈是「香蕉跳舞」，黃圈是「月亮打噴嚏」。站在圈裡的人很安全，鬼只能抓圈外的人，而且每個圈只能待到數完五下。
第一次試玩，由{name}當鬼。阿威推著輪子，在圈圈之間轉來轉去，大喊：「月亮打噴嚏！」就穩穩停進黃圈。{name}怎麼追都追不上，笑得肚子好痛。原來輪椅轉彎好快，阿威還想出一招，倒退著滑進圈圈，真是厲害極了。
笑聲傳到溜滑梯那邊。小傑和其他同學跑過來問：「你們在玩什麼？看起來好好玩！」說話慢慢的小美想加入，最愛吃酸梅的阿豪也想加入。阿威說：「每個人都可以發明一句新密碼喔！」大家安靜地等小美想好，她說出「烏龜開飛機」，全班都拍手叫好。
那天下午，空地上的圈圈越畫越多，全班都玩在一起。小傑還跑來對阿威說：「下次你可以教我倒退滑進圈圈那一招嗎？」準備回學校前，林老師笑著看看滿地彩色的圈圈。{name}和阿威用力擊掌：「下星期，我們再發明新密碼！」
en: On Friday afternoon, Ms. Lin took the whole class to the park for an outdoor lesson. The grass was bright green, and beside the slide was a wide, flat open space. {name}'s new friend Wei rolled along in his wheelchair, turning the wheels with both hands. "The breeze feels so nice today!" he said with a smile.

When break time came, everyone shouted, "Let's play tag!" In a flash, the kids raced far away. Wei stayed in the shade of a tree, watching them run and tapping his wheels with his fingers. Jay looked back and laughed. "Wei's too slow! He could never catch anyone!" A few kids laughed too.

{name} stopped running and saw Wei look down at his lap. {name} walked back to the tree, stood right beside Wei, and said to Jay, "Wei isn't slow. He gets around on wheels, and we get around on feet. That's just different." Jay scratched his head and ran off, a little embarrassed. Then {name} turned to Wei. "Want to make up our own game?"

Wei's eyes lit up. He pulled a box of colored chalk from his backpack. "We can draw circles on the ground!" Together they drew lots of big circles, red, yellow, and blue, each one wide enough for a whole wheelchair to fit inside. But {name} frowned. "Okay, we have circles. Now how do we play?"

Wei thought for a moment. "Every circle has a password. To get inside, you have to shout it out!" They wrote the passwords next to the circles: red was "Dancing Bananas," and yellow was "The Moon Sneezes." Inside a circle, you were safe. The tagger could only catch people outside, and you could only stay in a circle for a count of five.

For the first round, {name} was the tagger. Wei zipped between the circles, spinning his wheels, and shouted, "The Moon Sneezes!" Then he stopped neatly inside the yellow circle. No matter how hard {name} chased, Wei was always a little faster. His wheelchair could turn so quickly! He even invented a move, rolling backward into a circle. {name} laughed so hard it hurt.

The laughter floated over to the slide. Jay and the others ran up. "What are you playing? It looks like so much fun!" May, who spoke slowly, wanted to join, and so did Hao, who loved sour plums. "Everyone can invent a new password!" said Wei. The kids waited quietly while May thought. "Turtles Flying Planes," she said, and everyone clapped.

All afternoon, more and more circles appeared, and the whole class played together. Jay even came over to Wei. "Next time, could you teach me your backward move?" Before they headed back to school, Ms. Lin smiled at all the colorful circles covering the ground. {name} and Wei gave each other a big high five. "Next week, let's invent even more passwords!"

questions: 小傑笑阿威的時候，{name}做了什麼？你覺得阿威那時候有什麼感覺？
故事裡每個人都有不一樣的地方，像阿威用輪椅、小美說話慢慢的。你和朋友有哪些不一樣的地方，讓一起玩變得更有趣？
如果你看到有人被留在旁邊沒有人陪他玩，你會怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這個星期和孩子一起在家門口或公園畫粉筆圈，發明一個「每個人都能玩」的新遊戲，並請每位家人輪流想一句好笑的密碼。

questions: What did {name} do when Jay laughed at Wei? How do you think Wei felt then?
Everyone in the story was different in some way, like Wei using a wheelchair and May speaking slowly. What is different about you and your friends that makes playing together more fun?
If you saw someone left out with no one to play with, what would you do?
en.tip: This week, draw chalk circles outside with your child and invent a new game that everyone can play, letting each family member take a turn making up a silly password.

title.en: {name}, Pip the Bat, and the Moon Picnic

zh: 滿月升上夜空的那晚，森林要舉辦一年一度的月光野餐。{name}幫獾奶奶提著野餐籃，走在隊伍裡。蝙蝠皮皮從樹梢飛下來，想加入鳥兒那一邊。麻雀啾啾歪著頭說：「你全身毛茸茸，沒有羽毛，怎麼會是鳥？」皮皮只好轉向松鼠，松鼠卻甩甩尾巴：「你有翅膀耶，不是我們地上的動物。」
草地上鋪了兩條野餐墊，鳥兒一條，走獸一條。皮皮孤零零地倒掛在中間的樹枝上，和大家格格不入。小兔看他倒著啃無花果，忍不住咯咯笑：「你連吃東西都顛倒！」皮皮把翅膀收得緊緊的。{name}看見了，拿著一串葡萄走到樹下，坐在皮皮正下方，把葡萄舉高：「我們一起吃吧。」
「你為什麼總是倒掛著？」{name}好奇地問。皮皮眨眨小眼睛：「這樣起飛最快呀。我的眼睛不太好，可是我會發出很細很細的叫聲，聽回音就知道前面有什麼。」{name}閉上眼睛試了試，只聽見自己的心跳，兩個人都笑了。另一頭，大家正圍著獾奶奶的螢火蟲燈籠，唱著月亮歌。
忽然，一大片烏雲吞沒了月亮，夜風一吹，燈籠裡來作客的螢火蟲紛紛飛回家，燈光熄滅了。四周頓時伸手不見五指。麻雀撞到兔子，松鼠踩到刺蝟，「哎喲」聲此起彼落。大家七嘴八舌，有人說往左，有人說往右。獾奶奶緊緊牽著{name}的手：「別急，我們先停下來。」
黑暗中傳來細細的「吱、吱」聲。「我看不見路，可是聽得見！」皮皮說。{name}立刻大聲說：「大家跟著皮皮走，一個牽一個！」獾奶奶牽著{name}，{name}牽著小兔，松鼠抓住麻雀的翅膀尖，排成長長一列。皮皮低低飛在前面：「左邊有大樹，前面有樹根，抬腳！」刺蝟抬得太高，差點踢到自己的鼻子，大家都笑了。
不久，腳下踩到熟悉的軟苔蘚，大家回到了森林的空地。烏雲散開，月亮又探出頭來。麻雀啾啾低著頭飛到皮皮身邊：「對不起，我們說你不是鳥。可是今晚，要不是你和我們不一樣，大家還在黑漆漆的林子裡打轉呢。」小兔也紅著臉說：「倒著吃無花果，其實挺酷的。」
下一次月光野餐，兩條野餐墊緊緊靠在一起，中間那根樹枝成了最熱門的位子。鳥兒和走獸都擠到皮皮底下。松鼠和麻雀異口同聲地說：「皮皮有翅膀也有毛，兩邊都是他的家！」皮皮倒掛著笑：「從我這裡看，你們每個都很特別。」{name}躺在草地上，和大家一起倒過頭來看星星。
en: On the night of the full moon, the forest held its yearly Moon Picnic. {name} helped Grandma Badger carry the picnic basket down the path. Pip the Bat swooped from a treetop to join the birds. Chirp the Sparrow tilted her head. "You're fuzzy and you have no feathers. You can't be a bird!" So Pip flew to the squirrels, but Squirrel flicked his tail. "You have wings. You're not a ground animal like us."

Two blankets were spread on the grass, one for the birds and one for the furry animals. Pip hung upside down from a branch in between, all alone. Little Rabbit giggled as he nibbled a fig. "You even eat backwards!" Pip wrapped his wings tight. {name} noticed, picked up a bunch of grapes, sat right under Pip's branch, and held them up. "Want to share?"

"Why do you always hang upside down?" asked {name}. Pip blinked. "It's the fastest way to take off! My eyes aren't great, but I make tiny squeaks and listen for the echoes. They tell me what's ahead." {name} closed {his} eyes and tried it, but heard only a thumping heartbeat. They both laughed. Across the clearing, everyone sang moon songs around Grandma Badger's firefly lantern.

Suddenly a huge cloud swallowed the moon. A breeze blew, and the visiting fireflies drifted home. The lantern went dark. It was so black nobody could see a paw in front of their nose. Sparrow bumped Rabbit, Squirrel stepped on Hedgehog, and "Ouch!" popped up everywhere. Some said go left, some said go right. Grandma Badger held {name}'s hand. "Let's stop and stay calm."

Then came a soft "squeak, squeak." "I can't see the way, but I can hear it!" said Pip. "Everyone, follow Pip and hold on to each other!" called {name}. Grandma Badger held {name}, {name} held Rabbit, and Squirrel grabbed Sparrow's wingtip. Pip flew low ahead. "Big tree on the left! Root ahead, lift your feet!" Hedgehog lifted so high he nearly kicked his own nose, and everyone laughed.

Soon soft, familiar moss squished underfoot. They were back in the clearing. The cloud slid away, and the moon peeked out again. Chirp flew to Pip with her head bowed. "I'm sorry we said you weren't a bird. Tonight, if you weren't different from us, we'd still be lost." Rabbit blushed. "And eating figs upside down is actually pretty cool."

At the next Moon Picnic, the two blankets were pushed right together, and the branch in the middle became the best seat around. Birds and furry animals all crowded beneath it. "Pip has wings and fur, so both sides are his home!" said Squirrel and Sparrow together. Pip grinned upside down. "From up here, every one of you looks special." {name} lay back and tipped {his} head to see the stars upside down too.

questions: 皮皮被大家說「不是鳥也不是走獸」時，{name}做了什麼？
皮皮跟大家哪裡不一樣？這些不一樣後來怎麼幫助了大家？
如果你看到有人因為不一樣被笑，你可以怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這個星期每天晚餐時，家人輪流說一件「我和別人不一樣，而且我喜歡」的事，再請大家說一句欣賞的話。

questions: What did {name} do when the others said Pip wasn't a bird or a ground animal?
How was Pip different, and how did that difference help everyone?
If you saw someone being laughed at for being different, what could you do?
en.tip: Every dinner this week, take turns sharing one way you're different from others that you like, and have everyone answer with one kind word about it.

title.en: {name} and the Sea Turtle on the Beach

zh: 早上，太陽暖暖的。{name}和爸爸來到海邊。今天，大家要一起淨灘。爸爸拿出兩雙手套，還有一個大袋子。「我們來當海邊小幫手！」爸爸說。{name}戴上手套，開心地跳了一下。海浪嘩啦嘩啦，好像在說歡迎。
沙灘上有好多寶貝。有亮亮的貝殼，也有小螃蟹。{name}蹲下來看，小螃蟹橫著走開了。可是，沙灘上也有瓶蓋和吸管。{name}把它們撿起來，放進袋子裡。爸爸說：「海邊是大家的，我們讓它乾乾淨淨。」
走到大石頭旁邊，{name}停下腳步。「爸爸，你看！」一隻大海龜趴在沙上休息。牠的殼圓圓的，像一頂綠色的帽子。海龜旁邊，有一堆塑膠袋。風一吹，袋子沙沙地響。{name}好想跑過去，爸爸輕輕牽住{his}手。
這時，穿著制服的林阿姨走過來。她是照顧這片海邊的保育員。「我們站遠一點看，海龜才會安心。」林阿姨小聲說。{name}和爸爸往後退了幾步。海龜慢慢眨眨眼睛，好像在說謝謝。
「為什麼塑膠袋在牠旁邊？」{name}問。林阿姨指著大海說：「袋子漂在水裡，很像水母。海龜愛吃水母，有時會認錯。」{name}睜大了眼睛。「那我們把袋子撿走，海龜就不會認錯了！」
林阿姨給{name}一支長長的夾子。{name}一個一個夾起塑膠袋。爸爸撐開袋口，幫忙接住。旁邊還有一條舊漁網。還有三個瓶子和一隻破拖鞋。{name}夾呀夾，額頭冒出小汗珠。不知不覺，大袋子變得鼓鼓的。
「哇，整袋都滿了！」爸爸說。沙灘又變得乾乾淨淨。海龜動了動前腳，慢慢往前爬。牠滑過濕濕的沙子，游進藍藍的海裡。{name}輕輕揮手：「再見，海龜！」海龜的頭冒出水面一下，又不見了。
回家前，{name}把袋子交給林阿姨。林阿姨把垃圾分好，放進回收桶。「謝謝你，小保育員。」她笑著說。{name}拿出自己的水壺，喝了一口水。海水閃閃發亮，好美好美。「我們下次再來好嗎？」{name}問。爸爸握握{his}手：「好啊！」
en: The morning sun felt warm. {name} and Dad walked to the beach. Today was a beach clean-up day! Dad handed out two pairs of gloves and a big bag. "Let's be beach helpers!" said Dad. The waves went swish, swish, like a happy hello.

The sand had so many treasures. There were shiny shells and a tiny crab. {name} crouched down to look. The crab scuttled sideways. But there were bottle caps and straws, too. {name} put them in the bag. "The beach belongs to everyone," Dad said. "Let's keep it clean."

Near a big rock, {name} stopped. "Dad, look!" A large sea turtle was resting on the sand. Its shell was round, like a green hat. Beside it lay a pile of plastic bags. They rustled in the wind. {name} wanted to run closer. Dad gently held {his} hand.

A ranger in a uniform walked over. Her name was Ranger Lin. She looked after this beach. "Let's watch from back here," she whispered. "Then the turtle feels safe." {name} and Dad took a few steps back. The turtle blinked slowly, as if to say thank you.

"Why are bags next to the turtle?" asked {name}. Ranger Lin pointed at the sea. "Bags floating in water look like jellyfish. Turtles love jellyfish. Sometimes they get mixed up." {name} opened {his} eyes wide. "Then let's take the bags away!"

Ranger Lin gave {name} a long grabber. {name} picked up the bags, one by one. Dad held the big bag open. There was an old fishing net, too. There were three bottles and one torn flip-flop. {name} worked hard. Soon the big bag was round and full.

"Wow, the whole bag is full!" said Dad. The sand looked clean again. The turtle moved its front flippers. It crawled forward slowly. Then it slid over the wet sand into the clean blue sea. "Bye, turtle!" {name} waved. Its head popped up once, then it was gone.

Before going home, {name} gave the bag to Ranger Lin. She sorted the trash into the right bins. "Thank you, little ranger," she said with a smile. {name} took a sip from {his} own water bottle. The sea sparkled, bright and beautiful. "Can we come back soon?" {name} asked. Dad squeezed {his} hand. "Yes, we can!"

questions: {name}看到海龜旁邊的塑膠袋時，做了什麼事？
為什麼大家要站遠一點看海龜呢？
在家裡或公園，你可以做什麼小事來照顧大自然？
zh.tip: 這個星期出門時，和孩子一起帶上自己的水壺和購物袋，回家後一起把垃圾分類，並說一句「我們讓地球乾乾淨淨」。

questions: What did {name} do when {he} saw the plastic bags near the turtle?
Why did everyone watch the turtle from farther away?
What small thing could you do at home or at the park to take care of nature?
en.tip: This week, bring your own water bottles and a reusable bag when you go out together. At home, sort the trash side by side and say, "Let's keep our earth clean."

zh: 公園中央有一棵老榕樹，長長的氣根像鬍鬚一樣從枝幹垂下來。早上，林奶奶和朋友坐在樹蔭下泡茶聊天；下午，孩子們在粗樹枝上的鞦韆盪來盪去。麻雀一家住在樹頂，啾啾叫個不停，松鼠豆豆則把小果子藏在樹洞裡。
有一天，樹幹旁的公布欄貼了一張新公告。麻雀媽媽飛下來看，羽毛都蓬了起來：「鎮上想在這裡蓋停車場，下星期要開會，決定要不要把老榕樹移走！」豆豆急得在樹枝上團團轉：「那我們的家怎麼辦呢？」
這時，{name}和媽媽來公園散步。{name}蹲在樹根旁，好奇地看著一隻慢慢爬的蝸牛，看完又小心地把牠放回葉子上。豆豆看見了，小聲對麻雀媽媽說：「這個孩子對小生命好溫柔，也許能幫我們。」{name}讀完公告，皺起眉頭想了想。
「這棵樹是大家的，可是很多人沒發現它每天給了我們什麼。」{name}說：「我們來讓大家看見吧！」那天下午，{name}和媽媽撿起樹下的飲料罐和紙屑，分好類放進資源回收桶。麻雀們叼走散落的塑膠繩，豆豆把落葉推成一堆一堆。
接下來幾天，{name}每天帶著筆記本來觀察。{he}記下：早上有六位爺爺奶奶來乘涼，中午樹下比太陽底下涼快好多，傍晚有十二隻麻雀回巢。{name}還畫了樹洞裡的豆豆，在旁邊寫上：「這裡是豆豆的家。」
開會那天，太陽好大。鎮長和大人們站在公園的空地上，熱得一直擦汗。{name}舉起筆記本，有禮貌地問：「請大家到老榕樹下開會，好嗎？」大家走進樹蔭裡，一陣涼風吹過，鎮長忍不住說：「哇，真舒服！」
{name}一頁一頁念出筆記。林奶奶點點頭：「我在這棵樹下坐了三十年了。」孩子們拉著鞦韆繩，麻雀一家在頭頂啾啾唱歌，豆豆從樹洞探出頭，抱著一顆小果子。鎮長抬頭看了好久，笑著說：「原來這棵樹每天都在照顧我們。」
後來，停車場蓋好了，可是它繞著老榕樹圍成一個大圓圈，中間留著一片綠草地。{name}在樹旁的木牌上畫了麻雀和松鼠。每次離開公園前，{name}都會撿起一片紙屑，輕輕摸摸樹幹說：「明天見，老榕樹。我們會讓這裡一直這麼漂亮。」
en: In the middle of the park stood an old banyan tree, its long roots hanging down like a beard. In the mornings, Grandma Lin and her friends sipped tea in its shade. In the afternoons, children swung on the swings tied to its thick branches. A sparrow family chirped in the treetop, and Dou Dou the squirrel hid little fruits in a hollow.

One day, a new notice appeared on the board beside the trunk. Mother Sparrow fluttered down to read it, and her feathers puffed up. "The town wants to build a parking lot here! Next week they will meet to decide whether to move the old tree away!" Dou Dou scurried in circles. "But what about our home?"

Just then, {name} came for a walk with Mom. {name} crouched by the roots and watched a snail creep slowly along, then gently set it back on a leaf. Dou Dou whispered to Mother Sparrow, "That child is kind to little creatures. Maybe we can get some help." {name} read the notice and frowned, thinking hard.

"This tree belongs to everyone, but lots of people don't notice what it gives us every day," said {name}. "Let's show them!" That afternoon, {name} and Mom picked up cans and paper scraps under the tree and sorted them into the recycling bins. The sparrows carried off loose plastic string, and Dou Dou pushed the fallen leaves into tidy piles.

For the next few days, {name} came with a notebook to watch and learn. {he} wrote down that six grandparents rested there each morning, that the shade felt much cooler than the noon sun, and that twelve sparrows flew home at sunset. {name} also drew Dou Dou in the hollow and wrote, "This is Dou Dou's home."

On the day of the meeting, the sun blazed. The mayor and the grown-ups stood in the open part of the park, wiping sweat from their foreheads. {name} held up the notebook and asked politely, "Could we have the meeting under the old banyan tree, please?" Everyone stepped into the shade. A cool breeze drifted by. "Ahh," said the mayor. "That feels wonderful!"

{name} read the notebook aloud, page by page. Grandma Lin nodded. "I've sat under this tree for thirty years." Children held the swing ropes, the sparrows chirped overhead, and Dou Dou peeked out of the hollow, hugging a little fruit. The mayor gazed up for a long time and smiled. "So this tree has been taking care of us every single day."

Later, the parking lot was built, but it curved around the old banyan tree in a big circle, with a patch of green grass in the middle. {name} painted sparrows and a squirrel on a wooden sign beside the trunk. Before leaving the park each day, {name} picked up one scrap of paper, patted the bark, and said, "See you tomorrow, old tree. We'll keep it beautiful here."

questions: {name}做了哪些事，讓大家發現老榕樹每天給了我們什麼？
在我們家附近的公園或街上，有哪些樹、花或小動物是大家一起分享的？
如果你看到地上有垃圾，或是遇到一隻小蟲，你會怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這個星期去公園時，和孩子玩「離開前撿一片」的小遊戲：一起撿起一件垃圾並丟進正確的回收桶，再對一棵樹說聲「明天見」。

questions: What did {name} do to help everyone see what the old tree gives each day?
Which trees, flowers, or little animals near our home do we all share?
What would you do if you saw trash on the ground or met a tiny bug?
en.tip: On your next park visit this week, play "pick one before we go": together, pick up one piece of trash, put it in the right bin, and say "see you tomorrow" to a tree.

zh: 太陽出來了，暖暖的。{name}和奶奶到陽台。奶奶拿來小花盆。一盆、兩盆、三盆。還有小小的花苗。「我們來種花吧！」{name}拍拍手，笑嘻嘻。
挖呀挖，挖個小洞洞。放進一棵小花苗。拍拍土，拍拍土。黃色的花，紅色的花，還有白色的花。小花站好了，好像在說謝謝。
奶奶拿來小水壺。「小花口渴了。」滴答、滴答。{name}倒一點點，剛剛好。水還剩一些。{name}倒給旁邊的大盆栽。奶奶笑著說：「一滴都沒浪費！」
花苗的塑膠盒空了。{name}撿起來，走呀走。放進回收桶，咚！地上的土也掃一掃。沙沙、沙沙。陽台乾乾淨淨，小花漂漂亮亮。
嗡嗡、嗡嗡！誰來了？是小蜜蜂！一隻、兩隻，飛呀飛。{name}好想摸一摸。奶奶輕輕說：「小手安靜，眼睛看看。蜜蜂也是我們的朋友。」
{name}把小手合起來。安安靜靜，看呀看。蜜蜂停在黃色花上。扭一扭，跳跳舞。再飛到紅色花上。扭一扭，跳跳舞。好像小小的黃色朋友。
咦？一隻蜜蜂飛到奶奶身上！停在奶奶的花圍裙上。奶奶不動，{name}也不動。蜜蜂聞一聞，嗡？不是真的花呀！蜜蜂飛走了。{name}和奶奶咯咯笑。
蜜蜂吃飽了，嗡嗡飛遠了。「蜜蜂再見，明天再來喔！」小花給大家看，也給蜜蜂吃。{name}靠著奶奶，看著小花。陽台香香的，心裡暖暖的。
en: The sun is up. It feels warm. {name} and Grandma go to the balcony. Grandma brings little pots. One, two, three! And tiny baby flowers. "Let's plant!" {name} claps and giggles.
Dig, dig, dig. A little hole. In goes a baby flower. Pat, pat, pat the soil. Yellow flowers. Red flowers. White flowers too. They stand up tall. They look so happy.

Grandma brings a small watering can. "The flowers are thirsty." Drip, drop, drip. {name} pours just a little. Some water is left. {name} gives it to the big plant. Grandma smiles. "Not one drop wasted!"
The plastic flower box is empty. {name} picks it up. Walk, walk, walk. Into the recycling bin. Clunk! Now sweep the spilled soil. Swish, swish. The balcony is clean. The flowers look pretty.
Buzz, buzz! Who is here? Little bees! One, two, flying around. {name} wants to touch them. Grandma whispers, "Quiet hands. Watching eyes. Bees are our friends too."
{name} folds {his} hands. Still and quiet, {name} watches. A bee lands on a yellow flower. Wiggle, wiggle, dance! Then off to a red flower. Wiggle, wiggle, dance! Like tiny yellow friends.
Oh! A bee lands on Grandma! It sits on her flowery apron. Grandma stays still. {name} stays still too. Sniff, sniff. Buzz? That's not a real flower! Off it goes. {name} and Grandma giggle.
The bees are full now. Buzz, buzz, away they fly. "Bye-bye, bees! Come back tomorrow!" The flowers are for everyone. For people, and for bees. {name} snuggles Grandma. The balcony smells sweet.

questions: 蜜蜂來的時候，{name}的小手怎麼做？
水剩下來時，{name}把水給了誰？你會怎麼做？
如果你在外面看到小蟲或小花，你會怎麼看看它們？
zh.tip: 這週帶孩子幫家裡的一盆植物澆水，一起說「一點點就夠囉」，再把用完的東西放進正確的回收桶。

questions: What did {name} do with {his} hands when the bees came?
Who got the leftover water? What would you do with it?
If you see a little bug or flower outside, how would you look at it?
en.tip: This week, let your child water one plant at home, saying together "Just a little is enough," then put any empty packaging in the right recycling bin.

zh: 那年夏天熱得像蒸籠，城市好幾個星期沒下一滴雨。晚間新聞裡，水庫露出龜裂的泥土，像一塊烤焦的餅乾。{name}盯著螢幕，眉頭緊皺。隔天一到學校，{name}就把好朋友阿哲拉到走廊角落：「水是大家的，我們得做點什麼。從今天起，我們是雨滴偵探！」阿哲推了推眼鏡，鄭重點頭：「收到，搭檔。」
偵探的第一件任務，是追蹤每一滴漏掉的水。兩人帶著筆記本和碼錶，巡遍每間廁所和洗手台。三樓的水龍頭滴答滴答，一分鐘竟然滴了四十二下！阿哲算了算，忍不住咋舌：「一整天下來，夠裝好幾桶了。」{name}把位置一一記下，交給工友林伯伯。林伯伯拿出扳手，三兩下就修好了：「眼明手快，名不虛傳！」
可是有一個滴水聲始終找不到源頭。每到下午，操場邊就傳來「咚、咚、咚」，神出鬼沒。兩個偵探躡手躡腳地循聲搜尋，繞過花圃，終於在體育館後面發現真相：原來是冷氣機的排水管，正把乾淨的水一滴一滴灑在水泥地上，白白流走。{name}眼睛一亮：「這不是漏水，是寶藏！」
林伯伯在排水管下放了一個有蓋子的大水桶，又在屋簷落水管旁擺了幾個，等待難得的雨。「蓋子要蓋好，蚊子才不會來搗蛋。每個星期我來倒水、刷乾淨。」第一次開蓋時，一隻小蝸牛正慢吞吞爬在桶邊。{name}輕輕把牠捧起，放回濕潤的葉子上。桶裡的水拿去澆花，垂頭喪氣的向日葵又挺起了腰。
接著是最難的任務：洗澡。{name}和阿哲畫了一張張海報，上面有隻抱著沙漏的企鵝，寫著「兩分鐘洗澡挑戰！」貼海報時，兩人發現排水溝口卡著一個塑膠袋，便撿起來丟進回收桶。可是，{name}自己最愛在浴室裡唱歌，一首接一首，常常洗到手指皺成葡萄乾。
那天晚上，{name}站在蓮蓬頭下猶豫了一會兒，然後挑了一首最短最快的歌。歌還沒唱完，泡泡已經沖得乾乾淨淨。{name}裹著毛巾衝出浴室，得意洋洋地宣布：「一分五十八秒！」媽媽笑得前仰後合：「這是我聽過最快的演唱會。」後來全班都加入挑戰，連校長也報了名。
秋風吹起的那天，校長在朝會上公布結果：修好的水龍頭、冷氣水桶和兩分鐘洗澡，加起來省下的水，足足能裝滿一座游泳池！全場歡聲雷動。{name}和阿哲走到花圃，向日葵在陽光下搖頭晃腦，林伯伯正在刷洗水桶。阿哲問：「下一個案子是什麼？」{name}望著天空笑了：「讓這裡一直這麼漂亮。」
en: That summer the city baked like an oven, and not a single drop of rain fell for weeks. On the evening news, the reservoir showed cracked mud, like a burnt cookie. {name} frowned at the screen. The next morning, {name} pulled best friend Jay into a corner of the hallway. "Water belongs to everyone. We have to do something. From today on, we're rain detectives!" Jay pushed up his glasses and nodded solemnly. "Got it, partner."

Their first mission was to track down every wasted drip. Armed with a notebook and a stopwatch, they inspected every bathroom and sink. A faucet on the third floor went drip, drip, drip, forty-two times in one minute! Jay did the math and whistled. "That's buckets and buckets by tonight." {name} wrote down each leak and handed the list to Mr. Lin, the janitor. With a wrench and a few twists, he fixed them all. "Sharp eyes, detectives!"

But one dripping sound stayed a mystery. Every afternoon, a steady plunk, plunk, plunk echoed near the playground, then vanished. The two detectives tiptoed after it, around the flower beds, until they found the culprit behind the gym: the air conditioner's drain pipe was dribbling clean water onto the concrete, where it simply disappeared. {name}'s eyes lit up. "That's not a leak. That's treasure!"

Mr. Lin set a big covered bucket under the pipe and a few more beside the rain gutters, ready for any rain. "Keep the lids on so mosquitoes can't sneak in. I'll empty and scrub them every week." When they first lifted a lid, a tiny snail was creeping along the rim. {name} gently scooped it up and set it on a damp leaf. The saved water went to the garden, and the droopy sunflowers stood tall again.

Next came the hardest mission of all: showers. {name} and Jay drew posters of a penguin hugging an hourglass, with the words "Two-Minute Shower Challenge!" While hanging them up, they spotted a plastic bag stuck in a drain and dropped it into the recycling bin. There was just one problem. {name} loved singing in the shower, song after song, until {his} fingers wrinkled like raisins.

That night, {name} stood under the showerhead, hesitated, then picked the shortest, fastest song ever written. The bubbles were rinsed away before the last line. {name} burst out wrapped in a towel and announced, "One minute, fifty-eight seconds!" Mom laughed so hard she had to sit down. "That's the quickest concert I've ever heard." Soon the whole class joined the challenge, and even the principal signed up.

On the first breezy day of autumn, the principal shared the results at morning assembly. The fixed faucets, the air-conditioner buckets, and the two-minute showers had saved enough water to fill a whole swimming pool! Everyone cheered. {name} and Jay walked to the garden, where the sunflowers nodded in the sun and Mr. Lin was scrubbing a bucket. "So, what's our next case?" Jay asked. {name} looked up at the sky and smiled. "Keeping this place beautiful."

questions: {name}和阿哲發現冷氣機的滴水時，想到了什麼好辦法？
{name}看到桶邊的小蝸牛時，是怎麼做的？為什麼？
在我們家裡，你覺得哪裡可能有「偷偷流走」的水？
zh.tip: 這個星期和孩子一起當「雨滴偵探」，巡一遍家裡的水龍頭，再挑一首兩分鐘的歌當作洗澡計時歌。

questions: What clever idea did {name} and Jay have when they found the air conditioner dripping?
What did {name} do with the little snail on the bucket, and why?
Where in our home do you think water might be sneaking away?
en.tip: This week, be rain detectives together and check every faucet at home, then pick a two-minute song to use as your shower timer.

zh: 爺爺在院子種蘿蔔。爺爺每天澆澆水。太陽暖暖照呀照。蘿蔔長呀長，長呀長。變成好大好大的蘿蔔！爺爺笑呵呵：「今天煮蘿蔔湯！」
爺爺抓住綠葉子。嘿喲！嘿喲！拔呀拔，拔呀拔。蘿蔔動也不動。爺爺擦擦汗說：「太大了，拔不動。」奶奶跑過來：「我來幫忙！」
奶奶拉著爺爺。爺爺拉著蘿蔔。嘿喲！嘿喲！拔呀拔，拔呀拔。蘿蔔還是不動。{name}拍拍小手說：「我也來幫忙！」
{name}拉著奶奶。奶奶拉著爺爺。爺爺拉著蘿蔔。嘿喲！嘿喲！還是拔不動。{name}想一想：「我們叫小狗來！」爺爺點點頭：「好主意！」
汪汪！汪汪！小狗跑來了。小狗拉著{name}。大家一起拉。嘿喲！嘿喲！蘿蔔動了一點點。小狗搖搖尾巴：「汪汪！叫小貓來！」
喵喵！喵喵！小貓跑來了。小貓拉著小狗。嘿喲！嘿喲！還差一點點。吱吱！小老鼠探出頭：「我也能幫忙嗎？」大家說：「當然可以！」
小老鼠拉著小貓。一、二、三！嘿喲！嘿喲！啵！蘿蔔拔出來了！大家咕咚坐下。咚！大家哈哈笑，笑呀笑。
大家排隊輪流洗蘿蔔。嘩啦啦，嘩啦啦！奶奶煮好蘿蔔湯。香噴噴，熱呼呼。一人一碗，大家都有。小老鼠也有小小碗。小老鼠吱吱說：「好多手，湯好好喝！」
en: Grandpa planted a turnip seed. He watered it every day. The sun shone warm. The turnip grew and grew. It grew big, big, BIG! "Turnip soup today!" said Grandpa.
Grandpa held the green leaves. Heave-ho! Heave-ho! He pulled and pulled. The turnip did not move. "Too big for one," said Grandpa. "I'll help!" said Grandma.
Grandma pulled Grandpa. Grandpa pulled the turnip. Heave-ho! Heave-ho! They pulled and pulled. It still did not move. {name} clapped. "I can help too!"
{name} pulled Grandma. Grandma pulled Grandpa. Grandpa pulled the turnip. Heave-ho! Still stuck. {name} had an idea. "Let's call the dog!" "Good idea!" said Grandpa.
Woof, woof! The dog ran over. The dog pulled {name}. Everyone pulled together. Heave-ho! The turnip wiggled a tiny bit. The dog wagged. "Woof! Let's call the cat!"
Meow, meow! The cat came too. The cat pulled the dog. Heave-ho! Almost there! Squeak, squeak! A tiny mouse peeked out. "May I help?" "Yes, you may!" said everyone.
The mouse pulled the cat. One, two, three! Heave-ho! Heave-ho! POP! Out came the turnip! Everyone tumbled down. Thump! They laughed and laughed.
They took turns washing the turnip. Splish, splash! Grandma made the soup. It smelled so good. One bowl for each friend. A tiny bowl for the mouse. "Many hands," squeaked the mouse. "Yummy soup!"

questions: 爺爺一個人拔不動蘿蔔時，{name}做了什麼？
最小的小老鼠也來幫忙，結果怎麼樣了？
你和家人一起做過什麼事情呢？
zh.tip: 這週找一件家事一起完成，例如大家輪流把玩具放回箱子，並一起喊「嘿喲！」完成後擊掌慶祝。

questions: What did {name} do when Grandpa couldn't pull the turnip alone?
The tiny mouse helped too. What happened then?
What is something you like doing together with your family?
en.tip: This week, pick one chore to do together, like taking turns putting toys in the box while saying "Heave-ho!" Finish with a big high five.

zh: 雨停了，森林裡亮晶晶的。{name}和奶奶出來散步。葉子上還掛著小水珠。泥土聞起來香香的。奶奶說：「慢慢走，小心滑喔。」{name}點點頭，牽著奶奶的手。忽然，{he}聽見細細的聲音。
{name}蹲下來，跪在軟軟的草地上看。原來是一群小螞蟻！牠們的家在一棵老樹下。可是老樹前面有一個大水窪。水窪把回家的路擋住了。螞蟻隊長阿點著急地說：「我們回不了家了！」小螞蟻們都圍了過來。
阿點看見一片長長的葉子。「我把它推過去當橋！」阿點用力推呀推。葉子動也不動。阿點又用力拉呀拉。葉子還是不動。阿點累得坐下來，嘆了一口氣。{name}輕輕說：「一隻螞蟻好小喔。」
最小的螞蟻豆豆舉起腳。「我有一個點子！」大家都安靜下來聽。豆豆說：「我們一起抬葉子。每隻抬一點點就好。」大螞蟻說：「我力氣大，我抬中間。」小螞蟻說：「我跑得快，我來帶路。」阿點笑了：「好主意，大家一起來！」
螞蟻們排成一排。「一、二、三，抬！」長葉子慢慢離開了地面。牠們一步一步往前走。「左邊一點！」豆豆喊。大家就一起往左走。葉子的一頭碰到水窪對面了。可是另一頭晃來晃去。
「{name}，可以幫忙嗎？」阿點抬頭問。{name}看看奶奶。奶奶微笑說：「去吧，輕輕的就好。」{name}伸出一根手指頭。{he}輕輕按住葉子的一頭。葉子不晃了。它穩穩的，像一座小橋。
「大家輪流過橋喔！」阿點說。小螞蟻先走，大螞蟻在後面。搬食物的螞蟻走中間。有一隻螞蟻滑了一下。旁邊的螞蟻馬上扶住牠。大家一隻跟著一隻，走成一條長長的線。
最後一隻螞蟻也到家了。大家開心地跳起來。阿點說：「謝謝豆豆的點子，謝謝{name}的手指頭！」豆豆說：「也謝謝每一隻抬葉子的螞蟻！」螞蟻們一起分享甜甜的果子。{name}牽起奶奶的手，笑著說：「我們一起做到了！」
en: The rain had stopped, and the forest sparkled. {name} went for a walk with Grandma. Raindrops hung on every leaf. "Walk slowly, it's slippery," said Grandma. {name} nodded and held her hand. Then {he} heard tiny voices.
{name} knelt down on the soft grass to look. It was a group of little ants! Their home was under an old tree. But a big puddle sat right in the way. "We can't get home!" cried Dot, the ant leader.

Dot spotted a long, thin leaf. "I'll push it across for a bridge!" Dot pushed and pushed. The leaf didn't move. Dot pulled and pulled. It still didn't move. Dot sat down with a sigh. "One ant is very small," {name} said gently.

Then the tiniest ant, Bean, waved a leg. "I have an idea!" Everyone went quiet to listen. "Let's lift the leaf together. Each of us carries a little bit." A big ant said, "I'm strong. I'll take the middle." A small ant said, "I'm fast. I'll lead the way." Dot smiled. "Great plan!"

The ants stood in a row. "One, two, three, lift!" Slowly, the long leaf rose up. Step by step, they carried it forward. "A little to the left!" Bean called. Everyone moved left. One end reached the other side. But the other end wobbled.

"{name}, can you help?" Dot asked. {name} looked at Grandma. "Go ahead, just be gentle," she said with a smile. {name} reached out one finger and pressed the end of the leaf softly. The wobbling stopped. Now it was a steady little bridge.

"Take turns crossing!" said Dot. The little ants went first. The big ants came last. Ants carrying food walked in the middle. One ant slipped a bit. Right away, its neighbor held it up. One by one, they marched in a long, happy line.

Soon the last ant was home. Everyone jumped for joy. "Thank you, Bean, for the idea! Thank you, {name}, for your finger!" said Dot. "And thanks to every ant who lifted!" said Bean. The ants shared a sweet berry. {name} squeezed Grandma's hand. "We did it together!"

questions: 阿點一個人推不動葉子時，豆豆想到了什麼好點子？
螞蟻們過橋時是怎麼輪流、怎麼互相幫忙的？
你有沒有和家人一起完成一件事？那時你負責做什麼？
zh.tip: 這週找一件需要很多雙手的家事，例如一起摺棉被或收玩具，先請每個人說說自己的點子，再分工完成，最後一起說「我們一起做到了！」。

questions: When Dot couldn't move the leaf alone, what idea did Bean have?
How did the ants take turns and help each other while crossing the bridge?
What is something you did together with your family? What was your job?
en.tip: This week, pick a chore that needs many hands, like folding a blanket or tidying toys. Let everyone share an idea first, split the jobs, then cheer together: "We did it together!"

zh: 星期一早上，林老師宣布：「這個月，我們班要演一齣戲，叫做《森林裡的大雨》！」教室裡立刻熱鬧起來。佳佳舉手說想當兔子公主，大明大聲說要演勇敢的老熊，好多同學都搶著要當主角。
第一次排練，大家全擠在講台上。佳佳說兔子應該先出場，大明說老熊才最重要。有人搶台詞，有人搶道具樹，吵得像一窩小麻雀。{name}抱著劇本站在旁邊，看見坐在角落的小宇低著頭，一句話也沒說。
林老師拍拍手，可是大家還在吵。{name}深吸一口氣，走到中間說：「我們這樣吵，戲永遠排不完。要不要每個人輪流說一個點子？有人說的時候，其他人先安靜聽。」大家互相看了看，終於點點頭，圍成一個圓圈坐下。
佳佳說兔子可以跳一段舞，大明說老熊可以帶森林裡的動物躲雨。輪到小宇時，他小小聲地說：「下雨的聲音……可以用豆子做。」大家都愣住了。{name}輕輕問：「小宇，你可以示範給我們看嗎？」
小宇從抽屜拿出一個紙盒，倒進一把綠豆，慢慢左右搖晃。沙沙、沙沙，聽起來真的像雨落在樹葉上！接著他抖動一張大厚紙板，轟隆隆，像遠方傳來的雷聲。大家睜大眼睛，教室裡第一次這麼安靜。
「太酷了！」大明用力拍手。大家決定請小宇負責音效，還要畫一大張森林背景。可是背景紙比黑板還長，{name}一個人拉不開，顏料也塗不完。佳佳跑來壓住一角，大明幫忙拿刷子，大家輪流塗上綠色的樹和灰色的雲。
演出那天，台下坐滿了家長。兔子跳舞，老熊說台詞，{name}和同學們一起扮演搖擺的大樹。當小宇的豆子盒沙沙響起，厚紙板又轟隆一聲，台下的小朋友都驚呼：「真的下雨了！」
掌聲響起時，{name}跑到後台，拉著小宇的手走到前面。全班手牽著手排成一排，一起彎腰鞠躬。小宇紅著臉，笑得好開心。佳佳小聲說：「下次演戲，我們還要先聽聽每個人的點子。」
en: On Monday morning, Ms. Lin made an announcement. "This month, our class is putting on a play called The Big Rain in the Forest!" The room buzzed at once. Jia wanted to be the Bunny Princess, Daming wanted to be the brave Old Bear, and almost everyone wanted to be the star.

At the first rehearsal, everyone crowded onto the stage. Jia said the bunny should come out first. Daming said the bear mattered most. Kids grabbed lines and tugged at the paper trees, chirping like a nest of noisy sparrows. Holding the script, {name} noticed Yu sitting quietly in the corner, saying nothing at all.

Ms. Lin clapped her hands, but the arguing went on. {name} took a deep breath and stepped into the middle. "If we keep fighting, we'll never finish. What if each person shares one idea, and everyone else listens?" The kids looked at each other, then nodded and sat down in a circle.

Jia said the bunny could do a little dance. Daming said the bear could lead the forest animals out of the rain. When it was Yu's turn, he whispered, "We could make the rain sound with beans." Everyone blinked. {name} asked gently, "Yu, can you show us?"

Yu took a cardboard box from his desk, poured in a handful of dried beans, and tilted it slowly. Shhh, shhh. It sounded just like rain on leaves! Then he wobbled a big sheet of thick cardboard. Rumble, rumble, like faraway thunder. For the first time all day, the room was completely quiet.

"That's so cool!" Daming cheered. The class asked Yu to be in charge of sound effects. They also needed a forest backdrop, but the paper was longer than the whiteboard. {name} couldn't spread it out alone. Jia held one corner, Daming passed the brushes, and everyone took turns painting green trees and gray clouds.

On the day of the show, the room was full of families. The bunny danced, the bear said his lines, and {name} swayed with classmates as the forest trees. When Yu's bean box went shhh and the cardboard went rumble, the little kids in the audience gasped, "It's really raining!"

As the clapping began, {name} hurried backstage, took Yu's hand, and led him to the front. The whole class held hands in one long line and bowed together. Yu's cheeks turned pink, and his smile was huge. Jia whispered, "Next time, let's hear everyone's ideas first."

questions: 大家吵成一團的時候，{name}想出了什麼辦法？後來發生了什麼事？
小宇平常很安靜，但他的點子讓戲變得更好。你身邊有沒有很安靜、卻很厲害的朋友？
你曾經和別人一起完成一件一個人做不到的事嗎？那時候大家怎麼幫忙？
zh.tip: 這個星期吃晚餐時，玩「每人一個點子」：一起計畫週末要做的一件小事，每個家人輪流說一個想法，其他人先安靜聽完再說話。

questions: When everyone was arguing, what idea did {name} have? What happened next?
Yu was quiet, but his idea made the play better. Do you know a quiet friend who is great at something?
Have you ever done something with others that would be too big to do alone? How did everyone help?
en.tip: This week at dinner, play "One Idea Each": plan a small weekend activity together, with each family member sharing one idea while everyone else listens until they finish.

zh: 「我們要蓋全世界最雄偉的雪堡！」{name}揮舞著筆記本，上面畫著四座塔樓和一道拱門。小屋前的院子鋪滿新雪，像一塊剛出爐的奶油蛋糕。林叔叔在門廊上鏟雪，笑著說：「大建築師，只能在院子裡蓋喔！」小葵、阿哲和小表弟豆豆立刻戴好手套，摩拳擦掌。
「阿哲堆左邊！小葵堆右邊！豆豆去搬雪！」{name}發號施令，像個指揮千軍萬馬的將軍。大家手忙腳亂地把雪拍成牆，牆才長到膝蓋高，就「噗」一聲垮了。第二堵牆歪歪扭扭，第三堵被冷風一吹，碎成一地雪粉，豆豆的帽子上頂著一座小雪山。
「圖一定沒錯，是你們堆得不夠用力！」{name}跺著腳說。小葵張開嘴，又把話吞了回去。阿哲低頭踢著雪。豆豆吸著鼻子，小聲問：「可以休息一下嗎？」院子安靜得只剩風聲。{name}看看大家悶悶不樂的臉，再看看筆記本上那座漂亮卻孤零零的雪堡，心裡像被雪球砸了一下。
{name}深深吸了一口冰涼的空氣，闔上筆記本。「小葵，你剛剛想說什麼？」小葵眼睛一亮：「我奶奶教過我做雪磚！」她抓起豆豆的小沙桶，把雪一層層塞進去、壓緊，再「啪」地倒扣在地上。一塊方方正正、硬梆梆的雪磚誕生了。「哇，像真的磚頭！」{name}忍不住讚嘆。
阿哲也鼓起勇氣：「風一直從那邊吹來，牆才會倒，我們需要擋風的東西。」他在院子角落繞來繞去，忽然指著一座圓滾滾的大雪丘。大家用手套撥開雪，竟露出一排排整齊的木頭，原來是林叔叔堆好的柴堆！林叔叔點點頭：「借你們用，別拆就好。」
這一次，大家分工合作。{name}和小葵裝雪壓桶，豆豆把雪磚排好，阿哲用碎雪塞滿縫隙。手痠了就輪流交換，誰的磚頭歪了，旁邊的人馬上伸手扶正。連剛才垮掉的那堆雪，也成了最好用的材料。雪堡靠著柴堆一層層長高，風怎麼吹都文風不動。
最後一塊雪磚，{name}本來想自己放，卻轉身遞給豆豆：「你排得最整齊，你來！」豆豆踮起腳尖，把它放上牆頂。大家歡呼著鑽進雪堡，裡面寬敞得連林叔叔都擠得進來，還端來了熱可可。{name}翻開筆記本，在雪堡旁畫上五個小人，寫下：「我們的城堡。」
en: "We're going to build the most magnificent snow fort in the world!" {name} waved a notebook covered in sketches of four towers and a grand arch. The yard in front of the cabin was buried in fresh snow, smooth as frosting on a cake. Uncle Lin, shoveling the porch, grinned. "Okay, master builder, just keep it in the yard!" Kui, Jer, and little cousin Dou pulled on their mittens, ready to work.

"Jer, build the left side! Kui, the right! Dou, carry snow!" {name} barked orders like a general commanding an army. Everyone scrambled to pat the snow into a wall. It reached their knees, then flumped over. The second wall leaned like a sleepy giraffe. The third crumbled in a gust of wind, leaving a tiny snow mountain perched on Dou's hat.

"My plan is perfect. You're just not pushing hard enough!" {name} stamped a boot. Kui opened her mouth, then closed it. Jer kicked at the snow. Dou sniffled and whispered, "Can we take a break?" The yard went quiet except for the wind. {name} looked at the gloomy faces, then at the beautiful, lonely fort in the notebook, and felt as if a snowball had landed right in the chest.

{name} took a deep breath of icy air and shut the notebook. "Kui, what were you going to say?" Kui's eyes lit up. "My grandma taught me how to make snow bricks!" She grabbed Dou's little sand bucket, packed it tight layer by layer, then flipped it over with a thump. Out slid a hard, perfectly square brick. "Whoa, it's like a real brick!" {name} said, amazed.

Jer spoke up too. "The wind keeps blowing from over there. That's why the walls fall. We need something to block it." He wandered around the corner of the yard and pointed at a big, round mound of snow. Everyone brushed it with their mittens and uncovered neat rows of logs. It was Uncle Lin's woodpile! "You can borrow it," Uncle Lin called. "Just don't take it apart."

This time, everyone had a job. {name} and Kui filled and packed the bucket, Dou lined up the bricks, and Jer stuffed loose snow into the cracks. When arms got tired, they swapped jobs. If a brick wobbled, someone reached out to steady it. Even the snow from the fallen walls turned out to be perfect for packing. Leaning on the woodpile, the fort rose layer by layer, and the wind couldn't budge it.

{name} reached for the last brick, then held it out to Dou instead. "You line them up the best. You do it!" Dou stood on tiptoe and set it on top. Cheering, everyone crawled inside. The fort was so roomy that even Uncle Lin squeezed in, carrying mugs of hot cocoa. {name} opened the notebook, drew five little people beside the fort, and wrote, "Our Castle."

questions: {name}一個人指揮大家的時候，雪牆發生了什麼事？後來改變了什麼，雪堡才蓋成功？
小葵和阿哲各自想到了什麼好點子？你覺得你的朋友或家人有什麼你沒有的本領？
{name}為什麼把最後一塊雪磚交給豆豆？如果是你，你會怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這週找一件全家一起完成的小任務（像搭積木城堡或做晚餐），開始前請每個人先說一個點子，再一起決定怎麼分工、輪流做。

questions: What happened to the walls when {name} was giving all the orders? What changed so the fort could finally stand?
What good ideas did Kui and Jer have? What is something a friend or family member can do that you can't?
Why did {name} give the last brick to Dou? What would you have done?
en.tip: This week, pick a small family project, like building a block castle or making dinner. Before starting, have everyone share one idea, then decide together how to split the jobs and take turns.

title.zh: 麻雀的窩和烏鴉的對不起

zh: 春天的早晨，{name}和奶奶沿著森林小徑散步。高高的橡樹上，麻雀正忙著蓋新家。她來回飛了好多趟，嘴裡叼著一根根細樹枝，一層一層排成圓圓的小碗。「再一個下午就蓋好了！」麻雀開心地啾啾叫。
這時，烏鴉急急忙忙飛了過來。「呱！呱！今天一定要把窩蓋好，我還差好多樹枝！」他東張西望，一眼看見麻雀的窩，就一口氣叼走了好幾根樹枝，連問都沒問一聲，又咻地飛到旁邊的松樹上。
麻雀叼著新樹枝回來，一看，窩缺了一大塊，風從破洞呼呼灌進來。她的羽毛蓬了起來，眼眶也紅了。{name}踮起腳尖，輕聲問：「你還好嗎？」麻雀低著頭說：「我好難過，也好生氣。那些樹枝是我一根一根找來的。」
{name}想了想，說：「要不要告訴烏鴉，你心裡是什麼感覺？」麻雀深吸一口氣，飛到松樹上。「烏鴉，你拿走我的樹枝，我覺得自己的辛苦一下子不見了，心裡又酸又痛。」烏鴉愣住了，黑黑的翅膀慢慢垂了下來。
烏鴉看看自己的窩，又看看麻雀破了洞的窩。他一句話也沒說，就飛走了。過了好一會兒，他叼著樹枝回來，一根也沒少，還多帶了一小撮軟綿綿的羽毛。「對不起，我太著急了，只想到自己。這些羽毛可以讓你的窩更溫暖。」
麻雀看著那撮羽毛，卻沒有馬上開口。她小聲對{name}說：「我心裡好像壓著一顆石頭，好重喔。」{name}撿起地上的一顆小石頭，緊緊握在手心。「一直握著好累喔。」說完，{name}把石頭輕輕放在地上，手一下子就輕鬆了。
麻雀想了很久，終於點點頭，飛到烏鴉面前。「你拿走樹枝，真的讓我很難過。可是你已經道歉，也拿回來了，我原諒你。下次要先問我，好嗎？」烏鴉用力點頭：「呱！我答應你。」麻雀拍拍翅膀，覺得全身輕飄飄的。
整個下午，兩隻鳥一起找樹枝，{name}在樹下幫忙指出哪裡有掉落的細枝。傍晚，夕陽把樹葉染成金黃色，橡樹上和松樹上的兩個新窩遙遙相望，一個大、一個小。奶奶牽起{name}的手準備回家，樹上傳來啾啾和呱呱的道別聲。
en: One spring morning, {name} and Grandma went for a walk along the forest path. High up in an oak tree, Sparrow was busy building a new home. She flew back and forth with tiny twigs in her beak, weaving them into a round little bowl. "Just one more afternoon!" she chirped happily.

Just then, Crow came flapping by in a great hurry. "Caw! Caw! My nest must be done today, and I still need lots of twigs!" He looked around and spotted Sparrow's nest. Without asking, he grabbed a whole beakful of her twigs and zoomed off to the pine tree next door.

When Sparrow came back with a new twig, a big piece of her nest was gone, and the wind whistled through the hole. Her feathers puffed up, and her eyes grew teary. {name} stood on tiptoe and asked softly, "Are you okay?" Sparrow sniffed. "I'm sad and angry. I found every one of those twigs."

{name} thought for a moment. "Maybe you could tell Crow how you feel?" Sparrow took a deep breath and flew to the pine tree. "Crow, when you took my twigs, it felt like all my hard work just vanished. It made my heart ache." Crow froze, and his wings slowly drooped.

Crow looked at his own nest, then at Sparrow's broken one. Without a word, he flew away. After a while, he came back carrying every twig, plus a tuft of soft, fluffy feathers. "I'm sorry. I was in such a rush that I only thought about me. These feathers will keep your nest warm."

Sparrow stared at the feathers but didn't answer right away. She whispered to {name}, "It feels like there's a heavy stone inside me." {name} picked up a small pebble and squeezed it tight. "Holding on is tiring." Then {name} set the pebble gently on the ground and wiggled empty fingers. "Much lighter!"

Sparrow thought for a long time. At last, she nodded and flew to Crow. "Taking my twigs really hurt. But you said sorry and brought them back, so I forgive you. Next time, please ask first, okay?" Crow nodded hard. "Caw! I promise." Sparrow fluttered her wings and felt light as air.

All afternoon, the two birds gathered twigs together, while {name} pointed out fallen sticks below. By evening, the sunset turned the leaves gold, and two new nests faced each other across the gap, one in the oak and one in the pine, one big and one small. As Grandma took {name}'s hand to head home, chirps and caws called goodbye from the trees.

questions: 麻雀是怎麼告訴烏鴉她的感覺的？烏鴉聽了以後做了什麼？
{name}握著小石頭再放下來，你覺得那像是麻雀心裡的什麼？
如果有朋友拿走你的東西，後來跟你說對不起，你會怎麼說、怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這週練習一句話：「你那樣做，我覺得＿＿＿；謝謝你道歉，我原諒你。」也可以和孩子玩「握石頭、放石頭」的小遊戲，聊聊放下生氣後的輕鬆感覺。

questions: How did Sparrow tell Crow how she felt? What did Crow do after he heard it?
When {name} held the pebble and then put it down, what do you think it was like for Sparrow?
If a friend took something of yours and then said sorry, what would you say and do?
en.tip: This week, practice one phrase together: "When you did that, I felt ___. Thank you for saying sorry; I forgive you." You can also play the "hold the pebble, drop the pebble" game and talk about how letting go of anger feels lighter.

zh: 星期一的國語課，林老師說要玩「童年趣事大放送」，每個人分享一件小時候的糗事。教室裡笑聲此起彼落。輪到米洛時，他眼睛一亮，指著{name}大聲說：「我要分享{name}的！幼兒園演戲那天，{name}從頭打嗝到尾，我們都叫{he}『打嗝隊長』！」全班哄堂大笑，還有人故意「嗝」了一聲。
{name}的耳朵嗡嗡作響，胸口像被什麼緊緊揪住。{he}低頭盯著鉛筆盒，假裝在找橡皮擦，其實什麼也看不進去。下課時，幾個同學經過座位旁，也學著「嗝、嗝」叫。午餐時間，{name}端著餐盒躲進圖書館的角落，一口飯嚼了好久，怎麼也吞不下去。
接下來好幾天，{name}都刻意避開米洛。米洛在走廊揮手，{name}轉身就走；分組做實驗時，{name}悄悄換到別組。兩人的座位只隔一條走道，卻好像隔了一整片海洋。夜裡，{name}心裡沉甸甸的，像書包裝滿了石頭，怎麼放也放不下。{he}忍不住想：為什麼讓我最難受的，偏偏是最好的朋友？
星期五早上，米洛走上講台，雙手緊握，聲音有點發抖：「老師，我可以說一件事嗎？」全班安靜下來。「我讀幼兒園時，以為膠水是牛奶糖，偷偷舔了一大口，所以大家叫我『膠水大王』。」教室響起一陣驚呼和笑聲，米洛的耳朵紅得像番茄。他深吸一口氣：「星期一我把{name}的綽號說出來，是我不對。請大家以後別再叫了。」
下課鐘一響，米洛在籃球架旁找到{name}。他沒有嬉皮笑臉，而是認認真真地說：「對不起。我以為那只是好笑的回憶，沒想到會讓你這麼難過。」{name}沉默了好一會兒，才慢慢開口：「大家笑的時候，我好想縮成一顆小豆子消失。那天我一個人在圖書館吃午餐，覺得好丟臉。那種感覺，真的很不好受。」
米洛沒有替自己找藉口，只是用力點點頭：「我懂了。以後跟你有關的事，我一定先問你。」{name}看著他，心裡那袋石頭好像一顆一顆滾了出去。{he}忽然發現，一直生氣其實好累。「好吧，我原諒你。」{name}伸出小指：「不過，我們的祕密，要留在我們兩個之間。」米洛立刻勾住：「一言為定！」
從那天起，他們做了一個「祕密罐子」：好笑又有點丟臉的回憶都放進去，除非兩個人都點頭，才能拿出來分享。放學時走過操場，{name}突然「嗝」了一聲。米洛瞪大眼睛，{name}卻先噗哧笑了：「這個，我准你笑。」兩人的笑聲飄過操場，比從前更響亮，也更懂得小心珍惜彼此。
en: On Monday, Ms. Lin started a game called Funny Memory Share. Everyone told a silly story from when they were little, and giggles bounced around the classroom. When it was Milo's turn, his eyes lit up. He pointed at {name} and announced, "I'll tell one about {name}! In the preschool play, {name} hiccupped the whole time. We called {him} Captain Hiccup!" The class roared with laughter, and someone let out a fake "hic!"

{name}'s ears buzzed, and something squeezed tight inside {his} chest. Staring at the pencil case, {name} pretended to hunt for an eraser but couldn't see a thing. At recess, a few kids walked past going "hic, hic." At lunch, {name} carried a tray to a quiet corner of the library and chewed one bite for ages, unable to swallow it.

For days after that, {name} dodged Milo. When Milo waved in the hallway, {name} spun around and walked off. During the science lab, {name} quietly switched to another group. Their desks were only an aisle apart, but it felt like an ocean. At night, {name}'s heart felt as heavy as a backpack crammed with rocks. Why did the person who hurt most have to be a best friend?

On Friday morning, Milo walked to the front of the room, hands clenched, voice wobbly. "Ms. Lin, can I say something?" The class went still. "In preschool, I thought glue was caramel and licked a big glob. Everyone called me the Glue King." Gasps and laughs filled the room, and Milo's ears turned tomato red. He took a deep breath. "Telling {name}'s nickname on Monday was wrong. Please don't use it anymore."

When the bell rang, Milo found {name} by the basketball hoop. He wasn't joking around this time. "I'm sorry," he said. "I thought it was just a funny memory. I didn't know it would hurt you so much." {name} was quiet for a long moment. "When everyone laughed, I wanted to shrink into a tiny bean and vanish. I ate lunch alone in the library and felt so embarrassed. It really wasn't okay."

Milo didn't make excuses. He just nodded hard. "I get it now. Anything about you, I'll ask you first." Watching him, {name} felt the rocks inside start rolling away, one by one. Staying angry, it turned out, was exhausting. "Okay. I forgive you." {name} held out a pinky. "But our secrets stay between the two of us." Milo hooked it right away. "Deal!"

After that, they made a Secret Jar. Funny, slightly embarrassing memories went inside, and they only came out if both friends agreed. Crossing the playground after school, {name} suddenly let out a loud "hic!" Milo's eyes went wide, but {name} burst out laughing first. "That one, you're allowed to laugh at." Their laughter floated across the playground, louder than before, and a little more careful with each other.

questions: 米洛做了哪些事來表示他真的很抱歉？
{name}原諒米洛之前，先說了什麼？為什麼說出自己的感受很重要？
如果朋友讓你難過了，你會怎麼告訴他你的感覺？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子一起練習一句話：「你那樣做讓我覺得……，我需要你……」，並一起做一個家庭「祕密罐子」，約定只有雙方同意才能分享彼此的糗事。

questions: What did Milo do to show he was truly sorry?
What did {name} tell Milo before forgiving him, and why does sharing our feelings matter?
If a friend hurt your feelings, how would you tell them how you felt?
en.tip: This week, practice one sentence together: "When you did that, I felt..., and I need you to..." Then make a family Secret Jar where funny stories are only shared when both people agree.

zh: 公寓的走廊又長又亮，是{name}和鄰居孩子最愛的「室內球場」。咚、咚、咚，皮球一彈，整棟樓都跟著打拍子。可是每次彈不到三下，樓下那扇門就「砰」地打開，林爺爺皺著眉頭大喊：「吵死了！」大家一哄而散，私下都叫他「臭臉林」。奇怪的是，每當有人的球洩了氣，隔天早上它總會鼓鼓地躺在門口，誰也不知道是哪位好心人。
星期六清晨，{name}跟著媽媽下樓買早餐，正好碰見林爺爺拎著兩大袋菜，一步一步爬上樓梯。他穿著醫院警衛的制服，眼睛下面掛著兩團黑影。{name}發現，他每上一階，提袋子的手就抖一下，一根白蘿蔔差點滾了出來。{name}心想：原來一張臉也會說話，那張臉不是兇，是累得快撐不住了。
{name}深吸一口氣，走上前輕聲問：「林爺爺，您還好嗎？」林爺爺愣了一下，好像很久沒有人這樣問他了。「我在醫院值夜班，天亮才回家睡覺。」他揉揉眼睛，嘆了口氣，「你們的球一彈，我的天花板就像在打鼓。」媽媽接過一袋菜，{name}也提起另一袋，三個人一起慢慢爬上樓梯。
回到家，{name}躺在床上，閉起眼睛想像：如果自己整晚沒睡，好不容易躺下，頭頂卻咚咚咚響個不停，會是什麼感覺？大概像被一百隻啄木鳥圍攻，氣得想跳起來大叫吧。{name}忽然恍然大悟，林爺爺那一聲聲吼叫裡，其實藏著一句說不出口的話：「拜託，讓我睡一下。」
那天下午，{name}召集鄰居孩子開「走廊會議」。小凱嘟囔：「可是走廊最好玩啊！」{name}攤開一張大紙，畫了一顆戴睡帽的月亮，寫上「安靜時間：早上九點到下午四點」。「我們改去中庭玩，爸媽從樓上就看得到。還有，每天早上八點，誰有空，就幫林爺爺提菜上樓。」大家你看我、我看你，最後異口同聲：「好！」
計畫實行的第一週，走廊靜悄悄的，中庭倒是熱鬧非凡。每天早上，{name}和小凱在樓梯口等林爺爺，一人一袋，爬得氣喘吁吁，還比賽誰先到。有一回，小凱的球又扁了，大家正發愁，林爺爺從口袋掏出一支小打氣筒，三兩下就把球打得圓滾滾。{name}眼睛一亮：「原來門口那些球，都是您打的氣！」
林爺爺難得笑了，滿臉皺紋擠成一朵花。「我睡不著的時候，就幫你們修球。只是不知道該怎麼開口。」從那天起，孩子們改叫他「打氣林爺爺」。月亮海報下面，也多了一行歪歪扭扭的字：「謝謝，睡得很香。」{name}看著那行字，覺得心裡好像也被打滿了氣，鼓鼓的、暖暖的。
en: The long, bright hallway of the apartment building was {name}'s favorite indoor court. Thump, thump, thump went the ball, and the whole building seemed to keep the beat. But before the third bounce, the door downstairs would bang open. "Too loud!" Mr. Lin would bellow. The kids scattered and secretly called him Grumpy Lin. Strangely, whenever someone's ball went flat, it reappeared by their door the next morning, plump again. Nobody knew who did it.

Early one Saturday, {name} went downstairs with Mom to buy breakfast and spotted Mr. Lin trudging up the stairs with two heavy bags of groceries. He wore a hospital security guard's uniform, and dark smudges sat under his eyes. With every step, his hands trembled, and a fat white radish nearly tumbled out. {name} studied his face. It wasn't angry at all. It was exhausted.

{name} took a deep breath, stepped closer, and asked softly, "Mr. Lin, are you okay?" He blinked, as if nobody had asked him that in a long time. "I work nights at the hospital. I only get to sleep when the sun comes up." He rubbed his eyes. "When you bounce that ball, my ceiling sounds like a drum." Mom took one bag, {name} took the other, and the three of them climbed slowly together.

Back home, {name} lay in bed, eyes closed, imagining it. What if you stayed awake all night, finally lay down, and something above you went thump, thump, thump without stopping? It would feel like being attacked by a hundred woodpeckers. Anyone would want to leap up and yell. Suddenly {name} understood. Inside every shout from Mr. Lin was a quieter wish: Please, just let me sleep.

That afternoon, {name} called a hallway meeting. "But the hallway is the best place to play!" Kai grumbled. {name} unrolled a big sheet of paper with a moon in a nightcap and the words QUIET TIME: 9 A.M. TO 4 P.M. "We can play in the courtyard, where our parents can see us from upstairs. And every morning at eight, whoever's free can help carry Mr. Lin's groceries." The kids glanced at each other. "Deal!"

The first week, the hallway was hushed and the courtyard was buzzing. Each morning, {name} and Kai waited at the bottom of the stairs, grabbed a bag each, and raced Mr. Lin's groceries up, panting. One day Kai's ball went flat again. Mr. Lin pulled a little pump from his pocket and, in a few puffs, made it round as an orange. {name} gasped. "It was you! You fixed all those balls!"

Mr. Lin smiled, and his wrinkles bunched up like a flower. "When I can't sleep, I pump up your flat balls. I just never knew how to say hello." From then on, the kids called him Pump-Up Lin. Under the moon poster, someone added a wobbly line: Thank you. Slept like a log. {name} read it and felt pumped up too, full and warm inside.

questions: {name}看到林爺爺的臉和發抖的手時，發現了什麼？
{name}想像自己是林爺爺時，心裡有什麼感覺？你曾經因為很累而大聲說話嗎？
如果你發現一位鄰居或同學看起來不太對勁，你會怎麼問、怎麼幫忙？
zh.tip: 這個星期玩「看臉猜心情」：輪流做出累、難過、開心的表情，讓對方猜，再練習說一句「你還好嗎？」。

questions: What did {name} notice about Mr. Lin's face and shaking hands?
How did {name} feel when imagining being Mr. Lin? Have you ever sounded grumpy because you were tired?
If a neighbor or classmate looked upset, how would you ask and help?
en.tip: This week, play "Guess the Feeling": take turns making tired, sad, or happy faces for each other to guess, then practice saying, "Are you okay?"

zh: 星期五，老師宣布：「下星期，全班要在公園舉辦跳繩挑戰！」大家都歡呼起來。午休時，老師帶著全班到學校旁邊的公園練習。小美輕輕一跳，繩子就咻咻地轉個不停；阿傑也跳得又穩又快，好像永遠不會停下來。
輪到{name}了。{name}握緊兩端的握把，用力一甩，繩子卻「啪」的一聲勾到腳尖。再試一次，還是絆住了。第三次、第四次……繩子好像故意跟{name}作對。{name}低頭看著草地，小聲說：「我是不是永遠都學不會？」
放學回家，{name}把跳繩丟進角落，嘟著嘴說：「我不要參加了。」爸爸沒有生氣，只是倒了一杯水，坐到{his}身邊。「累了就先休息一下。」爸爸說，「等你喝完水，我們試試看小一點的步驟，好嗎？」{name}想了想，點點頭。
晚飯後，爸爸陪著{name}走到家門口的小空地。爸爸說：「今天不用跳很多下，只要跳一下就好。」{name}先把繩子甩到身後，看著它從頭上轉過來，等它碰到地面時，雙腳輕輕一跳。「一！」成功了！{name}忍不住笑出聲來。
「再來試試三下吧！」爸爸拍拍手。{name}一邊跳一邊大聲數：「一、二……」繩子又絆住了。這次{name}沒有生氣，反而停下來想：「我剛剛跳太高了，所以來不及。」{name}換個方法，跳得低一點、輕一點。「一、二、三！」
接下來幾天，{name}每天都和爸爸一起練習。被絆住了，就停下來喘口氣，再想想哪裡可以改變。有時候是手甩得太快，有時候是太早跳起來。每絆一次，{name}就多懂一點。數字從三慢慢變成五，又從五變成十。
挑戰日到了，公園的大樹下站滿了同學和爸爸媽媽。輪到{name}時，{his}心怦怦跳。{name}深吸一口氣，在心裡提醒自己：低一點、輕一點。繩子轉起來了，{name}一邊跳一邊數，大家也跟著喊：「十八、十九、二十！」
掌聲響起，小美和阿傑跑過來說：「好厲害！」{name}雖然不是跳最多下的人，卻笑得最開心。{name}想起那些被繩子絆住的晚上，每一次絆倒，都讓{him}離今天更近一點。回家的路上，{name}牽著爸爸的手，把跳繩握得緊緊的。
en: On Friday, the teacher made an announcement. "Next week, our class will have a jump-rope challenge in the park!" Everyone cheered. At lunchtime, the teacher took the class to the park next to school to practice. Mei's rope went whoosh, whoosh, around and around. Jay jumped so fast and steady, he seemed like he could go on forever.

Then it was {name}'s turn. {name} gripped the handles and swung hard, but snap! The rope caught on {his} toes. {name} tried again and tripped again. Three times, four times, the rope kept getting in the way. Looking down at the grass, {name} whispered, "Maybe I'll never learn."

At home, {name} tossed the rope into a corner. "I'm not doing the challenge," {he} grumbled. Dad wasn't upset. He poured a glass of water and sat down close by. "When you're tired, it's okay to rest," Dad said. "After your water, let's try a smaller step. Okay?" {name} thought for a moment, then nodded.

After dinner, Dad and {name} went out to the little open space by their front door. "Tonight you don't need lots of jumps," said Dad. "Just one." {name} swung the rope back, watched it come over the top, and as it touched the ground, hopped. "One!" It worked! {name} burst out laughing.

"Now let's try three," Dad said, clapping. {name} jumped and counted out loud. "One, two..." The rope caught again. But this time {name} stopped to think instead of getting mad. "I jumped too high, so I was too slow." {name} tried a new way, lower and lighter. "One, two, three!"

Every day that week, {name} practiced with Dad. After a trip, {name} would rest and catch a breath, then figure out what to change. Sometimes the swing was too fast. Sometimes the jump came too early. Each trip taught {name} something new. Three jumps became five, and five became ten.

Challenge day arrived. Classmates and parents gathered under the big trees in the park. When it was {name}'s turn, {his} heart went thump, thump. {name} took a deep breath and thought, lower and lighter. The rope began to spin. {name} counted, and everyone joined in: "Eighteen, nineteen, TWENTY!"

Everyone clapped. Mei and Jay ran over. "That was amazing!" {name} didn't have the most jumps, but {name} had the biggest smile. {name} remembered all those evenings of tripping, and how each one had led to today. Walking home, {name} held Dad's hand and held the jump rope tight.

questions: {name}想放棄的時候，爸爸建議了什麼？後來發生了什麼事？
{name}被繩子絆住後，發現自己哪裡可以改變？
你有沒有一件事，一開始很難，練習後變簡單了？
zh.tip: 這個星期選一件孩子覺得難的事，和孩子一起從「只做一次」開始，每天大聲數出進步的次數，並說：「你今天又多學到一點了！」

questions: When {name} wanted to quit, what did Dad suggest? What happened next?
After tripping, what did {name} figure out could be changed?
Is there something that felt hard at first but got easier after you practiced?
en.tip: This week, pick one thing your child finds hard and start with "just one try." Count the progress out loud together each day and say, "You learned a little more today!"

zh: 星期六中午，妹妹小梅拉著{name}的手。「我們來開茶會，好不好？」可是小梅一直揉眼睛。她打了一個好大的呵欠。媽媽說：「小梅該睡午覺囉。」小梅的嘴巴嘟起來，像一顆圓圓的小包子。
{name}想了想。下午有沒有別的事呢？不用上課，也不用出門。嗯，真的有空！{name}點點頭說：「睡醒以後，我陪妳開茶會。」小梅伸出小小的指頭。「打勾勾，蓋印章！」兩根小指勾一勾，大拇指碰一碰。小梅笑嘻嘻地去睡覺了。
{name}開始準備茶會。{he}搬出小桌子，鋪上花花的桌巾。再拿出兩個小茶杯，還有一個小茶壺。小熊布丁坐在椅子上，歪著頭。「布丁，你也想喝茶嗎？」{name}幫布丁戴上一頂紙帽子。布丁看起來好神氣喔！
鈴鈴鈴！電話響了。是好朋友阿樂打來的。「{name}，來我家玩積木好不好？我有一座新的大城堡喔！」{name}好想去。大城堡耶！可是{name}看看桌上的茶杯，又看看小梅的房門。剛剛的打勾勾，好像還在小指頭上暖暖的。
{name}說：「阿樂，對不起，我今天不能去。我答應妹妹要開茶會。」電話那頭安靜了一下下。這時，{name}想到一個好點子。「你要不要來參加茶會？我先問媽媽喔。」媽媽笑著說可以。阿樂的爸爸也說，會送阿樂過來。
叮咚！阿樂和爸爸來了。阿樂抱著一盒餅乾。{name}又拿出第三個茶杯。三個茶杯排排站，一、二、三。這時，房門打開了。小梅的頭髮翹翹的，揉著眼睛走出來。她看到桌子，眼睛一下子變得好亮。「茶會真的開始了！」
{name}倒出涼涼的水，當作香香的茶。「小姐，請喝茶。」小梅咯咯笑。阿樂分餅乾，一人一片。小梅把餅乾放到布丁嘴邊。「布丁說，好好吃！」可是餅乾屑全掉在布丁的肚子上。大家笑成一團。布丁好像也在笑呢。
小梅喝完茶，緊緊抱住{name}。「你說到做到耶！」阿樂說：「茶會比城堡還好玩。明天一起蓋城堡好嗎？」{name}想一想，明天也有空。「好，一言為定！」夕陽照進窗戶，三個茶杯亮晶晶。布丁戴著紙帽子，開心地坐在中間。
en: On Saturday at noon, little sister Mei tugged {name}'s hand. "Let's have a tea party!" she said. But Mei kept rubbing her eyes. She gave a big, big yawn. "Nap time first," said Mom. Mei puffed out her cheeks like a round bun.

{name} thought about the afternoon. No school. No trips outside. Yes, there was really time! "After your nap, we'll have a tea party," {name} said. Mei held up her tiny pinky. "Pinky promise, and stamp it!" Two pinkies hooked. Two thumbs pressed. Mei skipped off to bed, smiling.

{name} got everything ready. {he} set up the little table. {he} spread out a flowery cloth. Then came two tiny cups and a tiny teapot. Pudding the teddy bear sat on a chair. "Do you want tea too, Pudding?" {name} gave Pudding a paper hat. Pudding looked very fancy!

Ring, ring! The phone rang. It was {his} good friend Leo. "Come play blocks at my house! I have a giant new castle!" {name} really wanted to go. A giant castle! But {name} looked at the cups. Then at Mei's door. The pinky promise still felt warm.

"Sorry, Leo. I can't come today," {name} said. "I promised Mei a tea party." The phone went quiet for a moment. Then {name} had a bright idea. "Want to come to our tea party? I'll ask Mom." Mom smiled and said yes. Leo's dad said he would bring Leo over.

Ding-dong! Leo and his dad were at the door. Leo held a box of cookies. {name} took out a third cup. One, two, three cups in a row. Then Mei's door opened. Her hair stuck up. Her sleepy eyes went wide and bright. "The tea party is real!"

{name} poured cool water for pretend tea. "Your tea, my lady." Mei giggled. Leo shared the cookies, one for everyone. Mei held a cookie to Pudding's mouth. "Pudding says yummy!" But the crumbs tumbled onto Pudding's tummy. Everyone laughed and laughed. Even Pudding seemed to grin.

Mei hugged {name} tight. "You really did it!" Leo said, "This is more fun than my castle. Can we build it tomorrow?" {name} thought about it. Tomorrow was free. "Yes. That's a promise!" The late sun warmed the window. Three cups sparkled. Pudding sat happily in the middle, still wearing his paper hat.

questions: 阿樂打電話來的時候，{name}為什麼沒有去玩城堡？{he}後來做了什麼？
{name}答應小梅之前，先想了什麼？你答應別人之前，會先想一想嗎？
如果你答應了一件事，後來真的做不到，你可以怎麼說、怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這個星期和孩子一起做一個「打勾勾」小約定，例如睡前一起讀一本書，然後全家都說到做到。如果大人臨時做不到，就誠實說明，並約好補做的時間。

questions: When Leo called, why didn't {name} go to see the castle? What did {he} do instead?
What did {name} think about before making the pinky promise? Do you stop to think before you promise something?
If you promised something and then couldn't do it, what could you say and do?
en.tip: This week, make one small pinky promise together, like reading a book at bedtime, and keep it as a family. If a grown-up can't keep a promise, say so honestly and choose a new time to make it right.

title.en: {name} and the Fourteen Rungs by the Sea

zh: 暑假一開始，{name}就住進爺爺海邊的老房子。後院的大榕樹上，爺爺早已釘好樹屋的地板，卻還缺一座梯子。六歲的表妹桃桃仰著頭問：「暑假結束前，我們上得去嗎？」{name}沒有馬上回答，先蹲下來在沙地上算：十四根橫木，四十多天。算了兩遍，{name}才伸出小指：「我答應妳，暑假結束前一定完成。」
第二天清晨，爺爺牽著兩個孩子沿著退潮的沙灘撿漂流木。海鷗在頭頂嘎嘎叫，浪花輕輕舔著腳邊。回到後院，爺爺負責鋸木頭、敲釘子，{name}負責量尺寸、磨砂紙、刷油漆。第一根橫木就量錯了，短了整整五公分，桃桃笑得東倒西歪，{name}也忍不住跟著哈哈大笑，再量一次。
可是事情沒有想像中順利。午後雷陣雨一下就是好幾天，木頭濕答答的，砂紙磨得{name}手臂發痠，油漆還會滴得到處都是。轉眼到了八月中，梯子上只有孤零零的六根橫木。桃桃每天早上都跑來問：「快好了嗎？」{name}張開嘴，差點脫口說出「快了快了」。
{name}深吸一口氣，牽著桃桃坐到台階上，老老實實地說：「其實才做好六根，比我算的慢很多。不過我沒有放棄，我會想辦法。」桃桃眨眨眼，點點頭說：「那我幫你拿刷子！」當天晚上，{name}去找爺爺，請爺爺接下來每天下午都陪{him}一起趕工。爺爺摸摸{his}頭，笑著答應了。
於是，原本去放風箏的下午，都變成鋸木屑飛舞的下午。{name}量得一絲不苟，磨得光滑如鏡，爺爺的槌子叮叮咚咚，和遠方的海浪聲此起彼落。奇怪的是，桃桃總在黃昏前神神祕祕地跟著奶奶往沙灘走，回來時口袋鼓鼓的，問她在做什麼，她只是咯咯笑，什麼也不肯說。
暑假的最後一天，{name}刷上最後一筆藍色油漆。爺爺把每顆螺絲都鎖得牢牢的，用力搖了搖梯子，梯子穩如泰山。「可以上去了，我在下面看著。」爺爺說。{name}讓桃桃先爬，自己緊跟在後，一階、兩階……一直數到第十四階，兩顆小腦袋終於從樹屋的門口探了出來。
樹屋裡，窗邊掛著一串叮噹作響的貝殼風鈴。桃桃得意地說：「你每做一天，我就撿一顆貝殼，你數數看！」{name}一顆一顆數，整整四十三顆，原來每一個下午都被記住了。窗外，夕陽把大海染成金色，海鷗嘎嘎飛過。這時奶奶在樓下喊開飯了，兩個孩子相視一笑，小心地沿著梯子爬下去。
en: On the first day of summer, {name} arrived at Grandpa's old house by the sea. Up in the big banyan tree out back, Grandpa had already built the treehouse floor, but there was no ladder. Little cousin Taotao, who was six, squinted up. "Can we get up there before summer ends?" {name} didn't answer right away. Fourteen rungs, more than forty days. After counting twice, {name} held out a pinky. "I promise. Before summer ends."

Early the next morning, Grandpa led both kids along the low-tide beach to gather driftwood. Gulls squawked overhead, and little waves licked at their toes. Back in the yard, Grandpa did the sawing and hammering, while {name} measured, sanded, and painted. The very first rung came out five centimeters too short. Taotao giggled so hard she toppled over, and {name} laughed too, then measured again.

But things didn't go as smoothly as planned. Afternoon thunderstorms rolled in for days, soaking the wood. Sanding made {name}'s arms ache, and paint dripped everywhere. Suddenly it was mid-August, and the ladder had only six lonely rungs. Every morning Taotao ran over to ask, "Is it almost done?" {name} opened {his} mouth and nearly blurted out, "Almost!"

Instead, {name} took a deep breath, sat Taotao down on the step, and told her the truth. "Only six rungs are done. It's much slower than I thought. But I'm not giving up. I'll figure something out." Taotao blinked, then nodded. "Then I'll hold the brushes!" That night, {name} asked Grandpa to work on it together every afternoon from now on. Grandpa ruffled {his} hair, smiled, and said yes.

So the afternoons meant for kite flying became afternoons full of drifting sawdust. {name} measured with great care and sanded each rung smooth as glass, while Grandpa's hammer tapped along with the faraway waves. Strangely, before every sunset, Taotao slipped off to the beach with Grandma and came back with bulging pockets. Whenever anyone asked what she was up to, she only giggled.

On the last day of summer, {name} brushed on the final stroke of blue paint. Grandpa tightened every bolt and gave the ladder a hard shake. It stood as steady as a mountain. "Up you go. I'll watch from here," he said. {name} let Taotao climb first and followed close behind. One, two... all the way to fourteen, until two heads poked through the treehouse door.

Inside, a wind chime of seashells tinkled by the window. "I picked one shell for every day you worked," Taotao announced proudly. "Count them!" {name} counted, one by one. Forty-three shells. Every single afternoon had been remembered. Outside, the sunset turned the sea to gold, and gulls squawked past. Then Grandma called them for dinner, and the two cousins grinned and climbed carefully back down.

questions: {name}答應桃桃之前，先做了什麼事？你答應別人之前，會先想一想嗎？
梯子做得太慢時，{name}差點說「快了」，後來{he}怎麼做？如果是你，你會怎麼說？
桃桃為什麼要每天撿一顆貝殼？當別人說到做到時，你心裡有什麼感覺？
zh.tip: 這個星期，和孩子各自許下一個小小的約定（例如睡前一起讀一頁書），每做到一天就在紙上畫一顆貝殼。如果哪天做不到，就練習說：「今天我沒做到，我想這樣補回來……」

questions: What did {name} do before making the promise to Taotao? Do you stop and think before you promise something?
When the ladder was going slowly, {name} almost said "Almost done!" What did {he} do instead? What would you have said?
Why did Taotao collect a shell every day? How do you feel when someone keeps a promise to you?
en.tip: This week, you and your child each make one small promise (like reading one page together at bedtime), and draw a shell on paper for every day you keep it. If a day gets missed, practice saying, "I didn't do it today, and here's how I'll make it up."

zh: 美術課到了，教室裡香香的。到處都是顏料的味道。星期六是媽媽的生日，{name}要送媽媽一張卡片。卡片上有爸爸、媽媽，還有{name}。爸爸的鬍子畫得翹翹的，像兩條小蝌蚪。{name}看了，忍不住偷偷笑出聲。
隔壁的多多也在畫畫。多多畫了一隻大恐龍，綠綠的，胖胖的。「看！我的恐龍會跳舞！」多多開心地揮揮手。手一揮，碰到了洗筆的水杯。咚！杯子倒了。灰灰的水嘩啦啦流過去，全流到{name}的畫上。
爸爸的鬍子糊掉了。媽媽的笑臉變成一團灰。{name}的眉頭也皺成一團。心裡熱熱的，像一壺快煮開的水。「多多！你把我的畫弄濕了！」{name}大聲說。「這是給媽媽的生日禮物，我好生氣！」
多多愣住了，小手停在半空中。「對不起，對不起！」多多小聲地說，「我不是故意的。」多多趕快拿來衛生紙，輕輕壓在畫上。可是畫還是濕答答的，皺巴巴的。老師走過來，摸摸兩個人的頭。「先讓畫晾一晾吧。」
放學了，{name}一句話也不想說。回家的路上，媽媽牽著{his}手。{name}覺得心裡沉沉的。好像背著一顆大石頭。晚餐時，{name}只吃了一點點。小貓咪咪跑來蹭{his}腳。「喵——」{name}摸摸咪咪，嘆了一口氣。
第二天早上，多多站在教室門口。多多抱著一大疊彩色紙，還有一盒新顏料。「這些給你。」多多紅著臉說。「我們一起做新卡片，好不好？」多多把水杯推到桌子最旁邊。還用手臂比了一個大叉叉。{name}看了，噗哧一聲笑出來。
{name}看著多多，想了一想。「昨天我真的好難過喔。」{name}說。「我知道。」多多點點頭，「真的很對不起。」{name}心裡的大石頭，好像慢慢變小了。「好，我原諒你。」{name}笑著說，「我們一起畫吧！」多多開心得跳了起來。
兩個人一起畫畫。{name}畫爸爸、媽媽和自己。多多幫忙塗上金色的小星星。爸爸的鬍子，這次畫得更翹了。最後，{name}在角落畫了小小的多多。小多多正在揮手呢！「這是我的新朋友！」{name}說。多多的鼻子沾著藍顏料，笑得好開心。
en: It was art time, and the classroom smelled like paint. Mom's birthday was on Saturday. {name} was making her a card. On it were Dad, Mom, and {name}. Dad's mustache curled up like two tiny tadpoles. {name} giggled at it.

Dodo sat at the next table. Dodo was painting a big, round, green dinosaur. "Look! My dinosaur can dance!" Dodo waved happily. Oops! A hand bumped the paint water cup. Plop! Gray water splashed out and ran all over {name}'s picture.

Dad's mustache turned into a smudge. Mom's smile became a gray blob. {name} frowned a big frown. Inside, {name} felt hot, like a kettle about to whistle. "Dodo! You ruined my picture!" {name} said loudly. "It was Mom's birthday present. I'm so angry!"

Dodo froze, one hand still in the air. "I'm sorry, I'm so sorry," Dodo whispered. "I didn't mean to." Dodo grabbed tissues and gently patted the paper. But it stayed soggy and wrinkly. The teacher came over and patted both their heads. "Let's let it dry for now."

After school, {name} didn't feel like talking. Mom held {his} hand on the walk home. {name}'s heart felt heavy, like carrying a big rock. At dinner, {name} only ate a little. Mimi the cat rubbed against {his} legs. "Meow." {name} petted Mimi and sighed.

The next morning, Dodo was waiting at the classroom door. Dodo was hugging a stack of colorful paper and a brand-new box of paints. "These are for you," Dodo said, cheeks pink. "Can we make a new card together?" Dodo pushed the water cup far away. Then Dodo made a big X with both arms. {name} burst out laughing.

{name} looked at Dodo and thought for a moment. "I felt really sad yesterday," {name} said. "I know," Dodo nodded. "I'm really sorry." The heavy rock inside {name} seemed to get smaller. "Okay. I forgive you," {name} smiled. "Let's paint together!" Dodo jumped for joy.

They painted side by side. {name} painted Dad, Mom, and {name}. Dodo added little gold stars. Dad's mustache was even curlier this time. Last, {name} painted a tiny Dodo in the corner, waving hello. "This is my new friend!" {name} said. Dodo laughed, with blue paint on the tip of a nose.

questions: 多多打翻水杯以後，{name}說了什麼？多多又做了什麼？
{name}原諒多多以後，心裡的大石頭怎麼了？
如果有人不小心弄壞你的東西，你會怎麼說出自己的感覺？
zh.tip: 這週練習一句話：「我很生氣，因為……；謝謝你說對不起。」家裡有人犯小錯時，大家一起用這句話說說看。

questions: After Dodo spilled the water, what did {name} say, and what did Dodo do?
What happened to the heavy rock inside {name} after {he} forgave Dodo?
If someone broke something of yours by accident, how would you tell them how you feel?
en.tip: This week, practice one phrase together: "I feel upset because...; thank you for saying sorry." Use it whenever someone at home makes a small mistake.

zh: 寒假的午後，陽光斜斜地灑進客廳。爺爺在餐桌上鋪好毛氈，擺上硯臺、墨條和一支細長的毛筆。「今天先學一個字，」爺爺一邊磨墨，一邊慢條斯理地說，「就是『永』。別看它只有五畫，書法裡最基本的八種筆法，全都藏在這個字裡。」{name}睜大眼睛，躍躍欲試，心想：才五畫，有什麼難的？
沒想到，毛筆一點也不聽話。{name}寫的點，暈成一隻胖嘟嘟的小蝌蚪；橫畫抖得像在打寒顫；最後那一捺，軟趴趴地躺在紙上，活像一條睡過頭的毛毛蟲。{name}換一張紙，再寫；又換一張，還是歪七扭八。墨汁沾上手指，不知怎麼地，連鼻尖都多了一個小黑點。爺爺忍著笑，默默遞來一張面紙。
寫到第十張，{name}把筆一放，悶悶地說：「我根本不是這塊料，再練也沒用。」爺爺沒有多勸，只是剝了一顆橘子，分一半給{name}。「手累了，心也累了，先休息一下吧。」祖孫倆靠在窗邊，看麻雀在陽台欄杆上蹦蹦跳跳。橘子酸酸甜甜的，{name}緊繃的肩膀，一點一點鬆了下來。
吃完橘子，爺爺從書櫃最上層搬下一個生鏽的鐵盒。盒子裡是一疊泛黃的紙，上面全是「永」字：點像蝌蚪，捺像掃把，有一張還被筆戳破了一個洞。角落有一行褪色的小字，寫著爺爺的名字和「九歲」。{name}目瞪口呆：「這是爺爺寫的？」爺爺哈哈大笑：「我的老師說，我的捺像被颱風吹倒的掃把呢！」
「那爺爺後來是怎麼練好的？」「一天只練一筆。」爺爺說。從那天起，{name}每天只專心寫一種筆畫。練點的那天，{he}發現下筆要輕、收筆要頓；練橫的那天，{he}發現手腕放鬆，線條才不會發抖。有一天紙用完了，爺爺拿出一塊水寫布，清水寫上去會變黑，乾了又消失。{name}寫了一遍又一遍，像在變魔術。
日曆一頁頁撕下，桌上的練習紙越疊越高。那些原本調皮的筆畫，漸漸變得得心應手。除夕前一天，{name}屏住呼吸，一筆一畫寫下一個完整的「永」。鉤的地方還是有一點點抖，但點圓潤飽滿，捺穩穩地展開，像一隻伸開翅膀的鳥。{name}盯著它看了好久，嘴角忍不住往上揚。
除夕夜，爺爺親手把那張「永」貼在客廳牆上，旁邊還掛上爺爺九歲時那張歪歪扭扭的舊作。親戚們來拜年，都湊過來欣賞。表姊指著那個有點抖的鉤，{name}搶先笑著說：「那裡是我學會放慢的地方！」爺爺眼睛笑成了一條線，從抽屜拿出一張新紅紙：「明天開始，我們來寫『春』。」
en: On a sunny winter afternoon, Grandpa spread a soft felt mat across the dining table. He set out an ink stone, an ink stick, and a long, slender brush. "Today we'll learn just one character," he said, grinding the ink in slow circles. "Yǒng. It means forever. It has only five strokes, but all eight basic brush moves are hiding inside it." {name} leaned forward eagerly. Five strokes? Easy.

The brush had other ideas. {name}'s dot spread into a chubby tadpole. The flat stroke shivered like it was cold. The last sweeping stroke flopped across the paper like a caterpillar that had overslept. {name} tried a new sheet, then another, and another. Still wobbly. Somehow a speck of ink even landed on {his} nose. Grandpa pressed his lips together to hide a smile and quietly passed over a tissue.

On the tenth sheet, {name} set the brush down with a thump. "I'm just not good at this. Practicing won't help." Grandpa didn't argue. He peeled an orange and handed half across the table. "Tired hands make a tired heart. Let's take a break." Side by side at the window, they watched sparrows hop along the balcony rail. The orange was sweet and tangy, and little by little, {name}'s shoulders loosened.

Afterward, Grandpa lifted a rusty tin box down from the top shelf. Inside lay a stack of yellowed paper, every sheet covered in the same character. The dots looked like tadpoles. The sweeping strokes looked like brooms. One page even had a hole poked right through it. In the corner, in faded pencil, were Grandpa's name and the words age nine. {name} stared. "You wrote these?" Grandpa chuckled. "My teacher said my strokes looked like brooms knocked over by a typhoon!"

"So how did you get good?" "One stroke a day," said Grandpa. From then on, {name} practiced just one stroke each day. On dot day, {name} learned to touch down gently and pause before lifting. On flat-stroke day, a loose wrist turned out to stop the shaking. When the paper ran out, Grandpa brought a magic water cloth. Plain water turned black on it, then faded as it dried. {name} wrote again and again, as if doing a magic trick.

The calendar pages flew by, and the practice sheets piled higher. The once-naughty strokes slowly began to behave. The day before New Year's Eve, {name} held {his} breath and wrote the whole character, stroke by careful stroke. The little hook still had a tiny wobble. But the dot was round and full, and the final sweep stretched out steady and wide, like a bird opening its wings. {name} gazed at it for a long time, grinning.

On New Year's Eve, Grandpa hung {name}'s character on the living room wall. Right beside it, he hung his own wobbly page from when he was nine. When the relatives arrived, they gathered around to look. A cousin pointed at the shaky little hook, but {name} spoke first, beaming. "That's where I learned to slow down!" Grandpa's eyes crinkled with joy. He pulled a fresh red sheet from the drawer. "Tomorrow," he said, "we'll try spring."

questions: {name}寫到第十張想放棄的時候，爺爺做了什麼？你覺得累的時候，什麼方法能讓你好過一點？
爺爺為什麼要讓{name}看他小時候的練習紙？
你有沒有一件以前很難、現在變簡單的事？你是怎麼做到的？
zh.tip: 這個星期選一件孩子正在學的事，和孩子約好「一天只練一小步」，每天睡前一起說說今天學到的一個小發現。

questions: When {name} wanted to give up on the tenth sheet, what did Grandpa do? What helps you when you feel tired of trying?
Why do you think Grandpa showed {name} his old practice pages?
Is there something that used to be hard for you but is easier now? How did you get there?
en.tip: This week, pick one thing your child is learning and agree to practice just one small step a day. At bedtime, share one tiny thing each of you learned that day.

title.en: {name} and the Birthday Balloon That Flew Away

zh: 今天是{name}的生日。媽媽送給{name}一顆氣球。氣球亮晶晶的，是銀色的。上面還有一顆金色的星星。{name}把繩子繞在手指上，在院子裡慢慢走。氣球跟著{him}，輕輕晃來晃去。{name}覺得好開心，一直笑。
弟弟阿樂跑過來，眼睛亮亮的。「我可以拿一下嗎？一分鐘就好！」{name}想了想，點點頭。「要抓緊喔。」阿樂用小手握住繩子。他笑著轉圈圈，氣球也跟著轉。媽媽在旁邊澆花，笑著看他們。
突然，一陣風吹過來。阿樂的小手一鬆。「哎呀！」氣球飛起來了！它越飛越高，飛過籬笆，飛過屋頂。{name}伸長了手，可是抓不到。銀色的星星變得好小好小，最後不見了。
{name}的臉熱熱的。心裡好像有一團火在燒。{he}好生氣，好想大叫。{name}握緊拳頭，嘴巴張開了。可是，{name}想起媽媽教過的方法。{he}閉上眼睛，吸一口長長的氣。再慢慢吐出來。一次，兩次，三次。
{name}蹲下來，看著阿樂。「那是我的生日氣球。它飛走了，我好難過。」{name}的聲音有點抖。阿樂低下頭，眼睛紅紅的。眼淚一顆一顆掉下來。他小小聲說：「對不起，我不是故意的。」
阿樂擦擦眼淚，跑進屋裡。過了一會兒，他拿著一張紙跑出來。紙上畫著一顆銀色的氣球。還有一顆歪歪的金星星。「這個送給你。」{name}看著那張畫。心裡那塊重重的石頭，好像慢慢變輕了。
{name}牽起阿樂的手。「氣球飛走，我還是有點難過。可是我原諒你。」阿樂抱住{name}，又哭又笑。媽媽放下水壺，走過來抱住他們兩個。「謝謝你們，把心裡的話說出來。」三個人在院子裡抱了好久。
傍晚，天空變成橘色。{name}和阿樂坐在窗邊。「氣球會飛去哪裡呢？」阿樂說：「也許飛到雲上面睡覺！」{name}說：「也許飛去跟月亮說生日快樂。」兩個人一起揮揮手。「氣球，再見！」{name}把那張畫貼在床邊，心裡暖暖的。
en: Today is {name}'s birthday. Mom gives {name} a balloon. It is shiny and silver. A gold star sits on the front. {name} wraps the string around one finger. The balloon bobs along behind. {name} walks around the yard, smiling and smiling.

Little brother Leo runs over with bright eyes. "Can I hold it? Just for a minute!" {name} thinks, then nods. "Hold on tight." Leo grips the string with his small hand. He spins in circles, giggling. Mom waters the flowers nearby and smiles.

Then a gust of wind blows by. Leo's fingers slip. "Oops!" The balloon floats up! It drifts higher and higher. Over the fence. Over the rooftops. {name} reaches up, but it is too far. The silver star gets tiny, then disappears.

{name}'s cheeks feel hot. Anger burns inside like a little fire. {name} wants to shout, really loud. Two fists squeeze tight. Then {name} remembers Mom's trick. Eyes closed, {he} takes a long, slow breath. In and out. One, two, three times.

{name} kneels down and looks at Leo. "That was my birthday balloon. Now it's gone, and I feel so sad." {name}'s voice wobbles a little. Leo looks down. His eyes turn red, and tears roll out. "Sorry," he whispers. "I didn't mean to."

Leo wipes his eyes and runs inside. Soon he comes back with a piece of paper. On it is a silver balloon with a wobbly gold star. "This is for you." {name} looks at the drawing. The heavy feeling inside starts to melt away.

{name} takes Leo's hand. "I'm still a little sad. But I forgive you." Leo hugs {name}, laughing through his tears. Mom puts down her watering can. She wraps them both in a big hug. "Thank you for sharing your feelings."

That evening, the sky turns orange. {name} and Leo sit by the window. "Where will the balloon go?" Leo says, "Maybe it naps on a cloud!" {name} says, "Maybe it wishes the moon happy birthday." They wave together. "Goodbye, balloon!" {name} tapes the drawing by the bed, feeling warm inside.

questions: 氣球飛走的時候，{name}心裡有什麼感覺？{he}做了什麼讓自己冷靜下來？
阿樂說對不起之後，還做了什麼事？
如果有人不小心弄壞你的東西，你會怎麼說出你的感覺？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子一起練習「深呼吸三次」，再用「我覺得……因為……」說出心情。當有人道歉時，練習說：「我還是有點難過，可是我原諒你。」

questions: How did {name} feel when the balloon flew away? What did {he} do to calm down?
After Leo said sorry, what else did he do?
If someone broke something of yours by accident, how would you tell them how you feel?
en.tip: This week, practice three slow breaths together, then saying "I feel ... because ..." When someone says sorry, try the phrase: "I'm still a little sad, but I forgive you."

zh: 星期六早上，陽光暖暖的。奶奶戴上草帽，拿起小鏟子。「{name}，來菜園幫忙好嗎？」{name}開心地點點頭。菜園裡有綠綠的青菜，還有紫色的茄子。胖胖的茄子，好像在睡午覺。
奶奶教{name}拔雜草。{name}用力一拉，「啵！」雜草出來了。{name}差點坐到地上，奶奶笑出聲來。咦，泥土上有一張糖果紙。{name}撿起來說：「這不是菜園的東西！」糖果紙被丟進了垃圾桶。
{name}再挖一挖泥土。咦？有東西在動！一條粉紅色的小蟲，扭來扭去。旁邊又鑽出一條、兩條、三條。「哇！好多扭扭蟲！」{name}嚇了一跳，鏟子「咚」地掉了。
「奶奶，我們把牠們丟掉吧！」{name}拿起一片葉子，想把蟲撥走。奶奶輕輕搖頭：「先別急，牠們叫蚯蚓。」奶奶蹲下來，讓{name}看仔細。蚯蚓沒有腳，卻爬得好認真。
「蚯蚓在土裡鑽來鑽去，」奶奶說，「土就變得鬆鬆軟軟。下雨時，水也能流進去。」奶奶指著紫茄子：「根喝到水，茄子就又大又亮。」{name}看看蚯蚓，又看看茄子。「所以茄子要謝謝蚯蚓囉？」
{name}用雙手捧起一條蚯蚓。涼涼的、滑滑的，好癢喔！{name}咯咯笑。{he}輕輕把牠放回土裡。「別害怕，回家吧。」一條、兩條、三條，全都回家了。奶奶微笑說：「這片土，是大家一起的家。」
「你們是菜園小幫手！」{name}說。奶奶拍拍手：「好名字！」接著，奶奶說：「用桶子裡的雨水澆菜吧。」{name}把雨水倒在茄子根旁，一滴也沒浪費。最後，{name}把土拍平，把鏟子放回原位。
太陽慢慢下山，晚風涼涼的。奶奶摘下一顆紫茄子：「今晚煮茄子給你吃。」{name}對菜園揮揮手：「小幫手們，明天見！」土裡靜悄悄的，好像有人在偷偷笑。
en: It was a sunny Saturday morning. Grandma put on her straw hat. She picked up a little trowel. "{name}, will you help me in the garden?" {name} nodded happily. There were leafy greens and purple eggplants. The fat eggplants looked like they were napping.

Grandma showed {name} how to pull weeds. {name} tugged hard. Pop! Out came a weed. {name} almost sat down in the dirt, and Grandma laughed. Then {name} spotted a candy wrapper. "This doesn't belong in a garden!" Into the trash can it went.

{name} dug a little more. Hey, something was moving! A pink, wiggly thing twisted and turned. Then came another, and another. "Wow! So many wigglers!" {name} was so surprised the trowel dropped. Plop!

"Grandma, let's throw them away!" {name} picked up a leaf to brush them off. Grandma gently shook her head. "Wait. These are earthworms." She knelt down so {name} could look closely. The worms had no legs, but they crawled so busily.

"Worms tunnel through the dirt," Grandma said. "That makes the soil soft. Rain can soak in." She pointed at the eggplants. "The roots drink it up. Then eggplants grow big and shiny." {name} looked at the worms, then the eggplants. "So eggplants should thank the worms?"

{name} scooped up a worm with both hands. It felt cool and smooth. It tickled! {name} giggled. Gently, {he} set it back on the soil. "Don't be scared. Go home." One, two, three, every worm went home. Grandma smiled. "This garden is a home we all share."
