"You are garden helpers!" {name} said. Grandma clapped. "What a perfect name!" Next, Grandma said, "Let's water with rain from the barrel." {name} poured it right by the roots. Not one drop was wasted. Then {name} patted the soil smooth and put the trowel away.

Slowly, the sun went down. The evening breeze felt cool. Grandma picked a shiny purple eggplant. "I'll cook this for dinner tonight." {name} waved at the garden. "See you tomorrow, garden helpers!" The soil was quiet. It almost seemed to be smiling.

questions: {name}一開始想把蚯蚓丟掉，後來為什麼輕輕把牠們放回土裡？
{name}在菜園裡還做了哪些照顧大自然的小事？
如果你在公園看到小蟲或垃圾，你會怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這週找一天和孩子到公園或陽台，一起觀察一種小生物，看完後輕輕讓牠回到原處，並順手撿起一件垃圾丟進正確的垃圾桶。

questions: {name} first wanted to throw the worms away. Why did {he} gently put them back?
What other small things did {name} do to care for the garden?
If you saw a little bug or some trash at the park, what would you do?
en.tip: This week, visit a park or balcony together and quietly watch one small creature, then leave it where you found it. Pick up one piece of litter and put it in the right bin together.

title.en: {name} and the Hundred and Eight Crab Mothers

zh: 夏天的傍晚，{name}跟著爺爺來到海邊的小村子。路邊站著一群穿反光背心的叔叔阿姨，背心在夕陽下亮晶晶的。領隊的阿美阿姨笑著說：「今晚是紅色陸蟹媽媽過馬路的大日子，牠們要到海裡放寶寶喔！」
爺爺幫{name}穿上一件小小的反光背心，又遞給{him}一支手電筒和一本記錄本。阿美阿姨說：「你負責數螃蟹。記得一定要站在三角錐後面的草地上，跟在爺爺身邊。」{name}用力點點頭，把記錄本抱得緊緊的。
天黑了，草叢裡傳來沙沙的聲音。一隻、兩隻、三隻……紅通通的螃蟹舉著大鉗子，橫著走了出來。牠們的肚子下面抱著滿滿的卵，走得好慢好小心。{name}輕聲數著，在本子上畫下一條又一條小線。
遠方亮起了車燈。阿美阿姨舉起發光的指揮棒，站在路邊向司機揮手。車子慢慢停了下來，司機搖下車窗說：「原來是螃蟹在過馬路啊！我等牠們。」{name}和爺爺一起向司機揮揮手，大聲說謝謝。
三角錐旁的草地上，有一隻螃蟹的鉗子被塑膠袋纏住了。{name}想伸手去抓，爺爺輕聲說：「別急，用這個。」爺爺遞來一支軟軟的小刷子。{name}小心地撥開袋子，再把螃蟹輕輕推向前。螃蟹揮揮鉗子，繼續往海邊走。
{name}撿起那個塑膠袋，走到垃圾桶前仔細看了看，放進「可回收」那一格。爺爺說：「路上少一個袋子，螃蟹媽媽就好走多了。」{name}又在草叢邊找到兩個寶特瓶，也一起放好，心裡暖暖的。
夜越來越深，{name}一邊打哈欠，一邊繼續數。有個跟著媽媽來的小哥哥，想把一隻螃蟹帶回家當寵物。{name}小聲說：「牠的寶寶在等大海呢。」小哥哥想了想，把螃蟹放回草地上，看著牠橫著走向浪花。
天邊慢慢變成粉紅色。{name}數一數本子上的線，開心地說：「一百零八隻！」海浪嘩啦嘩啦地響，螃蟹媽媽在浪花裡抖一抖身體，把寶寶送進大海。{name}牽著爺爺的手，看著乾乾淨淨的海邊，笑得好燦爛。
en: One summer evening, {name} and Grandpa arrived at a little village by the sea. Along the road stood a group of grown-ups in bright vests that glittered in the sunset. Their leader, Auntie Mei, smiled and said, "Tonight is a big night. The red land crab mothers are crossing the road to bring their babies to the sea!"

Grandpa helped {name} put on a small shiny vest and handed over a flashlight and a notebook. "Your job is to count the crabs," said Auntie Mei. "Always stay on the grass behind the orange cones, right next to Grandpa." {name} nodded hard and hugged the notebook close.

When it grew dark, something rustled in the bushes. One, two, three... bright red crabs came out, walking sideways with their big claws held high. Each mother carried a bundle of tiny eggs under her belly, so she moved slowly and carefully. {name} counted softly, drawing a little line for every crab.

Headlights glowed far down the road. Auntie Mei lifted her glowing wand and waved from the roadside. The car slowed down and stopped. The driver rolled down the window and said, "Oh, the crabs are crossing! I'll wait for them." {name} and Grandpa waved and called out, "Thank you!"

On the grass beside the cones, one crab had its claw tangled in a plastic bag. {name} reached out to grab it, but Grandpa said gently, "Easy now. Try this." He passed over a soft little brush. {name} carefully brushed the bag away and nudged the crab forward. The crab waved its claws and kept going.

{name} picked up the plastic bag, looked closely at the trash bins, and dropped it into the recycling one. "One less bag makes the path easier for the crab mothers," said Grandpa. Then {name} found two plastic bottles by the bushes and put them in the right bin too.

The night grew late, and {name} yawned but kept counting. A boy who had come with his mom wanted to take a crab home as a pet. {name} whispered, "Her babies are waiting for the sea." The boy thought for a moment, set the crab back on the grass, and watched it scuttle toward the waves.

The sky slowly turned pink. {name} counted all the little lines in the notebook and cheered, "One hundred and eight!" The waves went swish, swash. In the foamy water, the crab mothers gave a little shake and sent their babies into the sea. Holding Grandpa's hand, {name} looked at the clean shore and smiled.

questions: {name}看到螃蟹被塑膠袋纏住時，是怎麼幫忙的？為什麼要用小刷子，而不是直接用手抓？
小哥哥想把螃蟹帶回家時，{name}說了什麼？如果你在海邊看到可愛的小動物，你會怎麼做？
你平常可以做哪些小事，讓公園或海邊保持乾淨漂亮？
zh.tip: 這個星期出門散步時，帶一個小袋子，和孩子一起撿起路上的垃圾並分類丟進正確的垃圾桶。回家前說一句：「我們讓這裡跟來的時候一樣美。」

questions: How did {name} help the crab tangled in the plastic bag? Why use a soft brush instead of grabbing it?
What did {name} say when the boy wanted to take a crab home? What would you do if you saw a cute little animal at the beach?
What small things can you do every day to keep a park or beach clean and beautiful?
en.tip: On a walk this week, bring a small bag and pick up litter together, sorting it into the right bins. Before heading home, say together, "We left it as beautiful as we found it."

zh: 森林裡好熱鬧。松鼠們在開派對。音樂盒咚咚咚，響得好大聲。果汁瓶、餅乾紙，丟得滿地都是。「好好玩喔！」松鼠們說。
大樹下，住著一隻穿山甲。音樂一響，牠就縮起來。縮成一顆圓圓的球。松鼠們笑著說：「穿山甲好害羞喔！」圓球動也不動。
{name}走過來，看見圓球。圓球輕輕發抖呢。{name}蹲下來，小聲問：「你還好嗎？」圓球裡傳來小小的聲音：「好吵，好亂喔。」
{name}看看四周。地上有瓶子，有紙片。花兒被壓彎了，小草也髒髒的。{name}說：「森林是大家的家。我們一起來幫忙吧！」
{name}戴上手套，撿起一個瓶子。松鼠們也跑來幫忙。撿一個，放進袋子。再撿一個，放進袋子。紙放這邊，瓶子放那邊。一下子就乾淨了！
{name}走到音樂盒旁邊。「小聲一點，好不好？」松鼠點點頭，轉小音樂。咚咚咚，變成叮叮叮。風兒沙沙吹，小鳥啾啾唱。
圓球慢慢動了動。穿山甲伸出頭，伸出腳。牠說：「謝謝你們，跟我來！」大樹後面，有一座小土堆。好多螞蟻排著隊，忙著搬食物。
「這是螞蟻的家，我一直在守護它。」穿山甲說。松鼠們睜大眼睛：「原來你不是害羞！」大家輕輕看，不去碰。森林又乾淨又安靜，跟原來一樣美。
en: The forest was so busy. The squirrels were having a party. The music box went boom, boom, boom! Juice bottles and cookie wrappers lay everywhere. "What fun!" said the squirrels.
Under a big tree lived a pangolin. When the music played, he curled up. He became a round, round ball. "Pangolin is so shy!" the squirrels giggled. The ball did not move.
Along came {name}. {name} saw the little ball. It was trembling a bit. {name} knelt down and whispered, "Are you okay?" A tiny voice said, "So noisy. So messy."
{name} looked around. Bottles here, wrappers there. The flowers were squashed. The grass was dirty. "The forest is everyone's home," said {name}. "Let's help!"
{name} put on gloves and picked up a bottle. The squirrels came to help too. Pick one up, into the bag. Pick another, into the bag. Paper here, bottles there. Soon it was clean!
{name} went to the music box. "Can we make it softer?" The squirrels nodded and turned it down. Boom, boom became ting, ting. The wind went whoosh. Birds sang tweet, tweet.
The ball wiggled a little. Out came a head. Out came four feet. "Thank you! Follow me!" said Pangolin. Behind the tree was a small hill. Lots of ants marched in a line, carrying food.

"This is the ants' home. I've been guarding it," said Pangolin. The squirrels' eyes grew wide. "You weren't shy at all!" Everyone looked gently, without touching. The forest was clean and quiet, beautiful as before.

questions: {name}看到地上的瓶子和紙片時，做了什麼？
為什麼穿山甲聽到很大的音樂就縮起來？
我們去公園或森林玩時，可以怎麼讓那裡保持漂亮？
zh.tip: 這週出門散步時，帶一個小袋子，把自己的垃圾帶回家分類，並一起輕聲說：「來的時候多漂亮，走的時候就多漂亮。」

questions: What did {name} do when {he} saw the bottles and wrappers?
Why do you think Pangolin curled up when the music was loud?
When we play at the park or in the woods, how can we keep it beautiful?
en.tip: On your next walk this week, bring a small bag to carry your own trash home and sort it together, saying softly, "Leave it as pretty as we found it."

zh: 星期六早上，媽媽要做鬆餅。打開冰箱，蛋盒卻空空的。媽媽說：「{name}，隔壁小店有賣蛋。你想自己去買嗎？我就在玻璃門外等你。」{name}的心咚咚跳，小聲說：「好，我試試看。」
媽媽把十個十元硬幣放進小錢包，交給{name}。兩人牽著手，沿著人行道走到隔壁。叮咚！玻璃門打開了。媽媽站在門外，指指玻璃說：「你一回頭，就看得到我喔。」{name}點點頭，一步走了進去。
店裡好安靜，架子好高。有麵包、有牛奶，還有一排排餅乾。林阿姨坐在櫃檯後面，正在整理收據。{name}的腿有點軟軟的。{he}回頭一看，媽媽在門外揮揮手。{name}吸一口氣，繼續往前走。
可是，蛋在哪裡呢？{name}找了一圈，都沒看到。也許可以問問林阿姨。{name}的聲音抖抖的：「林、林阿姨，請問蛋在哪裡？」林阿姨笑咪咪地說：「在冰箱旁邊的架子上喔。」
{name}找到一盒蛋，用兩隻手小心捧著。慢慢走，慢慢走，一顆都沒有搖晃。到了櫃檯，林阿姨說：「一盒一百元喔。」{name}打開小錢包。哎呀！硬幣一滑，叮叮噹噹掉了一地。
{name}的臉熱熱的，好想跑出去找媽媽。可是{name}回頭一看，媽媽在玻璃門外比了一個讚。{name}蹲下來，把硬幣一個一個撿起來。然後慢慢數：「一、二、三……十。」剛剛好十個！
{name}把硬幣放在櫃檯上。這一次，聲音比較穩了：「林阿姨，謝謝您！」林阿姨把蛋放進小袋子，輕輕交給{name}。林阿姨眨眨眼說：「我第一次買東西，手也抖個不停呢。」{name}聽了，忍不住笑了。
叮咚！{name}提著蛋，抬頭挺胸走出來。媽媽張開手，緊緊抱住{him}。回到家，鬆餅香香甜甜的。{name}咬一口，說：「媽媽，下次我可以去買麵包嗎？」媽媽笑著說：「當然可以，我一樣在門外等你。」
en: On Saturday morning, Mom wanted to make pancakes. But the egg box in the fridge was empty. "{name}, the little shop next door sells eggs," Mom said. "Would you like to buy them on your own? I'll wait right outside the glass door." {name}'s heart went thump, thump. "Okay. I'll try."

Mom put ten coins into a small purse. She handed it to {name}. They held hands and walked along the sidewalk. Ding-dong! The glass door opened. Mom stayed outside and tapped the glass. "Just turn around, and you'll see me." {name} nodded and stepped inside.

The shop was quiet, and the shelves were tall. There was bread, milk, and rows of crackers. Auntie Lin sat behind the counter, sorting receipts. {name}'s legs felt a little wobbly. {he} looked back. Mom was waving outside. {name} took a deep breath and kept walking.

But where were the eggs? {name} looked all around and couldn't find them. Maybe Auntie Lin could help. {name}'s voice came out shaky. "Auntie Lin, um, where are the eggs, please?" Auntie Lin smiled kindly. "On the shelf by the fridge, sweetie."

{name} found a box of eggs. {he} held it carefully with both hands. Slowly, slowly, not one egg wiggled. At the counter, Auntie Lin said, "That's ten coins, please." {name} opened the little purse. Oops! The coins slipped and rolled, clink, clink, all over the floor.

{name}'s cheeks felt hot. Running out to Mom sounded nice. But {name} looked back instead. Mom gave a big thumbs-up through the glass. {name} crouched down and picked up the coins, one by one. Then came slow counting. "One, two, three... ten." Exactly ten!

{name} set the coins on the counter. This time, the words came out steadier. "Thank you, Auntie Lin!" Auntie Lin put the eggs in a little bag. She handed it over gently and winked. "My hands shook the first time I went shopping too." {name} couldn't help smiling.

Ding-dong! {name} walked out, holding the bag high and proud. Mom opened her arms for a big hug. Back home, the pancakes smelled warm and sweet. {name} took a bite. "Mom, can I buy bread next time?" Mom smiled. "Of course. I'll wait right outside again."

questions: {name}找不到蛋的時候，心裡有點怕，{he}做了什麼？
硬幣掉了一地時，{name}是怎麼讓自己再試一次的？
有沒有一件事讓你有點怕，但你還是想試試看？我們可以怎麼一起準備？
zh.tip: 這個星期，帶孩子去熟悉的小店，讓孩子自己說一句「請問」或「謝謝」，您就站在看得到的地方等。事後一起說說剛才心裡的感覺。

questions: When {name} couldn't find the eggs and felt a little scared, what did {he} do?
When the coins fell on the floor, how did {name} try again?
Is there something that feels a little scary that you'd like to try? How could we get ready for it together?
en.tip: This week, visit a familiar shop and let your child say one "Excuse me" or "Thank you" on their own while you wait where they can see you. Afterward, talk together about how it felt.

zh: 公園裡，有一隻小麻雀。牠叫小啾。烏鴉嘎嘎叫，好大聲。鴿子咕咕叫，也好大聲。小啾縮著翅膀，不敢唱歌。{name}和奶奶坐在池塘邊的長椅上。
{name}問：「小啾，你怎麼不唱？」小啾小小聲說：「大鳥好大聲。我的聲音好小。」{name}笑一笑：「小小的聲音，也很好聽呀。」小啾低下頭，還是不敢唱。
忽然，風呼呼吹。天空變得灰灰的。滴答，滴答，下雨了。奶奶牽起{name}的手：「我們去涼亭躲雨。」小啾也飛進涼亭。大家靠在一起，暖暖的。
池塘那邊，鴨媽媽呱呱叫：「我的小鴨呢？」小鴨躲在高高的蘆葦裡。蘆葦沙沙搖。風好大，好吵。鴨媽媽聽不見小鴨。小鴨也聽不見媽媽。
{name}好想跑過去幫忙。可是外面在下雨。{name}拉拉奶奶：「奶奶，我們可以幫忙嗎？」奶奶說：「我們待在涼亭裡。用聲音幫忙。」烏鴉嘎嘎叫，聲音被風吹散了。
小啾從涼亭邊往外看。「我看見小鴨了！」{name}說：「小啾，你的聲音又高又亮！唱歌給鴨媽媽聽！」小啾的翅膀抖抖的：「可是我好怕。」{name}說：「我也有點怕。我們一起來。」
小啾吸一口氣。「啾啾啾！」聲音細細的，亮亮的，穿過了風。{name}拍拍手：「再一次！」「啾啾啾！小鴨在這裡！」蘆葦裡傳來：「嗶嗶嗶。」鴨媽媽跟著歌聲，一點一點游過去。
鴨媽媽找到小鴨了！小鴨鑽進媽媽的翅膀下。雨停了，太陽探出頭。鴨媽媽呱呱說：「謝謝你，小啾！」小啾說：「我剛剛好怕，可是我還是唱了。」{name}和奶奶都笑了。小啾站上樹枝，開心地唱：「啾啾啾！」
en: In the park lived a little sparrow. Her name was Chirpy. The crows cawed, so loud. The pigeons cooed, loud too. Chirpy tucked in her wings. She did not sing. {name} sat on a bench by the pond with Grandma.
"Chirpy, why don't you sing?" asked {name}. Chirpy whispered, "The big birds are so loud. My voice is so small." {name} smiled. "Small voices sound nice too." But Chirpy still did not sing.
Then the wind went whoosh! The sky turned gray. Drip, drop, here came the rain. Grandma took {name}'s hand. "Let's stay dry in the gazebo." Chirpy flew in too. They all snuggled close.
Across the pond, Mother Duck quacked. "Where is my duckling?" The duckling was hiding in the tall reeds. Swish, swish went the reeds. The wind was so noisy! Mother Duck could not hear her baby.

{name} wanted to run and help. But it was raining. {name} tugged Grandma's sleeve. "Can we help?" Grandma said, "We'll stay right here. We can help with our voices." The crows cawed, but the wind blew it away.

Chirpy peeked out. "I see the duckling!" {name} said, "Chirpy, your voice is high and clear! Sing for Mother Duck!" Chirpy's wings shook. "But I'm scared." "Me too, a little," said {name}. "Let's do it together."

Chirpy took a big breath. "Cheep, cheep, cheep!" Her song rang through the wind. {name} clapped. "Again!" "Cheep, cheep! The duckling is here!" From the reeds came, "Peep, peep." Mother Duck swam toward the song.

Mother Duck found her duckling! It snuggled under her wing. The rain stopped. The sun peeked out. "Thank you, Chirpy!" quacked Mother Duck. Chirpy said, "I was scared, but I sang anyway." {name} and Grandma smiled. Chirpy hopped on a branch. "Cheep, cheep, cheep!"

questions: 小啾說「我好怕」的時候，{name}說了什麼、做了什麼？
下雨的時候，{name}為什麼沒有跑去蘆葦那邊，而是先問奶奶？
你有沒有一件事，雖然有點怕，但還是試試看了？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子練習一句話：「我有點怕，可是我想試試看。」每當孩子嘗試一件新事情，就一起說這句話，並為這個小小的勇敢拍拍手。

questions: When Chirpy said "I'm scared," what did {name} say and do?
When it was raining, why did {name} ask Grandma first instead of running to the reeds?
Can you think of a time you felt a little scared but tried anyway?
en.tip: This week, practice one phrase together: "I feel a little scared, but I want to try." Each time your child tries something new, say it together and clap for that small brave step.

zh: 星期一早上，{name}把奶奶的舊木頭陀螺緊緊握在手心。陀螺有一圈褪色的紅條紋，底下的小鐵尖磨得亮亮的。今天是「我最喜歡的東西」分享日，每個人都要站到全班前面說一說。{name}一路上都在心裡練習，可是越走近教室，肚子就越像有蝴蝶在亂飛。
進教室前，{name}在門口停下來，小聲對林老師說：「老師，我的心跳得好快，可以請您幫忙嗎？」林老師蹲下來，輕聲說：「謝謝你告訴我。上台時你可以拿著陀螺，我會站在你旁邊。」{name}點點頭，覺得肚子裡的蝴蝶好像少飛了一隻。
分享開始了。美美拿出一個粉紅色的貝殼，小傑展示自己拼的積木機器人。小傑湊過來說：「你的陀螺放在窗台上轉，一定更酷！」{name}搖搖頭：「奶奶說，陀螺要在平平的桌子上轉，有大人在旁邊才可以。」接著，{name}舉手請林老師幫忙把講台前的桌子清空。
終於輪到{name}了。{name}走到前面，膝蓋抖個不停，全班的眼睛一起看過來。{name}張開嘴，可是早上練好的話，好像全被風吹走了，一個字也想不起來。教室裡安安靜靜的，連時鐘滴答滴答的聲音都聽得好清楚。
{name}想起奶奶說過：「心跳得快的時候，就慢慢吸一口氣，像陀螺一樣轉得穩穩的。」{name}深深吸了一口氣，把細繩一圈一圈纏好，林老師就站在桌子旁邊。手輕輕一拉，陀螺落在桌面上，嗡嗡嗡地轉了起來。
聽著那熟悉的嗡嗡聲，話一句一句回來了。「這是我奶奶的陀螺。」{name}說，「奶奶小時候，每天放學都在家門口玩它。上個暑假，奶奶花了好多天教我纏繩子，我失敗了好多次，後來才學會。」膝蓋還在抖，可是聲音越來越清楚。
陀螺慢慢停下來，同學們都舉起了手。美美問：「為什麼它會嗡嗡叫呢？」{name}想了想，老實說：「我也不知道，我回家問奶奶。」大家笑了，是開心的笑。小傑問能不能試試看，{name}看看林老師，老師點點頭，{name}就在桌邊教小傑怎麼纏繩子。
放學時，奶奶在校門口等著。{name}跑過去，一口氣說：「奶奶，我的腳一直抖，可是我還是講完了！」奶奶笑瞇瞇地牽起{his}小手。晚上，陀螺在廚房的餐桌上又轉了起來，嗡嗡嗡，好像也在為{name}拍手。
en: On Monday morning, {name} held Grandma's old wooden spinning top tightly. It had faded red stripes and a tiny metal tip, worn shiny. Today was Favorite Things Day, and everyone had to stand in front of the class and talk. {name} practiced the whole way to school, but the closer the classroom got, the more butterflies fluttered inside.

At the classroom door, {name} stopped and whispered to Ms. Lin, "My heart is beating really fast. Can you help me?" Ms. Lin knelt down and said softly, "Thank you for telling me. You can hold your top while you talk, and I'll stand right beside you." One butterfly seemed to settle down.

Sharing time began. Mia showed a pink seashell, and Leo showed a robot he had built from blocks. Leo leaned over. "Spin your top on the windowsill. That would be so cool!" {name} shook {his} head. "Grandma says tops spin on a flat table, with a grown-up close by." Then {name} raised a hand and asked Ms. Lin to clear the front desk.

At last it was {name}'s turn. Walking to the front, {name} felt both knees wobble as every face in the room turned to look. {name} opened up to speak, but all the practiced words had blown away like leaves. The room was so quiet that the clock's tick-tock sounded loud.

Then {name} remembered Grandma's words: "When your heart races, take one slow breath, and stay steady like a spinning top." {name} breathed in deeply and wound the string around the top, loop by loop, with Ms. Lin standing beside the desk. One gentle pull, and the top landed and began to hum.

Listening to that familiar hum, the words came back one by one. "This is my grandma's top," {name} said. "When she was little, she spun it after school every day. Last summer she taught me to wind the string. I got it wrong lots of times before I learned." The knees still shook, but the voice grew clearer.

The top slowed and stopped, and hands shot up. Mia asked, "Why does it hum?" {name} thought, then said honestly, "I don't know. I'll ask Grandma." Everyone laughed a happy laugh. Leo asked if he could try. {name} looked at Ms. Lin, who nodded, so {name} showed Leo how to wind the string.

After school, Grandma was waiting at the gate. {name} ran over and said all at once, "Grandma, my legs kept shaking, but I still finished my talk!" Grandma smiled and took {his} hand. That evening, the top spun on the kitchen table, humming away, as if it were cheering for {name} too.

questions: {name}的膝蓋發抖、話都忘了的時候，{he}做了什麼讓自己繼續說下去？
小傑說要把陀螺放在窗台上轉，{name}為什麼說不要？你覺得那樣也是勇敢嗎？
你有沒有心跳很快、卻還是試著去做一件事的時候？那時候你做了什麼？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子一起練習「陀螺呼吸」：緊張時慢慢吸一口氣、再慢慢吐出來，然後說一句「我有點怕，但我可以試試看」。

questions: When {name}'s knees shook and the words disappeared, what did {he} do to keep going?
Why did {name} say no to spinning the top on the windowsill? Do you think that was brave too?
Can you remember a time your heart was racing but you tried something anyway? What did you do?
en.tip: This week, practice "spinning-top breathing" together: take one slow breath in and out when nervous, then say, "I feel a little scared, but I can try."

title.en: {name} and the Second Cup of Tea

zh: 每天下午，阿嬤都會牽著{name}去公園散步。榕樹下的石桌旁，總坐著一位白髮爺爺，獨自擺著一盤象棋。幾個孩子邊跑邊竊笑：「他好奇怪，自己跟自己下棋，還會對空氣說話！」{name}放慢了腳步，悄悄多看了一眼。
這一看，{name}發現了一件怪事。爺爺身邊放著兩個茶杯，一杯在他手邊，另一杯擺在對面的空位上，飄著淡淡的麥茶香。爺爺每移動一顆棋子，就抬頭望向空位，嘴角動了動，又慢慢垂下眼睛。那張臉，看起來好安靜，也好寂寞。
{name}想起上學期，好朋友小安轉學了。午餐時，旁邊的座位空蕩蕩的，{his}便當吃起來一點都不香。「說不定爺爺也在等一個人。」{name}拉拉阿嬤的手：「我可以去跟爺爺說說話嗎？」阿嬤點點頭：「我就坐在旁邊的椅子織毛線，陪著你。」
{name}走到石桌旁，輕聲問：「爺爺，你還好嗎？」爺爺愣了一下，隨即笑出滿臉皺紋。「叫我陳爺爺吧。我的老棋友阿林，搬去南部跟女兒住了。我們在這裡下了三十年的棋，我倒茶倒習慣了，總是多倒一杯。」他摸摸對面的杯子，「這杯茶，等不到人喝。」
{name}深吸一口氣：「那……您可以教我下棋嗎？」陳爺爺的眼睛一下子亮了起來。他把紅棋推到{name}面前：「馬走日，象走田，小兵過了河才能橫著走。」{name}聽得頭昏腦脹，第一步就把象往河對岸推。「哎呀，大象過不了楚河漢界啦！」兩人都笑彎了腰。
那一盤，{name}輸得落花流水；第二天，又兵敗如山倒。可是{name}沒有放棄，回家後拿紙畫棋盤，一遍遍練習馬怎麼跳。到了第五天，{name}的馬巧妙一跳，直直盯住爺爺的將。「將軍！」陳爺爺拍腿大笑：「好樣的，青出於藍！」
這時，陳爺爺從口袋掏出一封信。「阿林寫信來，問我在公園有沒有新棋友。」他眨眨眼，「我昨天就回信了，說有個認真的小徒弟，每天準時報到。原來這第二杯茶，是在等你來喝的。」說完，他把對面那杯早已放涼的麥茶，推到{name}手邊。
從那天起，榕樹下的石桌旁又坐了兩個人。曾經竊笑的孩子們也湊過來看，有人小聲問：「可以教我們嗎？」陳爺爺笑呵呵地多拿出幾個杯子。夕陽把棋盤染成金色，阿嬤收起毛線，{name}揮揮手：「陳爺爺，明天見！」
en: Every afternoon, Grandma walked {name} through the park. Under the big banyan tree, a white-haired old man sat alone at a stone table, playing Chinese chess. Some kids ran past, giggling. "He's so weird! He plays against nobody and talks to the air!" {name} slowed down to take a closer look.

That was when {name} noticed something odd. The old man had two cups of barley tea. One sat by his hand. The other waited on the empty side of the table. After each move, he glanced at the empty seat, then looked down. His face seemed quiet, and very lonely.

{name} remembered when {his} best friend, Annie, changed schools. At lunch, the seat beside {him} stayed empty, and even a favorite lunch tasted dull. "Maybe Grandpa is waiting for someone, too." {name} tugged Grandma's hand. "Can I go talk to him?" Grandma nodded. "I'll knit right on that bench, close by."

{name} stepped up to the table and asked softly, "Grandpa, are you OK?" The old man blinked, then smiled until his whole face crinkled. "Call me Grandpa Chen. My old chess buddy, Lin, moved south to live with his daughter. We played here for thirty years. I still pour two cups out of habit." He patted the far cup. "Nobody comes to drink it."

{name} took a deep breath. "Could you teach me to play?" Grandpa Chen's eyes lit up. He slid the red pieces over. "Horses jump in an L, elephants step corner to corner, and soldiers move sideways only after crossing the river." {name}'s head spun. On the very first move, {name} pushed an elephant across the river. "Oops! Elephants can't cross the river!" They both laughed until their sides hurt.

{name} lost that game badly, and the next one, too. But {name} didn't give up. At home, {name} drew a board on paper and practiced the horse's jump again and again. On the fifth day, {name}'s horse leaped into place, aimed straight at Grandpa's general. "Check!" Grandpa Chen slapped his knee. "Well done! The student is catching up with the teacher!"

Then Grandpa Chen pulled a letter from his pocket. "Lin wrote to ask if I'd found a new chess friend." He winked. "I wrote back yesterday. I told him about a hardworking student who shows up every single day. I guess that second cup was waiting for you all along." He slid the cooled barley tea over to {name}.

From then on, two players sat at the stone table again. The kids who once giggled crept closer to watch. One whispered, "Could you teach us, too?" Grandpa Chen chuckled and brought out more cups. As the sunset turned the board golden, Grandma packed up her knitting, and {name} waved. "See you tomorrow, Grandpa Chen!"

questions: 別的小朋友說陳爺爺很奇怪，{name}卻看到了什麼，讓{name}覺得爺爺其實很寂寞？
{name}想起好朋友轉學的事，這怎麼幫助{name}知道爺爺的心情？你有過類似的感覺嗎？
如果你看到一個人獨自坐著、表情悶悶的，你可以怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這個星期吃晚餐時，玩「看臉猜心情」的小遊戲：輪流做一個表情，讓對方猜猜是什麼感覺，再練習說一句「你還好嗎？」。

questions: The other kids said Grandpa Chen was weird. What did {name} notice that showed he was actually lonely?
{name} remembered a best friend changing schools. How did that help {name} understand Grandpa Chen's feelings? Have you ever felt that way?
If you saw someone sitting alone with a sad face, what could you do?
en.tip: At dinner this week, play a "guess the feeling" game: take turns making a face while the other person guesses the feeling, then practice asking, "Are you OK?"

zh: 動物園裡住著一頭大象，名叫波波。波波很大，心也很大。牠最喜歡幫忙。牠幫長頸鹿搆樹葉，也幫小鴨推開樹枝。今天早上，{name}和飼育員阿美姐姐一起來看牠。波波舉起長鼻子，開心地叫：「嗚——叭！」
大象家旁邊，有一座小小的花園。那是小老鼠吱吱種的。裡面有紅色的小番茄，還有黃色的小花。吱吱每天都會去澆水。可是今天，波波急著去幫河馬搬南瓜。牠咚、咚、咚地走過去。哎呀！一隻大腳踩進了花園。
小花扁了，番茄也滾了出來。吱吱跳上石頭，吱吱吱地大叫。牠的小腳一直跺，尾巴抖個不停。波波低頭看，只看到一個小灰點。「我是去幫忙的呀！」波波說。牠的大耳朵垂下來，慢慢走開了。
{name}看見吱吱的臉皺皺的，眼睛紅紅的。{name}蹲下來，輕輕問：「你還好嗎？」吱吱吸吸鼻子說：「我已經種第三次了。」接著，{name}跟著阿美姐姐去找波波。波波的大眼睛也濕濕的。「你還好嗎？」{name}問。波波說：「吱吱生氣了，我好難過。」
{name}想了想，說：「波波，我們來玩個遊戲。你把身體趴低，低到跟吱吱一樣高。」波波慢慢彎下前腳，把下巴貼在草地上。阿美姐姐在旁邊笑著點頭。{name}也趴下來，跟波波一起看向花園。
哇，從這裡看，世界好不一樣！小花像大樹一樣高。番茄像紅色的大球。波波的大腳印，像一個好大的洞。波波小聲說：「原來吱吱的花園，對牠來說這麼大。我的腳一踩，就像房子倒了。」牠的鼻子輕輕捲了起來。
波波站起來，走到吱吱身邊。「對不起，我踩壞了你的花。」牠說。{name}指著花園旁邊的石頭小路。「以後走這條小路，好不好？」波波點點頭，一步一步慢慢走。牠每走一步，都先低頭看一看。吱吱的尾巴，不再抖了。
波波去水池吸了滿滿一鼻子水。牠把鼻子舉高，輕輕一噴。水像細細的雨，落進花園裡。扁扁的小花慢慢站起來了。吱吱拍手說：「謝謝你，波波！你是最小心的大象！」{name}笑了，波波也開心地叫：「嗚——叭！」
en: Bobo the elephant lived at the zoo. He was big, and he loved to help. He reached leaves for Giraffe. He moved branches for Duck. One morning, {name} visited with Amy the zookeeper. Bobo lifted his trunk and trumpeted hello!

Next to Bobo's yard was a tiny garden. Squeaky the mouse grew red tomatoes and yellow flowers there. She watered them every day. But today, Bobo hurried off to help Hippo carry pumpkins. Thump, thump, thump! Oops! One big foot landed in the garden.

The flowers went flat. The tomatoes rolled away. Squeaky jumped onto a rock. "Squeak, squeak, squeak!" Her tiny feet stamped. Her tail shook. Bobo looked down and only saw a little gray dot. "I was just helping!" he said. His ears drooped, and he walked away.

{name} saw Squeaky's scrunched-up face and wet eyes. {name} knelt down. "Are you OK?" "I've planted it three times," Squeaky sniffed. Then {name} and Amy went to find Bobo. His big eyes were wet too. "Are you OK?" {name} asked. "Squeaky is mad, and I feel sad," said Bobo.

{name} had an idea. "Let's play a game, Bobo. Lie down as low as Squeaky." Bobo slowly bent his front legs. He rested his chin on the grass. Amy smiled and nodded. {name} lay down too, and they peeked at the garden together.

Wow! Everything looked so different down here! The flowers were tall like trees. The tomatoes were like big red balls. Bobo's footprint looked like a giant hole. "Oh," Bobo whispered. "To Squeaky, my step is like a house falling down." His trunk curled up gently.

Bobo stood up and went to Squeaky. "I'm sorry I squashed your flowers," he said. {name} pointed to a little stone path. "Want to walk here from now on?" Bobo nodded. He walked slowly and looked down before every step. Squeaky's tail stopped shaking.

Bobo filled his trunk at the pond. He lifted it high and sprayed gently, like soft rain. The flat flowers slowly stood up again. "Thank you, Bobo!" Squeaky cheered. "You're the most careful elephant ever!" {name} laughed, and Bobo trumpeted happily.

questions: 吱吱生氣時，牠的臉和尾巴是什麼樣子？波波難過時又是什麼樣子？
{name}趴低看花園時，發現了什麼？那讓波波想到什麼？
如果你看到朋友臉皺皺的，你會怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這週玩「看臉猜心情」遊戲：輪流做出開心、難過、生氣的表情，另一個人猜，再練習問一句「你還好嗎？」。

questions: How did Squeaky's face and tail look when she was angry? How did Bobo look when he was sad?
What did {name} and Bobo notice when they lay down low? What did that help Bobo understand?
If you saw a friend with a scrunched-up face, what would you do?
en.tip: This week, play a 'guess my feeling' game: take turns making happy, sad, or angry faces, have the other person guess, then practice asking, "Are you OK?"

zh: 晚餐時間到了。叮叮噹，碗筷擺好了。阿姨也來了。阿姨抱著小表妹米米。米米小小的，軟軟的。{name}笑著說：「米米好！」
大家坐下來吃飯。玩具音樂盒在旁邊響。叮咚叮咚，好大聲。突然，米米哭了。哇——哇——哇！米米一直哭，一直哭。
{name}趕快摀住耳朵。哇！好吵喔！{name}皺起眉頭。可是，米米還在哭。{name}看看米米的小臉。小臉紅紅的。眼睛濕濕的。米米怎麼了呢？
{name}輕輕問：「米米，你還好嗎？」米米還不會說話。米米只會哭。{name}想一想。如果我是米米呢？我哭的時候，是怎麼了？
是肚子餓了嗎？阿姨拿來奶瓶。米米喝一口，咕嚕。哇——又哭了。不是肚子餓。是想睡覺嗎？米米揉揉眼睛。嗯，有一點點睏。
叮咚叮咚，音樂盒還在響。剛剛{name}也覺得好吵。米米的耳朵小小的。米米一定也覺得好吵！{name}跑過去，把音樂轉小聲。
屋子靜下來了。{name}靠近米米。{name}輕輕唱：「啦啦啦，米米乖，小星星，亮起來。」米米不哭了。米米睜大眼睛，看著{name}。
米米張開小嘴巴。啊——好大一個哈欠！{name}也打了一個哈欠。啊——大家都笑了。阿姨說：「謝謝你，{name}！」米米甜甜地睡著了。
en: Dinner time! Clink, clink, the bowls are ready. Auntie comes over. She carries baby cousin Mimi. Mimi is small and soft. "Hi, Mimi!" says {name}.
Everyone sits down to eat. A toy music box plays nearby. Ding-dong, ding-dong! So loud! Then Mimi starts to cry. Waaa! Waaa! Mimi cries and cries.
{name} covers {his} ears. Oh, so noisy! But Mimi keeps crying. {name} looks at Mimi's little face. It is red and wet with tears. What is wrong?
{name} asks softly, "Mimi, are you okay?" Mimi cannot talk yet. Mimi can only cry. {name} thinks and thinks. What if I were Mimi? Why do I cry?
Is Mimi hungry? Auntie brings a bottle. Gulp! Mimi drinks a little. Then, waaa! Not hungry. Is Mimi sleepy? Mimi rubs her eyes. Hmm, a little sleepy.
Ding-dong! The music box is still loud. It was too loud for {name}. Mimi has tiny ears. It is too loud for Mimi too! {name} turns the music down.
The room gets quiet. {name} sits close to Mimi. {he} sings softly, "La la la, Mimi dear. Little stars are shining here." Mimi stops crying. She looks at {name}.
Mimi opens her little mouth. Ahhh, a big yawn! Then {name} yawns too. Ahhh! Everyone laughs. "Thank you, {name}!" says Auntie. Mimi falls fast asleep.

questions: 米米一直哭的時候，{name}看了米米的哪裡？看到了什麼？
{name}覺得音樂很吵，為什麼想到米米也會覺得吵？
如果你的朋友哭了，你可以怎麼問他、幫他？
zh.tip: 這週吃飯時玩「看臉猜心情」：輪流做開心、難過、想睡的表情，讓孩子猜猜看，再一起練習說「你還好嗎？」。

questions: When Mimi kept crying, where did {name} look, and what did {he} see?
The music felt too loud for {name}. Why did {he} think it was too loud for Mimi too?
If a friend is crying, what could you ask, and how could you help?
en.tip: At dinner this week, play "Guess My Feeling": take turns making happy, sad, or sleepy faces, let your child guess, then practice saying "Are you okay?" together.

zh: 早上，太陽暖暖的。{name}和媽媽來到海邊。媽媽坐在大傘下，笑著揮揮手。{name}拿起小鏟子，開始堆沙堡。{he}挖呀挖，拍呀拍。先做城牆，再做一扇小門。海鷗在天上嘎嘎叫。
太陽越爬越高了。{name}堆出一座高高的塔。{he}用貝殼當窗戶，再插上一根羽毛當旗子。「完成了！」{name}開心地拍拍手。這是最棒的沙堡！媽媽說：「好漂亮，你好用心喔！」
這時候，阿樂追著海灘球跑過來。他跑得好快好快。「小心！」{name}大叫。可是來不及了。阿樂的腳踩了下去。噗的一聲，高塔垮了。羽毛旗子也倒在沙子裡。
「你弄壞了！」{name}大聲喊。心裡好像有一團火，燒得熱熱的。{name}轉過身，不想看阿樂。阿樂愣了一下，慢慢走開了。{name}坐在沙堡旁邊，一動也不動。
{name}看著倒掉的塔。心裡沉沉的，像裝滿溼沙的水桶。媽媽走過來，坐在旁邊。「很生氣，對不對？」{name}點點頭。媽媽輕輕抱了抱{him}。小小的浪花，刷刷地拍著沙灘。
過了一會兒，阿樂回來了。他提著紅色大水桶和小鏟子。「對不起，我不是故意的。」阿樂小聲說。「我可以幫你蓋回來嗎？」{name}想了想，說：「我做了一整個早上。塔倒了，我好難過。」
阿樂低下頭說：「我知道，真的對不起。」{name}看看阿樂，又看看水桶。心裡那團火，慢慢變小了。沉沉的感覺，也輕輕飄走了。「好，我們一起蓋！」{name}說。阿樂開心地笑了。
他們一起挖沙、裝桶、倒扣。一座、兩座、三座塔！這次的城堡又大又高。阿樂撿來亮亮的貝殼。{name}插上那根羽毛旗子。天空變成橘色時，媽媽幫他們拍照。兩個好朋友，笑得好開心。
en: The morning sun was warm. {name} and Mom came to the beach. Mom sat under a big umbrella and waved. {name} picked up a little shovel and started a sandcastle. Dig, dig. Pat, pat. First came the walls, then a tiny door. Seagulls squawked overhead.

The sun climbed higher. {name} built one tall, tall tower. Shells became windows. A feather became a flag. "Done!" {name} cheered and clapped. It was the best castle ever. "Beautiful," said Mom. "You worked so hard!"

Just then, Leo came running after a beach ball. He was running very fast. "Watch out!" {name} yelled. But it was too late. Leo's foot came down. Squish! The tower crumbled. The feather flag fell into the sand.

"You wrecked it!" {name} shouted. It felt like a hot fire inside. {name} turned away and would not look at Leo. Leo stood still for a moment. Then he slowly walked off. {name} sat by the broken castle, very quiet.

{name} stared at the fallen tower. Everything inside felt heavy, like a bucket full of wet sand. Mom came over and sat close by. "You feel really angry, don't you?" {name} nodded. Mom gave {him} a gentle hug. Little waves swished on the shore.

After a while, Leo came back. He carried a big red bucket and a small shovel. "I'm sorry," Leo said softly. "I didn't mean to. Can I help build it again?" {name} thought for a moment. "I worked all morning. When the tower fell, I felt so sad."

Leo looked down. "I know. I'm really sorry." {name} looked at Leo, then at the bucket. The fire inside grew smaller and smaller. The heavy feeling floated away. "Okay," {name} said. "Let's build together!" Leo grinned.

They dug, filled, and flipped the bucket. One tower, two towers, three towers! This castle was even bigger than before. Leo found shiny shells. {name} added the feather flag. When the sky turned orange, Mom took a picture. Two friends smiled side by side.

questions: 阿樂回來說對不起的時候，{name}告訴阿樂自己有什麼感覺？
{name}原諒阿樂以後，心裡那團火和沉沉的感覺發生了什麼事？
如果有朋友不小心弄壞你的東西，又跟你說對不起，你會怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子練習一句話：「我很難過，因為……；謝謝你說對不起。」可以先用玩偶演一演，讓孩子知道說出感受和原諒可以一起做到。

questions: When Leo came back to say sorry, what did {name} tell him about how it felt?
After {name} forgave Leo, what happened to the fire and the heavy feeling inside?
If a friend broke something of yours by accident and said sorry, what would you do?
en.tip: This week, practice one phrase together: "I felt sad because...; thank you for saying sorry." Act it out with stuffed animals first, so your child sees that sharing feelings and forgiving can go together.

zh: 森林裡有一條小溪。溪邊長滿高高的蘆葦。小水獺坐在草地上，忙了一整個早上。她用蘆葦編了一艘小木筏。木筏小小的，綁得整整齊齊。{name}和河狸爺爺坐在旁邊看。「好漂亮喔！」{name}說。小水獺開心得吱吱叫。
今天溪邊有游泳比賽。大水獺想當第一名。「讓開！讓開！」他一邊喊，一邊往前衝。砰的一聲，他撞到了小木筏。蘆葦一根根散開了。木筏變成一堆亂草。大水獺停下來，回頭看了一眼。
小水獺看著散掉的蘆葦。她的眼睛紅紅的。「我的木筏……」她小聲說。大水獺的心裡酸酸的。他想說對不起。可是他抬起下巴，說：「是它擋在路上啦。」說完，他把頭轉開。小水獺抱著蘆葦，一句話也不說。
{name}走到大水獺身邊。「你是不是也很難過？」{name}輕輕問。大水獺低下頭。「嗯……可是我是最大的水獺。說對不起好丟臉。」{name}想了想。「我做錯事時也會怕。可是說出來，心裡就輕輕的。」
「那我要怎麼說？」大水獺問。{name}說：「先說你做了什麼，再說對不起。」大水獺深深吸一口氣。他慢慢走向小水獺。他的腳步好重好重。河狸爺爺在一旁點點頭，微微一笑。
「小水獺，我跑太快，撞壞了你的木筏。對不起，是我錯了。」小水獺抬起頭。「我好難過，也好生氣。那是我編了一早上的。」大水獺點點頭。「你說得對。我可以幫你重新編一艘嗎？」
小水獺想了一下。她心裡那團重重的氣，慢慢變小了。「好，我原諒你。」她說，「可是你要綁緊喔！」大水獺笑了。他們一起撿蘆葦。{name}幫忙遞草繩。大水獺力氣大，把結拉得緊緊的。小水獺教他怎麼交叉編。
太陽爬到樹梢時，新木筏編好了。它比原來的更大，也更結實。小水獺把它放在淺淺的水邊。木筏穩穩地漂著，一點也不晃。「下次我們一起比賽吧！」大水獺說。兩隻水獺吱吱叫，{name}也開心地拍手。
en: A little stream ran through the forest. Tall reeds grew along its bank. Little Otter sat on the grass all morning. She was weaving a tiny raft from reeds. Every knot was neat and snug. {name} watched with Grandpa Beaver nearby. "It's beautiful!" said {name}. Little Otter squeaked with joy.

Today there was a swimming race. Big Otter wanted to be first. "Move! Move!" he shouted as he dashed ahead. Bump! He crashed right into the little raft. The reeds flew apart. The raft became a messy pile of grass. Big Otter stopped and looked back.

Little Otter stared at the scattered reeds. Her eyes turned red. "My raft…" she whispered. Big Otter's tummy felt tight and sour. He wanted to say sorry. But he lifted his chin and said, "It was in my way." Then he turned his head. Little Otter hugged her reeds and said nothing.

{name} walked over to Big Otter. "Do you feel sad too?" {name} asked softly. Big Otter looked down. "Yes. But I'm the biggest otter. Saying sorry feels silly." {name} thought for a moment. "I feel scared when I make mistakes. But saying it makes my heart feel light."

"What do I say?" asked Big Otter. "First say what you did," said {name}. "Then say sorry." Big Otter took a deep breath. He walked slowly to Little Otter. His feet felt so heavy. Grandpa Beaver nodded and smiled.

"Little Otter, I ran too fast and broke your raft. I'm sorry. I was wrong." Little Otter looked up. "I felt sad and angry. I worked on it all morning." Big Otter nodded. "You're right. May I help you weave a new one?"

Little Otter thought for a moment. The heavy, grumpy feeling inside her began to shrink. "Okay. I forgive you," she said. "But tie the knots tight!" Big Otter grinned. Together they gathered reeds. {name} passed them grass string. Big Otter pulled every knot strong. Little Otter showed him how to cross the reeds.

By the time the sun reached the treetops, the new raft was done. It was bigger and sturdier than before. Little Otter set it in the shallow water by the bank. It floated steady and still. "Let's race together next time!" said Big Otter. Both otters squeaked, and {name} clapped happily.

questions: 大水獺一開始為什麼不肯說對不起？後來{name}怎麼幫他？
小水獺原諒大水獺之前，先說了自己有什麼感覺？
如果有人弄壞你的東西，又來跟你道歉，你會怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子練習「道歉三步驟」：說出我做了什麼、說對不起、問「我可以怎麼幫忙？」。被道歉的一方也可以先說出自己的感覺，再決定要不要原諒。

questions: Why didn't Big Otter want to say sorry at first? How did {name} help him?
Before Little Otter forgave Big Otter, what did she say about how she felt?
If someone broke something of yours and then said sorry, what would you do?
en.tip: This week, practice a three-step sorry together: say what I did, say sorry, and ask "How can I help?" The one hearing the apology can share how they felt first, then choose to forgive.

title.en: The Little Heart in the Corner

zh: 星期四晚上，{name}終於把最後一顆行星塗好了。海報上，太陽金光閃閃，八顆行星整整齊齊排成一列，土星的光環還是用尺一筆一筆畫出來的。{name}伸了個懶腰，把海報攤在客廳桌上晾乾，心裡美滋滋的：明天交出去，老師一定會眼睛一亮。接著，{he}哼著歌去浴室刷牙。
刷完牙回來，{name}一下子愣住了。五歲的妹妹莫莫跪在椅子上，手裡握著一支紅色蠟筆，正在海報上塗得不亦樂乎。木星旁邊、地球上方，到處是歪歪扭扭的紅線條。「莫莫！」{name}大叫一聲，一把搶過海報。莫莫嚇了一大跳，蠟筆「咚」地滾到地上。
「妳把我的東西全毀了！」{name}的聲音又尖又響，「我花了整整三天！妳每次都這樣，最討厭了，以後不准再碰我的東西！」莫莫的嘴角往下垮，眼淚在眼眶裡打轉。她小聲說：「對不起……」然後轉身跑進房間。{name}氣呼呼地坐在沙發上，胸口像塞了一顆大石頭，又悶又重。
爸爸走過來，在{name}身邊坐下，沒有責備，只是輕輕拍了拍{his}背。過了好一會兒，{name}才又拿起海報，想看看還有沒有救。這一看，{he}忽然怔住了。那些紅線條根本不是亂畫的——是一顆顆小小的愛心，圍著{name}的名字繞了一圈，旁邊還有兩個東倒西歪的大字：「最棒」。
房門輕輕打開，莫莫抱著一捲膠帶和一盒蠟筆走出來，鼻子哭得紅通通的。「我只是想讓你的海報變漂亮，」她抽抽噎噎地說，「我可以幫忙重畫，這次我會很小心、很小心。」{name}看著她小手裡那捲膠帶，胸口那顆大石頭，好像悄悄鬆動了一點點。
{name}蹲下來，深深吸了一口氣。「莫莫，我剛才真的很生氣，也很難過，因為那是我努力好久的作品。下次想畫，先問我，好嗎？」莫莫用力點頭。「還有，」{name}接著說，「我不該說妳最討厭，對不起。我原諒妳了。」莫莫立刻破涕為笑，撲過來緊緊抱住{him}。
那天晚上，兩人在餐桌前並肩忙碌。{name}重新畫行星，莫莫負責遞彩色筆，還小心翼翼地幫土星光環塗上淡黃色。爸爸泡了熱可可，笑說這是「全家最強太空團隊」。完成時，{name}在右下角留了一小塊空白，讓莫莫畫上一顆紅色小愛心。那顆大石頭早已不見，只剩下暖暖的、輕輕的感覺。
en: On Thursday night, {name} colored the very last planet. The poster gleamed: a golden sun, eight planets marching in a neat line, and Saturn's rings drawn carefully with a ruler. {name} stretched, laid the poster on the living room table to dry, and grinned. Tomorrow the teacher would definitely be impressed. Humming a tune, {name} went off to brush {his} teeth.

When {name} came back, the grin vanished. Momo, who was five, was kneeling on a chair with a red crayon, scribbling away happily. Wobbly red lines looped around Jupiter and swirled above Earth. "Momo!" {name} yelled, snatching the poster away. Momo jumped, and the crayon clattered to the floor.

"You ruined everything!" {name} shouted. "I worked on this for three whole days! You always do this. You're the worst! Don't ever touch my stuff again!" Momo's lip trembled, and her eyes filled with tears. "Sorry," she whispered, and she ran to her room. {name} flopped onto the couch, feeling as if a heavy stone sat right in the middle of {his} chest.

Dad came over and sat down. He didn't scold; he just gently patted {name}'s back. After a long while, {name} picked up the poster again to see if it could be rescued. Then {he} froze. The red lines weren't random at all. They were tiny hearts, circling {name}'s name, and beside them, in big tumbling letters, was one word: BEST.

Momo's door creaked open. She shuffled out hugging a roll of tape and a box of crayons, her nose pink from crying. "I just wanted to make your poster prettier," she sniffled. "I can help fix it. I'll be super, super careful." {name} looked at the tape in her small hands, and the stone seemed to wobble loose, just a little.

{name} knelt down and took a deep breath. "Momo, I was really angry and sad, because I worked so hard on that. Next time, ask me first, okay?" Momo nodded hard. "And," {name} went on, "I shouldn't have called you the worst. I'm sorry. I forgive you." Momo's tears turned into a giggle, and she threw her arms around {him}.

That evening the two of them worked side by side at the table. {name} redrew the planets while Momo handed over markers and carefully colored Saturn's rings pale yellow. Dad brought mugs of hot cocoa and called them "the family's best space team." When they finished, {name} left a little space in the bottom corner, and Momo drew one small red heart there. The heavy stone was gone. Only something warm and light remained.

questions: 莫莫說對不起、還拿膠帶來幫忙時，{name}做了什麼？你覺得{name}為什麼願意原諒她？
{name}原諒莫莫時，還是說出了自己很生氣、很難過。你覺得把感受說出來有什麼幫助？
你有沒有被別人弄壞東西、或不小心弄壞別人東西的經驗？那時候發生了什麼？
zh.tip: 這週試著練習一句「我覺得＿＿，因為＿＿，我原諒你」，在家人之間發生小摩擦時，大人可以先示範說一次。

questions: What did {name} do when Momo said sorry and brought tape to help? Why do you think {name} chose to forgive her?
When {name} forgave Momo, {name} still said how angry and sad it felt. How can telling your feelings help?
Has someone ever broken something of yours, or have you accidentally broken something of someone else's? What happened?
en.tip: This week, practice the phrase "I felt ___ because ___, and I forgive you." The next time a small family conflict happens, model it yourself first.

title.en: A Rainbow for the Green Scooter

zh: 每天早上，街上都會傳來「噗噗噗」的聲音。{name}趴在窗邊，眼睛亮亮的。來了！是郵差阿福叔叔，騎著綠色的機車。他把信放進信箱，還對窗戶揮揮手。{name}也用力揮手，揮得像小風車一樣。
有一天，外面下起大雨。嘩啦啦，嘩啦啦。{name}心想：「今天阿福叔叔不會來了吧？」可是，噗噗噗的聲音又來了！阿福叔叔穿著黃色雨衣，像一根會跑的香蕉。{name}忍不住咯咯笑。信箱裡的信，一點都沒有濕。
「媽媽，阿福叔叔每天都來耶。」{name}說。媽媽點點頭：「下雨天也來，真的很辛苦。」{name}看著窗外想了想。掃街的阿姨也天天來。麵包店的伯伯，每天都烤香香的麵包。原來有好多人，默默在幫忙大家。{name}覺得心裡暖暖的、滿滿的。
「我想跟阿福叔叔說謝謝！」{name}說。可是叔叔騎得好快，噗噗噗就不見了。要怎麼說呢？{name}拿出蠟筆，眼睛一亮。「我來畫一張畫！」{name}先畫一台綠色機車。輪子圓圓的，像兩個甜甜圈。
畫著畫著，{name}又加上阿福叔叔。哎呀！叔叔的頭畫得太大了，像一顆大西瓜。{name}和媽媽一起哈哈大笑。沒關係，再畫一道彩虹吧！紅、橙、黃、綠、藍、紫，彎彎的彩虹，就掛在機車上面。
「要放在哪裡呢？」{name}問。「貼在信箱上，叔叔一定看得到。」媽媽說。媽媽牽著{name}的手，一起走到門口的信箱旁。{name}撕下膠帶，小心地把畫貼好。風吹過來，畫輕輕晃了晃，好像在打招呼。
隔天早上，噗噗噗的聲音又來了。{name}躲在窗簾後面偷看。阿福叔叔停下機車，看見了那張畫。他愣了一下，然後笑得好開心。他輕輕摸摸那道彩虹。接著，他在信箱裡放了一樣東西。
叔叔走後，媽媽陪{name}打開信箱。裡面有一張小紙條，畫著一個笑臉。媽媽念出來：「也謝謝你！」{name}抱著紙條，在屋子裡轉圈圈。窗外傳來兩聲喇叭：叭叭！綠色機車噗噗噗，開向下一個家。
en: Every morning, a sound comes up the street. Putt, putt, putt! {name} presses close to the window. Here comes Mr. Fu, the mail carrier, on his green scooter. He drops letters in the mailbox and waves. {name} waves back like a little windmill.

One day, big rain pours down. Splish, splash! "Mr. Fu won't come today," {name} thinks. But then, putt, putt, putt! Mr. Fu rides up in a yellow raincoat. He looks like a zooming banana! {name} giggles. The letters in the mailbox are still dry.

"Mom, Mr. Fu comes every single day," says {name}. Mom nods. "Even in the rain. That's hard work." {name} looks out and thinks. The street sweeper comes every day too. The baker bakes warm bread every morning. So many quiet helpers! {his} heart feels full and cozy.

"I want to thank Mr. Fu!" says {name}. But Mr. Fu zooms by so fast. Putt, putt, gone! How can {name} tell him? Out come the crayons. "I'll draw a picture!" First, a green scooter. Its wheels are round, like two donuts.

Next, {name} draws Mr. Fu. Oops! His head is way too big. It looks like a giant watermelon! {name} and Mom laugh and laugh. That's okay. Now for a rainbow! Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple. It curves right over the scooter.

"Where should it go?" asks {name}. "On the mailbox. Mr. Fu will see it there," says Mom. Holding hands, they walk to the mailbox by the door. {name} tears off some tape and sticks the picture on carefully. The wind makes it wiggle hello.

The next morning, putt, putt, putt! {name} peeks from behind the curtain. Mr. Fu stops his scooter. He sees the picture and blinks. Then he smiles a great big smile. He gently touches the rainbow. Then he slips something into the mailbox.

After he leaves, Mom and {name} open the mailbox. Inside is a tiny note with a smiley face. Mom reads it aloud: "Thank you too!" {name} hugs the note and spins around the room. Outside, a horn goes beep, beep! The green scooter putts off to the next house.

questions: {name}看到阿福叔叔下雨天也來送信，心裡覺得怎麼樣？
阿福叔叔看到那張畫，為什麼笑得那麼開心？
你身邊有誰每天默默幫忙你？你想用什麼小方法跟他說謝謝？
zh.tip: 這個星期和孩子一起當「謝謝小偵探」，每天睡前說出一個今天幫助過我們的人，再挑一位，一起畫張小卡或揮手說謝謝。

questions: How did {name} feel seeing Mr. Fu deliver mail even in the rain?
Why do you think Mr. Fu smiled so big when he saw the picture?
Who quietly helps you every day? What small thing could you do to thank them?
en.tip: This week, play "Thank-You Detective": each night at bedtime, name one person who helped you that day, then pick one to thank with a little drawing or a wave.

zh: 山坡上的梯田一層一層，像綠色的樓梯一路通到雲裡。小麻雀啾啾每天在田邊跳來跳去，啄著掉在地上的米粒。「米本來就在這裡呀！」啾啾吃飽了，就飛到竹籬笆上睡午覺，從來沒想過米是從哪裡來的。
這一年夏天，好久好久都沒有下雨。山溝裡的小溪變得細細的，田裡的泥土裂開一條一條的縫，稻葉也垂下了頭。{name}住在山腳下，常常來田邊找啾啾玩，這天卻發現啾啾安安靜靜地縮在籬笆上。
「怎麼了？」{name}問。啾啾用翅膀指著田埂：「你看。」天才剛亮，老水牛就拉著水車，一步一步慢慢走；林阿伯挑著兩桶水，從山泉那邊一趟一趟往上爬，汗水滴進乾乾的泥土裡。月亮出來了，他們還在忙。
啾啾小聲說：「原來我吃的每一粒米，都要花這麼多力氣才長得出來。我卻從來沒有說過謝謝。」{name}想了想，說：「那我們也來幫忙吧！」兩個好朋友一個飛、一個跑，一起去找林阿伯。
林阿伯笑著遞給{name}一個小水壺，帶{him}走到山泉邊，兩個人一起慢慢把水裝滿。啾啾也找來一片寬寬的葉子，把它當成小碗，盛著一點點水，飛到最乾的那株稻苗旁邊，輕輕地倒下去。
一壺水、一葉水，看起來好少好少。可是{name}和啾啾每天都來，跟在老水牛和林阿伯後面。老水牛低下頭，「哞——」地叫了一聲，好像在說謝謝。林阿伯擦擦汗說：「有你們陪著，這條山路好像變短了。」
終於有一天，烏雲飄過山頭，雨滴滴答答地落下來。稻苗喝飽了水，慢慢挺起腰，從綠色變成金黃色。秋天到了，整片梯田像一條條金色的毯子，在風裡沙沙地搖著。
收割那天，啾啾站在最高的稻穗上，張開翅膀，唱出最響亮的歌：「謝謝林阿伯！謝謝老水牛！謝謝雨水，也謝謝{name}！」林阿伯笑了，老水牛搖搖尾巴，{name}也拍著手一起唱。啾啾覺得心裡滿滿的，好像擁有了一整箱寶藏。
en: On the mountainside, rice terraces climbed like green stairs into the clouds. Every day, Little Sparrow hopped along the edges, pecking at fallen grains. "Rice is just always here!" Sparrow chirped. Then, with a full tummy, Sparrow napped on the bamboo fence and never once wondered where the rice came from.

One summer, the rain stayed away for a long, long time. The mountain stream shrank to a thin trickle. The mud in the fields cracked into lines, and the rice leaves drooped. {name}, who lived at the foot of the mountain, came to play and found Sparrow sitting very quietly on the fence.

"What's wrong?" {name} asked. Sparrow pointed with a wing. "Look." At sunrise, Old Buffalo was already turning the water wheel, step by slow step. Farmer Lin carried two buckets up the path from the spring, again and again, sweat dripping into the dry soil. When the moon rose, they were still working.

"Every grain I eat takes all that work to grow," Sparrow said softly. "And I never once said thank you." {name} thought for a moment. "Then let's help!" So the two friends, one flying and one running, went off together to find Farmer Lin.

Farmer Lin smiled and handed {name} a small watering can. He walked {him} to the spring, and together they filled it slowly. Sparrow found a wide leaf to use as a tiny bowl, scooped up a few drops, and flew to the driest rice plant to pour them out gently.

A can of water and a leaf of water didn't seem like much. But {name} and Sparrow came every single day, following Old Buffalo and Farmer Lin. Old Buffalo lowered his head and gave a long, low "Moo," as if to say thank you. Farmer Lin wiped his brow. "With you two here, this mountain path feels shorter."

At last, one day, dark clouds drifted over the peaks, and rain came pattering down. The rice drank and drank and slowly stood tall, turning from green to gold. By autumn, the terraces looked like golden blankets, rustling softly in the wind.

On harvest day, Sparrow perched on the tallest stalk, spread both wings, and sang loudly: "Thank you, Farmer Lin! Thank you, Old Buffalo! Thank you, rain, and thank you, {name}!" Farmer Lin laughed, Old Buffalo swished his tail, and {name} clapped and sang along. Sparrow's heart felt full, as rich as a chest of treasure.

questions: 啾啾看到老水牛和林阿伯辛苦工作以後，心裡有什麼改變？
{name}和啾啾用什麼方法說謝謝？你覺得林阿伯收到時感覺怎麼樣？
今天有誰默默幫助了你？你想用什麼小行動謝謝他們？
zh.tip: 今晚吃飯時，全家輪流說出一個今天幫助過自己的人或東西，再想一個小行動（例如幫忙擺碗筷）來表達謝意。

questions: How did Sparrow feel after seeing Old Buffalo and Farmer Lin working so hard?
How did {name} and Sparrow say thank you? How do you think Farmer Lin felt?
Who quietly helped you today, and what small action could you do to thank them?
en.tip: At dinner tonight, take turns naming one person or thing that helped you today, then pick one small action, like setting the table, to say thanks.

zh: 天黑了，月亮出來了。{name}洗好澡，躺在小床上。被子軟軟的，暖暖的。媽媽坐在床邊，輕輕拍拍被子。「今天，有誰幫助你呢？」媽媽小聲問。
{name}想一想，想起了奶奶。奶奶包的水餃，熱熱的，香香的。呼呼，吹一吹。啊嗚，吃一口。肚子飽飽的，好舒服。{name}小聲說：「謝謝奶奶。」
窗外，一閃，一閃。一顆小星星，亮起來了。「媽媽你看！」{name}輕輕指著窗戶。媽媽笑了：「星星聽見了喔。」媽媽又說：「明天，畫一張圖送奶奶吧。」{name}點點頭。
{name}又想一想，想起了爸爸。爸爸唸了故事書。有小熊，有小船。爸爸的聲音，低低的，慢慢的。{name}小聲說：「謝謝爸爸。」窗外，一閃，一閃。第二顆星星亮了。
然後，{name}想起了學校。好朋友小安，今天抱了{him}一下。抱抱暖暖的，像小太陽。{name}小聲說：「謝謝小安。」一閃，一閃。第三顆星星也亮了。
「還有誰呢？」媽媽輕輕問。{name}想啊想。軟軟的枕頭，暖暖的被子。還有一直陪著的媽媽。{name}伸出小手，抱抱媽媽。媽媽笑得眼睛彎彎：「謝謝你，寶貝。」
窗外好多星星，一閃，一閃。好像在說晚安。{name}心裡滿滿的，好像有好多寶貝。房間好安靜。風輕輕吹，呼——呼——。{name}打了一個小呵欠。
「晚安，奶奶。晚安，爸爸。」「晚安，小安。晚安，星星。」悄悄話，越來越小聲。{name}慢慢閉上眼睛。媽媽親親{his}額頭，關上小燈。「晚安，{name}。」
en: The moon is up. The sky is dark. {name} is snug in bed. The blanket is soft and warm. Mom sits close and pats the blanket. "Who helped you today?" she whispers.
{name} thinks and thinks. Grandma's dumplings! Hot and yummy. Puff, puff, blow. Yum, yum, munch. A full, happy tummy. {name} whispers, "Thank you, Grandma."

Outside the window, twinkle, twinkle. One little star lights up! "Look, Mom!" {name} points softly. Mom smiles. "The star heard you." Then she says, "Let's draw Grandma a picture tomorrow." {name} nods.
Then {name} thinks of Dad. Dad read a storybook. A little bear. A little boat. His voice was low and slow. "Thank you, Dad." Twinkle, twinkle. A second star shines.
Next, {name} thinks of school. Best friend An gave a big hug today. It felt warm, like a little sun. "Thank you, An." Twinkle, twinkle. A third star shines too.
"Anyone else?" Mom asks softly. {name} thinks some more. A soft pillow. A cozy blanket. And Mom, always close by. {name} reaches up and hugs Mom tight. Mom's eyes crinkle. "Thank you, sweetheart."
Now many stars twinkle outside. They seem to say goodnight. {name} feels full inside, rich with treasures. The room is quiet. The wind goes whoo, whoo. {name} gives a little yawn.
"Night, Grandma. Night, Dad." "Night, An. Night, stars." The whispers grow softer and softer. {name}'s eyes slowly close. Mom kisses {his} forehead and turns off the light. "Goodnight, {name}."

questions: {name}對媽媽說謝謝的時候，用了什麼小動作？媽媽有什麼感覺？
今天有誰幫助了你？你想點亮哪一顆謝謝星星？
明天你想用什麼方法，跟一個人說謝謝？
zh.tip: 今晚睡前和孩子一起說出三件今天想感謝的人或事，每說一件就在空中畫一顆星星。也可以約好明天用一個抱抱或一張小畫送給其中一個人。

questions: What small action did {name} use to thank Mom? How did Mom feel?
Who helped you today? Which thank-you star would you light up?
How would you like to show someone thanks tomorrow?
en.tip: Tonight at bedtime, name three people or things you are thankful for together, and draw a star in the air for each one. You can also plan to give one of them a hug or a little drawing tomorrow.

zh: 隔壁的林奶奶要去南部看妹妹，一走就是五天。她指著陽台上三盆綠油油的番茄說：「{name}，你能每天早上幫我澆水嗎？」{name}沒有馬上點頭，先想了想：「每天都要喔……媽媽，你可以陪我一起去嗎？」媽媽笑著說好，{name}這才大聲回答：「林奶奶，我答應你！」
林奶奶把一把銀色的小鑰匙交給媽媽，還摸摸{name}的頭說：「謝謝你，有你在，我就放心了。」第一天早上，媽媽拿著鑰匙開門，{name}提著小小的澆花壺走到陽台。番茄藤上掛著一顆顆青綠色的小果子，像一串害羞的小彈珠。
第二天，城市熱得像烤箱，馬路上的車子嗡嗡地跑。{name}記得林奶奶教過的方法，蹲下來慢慢把水倒在根旁邊，不讓水濺到葉子上。「一盆、兩盆、三盆。」{name}數得清清楚楚，媽媽在旁邊點點頭，豎起了大拇指。
第三天一早，門鈴叮咚響了。好朋友小安和爸爸站在門口，手上拿著泳圈：「{name}，我們要去水上樂園，現在就出發，一起來嘛！」{name}眼睛一亮，跳起來就想去拿泳衣。那裡有長長的滑水道，還有會噴水的大蘑菇呢！
可是{name}忽然停下腳步，想起昨天傍晚看見的番茄葉子，被太陽曬得軟軟的，垂著頭。{name}深吸一口氣，對小安說：「我答應林奶奶要幫番茄澆水。可以等我十五分鐘嗎？如果來不及，你們先走，我請媽媽晚點帶我去找你們。」
小安的爸爸笑了：「沒問題，我們在樓下等你。」媽媽拿起鑰匙，和{name}一起快步走進隔壁。{name}一盆一盆仔細澆水，水慢慢滲進土裡。過了一會兒，垂下來的葉子好像伸了個懶腰，又挺了起來。{name}開心地說：「番茄，明天見！」
那天，{name}和媽媽、小安一家在水上樂園玩得好痛快，滑水道衝下去時，大家笑得水花亂飛。接下來兩天，不管多想多睡一下，{name}還是準時起床去澆水。第五天早上，{name}發現有一顆小番茄的臉，悄悄變成了橘紅色。
傍晚，林奶奶拖著行李回來了。她到陽台看了好久，摘下第一顆紅通通的番茄，放在{name}手心：「這一趟出門，我一次都沒擔心過我的番茄。」{name}和媽媽、林奶奶一起分著吃，酸酸甜甜的味道，在嘴巴裡慢慢散開。
en: Grandma Lin next door was going to visit her sister for five whole days. She pointed to three leafy tomato pots on her balcony. "{name}, could you water them every morning?" {name} didn't answer right away. "Every day... Mom, can you come with me?" Mom nodded, and {name} said, "Yes, Grandma Lin, I promise!"

Grandma Lin gave Mom a small silver key and patted {name} on the shoulder. "Thank you. Now I won't worry." On the first morning, Mom unlocked the door, and {name} carried a little watering can to the balcony. Tiny green tomatoes hung on the vines like shy marbles.

On the second day, the city was as hot as an oven, and cars hummed along the street below. {name} remembered Grandma Lin's tip and crouched down, pouring slowly near the roots so the water wouldn't splash the leaves. "One pot, two pots, three pots." Mom gave a big thumbs-up.

Early on the third day, the doorbell rang. Anan and his dad stood there holding swim rings. "{name}, we're going to the water park right now! Come with us!" {name} jumped up to grab a swimsuit. There were long, twisty slides and a giant mushroom that sprayed water!

Then {name} stopped. Yesterday evening, the tomato leaves had looked soft and droopy in the heat. {name} took a deep breath. "I promised Grandma Lin I'd water her tomatoes. Can you wait fifteen minutes? If you can't, go ahead, and Mom can bring me later."

Anan's dad smiled. "No problem. We'll wait downstairs." Mom picked up the key, and they hurried next door. {name} watered each pot carefully and watched the water soak into the soil. Soon the droopy leaves seemed to stretch and stand tall again. "See you tomorrow, tomatoes!"

At the water park, {name}, Mom, and Anan's family zoomed down the slides, laughing as water splashed everywhere. For the next two mornings, even when bed felt cozy, {name} still got up on time to water. On the fifth morning, one little tomato had quietly turned orange-red.

That evening, Grandma Lin came home with her suitcase. She looked at her balcony for a long time, then picked the first bright red tomato and placed it in {name}'s hand. "I didn't worry about my tomatoes even once." They shared it together, sweet and tangy and warm from the sun.

questions: 林奶奶請{name}幫忙時，{name}為什麼先想一想、還問了媽媽，才說「我答應你」？
小安來邀{name}去水上樂園時，{name}是怎麼跟朋友說的？如果你遇到一樣的情況，你會怎麼做？
你有沒有答應過別人一件事？做到的時候，你和對方的心情是什麼樣子？
zh.tip: 這個星期和孩子一起選一件小小的承諾，例如每天幫植物澆水或擺好餐具，做到時一起在月曆上畫一個笑臉。如果有一天做不到，就練習說：「對不起，今天我沒做到，我可以怎麼補救？」

questions: When Grandma Lin asked for help, why did {name} stop to think and ask Mom before saying "I promise"?
What did {name} tell Anan when the water park invitation came? What would you do in the same situation?
Have you ever promised someone something? How did you both feel when you kept it?
en.tip: This week, pick one small promise together, like watering a plant or setting the table, and draw a smiley face on the calendar each day it's done. If a day gets missed, practice saying, "Sorry, I didn't do it today. How can I make it right?"

zh: 森林裡住著老烏龜。牠走得很慢，可是很穩。這天下午，{name}陪老烏龜散步。貓頭鷹飛下來，咕咕地叫。「老烏龜，你能幫我送信嗎？」「要送給草原那邊的小鹿。」「月圓以前一定要送到喔！」
老烏龜沒有馬上回答。牠看看天空，又看看小路。「草原很遠，我走得慢。」「不過現在出發，應該來得及。」牠想了想，才點點頭。「好，我答應你。」貓頭鷹交給牠一封葉子信。{name}說：「我陪你一起去！」
老烏龜把葉子信夾在殼邊。{name}走在牠旁邊。兩個好朋友走過高高的蕨葉。接著，又爬上一個小山坡。老烏龜一步、一步，慢慢走。{name}也放慢腳步，等著牠。老烏龜說：「謝謝你陪我。」
走到大榕樹下，好熱鬧呀！猴子們正在開水果派對。香蕉、芒果、甜甜的木瓜，堆得像小山一樣。小猴子吱吱叫：「老烏龜，一起來吃！」「{name}也來吧！」{name}聞到香香的味道，肚子咕嚕咕嚕響。
{name}抬頭看看老烏龜。「我們吃一點點，好不好？」老烏龜搖搖頭，笑得很溫柔。「答應了，就要做到。」「貓頭鷹相信我，我不想讓牠失望。」{name}想了一想，點點頭。「對，小鹿也在等我們。」
老烏龜對小猴子說：「對不起，今天不能來。」「我答應過，要先去送信。」「明天我和{name}來幫忙，好嗎？」小猴子拍拍手：「好呀！說好了喔！」牠送給{name}一根香蕉。「帶著路上吃！」
太陽慢慢下山了。天空變成橘色，又變成深藍色。{name}和老烏龜一起分著吃香蕉。兩個好朋友繼續走，一步也沒停下。終於，眼前出現一大片草原。小鹿站在草地上，伸長脖子張望。
就在這時，圓圓的月亮升起來了。老烏龜把葉子信交給小鹿。小鹿打開來看，笑得眼睛彎彎。「貓頭鷹邀我明晚聽牠唱歌！」「你們真的準時送到了！」老烏龜看著{name}，眨眨眼睛。「明天，換我們去找小猴子囉！」
en: Old Tortoise lived in the forest. He was slow but steady. One afternoon, {name} went walking with him. Owl swooped down. "Hoo, hoo! Tortoise, can you take a message for me?" "It's for Deer, in the far meadow. It must get there before the full moon!"

Tortoise did not answer right away. He looked at the sky and the long path. "The meadow is far, and I am slow. But if I start now, I can make it." Then he nodded. "Yes, I promise." Owl gave him a leaf letter. "I'll come too!" said {name}.

Tortoise tucked the leaf letter by his shell. {name} walked right beside him. They passed tall ferns. They climbed a little hill. Step, step, step went Tortoise. {name} slowed down to match him. "Thank you for walking with me," said Tortoise.

Under a big fig tree, the monkeys were having a fruit party! Bananas, mangoes, and sweet papayas were piled high. "Ooh-ooh-ah-ah! Come and eat, Tortoise!" called Little Monkey. "You too, {name}!" {name} smelled the fruit. Grumble went {his} tummy.

{name} looked up at Tortoise. "Can we stop for a bit?" Tortoise shook his head with a gentle smile. "A promise is a promise. Owl trusted me. I don't want to let her down." {name} thought for a moment. "You're right. Deer is waiting for us too."

Tortoise turned to Little Monkey. "I'm sorry. I can't come today. I promised to deliver a letter first. Can {name} and I come help tomorrow?" Little Monkey clapped. "Yes! It's a deal!" She gave {name} a banana. "For the road!"

The sun sank low. The sky turned orange, then deep blue. {name} and Tortoise shared the banana. They kept going and never stopped. At last, a wide meadow opened up ahead. Deer stood in the grass, stretching her neck to look.

Just then, the round full moon rose. Tortoise gave Deer the leaf letter. Deer read it and smiled. "Owl wants me to hear her sing tomorrow night! And you got here right on time!" Tortoise winked at {name}. "Tomorrow, we visit the monkeys!"

questions: 老烏龜答應貓頭鷹以前，先做了什麼事？為什麼？
小猴子邀請的時候，老烏龜怎麼說，讓小猴子還是很開心？
你有沒有答應過別人一件事？後來你是怎麼做到的？
zh.tip: 這週和孩子玩「說到做到」小約定：每天一起訂一個小承諾，例如睡前收好玩具，做到了就在月曆上畫一個小月亮。

questions: What did Tortoise do before he promised Owl? Why do you think he did that?
When the monkeys invited him, what did Tortoise say that still made them happy?
Have you ever promised someone something? How did you keep your promise?
en.tip: This week, make one tiny promise together each day, like putting toys away before bed, and draw a little moon on the calendar each time it's kept.

title.en: {name} and the Garden Behind the Gym

zh: 陳伯伯在學校當了三十年的工友，下個月就要退休了。放學後，他把{name}帶到體育館後面的小花園，指著一排排金盞花和繡球花說：「這些花陪了我好多年，你願意幫我照顧它們嗎？」{name}沒有馬上點頭，而是蹲下來盤算：每天下課澆水、拔草，自己真的辦得到嗎？想清楚之後，{name}才認真地說：「我可以，我答應您。」
頭幾個星期，{name}風雨無阻，天天拎著水壺報到。沒想到梅雨季一來，大雨整整下了五天。雨停那天，林老師陪著{name}來到花園，眼前的景象讓人傻了眼：花圃變成一池泥湯，繡球花東倒西歪，金盞花的花瓣泡得軟趴趴的。「怎麼辦？」{name}喃喃地說，「我答應過陳伯伯的。」
林老師陪{name}繞著花園仔細觀察，終於找出原因：花園比旁邊的走道還低，雨水只進不出。「如果挖一條小水道，把水引到排水溝呢？」{name}眼睛一亮。可是一個人怎麼挖得完？第二天，{name}找來好朋友阿凱、小芸和大寶。大寶拍著胸脯說：「我家有好多鏟子，明天全部帶來！」
隔天，林老師借來學校的工具，在一旁看著大家捲起袖子。大寶卻兩手空空，紅著臉走過來：「對不起，我回家才發現只有一把小鏟子，還是阿嬤種菜要用的。我不該還沒看清楚就亂答應。」他想了想，又說：「不過運泥土交給我，保證一趟都不偷懶！」果然，他推著獨輪車來來回回，跑得滿頭大汗。
大家挖了整整兩個下午，一條彎彎曲曲的小水道終於從花圃延伸到排水溝。林老師提來一桶水試試看，水嘩啦啦地順著溝渠流走，大家忍不住歡呼。接著是補種：小芸從園藝社分來幾株幼苗，阿凱救回還有根的繡球花，{name}一株一株把它們重新種好，連指甲縫裡都塞滿了泥巴。
一個月後，陳伯伯回學校看看。{name}走在前面，心裡七上八下。轉過體育館的牆角，大家都愣住了：金盞花開得黃澄澄，繡球花像一團團藍色的雲。花園入口還立著一塊新木牌，上面寫著「陳伯伯的花園」。連{name}都不知道這塊牌子是哪來的！大寶嘿嘿一笑：「我們三個偷偷做的，這是送給你們兩個的。」
陳伯伯摸著木牌，眼眶有點紅。「下了那麼久的雨，我還以為花都沒救了。」他笑著說，「原來我把花園交給了最靠得住的人。」{name}搖搖頭：「是大家一起救回來的。」陳伯伯從口袋拿出一小包種子：「那明年春天，換你們種點新的吧。」這一次，{name}很快就點了頭，因為心裡清楚：有這群朋友在，一定做得到。
en: Uncle Chen had been the school janitor for thirty years, and next month he was retiring. After school, he led {name} to the little garden behind the gym and pointed at the rows of marigolds and hydrangeas. "These flowers have kept me company for years. Will you look after them for me?" {name} didn't answer right away. Watering and weeding every single day? Could {he} really manage that? After thinking it through, {name} said, "Yes. I promise."

For the first few weeks, {name} showed up every day, rain or shine, with a watering can. Then the rainy season arrived, and it poured for five days straight. When the rain finally stopped, Ms. Lin walked with {name} to the garden. They stared. The flower beds had turned into a muddy soup. The hydrangeas slumped sideways, and the marigolds were soggy and limp. "What do I do?" {name} whispered. "I promised Uncle Chen."

Ms. Lin and {name} circled the garden, studying every corner, until they found the problem. The garden sat lower than the path beside it, so rain poured in and couldn't get out. "What if we dig a little channel to the drain?" {name} said, eyes lighting up. But that was far too much digging for one person. The next day, {name} recruited three friends: Kai, Yun, and Bao. Bao thumped his chest. "My house has tons of shovels. I'll bring them all tomorrow!"

The next afternoon, Ms. Lin borrowed tools from the school shed and stayed nearby as everyone rolled up their sleeves. But Bao arrived empty-handed, cheeks pink. "Sorry. When I got home, I found just one small shovel, and my grandma needs it for her vegetables. I shouldn't have promised before I checked." He thought for a moment. "But I'll haul all the dirt. Every single load!" And he did, racing the wheelbarrow back and forth until he was dripping with sweat.

It took two whole afternoons, but at last a winding little channel stretched from the flower beds to the drain. Ms. Lin poured in a bucket of water to test it. Whoosh! The water rushed away, and everyone cheered. Then came the replanting. Yun brought seedlings from the gardening club, Kai rescued the hydrangeas that still had roots, and {name} tucked each plant back into the soil until there was mud under every fingernail.

A month later, Uncle Chen came back to visit. {name} walked ahead, heart fluttering. They turned the corner of the gym, and everyone froze. The marigolds glowed golden, and the hydrangeas puffed up like blue clouds. At the entrance stood a brand-new wooden sign: Uncle Chen's Garden. Even {name} had no idea where it came from! Bao grinned. "The three of us made it in secret. It's for both of you."

Uncle Chen ran his hand over the sign, his eyes a little wet. "After all that rain, I thought the flowers were gone," he said, smiling. "Turns out I left my garden with the most dependable person I know." {name} shook {his} head. "We saved it together." Uncle Chen pulled a small packet of seeds from his pocket. "Then next spring, why not plant something new?" This time, {name} nodded right away. With friends like these, it could definitely be done.

questions: 陳伯伯請{name}照顧花園時，{name}為什麼沒有馬上答應？你答應別人之前，會先想些什麼？
大寶沒辦法帶鏟子來時，他做了什麼來彌補？如果你答應的事做不到，你會怎麼說、怎麼做？
你覺得陳伯伯看到花園盛開時，心裡有什麼感覺？有沒有人對你說到做到，讓你覺得很被重視？
zh.tip: 這個星期，全家一起練習一句話：「讓我想一想，我做得到再答應你。」每晚睡前分享一件今天說到做到的小事。

questions: When Uncle Chen asked {name} to care for the garden, why didn't {name} say yes right away? What do you think about before you make a promise?
When Bao couldn't bring the shovels, what did he do to make it right? What would you say and do if you couldn't keep a promise?
How do you think Uncle Chen felt when he saw the garden blooming? Has someone kept a promise to you and made you feel important?
en.tip: This week, practice one family phrase together: "Let me think first, so I only promise what I can do." At bedtime each night, share one small promise you kept that day.

zh: 星期五要去校外教學了！老師說，大家要穿有鞋帶的球鞋。{name}看著鞋帶，小聲說：「我還不會綁。」{name}拿起鞋帶，繞一圈，拉一拉。圈圈一下子散開了，像兩條軟軟的麵條。
{name}又試了一次，還是散開了。第三次，鞋帶打成一團小結。{name}把鞋子推開，嘟著嘴說：「我不要綁了！」奶奶從廚房走過來，坐在{his}旁邊。「我們先喝杯牛奶，休息一下吧。」
喝完牛奶，奶奶拿出一個紙箱。她剪下一塊硬紙板，畫成一隻大鞋子。奶奶戳了兩排小洞，穿上一條紅色粗繩。「先在大紙鞋上練習，比較好拉喔。」{name}摸摸紙鞋，開心地笑了。
奶奶說：「我教你一首兔耳朵歌。」她輕輕唱著：「做一隻耳朵，再做一隻耳朵，兩隻耳朵交叉，鑽進小洞，用力拉！」{name}跟著唱，慢慢做出一隻兔耳朵。可是第二隻耳朵歪歪的，咚一聲倒了下去。
「沒關係，我們先只練一隻耳朵。」奶奶說。{name}做了一隻，又做了一隻。每天晚上吃完飯，{name}都抱著紙鞋練習。星期一，兔耳朵站起來了。星期二，耳朵會交叉了。{name}發現，手指捏緊一點，耳朵就不會倒。
星期三晚上，{name}換成真的鞋子。鞋帶比紅繩細，滑滑的好難抓。{name}深深吸一口氣，輕輕唱起兔耳朵歌。綁好的結有點鬆，一隻耳朵大，一隻耳朵小。奶奶拍拍手說：「你自己綁好了耶！」{name}看著歪歪的蝴蝶結，忍不住笑了。
星期四，{name}聽說好朋友小安綁得又快又漂亮。「我綁得好慢喔。」{name}嘆了一口氣。奶奶溫柔地抱抱{him}：「慢慢綁，也能綁得很牢。你每天都在進步呀。」{name}點點頭，睡前又拿起紙鞋，多練了好幾遍。
校外教學那天早上，{name}坐在門口。做耳朵，交叉，鑽洞，用力拉！一隻鞋綁好了，另一隻也綁好了。{name}跳起來大喊：「奶奶，我自己綁好了！」奶奶緊緊抱住{him}。爸爸在門口等著陪{him}去學校，{name}牽著爸爸的手，開心地衝出門。
en: The class field trip is on Friday! Everyone must wear sneakers with laces. {name} stares at the laces. "I can't tie them yet," {he} whispers. {name} makes a loop and pulls. It flops apart like a soft noodle.

{name} tries again. It falls apart again. The third time, the laces turn into a tiny tangled knot. {name} pushes the shoe away. "I quit!" Grandma comes over and sits close by. "Let's have some milk and rest first."

After the milk, Grandma finds a cardboard box. She cuts out a big flat shoe and pokes two rows of holes. Then she threads a thick red string through. "This big shoe is easier to practice on." {name} grins.

"I know a bunny-ears rhyme," says Grandma. She sings softly, "Make one ear, make two ears. Cross the ears, through the hole, pull them tight!" {name} sings along and makes one bunny ear. But the second ear wobbles and flops over.

"That's okay. Let's practice just one ear," says Grandma. {name} makes one ear, then another. Every evening after dinner, {name} practices on the cardboard shoe. On Monday, the ears stand up. On Tuesday, they cross. Pinching tighter keeps them from flopping!

On Wednesday night, {name} tries a real shoe. The laces are thin and slippery. {name} takes a deep breath and sings the rhyme. The bow is a little loose. One ear is big, one is small. Grandma claps. "You tied that on your own!" {name} giggles at the wobbly bow.

On Thursday, {name} hears that friend An ties shoes super fast. "I'm so slow," {name} sighs. Grandma gives {him} a gentle hug. "Slow bows hold tight too. And you get better every day." {name} nods and practices a few more times before bed.

On field trip morning, {name} sits by the door. Make the ears, cross them, through the hole, pull tight! One shoe is done. Then the other! "Grandma, I did it!" {name} shouts. Grandma hugs {him} tight. Dad is waiting to walk to school, and {name} races out the door holding Dad's hand.

questions: {name}想放棄的時候，奶奶做了哪些事幫助{him}？
{name}綁得比小安慢，為什麼還是很開心？
你最近有沒有一件很難、但一直在練習的事？
zh.tip: 這個星期，和孩子一起挑一件小小的難事（像扣釦子或綁鞋帶），每晚練習三分鐘，結束時說一句：「你今天又比昨天多試了一次！」

questions: When {name} wanted to quit, what did Grandma do to help {him}?
{name} tied bows more slowly than An. Why was {name} still happy?
Is there something hard you are practicing right now?
en.tip: This week, pick one small hard task together, like buttons or laces, and practice for three minutes each evening. End by saying, "You tried one more time than yesterday!"

title.en: The Little Drop and Grandpa Stone

zh: 高高的山裡，有一個涼涼的山洞。洞頂掛著一顆小水滴，名叫滴滴。滴滴看著地上那塊又大又硬的石頭爺爺，大聲說：「我要在你身上滴出一個小洞！」石頭爺爺笑得直搖晃：「哈哈哈，小不點，你連我一粒沙都動不了喔！」
「咚！」滴滴跳了下去，摔成一朵小水花，石頭上卻什麼痕跡也沒有。可是滴滴沒有消失，它順著石縫流回山裡，跟著雨水又回到洞頂。第二次，它發現自己歪了一點；第三次，它學會先晃一晃，對準同一個地方再跳。
夏天來了，山洞又悶又乾，滴滴累得只剩小小一顆。「我是不是太小了？」住在石縫裡的青苔奶奶輕聲說：「累了就先歇一歇。今天不用滴出洞，只要讓石頭亮一下就好。」滴滴休息了一整天，再輕輕落下，石頭真的閃了一下光。
冬天一到，滴滴凍成了一根硬梆梆的冰柱，一動也不能動。「這下滴不下去了！」它想了又想，決定換個辦法：等太陽暖暖照進洞口，就一點一點融化，順著冰柱尖尖滑下去。「咚、咚、咚」，竟然比以前更準了。
春去秋來，日復一日，滴滴從沒停過。有一天，石頭爺爺不笑了，反而「哎喲」一聲：「好癢！我身上怎麼多了一個淺淺的小窩？」滴滴開心得直打轉：「它不是世界上最大的洞，可是每一滴都是我滴的！」石頭爺爺佩服地說：「了不起。」
很多很多年以後，{name}跟著外婆去爬山。一路上，{name}一直在練習吹口哨，可是嘴巴只吹得出「呼——呼——」的風聲。「我不想學了。」{name}嘟著嘴說。外婆牽起{his}手：「先陪我進那個山洞涼一涼吧。」
外婆打開手電筒，兩人手牽手走進淺淺的洞口。「咚。」一聲清脆的響聲傳來。{name}蹲下一看，大石頭中間竟然有一個光滑的小水池，圓得像一個碗。一顆小水滴剛好落進池裡，閃閃發亮，好像在對{him}眨眼睛。
「是誰把石頭變成碗的？」{name}驚訝地問。外婆指指洞頂：「就是它呀，一滴一滴慢慢來的。」{name}看了好久，深吸一口氣，噘起嘴輕輕吹——「咻～」細細的口哨聲飛了出來！「雖然很小聲，可是是我自己吹的！」池裡的水滴，也跟著亮了一下。
en: High in the mountains, there was a cool, quiet cave. A tiny water drop named Dipdip hung from the ceiling. Dipdip looked down at Grandpa Stone, big and hard, and called, "I'm going to make a little hole in you!" Grandpa Stone rumbled with laughter. "Ho ho! Little speck, you can't even move one grain of my sand!"

Plink! Dipdip jumped and burst into a tiny splash. The stone didn't change at all. But Dipdip didn't vanish. It trickled through the cracks, rode the rain, and came back to the ceiling. The second time, it noticed it had landed a little crooked. The third time, it wobbled first, aimed, and dropped on the very same spot.

Summer came, and the cave grew stuffy and dry. Dipdip shrank, tired and small. "Maybe I'm just too tiny." Granny Moss, who lived in a crack, whispered, "Rest when you're tired. Today you don't need a hole. Just make the stone shine." Dipdip rested all day, then fell gently. The stone gleamed!

When winter arrived, Dipdip froze into a stiff icicle and couldn't move at all. "Now I can't drop!" It thought and thought, then tried a new way. When the warm sun peeked into the cave, Dipdip melted bit by bit and slid down the icicle's tip. Plink, plink, plink! Its aim was better than ever.

Seasons came and went, day after day, and Dipdip never stopped. One morning Grandpa Stone didn't laugh. He said, "Ooh, that tickles! Where did this little dip come from?" Dipdip spun with joy. "It's not the biggest hole in the world, but I made every drop of it!" Grandpa Stone said softly, "Well done."

Many, many years later, {name} went hiking with Grandma. All along the trail, {name} practiced whistling, but only a windy "whoo, whoo" came out. "I don't want to learn anymore," {name} grumbled. Grandma took {his} hand. "Come cool off with me in that cave first."

Grandma switched on her flashlight, and they walked hand in hand into the shallow mouth of the cave. Plink. A clear little sound rang out. {name} crouched down and gasped. In the middle of a big stone was a smooth little pool, round as a bowl. A drop landed in it, sparkling, as if winking at {him}.

"Who turned the stone into a bowl?" {name} asked. Grandma pointed to the ceiling. "That little drop did, one plink at a time." {name} watched for a long while, took a deep breath, and puckered up. Wheet! A thin whistle floated out. "It's small, but I did it!" Down in the pool, the drop seemed to sparkle too.

questions: 滴滴覺得好累、想放棄的時候，它做了什麼？
{name}最後吹出口哨了嗎？你覺得{he}為什麼又願意試一次？
你有沒有一件事，是一開始很難、練習以後變簡單的？
zh.tip: 這週挑一件孩子正在學的小事，每天只練一下下，練完一起說：「今天又多了一滴！」並在紙上畫一顆水滴做紀錄。

questions: What did Dipdip do when it felt tired and wanted to give up?
Did {name} whistle in the end? Why do you think {he} tried again?
Is there something that was hard for you at first but got easier with practice?
en.tip: This week, pick one small thing your child is learning and practice it for just a moment each day. Afterward, say together, "One more drop today!" and draw a little water drop on a chart.

zh: 星期一晚上，{name}坐在書桌前，盯著一張紅色的正方形色紙。奶奶膝蓋開刀，正在醫院休養，媽媽說奶奶最喜歡紙鶴了。「我要摺一隻最漂亮的送給奶奶！」{name}信心滿滿地宣布。可是十分鐘後，紙角被戳破一個洞，成品看起來像一隻打呵欠的鴨子。
第二張，翅膀一高一低，歪七扭八。第三張，摺線壓得太用力，「嘶」的一聲裂成兩半。家裡的貓咪豆花跳上桌，叼走一團廢紙，彷彿在說：這種東西只配當玩具。{name}把頭埋進手臂裡，悶悶地說：「我是不是天生手很笨？」
爸爸端來一杯熱可可，沒有急著安慰，只是在旁邊坐下。「手累了，就先讓它休息一下。」他說，「明天我們換個方法試試看。」{name}喝完可可，把那堆皺巴巴的紙收進一個舊餅乾盒，在蓋子上寫下三個字：練習用。
星期二，爸爸找出一支摺紙教學影片。影片裡的老師慢條斯理，每摺一下就停一停。{name}這才發現，自己以前太心急，總想一口氣摺完。這次{he}不摺整隻鶴，只練第一步，用舊廣告單摺了一遍又一遍。原來對齊紙角時要先輕輕按住，確定了再用指甲刮出摺線。
星期三練鶴頸，星期四練翅膀。廣告單太滑，{name}改用舊月曆紙，竟然好摺多了。每失敗一次，{he}就記住一件事：這裡要對準中線，那裡不能太用力。到了星期五，餅乾盒塞得滿滿的，紙鶴從「打呵欠的鴨子」漸漸變成「很像鳥的東西」。豆花照樣偷走幾隻，大概覺得越來越好玩了。
星期六早上，{name}深吸一口氣，拿出紅色色紙。對角、壓線、翻面、拉頸，{his}手指不再發抖。翅膀輕輕展開時，紙鶴挺著胸膛站在桌上，左右對稱，神氣極了。{name}又拿出一張藍色色紙：「林護理師每天細心照顧奶奶，也送她一隻！」第二隻摺得又快又穩，彷彿手指自己記得路。
出發去醫院前，奶奶打了視訊電話來。{name}得意地舉起兩隻紙鶴，奶奶笑得眼睛瞇成一條縫。「你知道嗎？我這星期也在練習。」奶奶扶著助行器，慢慢地、穩穩地走了三步。「第一天我只能站一下，今天走得到窗邊了。」{name}看看奶奶，又看看那盒歪歪扭扭的練習紙鶴，決定把整盒也一起帶去。
en: On Monday night, {name} sat at the desk, staring at a square of red paper. Grandma was resting in the hospital after knee surgery, and Mom said paper cranes were her favorite. "I'm going to fold the most beautiful crane ever," {name} announced. Ten minutes later, one corner had a hole poked through it, and the crane looked like a yawning duck.

The second try had one wing up and one wing down, hopelessly lopsided. The third ripped right down the middle because {name} pressed too hard. Doufu the cat hopped onto the desk and batted a crumpled ball away, as if to say, these are toys now. {name} buried {his} face in folded arms. "Maybe my hands are just clumsy."

Dad brought over a mug of hot cocoa. He didn't rush to cheer things up; he simply sat down nearby. "When your hands get tired, let them rest," he said. "Tomorrow, let's try a different way." After the cocoa, {name} gathered the wrinkled scraps into an old cookie tin and wrote two words on the lid: For Practice.

On Tuesday, Dad found a folding video. The teacher moved slowly, pausing after every crease. {name} realized the trouble had been rushing to finish everything at once. So this time, instead of a whole crane, {name} practiced only the first step, again and again, using old flyers. The trick was to line up the corners gently first, then press the crease firm.

Wednesday was for necks. Thursday was for wings. The flyers were too slippery, so {name} switched to old calendar pages, and suddenly folding felt easier. Every mistake taught {him} something: match this edge to the middle, go softer here. By Friday the tin was stuffed full, and the cranes had gone from yawning ducks to almost-real birds. Doufu still stole a few.

On Saturday morning, {name} took a deep breath and picked up the red paper. Corner to corner, crease, flip, pull the neck. No shaky fingers this time. When the wings opened, the crane stood proud and perfectly even. {name} cheered, then grabbed a blue sheet. "Nurse Lin takes such good care of Grandma. She should have one too!" The second crane came quickly, as if {his} fingers remembered the way.

Before they left for the hospital, Grandma video-called. {name} held up both cranes, and Grandma's eyes crinkled with joy. "Guess what? I've been practicing too." Holding her walker, she took three slow, steady steps. "On the first day, I could only stand. Today I made it to the window." {name} looked at Grandma, then at the tin of crooked practice cranes, and decided to bring the whole box along.

questions: {name}覺得自己手很笨的時候，爸爸建議了什麼？後來{name}換了哪些方法？
奶奶為什麼說她也在練習？你有沒有一件事，是慢慢練習之後變得更厲害的？
如果你也有一盒「練習盒」，你想放進什麼？
zh.tip: 這星期和孩子準備一個「練習盒」，把練習中的作品（畫、字、摺紙）放進去，週末一起打開，比較第一個和最後一個，說說進步在哪裡。

questions: When {name} felt clumsy, what did Dad suggest? What new ways did {name} try afterward?
Why did Grandma say she was practicing too? Is there something you got better at by practicing a little at a time?
If you had your own practice box, what would you put inside?
en.tip: This week, make a practice box with your child for in-progress work like drawings, writing, or folding. On the weekend, open it together, compare the first and latest pieces, and name what improved.

zh: 早上，教室裡好安靜。大家都在練習寫字。{name}握著鉛筆，用左手一筆一筆慢慢寫。「大」字寫好了，「小」字也寫好了。{name}看著本子，開心地笑了。今天的字，好像特別整齊呢！
坐在旁邊的小凱探過頭來。「咦，你怎麼用左手寫字？」小凱皺起眉頭說：「那樣是錯的啦！」幾個同學轉過來看。{name}的臉一下子變得好燙。{he}把左手藏到桌子底下，鉛筆也不敢拿了。
美工課到了，大家要剪紙蝴蝶。{name}拿起剪刀，可是剪刀卡卡的。紙一直被折歪，蝴蝶的翅膀還破了一個洞。{name}低著頭，小聲嘆氣。坐在前面的美美回頭說：「沒關係，我陪你再剪一次。」
林老師走過來，蹲在{name}身邊。她看了看剪刀，笑著說：「原來是剪刀的問題。」她從抽屜裡拿出一把綠色剪刀。「這是左手專用剪刀，刀片的方向不一樣。」{name}試了一下，喀嚓喀嚓，好順喔！
下課前，林老師打開大螢幕。螢幕上有畫家、網球選手，還有棒球投手。「他們都是用左手的喔！」老師說。有人用左手畫出美麗的畫，有人用左手打出好球。小凱張大了嘴巴：「哇，好厲害！」
老師又說：「我們來玩個遊戲，換另一隻手寫名字。」教室裡一下子好熱鬧。小凱的字歪歪扭扭，像一條小蟲。美美笑到趴在桌上。小凱抓抓頭，對{name}說：「對不起，換一隻手真的好難。用左手一點也沒錯。」{name}笑了。
林老師問：「誰想幫忙布置左手剪刀角？」{name}第一個舉手。{he}把綠色剪刀排整齊，又畫了一張小牌子。牌子上的字寫歪了，{name}就擦掉重寫。寫了三次，終於好漂亮。小凱和美美也來幫忙貼彩色星星。
從那天起，教室角落多了一個小天地。用左手的同學來拿剪刀，用右手的同學也來試試看。小凱說：「我剪不好，可是好好玩！」{name}拿起鉛筆，用左手大大方方地寫字。窗外的陽光，暖暖地照進教室。
en: The classroom was quiet in the morning. Everyone was practicing writing. {name} held a pencil in the left hand. Stroke by stroke, the letters came out neat. {name} looked at the page and smiled. Today's writing looked extra tidy!

Kai sat at the next desk. He leaned over and frowned. "Why are you writing with your left hand?" he asked. "That's wrong!" A few kids turned to look. {name}'s cheeks felt hot. {name} hid {his} left hand under the desk.

Then it was art time. The class was cutting paper butterflies. {name} picked up the scissors, but they kept getting stuck. The paper bent and tore. One wing ended up with a hole. {name} sighed softly. Mei turned around. "It's okay. Let's try again together."

Ms. Lin came over and knelt beside {name}. She looked at the scissors and smiled. "Ah, these are the trouble." She took green scissors from her drawer. "These are made for left hands. The blades face the other way." Snip, snip! They cut so smoothly!

Before the bell, Ms. Lin turned on the big screen. It showed a painter, a tennis player, and a baseball pitcher. "They all use their left hands," she said. One painted beautiful pictures. Others hit great shots. Kai's mouth fell open. "Wow, so cool!"

"Let's play a game," said Ms. Lin. "Write your name with your other hand." The room got noisy and giggly. Kai's letters wiggled like a little worm. Mei laughed so hard she put her head down. Kai scratched his head. "Sorry, {name}. Switching hands is hard. Left isn't wrong at all." {name} smiled.

"Who wants to help make a left-handed scissors corner?" asked Ms. Lin. {name}'s hand shot up first. {name} lined up the green scissors and drew a little sign. The letters came out crooked, so {name} erased them and tried again. After three tries, the sign looked great! Kai and Mei stuck colorful stars around it.

From that day on, the corner was a busy little spot. Left-handed kids picked scissors there. Right-handed kids came to try them too. "I can't cut well with these, but it's fun!" said Kai. {name} wrote with the left hand, proud and happy. Warm sunshine filled the classroom.

questions: 小凱說用左手是錯的時候，{name}心裡有什麼感覺？
美美和林老師做了什麼，讓{name}覺得好一點？
如果你看到有同學因為不一樣被笑，你可以怎麼做？
zh.tip: 今晚和孩子一起玩「換手挑戰」：用不常用的那隻手畫畫或刷牙，再聊聊大家用不同方式做事有什麼有趣的地方。

questions: How did {name} feel when Kai said using the left hand was wrong?
What did Mei and Ms. Lin do that helped {name} feel better?
If you saw a classmate being laughed at for being different, what could you do?
en.tip: Tonight, play a "switch hands" challenge together: draw or brush teeth with your other hand, then chat about what's fun about people doing things in different ways.

zh: 太陽慢慢下山了。森林要開音樂會囉！貓頭鷹飛來了，烏鴉飛來了，白頭翁也飛來了。{name}坐在大樹下，拍拍小手，等著聽歌。
貓頭鷹先唱：「嗚——嗚——」烏鴉也唱：「嘎！嘎！」白頭翁也唱：「啾哩，啾哩！」三隻鳥一起大聲唱，誰也不讓誰。
嗚嗚，嘎嘎，啾哩啾哩！聲音全都撞在一起。樹葉抖一抖，小兔子摀住耳朵。{name}眨眨眼睛：「好吵喔！」
貓頭鷹說：「我的歌最好聽！」白頭翁說：「我的才最好聽！」兩隻鳥看看烏鴉，笑著說：「你的聲音好粗，不要唱啦。」烏鴉低下頭，躲到樹枝後面。
{name}走到烏鴉旁邊，輕輕摸摸烏鴉的翅膀。「我喜歡你的嘎嘎聲。好響亮，好有精神！」烏鴉抬起頭，眼睛亮亮的。
{name}對大家說：「我們輪流唱，好不好？一個唱，大家聽。」貓頭鷹點點頭。白頭翁點點頭。烏鴉也點點頭。
貓頭鷹唱，嗚——嗚——，低低的，好溫柔。烏鴉唱，嘎！嘎！響響的，好有力。白頭翁唱，啾哩啾哩，高高的，好輕快。白頭翁說：「原來你們的歌也好好聽！」
{name}說：「現在，一起唱吧！」嗚嗚，嘎嘎，啾哩啾哩，變成一首新的歌。星星一顆顆亮起來，風也輕輕搖。烏鴉笑了：「不一樣的聲音，放在一起最好聽！」
en: The sun was sinking low. The forest was having a concert! Owl flew in. Crow flew in. Bulbul flew in too. {name} sat under a big tree, clapping, ready to listen.
Owl sang first. "Hoo, hoo!" Crow sang too. "Caw! Caw!" Bulbul sang too. "Tweedle-tweet!" All three sang loud. Nobody would wait.
Hoo, caw, tweedle-tweet! The sounds bumped and crashed together. The leaves shook. Little Rabbit covered both ears. {name} blinked. "That's so noisy!"
"My song is the best!" said Owl. "No, mine is!" said Bulbul. Then they looked at Crow and giggled. "Your voice is too scratchy. Stop singing." Crow drooped and hid behind a branch.
{name} went over and gently patted Crow's wing. "I like your caw. It's loud and bright and happy!" Crow looked up with shining eyes.
"Let's take turns," said {name}. "One bird sings. Everyone listens." Owl nodded. Bulbul nodded. Crow nodded too.
Owl sang, "Hoo, hoo," soft and low. Crow sang, "Caw! Caw!" strong and loud. Bulbul sang, "Tweedle-tweet," high and light. "Oh!" said Bulbul. "Your songs are lovely too!"

"Now let's sing together!" said {name}. Hoo, caw, tweedle-tweet! It became a brand-new song. One by one, the stars came out. The wind swayed along. Crow smiled. "Different voices sound best together!"

questions: 大家笑烏鴉的時候，{name}做了什麼？你覺得烏鴉心裡感覺怎麼樣？
貓頭鷹、烏鴉和白頭翁的聲音哪裡不一樣？你和你的朋友有什麼不一樣的地方？
如果你看到有小朋友被笑，你可以怎麼做？
zh.tip: 這個星期玩一個「輪流唱」遊戲：每個家人用自己喜歡的聲音唱一句，大家安靜聽完再一起合唱，最後互相說一句「我喜歡你的聲音」。

questions: What did {name} do when the others laughed at Crow? How do you think Crow felt?
How were Owl, Crow and Bulbul's voices different? How are you and your friends different?
What could you do if you saw someone being laughed at?
en.tip: This week, play a "take turns" song game: each family member sings one line in their own favorite voice while everyone listens, then sing together. End by telling each other, "I like your voice."

zh: 放學回家，{name}把書包往沙發一丟，一聲不吭地剝著橘子。阿嬤在一旁摺衣服，抬頭問：「今天怎麼像洩了氣的皮球？」{name}嘆了口氣說，班上新來的小芸戴著助聽器，下課時，有幾個同學躲在走廊竊竊私語，還偷偷叫她「機器人耳朵」。{name}明明聽見了，卻只是低著頭走開。
阿嬤沒有說話，只是輕輕撥開耳邊的頭髮，露出一個小小的、米色的助聽器。{name}愣住了。對啊，阿嬤也戴著它呢！吃飯時，阿嬤總要大家面對她說話；看新聞時，她會笑瞇瞇地盯著主播的嘴巴看。「我用眼睛幫耳朵的忙，」阿嬤說，「每個人聽世界的方法本來就不一樣，這有什麼好笑的？」
{name}眼睛一轉：「阿嬤，妳會手語嗎？」沒想到阿嬤竟然點點頭，說她年輕時在社區教室學過。她慢慢比給{name}看：「你好」、「謝謝」，還有「朋友」——兩隻手的手指勾在一起。{name}依樣畫葫蘆，手指卻像打了結，把「謝謝」比得像在搧風。阿嬤笑得前俯後仰：「你這是在謝謝電風扇嗎？」
那天晚上，{name}對著浴室的鏡子練了一遍又一遍，比到手腕都痠了，也不肯半途而廢。第二天早上出門前，還拉著阿嬤再考一次試。這回每個手勢都比得穩穩的。阿嬤豎起大拇指，又輕輕拍拍{his}肩膀：「勇敢一點，大家會懂的。」
分享時間到了，{name}心臟怦怦跳，走上講台說：「我想教大家三個手語。」教室裡一陣交頭接耳。{name}深吸一口氣，一個一個慢慢比。比到「朋友」時，小芸忽然坐直身子，雙手手指也勾在一起。{name}恍然大悟：這幾天午餐時，小芸常對著{him}做這個動作，原來不是在玩手指，而是在問：「我們當朋友好嗎？」
小芸走上台，笑著把{name}歪掉的「謝謝」調整好，接著教大家「早安」和「加油」。連叫過她「機器人耳朵」的阿哲也舉手問：「『對不起』怎麼比？」小芸大方示範，阿哲紅著臉，認認真真地對她比了一次。下課鐘響了，大家還圍著小芸，七嘴八舌地要學更多。
星期六，小芸和幾個同學來{name}家玩。阿嬤和小芸用手語聊得眉飛色舞，大家搶著學「橘子」和「好吃」怎麼比，客廳裡笑聲此起彼落。阿嬤直誇小芸比得比她還道地。臨走前，小芸對{name}勾起雙手的手指，{name}笑著勾了回去。這一次，不用說一句話，彼此就都懂了。
en: After school, {name} dropped a backpack on the sofa and peeled an orange without a word. Grandma looked up from her folding. "You look like a balloon with the air let out." {name} sighed. A new classmate, Yun, wore hearing aids, and at recess some kids whispered about her in the hallway and called her "Robot Ears." {name} had heard every word, but just walked away.

Grandma said nothing. She simply tucked back her hair and showed a tiny beige hearing aid. {name} blinked. Of course! Grandma wore one too! At dinner she always asked everyone to face her, and during the news she watched the reporter's lips with a little smile. "My eyes help my ears," Grandma said. "Everyone hears the world in a different way. What's funny about that?"

An idea sparked. "Grandma, do you know sign language?" To {name}'s amazement, she nodded. She had taken a class at the community center years ago. Slowly, she showed "hello," "thank you," and "friend," with fingers hooked together. {name} copied her, but those fingers got tangled, and "thank you" came out like flapping a fan. Grandma burst out laughing. "Are you thanking the electric fan?"

That night, {name} practiced in front of the bathroom mirror again and again until both wrists ached, refusing to give up. Before school the next morning, {name} begged Grandma for one last quiz. This time every sign was steady and clear. Grandma gave a big thumbs-up and patted {his} shoulder. "Be brave. They'll understand."

At sharing time, {name}'s heart thumped like a drum. "I want to teach everyone three signs." Whispers rippled around the room. {name} took a deep breath and signed each word slowly. At "friend," Yun sat straight up and hooked her fingers together too. Suddenly {name} understood. All week at lunch, Yun had made that very shape. She hadn't been fidgeting. She'd been asking, "Will you be my friend?"

Yun came to the front, smiled, and gently fixed {name}'s wobbly "thank you." Then she taught everyone "good morning" and "you can do it." Even Jay, who had called her Robot Ears, raised his hand. "How do you sign 'sorry'?" Yun showed him, and Jay, cheeks pink, signed it to her carefully. When the bell rang, everyone still crowded around Yun, begging to learn more.
